components.name: Accordion

does.text: Renders a vertical stack of sections from the `items` array; each section is a header button (title plus chevron) with a content panel below it.
All sections start collapsed; clicking a collapsed header expands it and shows its content panel.
In single mode (default) expanding a section collapses the one that was open, so at most one section is open.
In single mode clicking the open section's header collapses it, so none is open.
With `multiple`, clicking a header toggles only that section; other open sections stay open.
With `defaultValue`, the named section(s) are open on first render and the user can still toggle them (uncontrolled).
With `value` + `onValueChange` the open sections follow `value`; without updating `value` the clicked panel does not open (controlled).

`onValueChange` receives the item `value` string when one opens in single mode, `null` when the open one is collapsed in single mode, and the full array of open values in `multiple` mode (e.g. `['item-1','item-2']`).
The collapsed panel is removed from the page (not just hidden) after the collapse animation (about 0.2 s; none when the user prefers reduced motion).
The header title is the item's `header` content; the expand chevron stays and rotates 180 degrees while the section is open.

Each header button has `id="accordion-header-<value>"` and `aria-controls="accordion-panel-<value>"`; each open panel has `id="accordion-panel-<value>"` and `aria-labelledby="accordion-header-<value>"` (so it is exposed as a region).
Each header button is wrapped in a heading element of the `headerTag` level (`<h3>` by default).
The root container carries the `aria-label` prop when given.
The header button reports `aria-expanded` `true` or `false` for its section.
Clicking anywhere on the header button, including the chevron, toggles the section.

doesNot.text: Does not support nested or child-element composition (no `Accordion.Item`, no JSX children); sections come only from `items`.
Does not collapse the open section on header click when `collapsible` is `false` in single mode; it stays open and `onValueChange` is not called.
Does not toggle or call `onValueChange` when the whole accordion or the clicked item is disabled.
Does not collapse an open section when the accordion is disabled (it keeps showing open if it was open).
Does not apply `collapsible` in `multiple` mode; there every open section can be collapsed.
Does not forward `aria-labelledby` to the root (only `aria-label` is applied).
Does not render any content for sections without `content`, and does not render the header title for items without `header` (the button still shows the chevron).
Does not keep the content of a collapsed section in the page.

defaults.text: `variant` `separated`: sections separated by a gap, each with a rounded corner, an outline only while open, and a filled header (primary container colour) while closed.
`multiple` `false`, `collapsible` `true`, `headerTag` `h3`, `expandIconPosition` `end`, `disabled` `false`.
Chevron icon `ArrowDownSLine` (pointing down when closed, rotated 180 degrees when open).
No section is open when neither `value` nor `defaultValue` is given.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `variant`: `bordered` (a divider line under each section, no gap), `contained` (one outer border with rounded corners around all sections, dividers between, open section filled), `filled` (rounded sections with a gap, open section filled), `separated` (default).
`multiple`: allows several open sections and makes the expanded state an array.
`collapsible={false}`: in single mode the open section cannot be collapsed by clicking it; opening another still switches.
`expandIconPosition="start"`: chevron before the title; `end` after it.
`expandIcon`: replaces the chevron; a static icon rotates 180 degrees while open, a render function receives `{ expanded, className }` and its output is not rotated automatically.
`headerTag`: `h1` to `h6` or `div` wraps the header button (`div` means no heading semantics).
`disabled` on the accordion: every header button is disabled (`disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"`, half opacity, `not-allowed` cursor) and nothing toggles.
`disabled` on an item: only that header is disabled the same way; other sections still work.
`className` on the accordion adds a class to the root; `className` on an item adds a class to that section; `pt` (also per item) is styling only.
`aria-label`: names the accordion root (the label `Spectra.findAccordion(label)` matches).

keyboard.text: Tab moves focus to the header buttons (disabled ones are skipped).
Enter or Space on a focused header toggles its section (once, no double toggle).
ArrowDown moves focus to the next header and wraps from the last to the first; ArrowUp moves to the previous and wraps from the first to the last.
Home focuses the first header, End focuses the last; focus only moves, nothing is expanded.
Arrow, Home and End keys do not skip disabled headers; focus stays where it is when the target header is disabled.

states.text: Collapsed: `aria-expanded="false"`, no content panel in the page.
Expanded: `aria-expanded="true"`, content panel visible, chevron rotated.
Disabled (accordion or item): header button disabled, half opacity, an already open disabled section stays open and cannot be closed.
Focused: header button shows a primary focus outline for keyboard focus (`focus-visible`).
Hover: an enabled, not-open header gets the primary container background in `bordered`, `contained` and `filled`; in `separated` closed headers are already filled.

testApi: `Spectra.findAccordion(label)` / `queryAccordion(label)` (`null` when missing): the root by its `aria-label`.

`getItems()` (all items), `getItem(label)` (by header text, exact or contained; throws when missing), `hasItem(label)`, `getExpandedItems()` (items with `aria-expanded="true"`), `getChildElements()` (raw collection of item elements), `getContainer()`.
`isDisabled()` / `shouldBeDisabled()`: true only when every item is disabled (false for zero items).

`shouldHaveExpandedItemsCount(n)`; each item is an AccordionItem wrapper (see AccordionItem draft: `isExpanded`, `expand`, `collapse`, `toggle`, `getTriggerElement`, `getContentElement`, `getHeaderElement`, `getExpandIconElement`, `focus`, `blur`).

components.name: AccordionItem

does.text: Shows `header` as the title inside a header button, with the expand chevron next to it; the section opens and closes per `Accordion#2` to `Accordion#5`.
When open, shows `content` in a panel below the header (`Accordion#9`, `Accordion#11`).

`value` is the item's identity: it is what `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` carry and what builds the ids `accordion-header-<value>` and `accordion-panel-<value>` (`Accordion#8`, `Accordion#11`).

`disabled: true` disables only this section's header button (`disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"`, half opacity, `not-allowed` cursor); clicking it does nothing and other sections keep working (`Accordion#35`).
`className` adds a class to this section's root element.

doesNot.text: Does not open or close a disabled item by click or Enter/Space; an item that is open and disabled stays open.
Does not render its own `aria-label`: the accessible name of the header button is its header text.
Does not support nested items or its own `onChange`; state lives on the Accordion.
Does not stay unique when two items share a `value`: both open and close together and their ids collide.

defaults.text: Enabled, collapsed, no `className`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `header`: the title; may be any node, a custom node replaces only the title text, the chevron stays.
`content`: the panel body shown when open.
`disabled`: see `AccordionItem#4`.
`pt`: styling only for this item (merged over the Accordion `pt`).

keyboard.text: Same as `Accordion#38` to `Accordion#42`; a disabled item's header cannot take focus.

states.text: Collapsed, expanded, disabled: as `Accordion#43` to `Accordion#45`.

testApi: `Spectra.findAccordionItem(label)` / `queryAccordionItem(label)` (`null` when missing): by the item root, or any element inside it such as the header text; `accordion.getItem(label)` finds one inside an Accordion.
`isExpanded()` / `shouldBeExpanded()` / `shouldNotBeExpanded()` (reads `aria-expanded` of the header button); `isDisabled()` / `shouldBeDisabled()` (header button disabled or `aria-disabled="true"`).
`expand()`, `collapse()`, `toggle()` (clicks the header button; throws on a disabled item), `focus()`, `blur()`.
`getTriggerElement()` (header button), `getHeaderElement()` (heading wrapper), `getExpandIconElement()`, `getContentElement()` (only exists while expanded).

components.name: Alert

does.text: Shows an inline message box with a severity icon, an optional bold `title`, the `children` as description text, an optional `action` and an optional close button.
The icon follows the severity: `success` a check circle, `danger` a cross circle, `warning` an exclamation, `info` and `secondary` the same information icon (they differ by colour only).
Clicking the close button calls `onClose` and then removes the whole alert from the page; it does not come back on re-render (only a remount shows it again).
The root is always a live region: `role="alert"`, `aria-live="assertive"`, `aria-atomic="true"`, for every severity and variant.
The `title` and the description are each rendered only when given; a title-only or description-only alert leaves no empty element for the missing part.
Reports its look on the root as `data-severity` and `data-variant`.
The close button is coloured by the alert severity; for `secondary` it uses the button's default colour.

doesNot.text: Does not close by itself, by timeout, Escape or clicking outside; only the close button dismisses it.
The close button has no `aria-label` and no accessible name (icon-only, no default text), so it cannot be found by name.
Does not hand out focus: the alert itself is not focusable and takes no focus when it appears; only the close button and what `action` holds are focusable.
`role` cannot be overridden: it is always `alert`, whatever the caller passes.
The `action` slot is inert: nothing connects it to the alert, closing it or not is the action's own business.
No controlled visibility prop: the alert cannot be re-opened by the caller after closing.

defaults.text: `severity` `info`; `variant` `light`; `showIcon` true; `closable` false.
No title, no action, no close button.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `severity`: `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info` or `secondary` changes colour and the default icon (see `Alert#2`).
`variant`: `light` (tinted background), `filled` (solid background), `outline` (transparent with coloured border).
`title`: shows the bold title line above the description.
`showIcon={false}`: no icon at all, also when `icon` is given.
`icon`: replaces the severity icon (while `showIcon` is not false).
`action`: shows the node at the far end of the alert, vertically centred.
`closable`: shows a close button after the action; without it there is none.
`onClose`: called once when the close button is clicked, before the alert disappears.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `className`, `style` and any other div attribute: applied to the root; `pt`: styling only.

builtInText.text: none: no built-in text and no built-in `aria-label`.

keyboard.text: Tab reaches the close button (when `closable`) and the focusable parts of `action`; Enter or Space on the close button closes the alert (native button).

states.text: Visible: the default; Closed: removed from the page after the close button is clicked.
Focused: only the close button and action controls take focus; the alert has no focus state of its own.
Disabled, loading, selected: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findAlert(label)`: by the alert's visible text (title or description) or `aria-label`; `Spectra.queryAlert(label)`: `null` when missing; `shouldNotFindAlert(label?)`, `shouldFindAlertCount(label?, n)`.
Sub-parts: `getContainer()`, `getContent()`, `getTitle()`, `getDescription()`, `getIcon()`, `getAction()`, `getCloseButton()` (each throws when the part is not rendered).
Presence: `hasTitle()`, `hasDescription()`, `hasIcon()`, `hasAction()`, `hasCloseButton()`, `isClosable()` (same as `hasCloseButton()`); each has a polling `shouldHave*` / `shouldNotHave*`.
Look: `getVariant()` / `shouldHaveVariant(v)`, `getSeverity()` / `shouldHaveSeverity(s)` (read `data-variant` / `data-severity`).
Text: `getTitleText()`, `getDescriptionText()`, `getText()` with their `should*Text` forms.
Actions: `close()` (alias `dismiss()`): clicks the close button and waits until the alert is gone; `focus(target)` / `blur(target)` with target `closeButton` or `action`.
`isDisplayed()` / `shouldBeDisplayed()`.

components.name: AutoComplete

does.text: Wraps one input child and adds a floating suggestion panel under it as the user types; the child input keeps its own look, size, icons and addons.
Typing at least `minLength` characters opens the panel; with fewer characters (or an emptied input) the panel closes.
Without `onSearch`, the list is filtered locally to options whose label contains the typed text, case-insensitively; with no text, all options are listed.

With `onSearch`, no local filtering is done: the list shows exactly the `options` the parent passes, and `onSearch` is called with the typed text after the `delay` debounce and only once the text reaches `minLength`.
Clicking an enabled suggestion puts its label into the input, closes the panel, and keeps focus in the input.
Disabled options (`optionDisabled` or a `disabled` field, or a disabled group) show `aria-disabled="true"`, cannot be picked, and clicking one leaves the panel open and the input unchanged.
Grouped options show a non-selectable group header above their options; a group whose options are all filtered out shows no header.
The highlighted option has `aria-selected="true"`; hovering an option highlights it.
`loading` replaces the list with a spinner (and `loadingText` when given); `loading` takes priority over the list and the empty message.
With no matching option the panel shows `No results found` (or `emptyMessage`).

The input is a combobox: `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded` follows the panel, `aria-controls` points to the list while open, `aria-activedescendant` points to the highlighted option.
With a multi-value child (`BadgeInput`), picking a suggestion clears the typed text and calls `onChange` with the option's value; it does not write into the child.
Clicking outside the input and panel closes the panel.
The list scrolls when taller than `panelMaxHeight`; the highlighted option is scrolled into view.

doesNot.text: It has no input of its own and no `disabled`, `invalid`, `readOnly` props: those belong to the child input (the child's disabled and invalid states stay as the child shows them).
No dropdown caret or toggle button, and no clear button.
The panel is not opened by focusing or clicking the empty input; only typing at least `minLength` characters or ArrowDown opens it.
Free text is allowed: leaving the input with text that matches no option keeps the text; nothing is forced to be an option.
It does not fetch data: the parent loads suggestions in `onSearch`, sets `loading`, and passes `options`.
`onSearch` does not fire when an option is picked, nor for text shorter than `minLength`.
Enter with no highlighted option does nothing (and does not submit a form); Enter does not pick a disabled option.
Escape closes the panel but keeps the typed text.
The arrow keys do not skip disabled options.
No default loading text: only the spinner shows unless `loadingText` is given.
Group headers are never highlighted or picked.
No label, helper text or error text: those come from the wrapping Field.
The `onChange` argument is the typed or picked label text, not the option object or its `optionValue` (except with a multi-value child).

defaults.text: `minLength` 1; `delay` 300 ms; `closeOnSelect` true; `panelMaxHeight` `200px`.
`optionLabel` `label`, `optionValue` `value`, `optionDisabled` `disabled`, `optionGroupChildren` `items`, `optionGroupLabel` `label`; string and number options are used as their own label and value.
`size` is the child input's size when it has one, else `xs`; an explicit `size` on AutoComplete wins.
Panel closed, input empty; the panel is as wide as the input.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `options`: flat list (strings, numbers, objects) or groups (objects with `items`).
`value` + `onChange`: controlled input text; `defaultValue`: initial text.
`onSearch`, `minLength`, `delay`: remote search as above.
`loading`, `loadingText`: spinner state and its optional text.
`emptyMessage`: replaces `No results found` (not passed through `t()` when given).
`closeOnSelect={false}`: the panel stays open after a pick; Escape then closes it.
`optionLabel`, `optionValue`, `optionDisabled`: a field name, or a function; a label function must return a string or number.
`optionGroupChildren`, `optionGroupLabel`, `renderGroupHeader`: group field names and a custom header.
`renderOption`: custom row content.
`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`: control or start the panel open.
`panelMaxHeight`: number (px) or CSS size.
`pt`: styling of panel, list, item, group header, empty and loading parts.

builtInText.text: Empty panel: `No results found` (locale en, no trailing period, passed through `t()`).

keyboard.text: ArrowDown opens a closed panel (even with fewer than `minLength` characters); with the panel open it moves the highlight down and stops at the last option.
ArrowUp moves the highlight up and stops at the first option; it does nothing when the panel is closed.
Home and End jump the highlight to the first and last option while the panel is open.
Enter picks the highlighted option, closes the panel (unless `closeOnSelect` is false) and puts its label in the input.
Escape closes the panel.
Focus stays in the input throughout; there is no Tab handling by the component.

states.text: Closed / open (`aria-expanded` false / true).
Loading: spinner in the panel.
Empty: the empty message in the panel.
Option highlighted / disabled.
Disabled, invalid, read-only: those of the child input (`disabled`, `aria-invalid="true"`).

testApi: `Spectra.findAutoComplete(name)`: by the input's accessible name; `Spectra.queryAutoComplete(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getValue()` (the input text), `setValue(text)` (types it, opens the panel), `clearValue()`, `selectOption(label | RegExp)`.
`open()`, `close({ via })`, `toggle()`, `isOpen()`.
`getPanel()`, `getContent()`, `getList()`, `getOptions()`, `getOption(...)`, `hasOption(...)`.
`getGroupHeaders()`, `getGroupHeader(...)`, `hasGroupHeader(...)`.
`getEmptyMessage()`, `hasEmptyMessage()`, `getLoadingMessage()`, `hasLoadingMessage()`, `getLoadingIcon()`, `hasLoadingIcon()`, `isLoading()`.
`highlightNext()`, `highlightPrevious()`, `getHighlightedOption()`, `hasHighlightedOption()`, `getHighlightedOptionText()`.
`getInput()`, `getTrigger()`, `getContainer()`, `focus()`, `blur()`, `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()` (read from the child input).

components.name: Avatar

does.text: Shows a round (or square) picture of a person: the photo from `src` or `user.profilePicture`, a person silhouette when there is no photo, or the given `icon`.

The photo is an image whose `alt` is the full name (`name`, else `user.fullName`, else `firstName` and `lastName` joined by a space), or `avatar` when there is no name; the image `width` and `height` are `xs` 16, `sm` 24, `md` 32, `lg` 48, `xl` 64 px.
With no photo, or when the photo fails to load, it shows the person silhouette (an `svg` with `role="img"` and `aria-label` the full name, or `avatar`); the name beside it, if shown, stays.
While the photo loads it shows a shimmer block in its place (see `Shimmer#21`); inside a loading Shimmer it stays a block (see `Shimmer#7`).

`getImageUrl(src)` resolves the real URL (also async) and the photo uses the result; when it resolves to nothing the original `src` is used; when it throws the silhouette shows. Only for a string `src`.
With `showName` a text name shows beside the picture, and the picture keeps its size.

The shown name is `displayName` verbatim when given; otherwise with `formatName` true and no `name` prop, a `user` with both `firstName` and `lastName` shows the short name `First L` (first name whole, last initial, e.g. `Zain K` for Zain Kurnia); any other name shows whole.
`formatName` as a function: its result for the full name is the shown text; `formatName={false}`: the full name shows.
When the shown name differs from the full name, hovering it shows a tooltip above with the full name (see `Tooltip#9`).

With `showPanel` and a `user`, the avatar becomes a button (`role="button"`, `tabindex` 0, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`): clicking it opens a popover panel under it and clicking again closes it (see `Popover#1`, `Popover#4`).

The default panel shows the user's photo, the name (`fullName`, else first and last name, else `nickName`), the email when the user has one, and, when `detailUserPath` is set, a link `View Detail` whose `href` is the path with `{userId}` replaced by `user.id`.

Opening the panel with `getUserDetail` (and `fetchDetailOnPanelShow` true) fetches the full user by `user.id`: the panel shows a shimmer with placeholder name and email while loading, then the fetched user's details.
`onClick(event, { isPanelShown })` is called on each click with the panel state from before that click (`false` on the opening click, `true` on the closing click).
With no `user`, `src`, `name` and `icon` it still renders the root with the silhouette (label `avatar`) and never a panel.
The panel shares the Popover rules for closing: outside click and Escape close it (see `Popover#7`, `Popover#8`); two avatars each have their own panel (see `Popover#4`).

doesNot.text: Does not show initials: with no photo it is the silhouette, never letters from the name.
The panel never opens without a `user`, even with `showPanel`, `panelContent` or `getUserDetail`.
An icon avatar never shows a photo (`icon` and `src`/`user` are mutually exclusive in the types; with `icon` the icon wins).
The formatted short name is never applied to `displayName`, nor to a `name` prop, nor to a `user` with only `fullName`: those show whole.
`onClick` is the only callback: the panel's detail link has no callback (the `onDetailClick` prop is not implemented).
The detail link text cannot be changed and is not translated (`detailUserAnchorText` is not implemented).
A failed `getUserDetail` shows no error element: the panel shows what the given `user` already holds (name, email); the error is logged to the console.
Without `showPanel` the avatar is not focusable, has no role and no `aria-expanded`.
No tooltip when the shown name equals the full name.
The panel is empty when the user object has only `id` (one key) and no `panelContent`.

defaults.text: `size` `md` (32 px); `shape` `circle`; `showPanel` false; `showName` false; `formatName` true; `fetchDetailOnPanelShow` true.
No name beside the avatar, no panel, no link.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` (16, 24, 32, 48, 64 px); may be responsive per breakpoint.
`shape="square"`: rounded corners that grow with the size instead of a circle.
`icon`: shows that element instead of a photo or the silhouette.
`src` overrides `user.profilePicture`; a `Blob` `src` is shown through an object URL.
`name`: the full name used for `alt`, `aria-label` and the name beside the avatar; wins over the `user` name.
`showName`, `displayName`, `formatName`: see `Avatar#6`, `Avatar#7`, `Avatar#8`; a non-text `displayName` (node) shows in place without a tooltip.

`showPanel`: see `Avatar#10`; `panelContent` (node, or function `(user, loading, error)`) replaces the default panel body, `getUserDetail` and `fetchDetailOnPanelShow={false}` (show only the given `user`, no fetch) change the content source; `detailUserPath` adds the link.
`getImageUrl`: see `Avatar#5`; `className`, `pt`, `ref`: root styling and handle.

builtInText.text: Panel link: `View Detail` (locale en, not translated).

Placeholder names: `avatar` (the `alt` and silhouette label with no name), `user avatar` (the panel photo `alt` when the user has no name), `User Full Name` and `user.email@example.com` (shimmer placeholders while the panel loads).

keyboard.text: With `showPanel` the avatar is a tab stop; Enter or Space opens and closes the panel (Popover's click behaviour on a button role)
Enter and Space on a focused avatar call `onClick` (same handler as the click); other keys such as Tab and the arrows do not.

states.text: Photo, silhouette, icon; photo loading (shimmer); panel closed or open (`aria-expanded`).
Panel loading (shimmer while `getUserDetail` runs); panel after a failed fetch (the known user, no error element).
Disabled, selected: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findAvatar(name)`: by accessible name (visible name, photo `alt`, or an `aria-label` passed on the root through `pt.root`); `Spectra.queryAvatar(name)`: `null` when missing.

Sub-parts: `getContainer()`, `getImage()`, `getIcon()`, `getDisplayName()`; presence `hasImage()`, `hasIcon()`, `hasPlaceholder()`, `hasDisplayName()`, `hasPanel()` (panel support is configured), `isPanelOpen()`.
Readers: `getDisplayNameText()`, `getImageSrc()`, `getImageAlt()`, `getPanelUsername()`, `getPanelEmail()` with their polling `should*` forms.
Actions: `openPanel()`, `closePanel()`, `togglePanel()`, `getPanel()`, `clickDetailLink()`, `click()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.

components.name: AvatarGroup

does.text: Shows its `Avatar` children as one overlapping row; each avatar keeps its own rules (see `Avatar#1`) and the whole group has no role of its own.
At most `max` avatars show, always the first ones in the given order; the rest are not in the page at all.
When avatars were left out, a round `+N` indicator shows after the last avatar, N being the number left out.
Only valid elements are counted: `null`, `false`, `undefined` and plain text children are ignored, so they neither take a slot nor add to `+N`.
The indicator is sized and its text styled by the group `size`; when `size` is not set it follows the `size` of the first shown avatar, else `md` (`xs` 16, `sm` 24, `md` 32, `lg` 48, `xl` 64 px).
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` go on the group root, which is what names it.

doesNot.text: The `+N` indicator is not interactive: it opens nothing and no hidden avatar can be reached.
No indicator when the number of avatars is at or below `max`.
The group `size` is not given to the avatars: each avatar keeps its own `size` (default `md`); only the indicator follows `size`.
A fragment or wrapper element counts as one child, not as the avatars inside it.
Does not name its members: the group name is not the avatars' names.

defaults.text: `max` 3.
No `size` (derived, see `AvatarGroup#5`); no accessible name.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `max`: how many avatars show before `+N`.
`size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` for the `+N` indicator.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`: see `AvatarGroup#6`; `className`, `style`, `pt`: root and indicator styling.

builtInText.text: Indicator: `+<N>` (a number, no words, not translated).

keyboard.text: none: the group and the indicator are not tab stops; avatars with `showPanel` keep their own keyboard rules.

states.text: With or without the indicator; no disabled, loading or selected state.

testApi: `Spectra.findAvatarGroup(name)`: by the `aria-label` of the group; `Spectra.queryAvatarGroup(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getContainer()`, `getAvatars()`, `getAvatar(index | name | RegExp)`, `hasAvatar(name | RegExp)`, `getAvatarCount()`.
Indicator: `getExcessIndicator()`, `hasExcessIndicator()`, `getExcessCount()`, `getExcessText()`.
`isDisplayed()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.

components.name: Badge

does.text: Shows a small inline label chip with the `label` text, coloured by `severity` and `variant`; the root is `role="status"` and its `aria-label` is the label text.
A missing, empty or `-` label (not a dot) shows a plain `-` with no badge styling and `aria-label` `Invalid value`; the number `0` counts as a real value and shows a normal badge.
With `variant="dot"` it shows only a small coloured circle: no label text and no remove button, whatever `label` holds.
Reports its look on the root as `data-severity`, `data-variant` and `data-size`.
`textOverflow="middle-ellipsis"` shows a label longer than 25 characters as its first 12 characters, `..`, its last 12; a label of 25 or fewer characters shows whole.
When the shown text differs from the label (truncated or reformatted), hovering the badge shows a tooltip above it with the full label (see `Badge#15`).
A `textOverflow` function receives the label and its result is the shown text.
A removable badge shows a round remove button after the label; clicking it calls `onRemove`.
An editable badge lets the user type into the label in place (the label is a `textbox`, content-editable); Enter or Tab ends the edit and commits, Backspace, Delete and the arrow keys always work.
Committing an edit trims the text and calls `onChange(newLabel, previousLabel)`; it is called on every end of edit, also when the text did not change.
Escape while editing cancels: the label text returns to what was shown before, `onChange` is not called, and the Escape does not reach an enclosing Dialog.
With `maxLength`, typing a character at or beyond that length while editing is blocked.
With `restoreOnEmpty`, committing an empty text puts the previous label back.
Committing an empty text on a `removable` badge without `restoreOnEmpty` removes the badge from the page and calls `onRemove`.
The tooltip of `Badge#6` is the shared Tooltip: timing and keyboard behaviour are `Tooltip#1`, `Tooltip#2`; this use is `Tooltip#9`.

doesNot.text: Does not wrap or grow: the label stays on one line and is clipped when the space is short (`clip` never shortens the text).
`textOverflow="user-name-ellipsis"` is deprecated and shortens nothing: the label shows whole.
The editable label and the remove button are not tab stops (`tabindex` -1); Tab does not reach them.
A disabled badge is not editable: its label is plain text, not a `textbox`; its remove button is disabled and clicking it does not call `onRemove`.
An empty edit does not remove the badge when `removable` is not set, and does not call `onRemove`.
The remove button is not shown on the `dot` variant.
No tooltip when the label is shown whole and no `tooltip` is given.
Pasting is not length-limited by `maxLength` (only typed keys are checked)

defaults.text: `severity` `primary`; `variant` `light`; `size` `xs`; `textOverflow` `clip`; `role` `status`.
Not editable, not removable, not disabled; `restoreOnEmpty` false; no tooltip.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `severity`: `primary`, `secondary`, `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info` or `contrast` sets the colour.
`variant`: `light` (tinted), `filled` (solid), `outline` (border only), `dot` (see `Badge#3`).
`size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`; may be responsive per breakpoint.
`tooltip`: shows that text as the hover tooltip instead of the automatic full-label tooltip.
`removable`: shows the remove button (see `Badge#8`).
`removeButtonDisabled`: shows a disabled remove button on a badge that is not `removable`; with `removable` set the button stays enabled.
`disabled`: the whole badge is disabled (`data-disabled` `true`), see `Badge#19`.
`editable`: enables in-place editing (see `Badge#9`).
`role`, `aria-label`: replace the defaults; other span attributes and `className`, `style` go to the root; `pt`: styling only.

builtInText.text: Remove button `aria-label`: `Remove badge` (locale en, passed through `t()`).
Placeholder for a missing label: `-` with `aria-label` `Invalid value` (locale en, passed through `t()`).

keyboard.text: While editing: Enter or Tab commits (nothing is inserted), Escape cancels, see `Badge#9`, `Badge#11`.
Nothing else: the badge, the label and the remove button are not tab stops.

states.text: Normal, disabled (`Badge#19`), editing (cursor in the label, root shows the primary focus outline)
Tooltip: shown on hover when the shown text differs from the label or `tooltip` is set; also while the DataTable cell holding the badge has keyboard focus
Selected, loading: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findBadge(label)`: by the label text or `aria-label` (a dot badge needs an `aria-label`); `queryBadge(label)`: `null` when missing; `findBadgeAt(index)` / `queryBadgeAt(index)`: by 0-based position in document order (inside a wrapper it searches inside it), for badges without a name; `Spectra.shouldHaveBadgeCount(n)` polls the count (also on a wrapper).
Sub-parts: `getContainer()`, `getLabelElement()`, `getRemoveButton()`; `hasLabel()`, `hasRemoveButton()`, `isRemovable()`.
Readers: `getText()`, `getValue()` (label string), `getSize()`, `getVariant()`, `getSeverity()` with `shouldHaveSize`, `shouldHaveVariant`, `shouldHaveSeverity`, `shouldHaveValue`.
State: `isDisplayed()`, `isDisabled()`, `isEditable()`, `isRemoveButtonDisabled()` and their `shouldBe*` forms.

Actions: `remove()` clicks the remove button; `setValue(text)` replaces the text and commits; `clearValue()`; `type(text)` types by keystroke and commits nothing; `paste(text)` pastes into the label being edited; `clearDraft()` empties the label by keystroke and leaves the edit open.

components.name: BadgeGroup

does.text: Shows `items` as a single row of read-only badges (see `Badge#1`), each a `role="listitem"` inside a root with `role="list"`; the row does not wrap.
An item is a plain string or `{ label, severity?, tooltip? }`; a string is the same as an item with only a label.
With `limit`, only the first `limit` badges show and, when more items exist, a `+N more` button shows after them, N being the number hidden.
Clicking `+N more` opens a modal dialog (`size` small) headed `All Items` that lists every item as a badge, the shown ones too, not only the hidden ones.
The dialog closes like any Dialog (close button, Escape, backdrop; see `Dialog#3`, `Dialog#4`, `Dialog#5`); Escape closes only the overflow dialog, not a Dialog the group sits in.
The `+N more` button names the dialog it opens (`aria-controls`) and reports `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`; clicking it does not bubble to a clickable parent (such as a table row).
An item `severity` wins over the group `severity`; an item `tooltip` shows on hover of that badge (see `Badge#29`).
`textOverflow` applies to every badge, in the row and in the dialog (see `Badge#5`, `Badge#6`).
With no items (empty list) it shows only a plain `-` with `aria-label` `Invalid value`, not a list.

doesNot.text: Badges in the group are not editable, not removable and not disabled; the group takes no `onChange` or `onRemove`.
Without `limit` there is no `+N more` button and no overflow dialog at all; there is no automatic cap.
`limit={0}` is the same as no limit: all badges show and no overflow dialog exists.
The `+N more` button is absent when the item count is at or below `limit`, even though the dialog element is mounted (closed).
The group does not shrink to fit the width: items past `limit` are never hidden by space, only by `limit`.
The `moreLabel` and `overflowDialogHeader` texts are shown as given; they are not passed through the translator.

defaults.text: `severity` `primary`; `textOverflow` `clip`; no `limit` (all items show).
`moreLabel` `more` (button reads `+N more`); `overflowDialogHeader` `All Items`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `limit`: shows the first `limit` items and enables the `+N more` button and dialog.
`moreLabel`: replaces the word after the count (`+4 <moreLabel>`).
`overflowDialogHeader`: replaces the dialog title.
`overflowDialogContent(items)`: replaces the badge list in the dialog body; it receives all items as `{ label, severity?, tooltip? }`, not only the hidden ones, and the dialog header stays.
`severity`, `textOverflow`: group defaults for every badge (see `Badge#26`, `Badge#5`).
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`: name the list; `className`, `pt`: styling only.

builtInText.text: Overflow button: `+<N> more` (locale en, not translated, see `BadgeGroup#15`).
Dialog header: `All Items` (locale en, not translated).
Empty group placeholder: `-` with `aria-label` `Invalid value` (locale en, through `t()`).

keyboard.text: The `+N more` button is a native button: Tab focuses it, Enter or Space opens the dialog; inside the dialog focus rules are `Dialog#8`, `Dialog#48`; Escape closes it (`BadgeGroup#5`).

states.text: Overflow dialog closed (initial) or open; the button reports it with `aria-expanded`.
Selected, disabled, loading: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findBadgeGroup(name)`: by the `aria-label` of the list; `Spectra.queryBadgeGroup(name)`: `null` when missing.
Inline badges: `getBadges()`, `getBadge(index | label | RegExp)`, `hasBadge(label)`, `getBadgeCount()`, `getBadgeLabels()`.
More button: `getMoreButton()`, `hasMoreButton()`, `getMoreCount()`, `getMoreText()`, `clickMoreButton()`.

Overflow dialog: `isOverflowDialogOpen()`, `openOverflowDialog()`, `closeOverflowDialog()`, `getOverflowDialog()`, `getOverflowDialogHeader()`, `getOverflowBadges()`, `getOverflowBadge(index | label | RegExp)`.
`isDisplayed()`.

components.name: BadgeInput

does.text: Typing text and pressing Enter turns the trimmed text into a new badge at the end of the list, empties the text field and keeps focus in it.
Text still in the field when it loses focus is added as a badge just like Enter.
Leading and trailing spaces of an entry are removed before it becomes a badge.
A new entry that equals an existing badge exactly (case-sensitive) is rejected: no badge is added and a popover with `Value already exists` appears under the field.
A `validate` message for a new entry is rejected the same way: no badge is added, the typed text stays in the field and the message shows in a popover under the field.
An error popover goes away as soon as the user types, focuses a badge, or edits a badge.
Clicking a badge's remove button removes that badge.
Backspace in an empty text field removes the last badge.
Every badge is editable inline by default: the user edits its text in place and the change is committed on Enter, Tab or when the badge loses focus.

An edited badge is checked against the other badges only, so a case-only rename of itself is accepted while a rename onto another badge is rejected with `Value already exists` shown in a popover above that badge, which keeps its old text.
Pressing Escape while editing a badge cancels the edit, restores the old text and does not close an enclosing Dialog.
Clearing the text of a badge being edited removes that badge.
Badges show in the secondary colour, in the order they were added.
With `draftFilter`, typed or pasted text is rewritten by the filter before it shows in the field; badges already added are not changed.
With `validateEmpty`, Enter or blur on an empty draft runs `validate` with an empty text and shows the message it returns in the error popover; a draft that passes is still not added.
With `maxLength`, the text field and an inline badge edit both stop accepting characters past that length.
Badge removal, edit and add each call `onChange` with the full new list, and `onAddBadge`, `onRemoveBadge`, `onEditBadge` with their own arguments.

doesNot.text: An empty or whitespace-only draft never becomes a badge, with or without `validateEmpty`.
Without `validateEmpty`, an empty draft on Enter or blur is dropped silently: no error shows and `validate` is not called.
There is no built-in format check (email or otherwise); only `validate` and the duplicate check reject an entry.
Typing a separator such as a comma does not create a badge; only Enter or blur does.
The duplicate check does not trim or ignore case: `react` is not a duplicate of `React`.
Pressing Backspace in an empty field does not remove a badge that `isRemovable` rejects.
A rejected entry is never added, and the typed text stays in the field.
The `Value already exists` text is not translated.
No label, description or required marker is shown by the component; a Field supplies those.

defaults.text: Placeholder `Enter value`.
Size `xs`.
Starts with no badges and an empty text field when neither `value` nor `defaultValue` is given.
Duplicates are rejected, every badge is editable and removable, and the remove button is hidden (not disabled) on a badge that is not removable.
Clearing an edited badge removes it instead of restoring the old text.
No `maxLength`, no `validate`, no start or end element or addon.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `value` with `onChange`: controlled; a `value` without `onChange` refuses every add, edit and removal.
`defaultValue`: initial badges, the component keeps the list itself.
`allowDuplicates`: the same text can be added again and the duplicate message never shows.
`isEditable(value, index)` returning false: that badge cannot be edited inline.
`isRemovable(value, index)` returning false: that badge has no remove button and cannot be removed by click, Backspace or Delete.
`removeButtonVariant: 'disabled'`: a badge that is not removable shows its remove button greyed out instead of hiding it.
`restoreValueOnEmpty`: clearing a badge being edited restores its old text instead of removing it.
`errorOverlayMessage(reason)`: replaces the text in the error popover.
`errorOverlayIcon`: replaces the warning icon in the error popover.
`size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md` or `lg` (also per breakpoint) sets the badge and text size.
`placeholder`: replaces `Enter value`.
`startElement`, `endElement`: content inside the field border; `startAddon`, `endAddon`: content outside it.
`disabled`: the text field is disabled, the badges are greyed out, nothing can be clicked, typed, edited or removed.
`readOnly`: the text field is read-only, badges show no remove button and cannot be edited, and nothing can be added or removed.
`invalid`: the field is styled invalid and the text input carries `aria-invalid="true"`; an explicit `aria-invalid` wins.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling only (`className` and `style` apply to the badge container).

builtInText.text: Placeholder: `Enter value` (locale en).
Duplicate message: `Value already exists` (not localized).
The remove button of each badge has the accessible name `Remove badge` (locale en).
The text field and the badges expose no built-in accessible name; the name comes from a `<label>`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

keyboard.text: Enter in the text field adds the draft as a badge.
Backspace in an empty text field removes the last badge.
ArrowLeft with the caret at the start of the text field moves focus to the last badge.
On a focused badge, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move to the previous and next badge; ArrowRight on the last badge returns to the text field.
On a focused badge, Backspace or Delete removes it and focus moves to the previous badge, else the next, else the text field.
On a focused badge, Enter starts editing its text with the caret at the end.
While editing a badge: Enter or Tab commits, Escape cancels.
Arrow keys on a badge do nothing while its text is being edited.

states.text: Idle: badges and an empty text field with the placeholder.
Draft: text in the field, not yet a badge.
Error: a popover with the reason under the field (new entry) or above the badge (edit), until the user types or focuses a badge.
Editing: one badge is editable in place.
Disabled, read-only, invalid: see the configured props.
Loading: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findBadgeInput(label)`: by the accessible name of the text field (label, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`); `Spectra.queryBadgeInput(label)`: `null` when missing.
`getContainer()`, `getInput()`, `isDisplayed()`, `getInputValue()` (draft, untrimmed), `getPlaceholder()`.
`focus()`, `blur()`, `type(text)`, `clearDraft()`, `paste(text)`, `addBadge(value)` (types and presses Enter).
`getBadges()`, `getBadge(indexOrLabel)`, `hasBadge(label)`, `getBadgeCount()`, `getValues()`.
`removeBadge(indexOrLabel)`, `editBadge(indexOrLabel, newValue)`, `cancelEdit()` (Escape), `clearAll()`.
`getErrorText()`: text of the open error popover.

`isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`; `should*` for each reader (`shouldHaveBadgeCount`, `shouldHaveValues`, `shouldContainValues`, `shouldHaveBadge`, `shouldNotHaveBadge`, `shouldHavePlaceholder`, `shouldHaveInputValue`).

components.name: Breadcrumb

does.text: Shows the trail of `items` in order as an ordered list inside a `<nav>`, with a separator between neighbours.
The last item is the current page: its `<li>` has `aria-current="page"`, no other item does, and its text is drawn emphasised in a muted colour.
An item with `href` is a link that goes to that route inside the app without a full page reload (through the router link); an item without `href` is plain text in a `<span>`, with no anchor.
An item may show an icon before its label; an item without `icon` has no icon part.
The separator sits only between items (count is items minus one), is hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`) and is not clickable.
With `renderLink`, every item that has `href` is drawn by the app's own link component, given `href` and the icon plus label; items without `href` still render as plain text.
A single item shows no separator and is the current page.
The nav can be named with the app's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
A non-last link is coloured like a link (brand accent); the current page and any item without `href` use neutral text colours and a default cursor.

doesNot.text: Does not collapse or shorten long trails: no ellipsis or "more" menu, every item is shown.
Does not work out the trail from the URL: the app passes every item.
Does not turn the last item into plain text for you: if the last item has `href` it still renders as a link (the cursor is the default one), and still has `aria-current="page"`.
An item without `href` in the middle of the trail (a non-navigable ancestor) is plain text, not a link, and still has a separator after it.
Does not translate item labels: they show exactly as given.
A custom link from `renderLink` does not get the built-in link styling or `data-ui-section` parts of the default link.
Only `className`, `ref`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` reach the `<nav>`: other HTML attributes (such as `id` or `data-*`) are not forwarded.
The default link needs a router around the app: it is not a plain `<a>`.

defaults.text: `separator` is a small right-pointing chevron icon (3.5 units wide); `renderLink` is the router link.
The nav's accessible name is `Breadcrumb` when no `aria-label` is given.
With `items: []`, the nav and an empty list render, with no item and no separator.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `separator`: replaces the chevron between every pair of items with the given node.
`renderLink`: replaces the router link for items with `href` (see `Breadcrumb#6`).
`aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`: changes the nav's accessible name; given `aria-labelledby` without `aria-label`, `aria-label` is still `Breadcrumb` and the labelling element wins.
`item.icon`: shows the icon before the label (a node, a component or a render function).
`className` is added to the `<nav>`; `ref` points at the `<nav>`.

builtInText.text: The nav's `aria-label` is `Breadcrumb` (English, through the app's translation).

keyboard.text: Tab moves through the links in order (native anchors), Enter follows the focused link; items without `href` are not focusable.

states.text: Current page: `aria-current="page"` on the last `<li>`.
Link item: hover changes colour; a focused link shows a primary focus ring.
Empty trail: see `Breadcrumb#20`.

testApi: `Spectra.findBreadcrumb(label)` / `queryBreadcrumb(label)`: the nav by accessible name (`Breadcrumb` by default); `queryBreadcrumb` gives `null`. `Spectra.shouldNotFindBreadcrumb(label?)`, `Spectra.shouldFindBreadcrumbCount(label?, count)`. Also chained from a container.
`getContainer()`, `getList()`, `element`: the nav, the `<ol>`.
`getItems()` / `getItemCount()` (`shouldHaveItemCount(n)`) / `getItemLabels()` (`shouldHaveItemLabels([...])`).
`getItem(index)` / `getItemByLabel(label | RegExp)`: the `<li>`.
`getItemLink(index)` / `getItemLinkByLabel(label)`: the link, or the text span for an item without `href`.
`getItemHref(index)`: the `href` or `null`; `shouldHaveItemHref(href | null, index)`.
`clickItem(indexOrLabel)`: clicks the item's link.
`getCurrentItem()`, `getCurrentItemLabel()` (`shouldHaveCurrentItemLabel`), `isCurrentItem(indexOrLabel)` (`shouldBeCurrentItem` / `shouldNotBeCurrentItem`).
`getSeparators()` (`shouldHaveSeparatorsCount(n)`), `getSeparatorText(index?)`.
`hasIcon(indexOrLabel)` (`shouldHaveIcon` / `shouldNotHaveIcon`), `getIcon(indexOrLabel)`.

components.name: BulkActionButton

does.text: The bar is on the page only while at least one row is selected; with an empty selection nothing is rendered and no space is reserved.

With the default `select` type the bar shows, left to right: the action menu trigger, extra content (`children`), Apply (only for a staged addition-slot action), the selection message, the select-all button, and a clear X.
The selection message counts every selected row across all pages: `1 item selected`, `3 items selected` (locale en).
The default action trigger is an outlined dropdown button labelled `Bulk Action` with a down chevron; clicking opens an inline menu of the `options`.
Picking a menu item with a `command` runs it, closes the menu and keeps the selection.

Picking an item with `useAdditionSlot` does not run its command: the trigger label becomes that item's label, the `children` render function receives the item, and `Apply` appears; Apply runs the command, removes Apply and restores the label `Bulk Action`.
Menu items with `visible: false` are not listed; `danger` items are marked danger; a `disabled` item is listed but its click does nothing; an item `tooltip` shows on hover and goes away on unhover.

An item with `url` (and no `command`) calls `window.open(url, target)` for http/https URLs only (a new window or the item's `target`, no opener); an item with `route` (and no `command`/`url`) only calls `history.pushState` with it: no page reload, and a router is not told.

A select-all button appears when the selection is non-empty, the bar is not disabled, at least one selectable record exists, and there is a `dataView` or a `fetchAll`; its visible text is `Select All (N records)`.
N is the count of all selectable rows matching the current search and filters (disabled/unselectable rows excluded), whether or not some are already selected; `1` reads `Select All (1 record)`.

Clicking select-all fetches every matching record and selects them all, showing a loading state on the button meanwhile; once everything selectable is selected the button reads `Unselect All (N records)` and clicking it clears the selection (the bar disappears).

The select-all text is `Select All (N records)` while the selected count differs from N, and `Unselect All (N records)` exactly when the selected count equals N (N = table total under the current search/filters minus disabled rows; equal counts, not membership). Selection on one page or spread over several pages but short of N reads `Select All`; it flips to `Unselect All` only once all N are selected, whether by the button or by hand across pages. It does not depend on the current page or on `selectAllAcrossPages` of the DataTable; it is absent at zero selected (the bar is hidden).
The clear X empties the selection and the bar disappears.
Closing the menu with Escape or an outside click keeps the selection.
With `disabled` the action trigger is disabled and the select-all button is hidden; the message and the clear X stay.

doesNot.text: The bar does not select rows itself; it only reads and clears the table's selection.
Selecting an action does not clear the selection.
Select-all over the cap with no `onSelectAllExceedsMax` does nothing visible (dev console error only); no dialog is shown by the component.
A failing `fetchAll` selects nothing and shows no message; the error only goes to the console unless `onSelectAllError` is given.
The visible select-all text and its accessible name differ: text `Select All (N records)`, name `Select all records` (`Unselect all records` when everything is selected).
The clear X has no text, only an accessible name.
The overlay-panel ellipsis trigger has no text and no aria-label from the component.
The clear X is not disabled by `disabled`.
A DataTable does not render a BulkActionButton; the page places it and pairs it with the same `dataView`.
The menu is not portaled; it renders inside the bar.
No confirm dialog on clear.

defaults.text: Bar hidden (null) until rows are selected.
`selectMenuType` `'select'`; menu trigger shown (`hideActionMenu` false); `disabled` false.
`maxSelectAllRecords` 10000; over the cap with a confirm handler the handler decides, without one the select-all aborts.
`tableName` `datatable`.
Select-all count is the table's selectable total; standalone it is the `totalRecords` prop (0 hides select-all).
English default texts from locale constants (`bulkSelectionMessage`, `bulkSelectAll`, `bulkUnselectAll`); the other labels are component props.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `ariaLabel` makes the root a `role="toolbar"` with that name; without it the root is an unnamed plain container.
`selectMenuType: 'overlay-panel'` replaces the labelled dropdown with a small round icon-only ellipsis trigger placed after the select-all button; the menu is the same.
`hideActionMenu` removes the menu trigger (both types); message, select-all and clear X stay.
With no visible `options` the trigger still renders and opens a menu showing `No options available`.
`useAdditionSlot` on an item enables the staged-action flow (see BulkActionButton#6) and `onApply()` fires after Apply.

`selectionMessage`, `selectAllMessage`, `unselectAllMessage` (ICU with `{count}`) change the texts; the deprecated `naming` or `currentSelectionMessage` build the legacy `{n} {naming} selected` selection text (e.g. `3 Asset selected`) only while `selectionMessage` is not set; `selectAllRecords` / `allRecordSelected` build the legacy select-all text only while `selectAllMessage` / `unselectAllMessage` is not set.
`dropdownPlaceholder`, `applyButtonLabel`, `selectAllAriaLabel`, `unselectAllAriaLabel`, `clearSelectionAriaLabel` rename the trigger text, Apply text and accessible names.
`maxSelectAllRecords` sets the select-all cap; `onSelectAllExceedsMax(count)` (may be async) resolving `true` lets an over-cap select-all proceed, `false` aborts.
`fetchAll` supplies the full set for select-all when no `dataView` (or another source); `onSelectedDataChange(rows)` receives the result and `[]` on clear.
`selectedData` / `totalRecords` props override the `dataView` values; with `selectedData` and no `dataView` the bar is standalone, and clear X only calls `onSelectedDataChange([])`.
`onSelectAllError(error)` receives a failed `fetchAll`.

`children(selectedOption)` renders custom controls next to the trigger; it is called also with `undefined` when no action is staged, and only while the menu trigger is shown (not with `hideActionMenu`).
`disabled` (see BulkActionButton#14).

builtInText.text: `Bulk Action` (trigger label, `dropdownPlaceholder`).
`1 item selected` / `N items selected` (selection message, locale en).
`Select All (N records)` / `Select All (1 record)`; `Unselect All (N records)` / `Unselect All (1 record)` (select-all text).
`Select all records` / `Unselect all records` (select-all aria-label).
`Clear selection` (clear X aria-label).
`Apply` (staged-action button).
`No options available` (empty menu).

keyboard.text: Trigger, select-all, Apply and clear X are native buttons: Tab to focus, Enter or Space to activate.
Escape closes an open menu, the selection stays; when focus was inside the menu it returns to the element that was focused before the menu opened (normally the trigger).
The selection message is an `aria-live="polite"` `role="status"` region.

states.text: Hidden (no selection) / shown.
Menu closed / open (`aria-expanded` on the trigger, `aria-haspopup="true"`).
Action staged (trigger shows the item's label, Apply present) / none.
Select-all label `Select All` / `Unselect All` (everything selected); loading while fetching.
Disabled (trigger disabled, select-all hidden).

testApi: `Spectra.findBulkActionButton(name)` / `queryBulkActionButton(name)`: by `ariaLabel`, or without one by the trigger label (`Bulk Action`). `find*` throws when the bar is absent (no selection); `query*` returns `null`. Look up after the selection exists.
`getSelectionMessage()`: shouldHaveSelectionMessage(text); `getSelectedCount()`: shouldHaveSelectedCount(n), parsed from the message.
`isDisabled()`: shouldBeDisabled / shouldNotBeDisabled (action menu).

`hasMenuTrigger()`: shouldHaveMenuTrigger (absent under `hideActionMenu`); `isMenuOpen()`: shouldBeMenuOpen / shouldNotBeMenuOpen; `openMenu()`, `closeMenu({ method })` (Escape, or `'trigger'`); selection stays.

`getMenuItems()`: shouldHaveMenuItems([...]); empty while closed; `isMenuItemDanger(label)`, `isMenuItemDisabled(label)`, `getMenuItemIconName(label)` (shouldHaveMenuItemIconName): open the menu first.
`selectAction(label)`: opens the menu if needed and picks the item; throws when absent.
`getPartLabels()`: shouldHavePartLabels([...]); bar parts left to right, text or accessible name.
`hasSelectAll()`: shouldHaveSelectAll; `getSelectAllLabel()`; `selectAllRecords()` toggles select/unselect; `isAllRecordsSelected()`: shouldBeAllRecordsSelected.
`clearSelection()`: clicks the X (bar unmounts); `hasApply()`: shouldHaveApply; `apply()`: clicks Apply.
`getContainer()`: the root.

components.name: Button

does.text: Clicking an enabled button calls `onClick` once per click.
A disabled button (`disabled`) is a native disabled button with `aria-disabled="true"`: it cannot take focus, a click does nothing, the pointer is inert and the cursor is the default arrow.
A loading button (`loading`) behaves as disabled: native disabled, `aria-disabled="true"`, `aria-busy="true"`, `onClick` is not called. `isDisabled()` and `isLoading()` are both true.
Loading shows a spinner in the left-icon position: `leftIcon` is replaced by it; `rightIcon` and the icon-only `icon` are hidden. With no `leftIcon` the spinner still shows before the label.

Loading with `loadingText` replaces the visible label text with `loadingText`; loading without `loadingText` keeps the label unchanged; an icon-only button (no label, no children) shows no `loadingText`, only the spinner.
The label is `label`, else `children`, rendered in one label element; `label` wins when both are given.
An icon-only button (no `label`, no `children`, `icon` set) shows only the icon; `icon` is not drawn when a label or children exist (use `leftIcon` / `rightIcon`).
`badge` (a string) shows as a count badge after the label and before `rightIcon`; the badge text is the readable `getBadgeText()`.
The root always carries the rendered look as attributes: `data-variant`, `data-severity`, `data-size`.

doesNot.text: No tooltip: not on hover, not on focus, not when disabled, not when loading (Button has no tooltip wiring; a disabled button does not explain itself; a native `title` passed through `...rest` is the only hover text).
A disabled or loading button never calls `onClick`, also on `click({ force: true })` (native disabled plus an inert pointer plus a guard in the handler).
No built-in loading text: with `loading` and no `loadingText` nothing like `Loading...` appears.
No default `aria-label`: an icon-only button without `aria-label` has no accessible name, and `Spectra.findButton(name)` cannot find it.
Not a submit button by default: it does not submit a form unless `type="submit"`.
The spinner and every icon are `aria-hidden`; they add nothing to the accessible name.

With `asChild`: the spinner, `loadingText`, label, icons and badge are not rendered by Button; it only merges its props, `aria-disabled`, `aria-busy` and the `data-*` look into the child, and the child is not natively disabled (clicks are suppressed by the handler).

defaults.text: `type="button"`, `disabled` false, `loading` false, `asChild` false.
Look when unset: variant `filled`, severity `primary`, size `xs` (as data attributes).
No label, no icon, no badge until given.
An enabled, idle button carries `aria-disabled="false"` and `aria-busy="false"` (not absent); they become `true` when disabled or loading.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `label` / `children`: the visible text and the accessible name (when no `aria-label`).
`icon`: the sole content of an icon-only button; `leftIcon` / `rightIcon`: icon before / after the label.
`loading`: see `Button#3`, `Button#4`; `loadingText`: see `Button#5`.
`badge`: count badge text.

`variant` (`filled`, `light`, `outline`, `text`, `link`), `severity` (`primary`, `secondary`, `danger`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, `contrast`), `size` (`xxs`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, or a responsive value), `raised`, `rounded`, `plain`: look only.
`type="submit"` or `"reset"`: native form behaviour.
`asChild`: renders the single child element instead of a `<button>`; an invalid child renders nothing.
`aria-label` and any other native attribute: passed to the `<button>`.

builtInText.text: none: Button has no built-in text and no built-in `aria-label`.

keyboard.text: A native button: Tab focuses it, Enter or Space activates it (`onClick`). A disabled or loading button is skipped by Tab.

states.text: Enabled: clickable, focusable.
Disabled: `Button#2`.
Loading: `Button#3`; `isLoading()` is true through `aria-busy` or the spinner.
Focused: standard focus ring; `aria-pressed` is not set by Button (a toggle passes `aria-pressed` itself, read by `isPressed()`).
Hover and pressed: look only.

testApi: `Spectra.findButton(name)`: by the visible label text or `aria-label`; `Spectra.queryButton(name)`: `null` when missing.
`click(options?)`: waits for a submit button's field checks first; `{ force: true }` clicks a disabled one and proves it does nothing; `doubleClick(options?)`: two clicks in one gesture (web only).
`getText()`, `getLabelText()`, `getBadgeText()`, `getType()`, `getVariant()`, `getSeverity()`, `getSize()` (`shouldHaveSize(size)`).

`getLabel()`, `getIcon()`, `getLeftIcon()`, `getRightIcon()`, `getLoadingIcon()`, `getBadge()` and `hasLabel()`, `hasIcon()`, `hasLeftIcon()`, `hasRightIcon()`, `hasLoadingIcon()`, `hasBadge()` (`shouldHave*` / `shouldNotHave*`).

`isDisabled()` (true when disabled or loading), `isLoading()`, `isPressed()` (`shouldBePressed()`, `shouldNotBePressed()`), `isFocused()`, `focus()`, `blur()`; `shouldBeDisabled()`, `shouldBeLoading()` and their `shouldNot*`.

components.name: ButtonGroup

does.text: Joins its buttons into one control: they sit side by side (or stacked with `orientation` `vertical`), touching, with the shared borders overlapping by 1 px and square corners where two buttons meet; only the outer ends of the group keep rounded corners.
The root is a `div` with `role="group"`; its accessible name is its `aria-label`, so the group is found by it (TC-0110).
Each button keeps its own behaviour: a click calls that button's `onClick` (Button#1), and a disabled or loading button stays disabled (Button#2, Button#3) while its neighbours stay active (TC-0113).
Keyboard focus on a button draws a primary-colour outline raised above its neighbours; on a primary or danger button the outline is the neutral outline colour.
A vertical group makes every direct child as wide as the group.
An empty group renders an empty `role="group"` element with no buttons (TC-0111).
Any content is accepted as children; icon-only buttons keep their own accessible names (TC-0112).

doesNot.text: Does not choose or mark an active button: there is no selected state and no `aria-pressed`; a mutually exclusive choice is a SegmentedControl.
Does not pass `variant`, `severity`, `size`, `disabled` or `loading` to its buttons: each button sets its own, and there is no group-level disable.
Does not move focus with arrow keys: every button is a normal tab stop, Tab moves between them.
Does not join buttons that are not direct children: a button wrapped in a `div` or fragment keeps its own corners and spacing.
Does not show a label, title or tooltip of its own.

defaults.text: `orientation` `horizontal`; the group is inline-sized (as wide as its buttons), not full width.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `orientation="vertical"`: the buttons stack in a column, joined at their top and bottom edges.
`aria-label`: the group's accessible name; without it the group has no name and a finder by name cannot locate it (TC-0110).
`className`, `style`, `pt.root`: styling only.

keyboard.text: Tab focuses each button in order, Enter or Space activates the focused button (Button#1).

states.text: Each button has its own state (default, disabled, loading, focused); the group itself has no state.

testApi: `Spectra.findButtonGroup(name)` by the group's `aria-label`; `Spectra.queryButtonGroup(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getButtons()`: Button wrappers of the buttons inside; `getButtonCount()`; `getButtonLabels()`; `getButton(indexOrLabel)` by 0-based index, label or RegExp (throws when none); `hasButton(label)`.
`clickButton(indexOrLabel)`: clicks that button.
`getContainer()`, `isDisplayed()`.

components.name: Calendar

does.text: Shows an always-visible month panel: a header with the month name and year, a weekday row, and a grid of 6 weeks (42 days) starting on Sunday, including greyed days of the previous and next month.
Today's day is marked (`data-today`, `aria-current="date"`).
Clicking a day in single mode reports that day (00:00, or at the time picker's time when `showTime`) through `onChange` and `onDateSelect`.
The calendar keeps no selection of its own: the selected mark (`data-selected`, `aria-pressed` true) shows only for the `value` the caller passes.
In multiple mode clicking a day adds it, clicking a selected day removes it, and the reported list is sorted by date.
In range mode the first click sets the start, the second click sets the end, and a click after a complete range starts a new range.
In range mode the days between start and end are marked in range (`data-in-range`) and start and end are marked selected.
In range mode, with a start picked and no end yet, days before the start are disabled; clicking the start day again gives a one-day range.
The previous and next buttons move one month; the month and year in the header update and `onMonthChange` reports `{ month, year }` (month 0-based).
Clicking the month title opens a 12-month view (short names `Jan` ... `Dec`); picking a month returns to the day grid in that month and calls `onMonthChange`.
Clicking the year title opens a 10-year view of the decade (header shows the range such as `2020 - 2029`); picking a year opens the month view of that year and calls `onYearChange`.
In the month view the previous and next buttons move one year; in the year view they move ten years; both call `onYearChange`.
Days outside `minDate`/`maxDate` (compared by day) and days for which `disabledDate` returns true are disabled and cannot be clicked.
Months and years beyond `minDate`, `maxDate`, `maxMonth` or `maxYear` are disabled in the month and year views.
When `value` changes from outside (for example the caller sets a date in another month), the panel jumps to that month; with several dates or a range it follows the last date or the range end.
Without a value the panel opens on the month of `defaultViewDate`, otherwise on the current month.
The days and the month/year grids render in the `timeZone` when given (today mark and selection use that zone).
With `showTime` a time picker under the day grid shows hour and minute with up and down buttons; each press changes by `stepHour` / `stepMinute` and wraps around (23 to 0, 59 to 0).
Changing the time re-reports the current value at the new time (the last date in multiple mode, the end or else the start in range mode); with no value only the displayed time changes.
With `hourFormat` 12 the hour shows 01-12 and an AM/PM control appears; toggling it moves the hour by 12 hours and reports the value.
With `view` `month` or `year` the calendar starts in that view and a click on a month or year selects it (month: the 1st of that month; year: 1 January) instead of drilling down.
`renderDay` content replaces the day number inside each day button; the button keeps selected, today, disabled behavior.

doesNot.text: Has no input field and no popup; it is the panel only.
Does not select any date by itself without `value`: it is controlled by `value`/`onChange` only.
Does not change the week start: the first weekday column is always Sunday.
Does not show week numbers.
Does not disable the previous/next buttons at `minDate`/`maxDate`; navigation continues, the days are disabled.
`maxMonth` and `maxYear` do not disable day cells; only the month and year views.
Clicking a greyed day of the neighbour month selects it but the panel changes month only when `value` changes (controlled).
Does not respond to disabled or read-only clicks: no `onChange`, no navigation, no view switch.
Has no arrow-key movement between days; days are reached by Tab.
The time picker is not shown in the month or year view, and has no seconds.
Does not change the time of the value when a day is clicked without `showTime` (the day is reported at 00:00).
Has no "today" or "clear" button.

defaults.text: `mode` `single`, `view` `date`, `size` `xs`.
`showYear` on (year title is a button), `showTime` off.
`hourFormat` `24`, `stepHour` 1, `stepMinute` 1, `timeSeparator` `:`.
Not disabled, not read-only; `timeZone` is the device zone.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `mode: 'multiple'` (value is a list) or `mode: 'range'` (value is `[start, end]`).
`view`: starting view (`date`, `month`, `year`) and what a month/year click does (`Calendar#21`).
`minDate`, `maxDate`, `disabledDate`: disable days (`Calendar#13`).
`maxMonth` (0-11 or `'current'`), `maxYear` (number or `'current'`): disable later months/years in the pickers.
`showYear: false`: no year button in the day view, and in the month view the header (with navigation) is hidden.
`showTime`, `hourFormat`, `stepHour`, `stepMinute`, `timeSeparator`: the time picker (`Calendar#18`-`Calendar#20`); the separator text replaces `:`. [unverified] [unverified]
`timeZone`, `defaultViewDate`, `renderDay`: see `Calendar#17`, `Calendar#16`, `Calendar#22`. [unverified]
`disabled`: all buttons disabled. `readOnly`: root `aria-readonly` true and all buttons disabled.
`size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, or responsive): styling only.
`aria-label`, `id`, `className`, `style`, `pt`: accessible name, id, styling.

builtInText.text: Previous / next button aria-labels: `Previous month` and `Next month` (locale en; passed through `t()`); the same labels are used in the month and year views.
Month names in the header: full locale names (`August`); in the month view short names (`Jan`); weekday headers short (`Sun`, `Mon`, ... `Sat`).
Day buttons have aria-label equal to the day number; year buttons the year; month buttons the short month name.
Time picker aria-labels: `Next Hour`, `Previous Hour`, `Next Minute`, `Previous Minute`; AM/PM options `AM` and `PM` (locale en; these are not passed through `t()`).

keyboard.text: Tab moves through the enabled buttons (navigation, titles, days); Enter or Space on a focused button activates it like a click.
No other key handling: arrows, Home, End, PageUp and PageDown do nothing.

states.text: Selected day: `data-selected`, `aria-pressed` true; range days between: `data-in-range`; today: `data-today`.
Disabled day: `data-disabled`, `aria-disabled` true, button disabled.
Greyed neighbour-month day: `data-other-month` on its cell.
Disabled or read-only calendar: buttons disabled, root `aria-readonly` only when read-only.
Current view: date (day grid), month (12 months), year (10 years).

testApi: `Spectra.findCalendar(label)`: by the root `aria-label`; `Spectra.queryCalendar(label)`: `null` when missing.
`getCurrentView()` (`date`|`month`|`year`), `getDisplayedMonth()`, `getDisplayedYear()`.
`getPreviousButton()`, `getNextButton()`, `getMonthTitleButton()`, `getYearTitleButton()`; `navPrevious()`, `navNext()`, `openMonthView()`, `openYearView()`.
`getDayCell(day)`, `getMonthCell(month)`, `getYearCell(year)`; `selectDate(day)`, `selectMonth(month)`, `selectYear(year)` (day cells of the displayed month only).
Readers with should*: `isDateSelected(day)`, `isDateInRange(day)`, `isDateDisabled(day)`, `isDateToday(day)`, `isMonthSelected(m)`, `isMonthDisabled(m)`, `isYearSelected(y)`, `isYearDisabled(y)`.
Time: `hasTimePicker()`, `getTimePicker()`, `getDisplayedTime()`, `incrementHour()`, `decrementHour()`, `incrementMinute()`, `decrementMinute()`, `toggleAmPm()`, `setHour(h)`, `setMinute(m)`.
`isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `focus()`, `blur()`, `element`, `getContainer()`.

components.name: Card

does.text: Shows a plain container (a `div`, no role) that groups content: an optional `header` at the very top, then a body holding the title block, the `children` and an optional `footer`.
The `header` is outside the padded body, above the title, separated from it by a bottom border line.
`title` and `subTitle` show in the body above the content; `titleEnd` shows at the far end of the title line (top right), the title and subtitle staying on the left.
A `subTitle` alone, or a `titleEnd` alone, still shows the title block (nothing is dropped for lack of a `title`).
The `footer` shows at the bottom of the body, separated from the content by a top border line.
Reports its look on the root as `data-variant` (`elevated`, `outlined`, `filled`, `flat`) and, only when `clickable`, `data-clickable` `true`.

`variant`: `elevated` shows a raised surface with a shadow, `outlined` a surface with a 1 px outline and no shadow, `filled` a tinted solid surface, `flat` a transparent card; the corners are rounded and the content is clipped to them.
`elevation` (1, 2, 3) deepens the shadow of an `elevated` card, and in dark mode lifts the surface one tonal step per level; the other variants ignore it.

`clickable` shows a pointer cursor and a hover effect (an `elevated` card rises one shadow level on hover, `outlined` and `filled` get a level 1 shadow); the `onClick` passed to the card runs on a click anywhere on it.
`subTitlePosition="end"` puts the subtitle on the title's line at the far end (a `Title | Last updated` header) instead of under it.
`padding` sets the body padding: `sm` 16 px, `md` 32 px, `lg` 36 px, `none` 0 (and the card then has no rounded corners).
`title`, `subTitle`, `header`, `footer`, `children` accept any node (text, buttons, images); `title` is the heading text of the card and is not set as a tooltip attribute.

doesNot.text: Does not make itself interactive: `clickable` adds only the hover style and pointer cursor, no `role`, no `tabindex`, no Enter or Space handling; a real link or button inside, or the caller's own role, `tabIndex` and key handler, make it operable.
No built-in loading, disabled, selected or pressed state; a loading Shimmer inside, `aria-disabled` or `aria-pressed` set by the caller are the caller's, and the card applies no style for them.
No hover or pressed background colour change (only the shadow change of `Card#9`).
The `header`, `footer` and title block are not rendered when not given (no empty element); the content wrapper is always rendered, also with no `children`.
Does not collapse, scroll or resize its content; no built-in close, expand or menu button.

defaults.text: `variant` `elevated`; `elevation` 1; `padding` `md`; `clickable` false; `subTitlePosition` `bottom`.
No header, no title block, no footer, no `data-clickable`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `variant`, `elevation`, `padding`, `subTitlePosition`: see `Card#7`, `Card#8`, `Card#11`, `Card#10`.
`header`, `title`, `subTitle`, `titleEnd`, `footer`: show the part (see `Card#2` to `Card#5`).
`clickable`: see `Card#9`, `Card#13`.

Any div attribute (`onClick`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `role`, `tabIndex`, `id`) passes to the root and may override `data-clickable` and `data-variant`; `className`, `style`: root styling; `pt`: styling only.

builtInText.text: none: no built-in text or `aria-label`; the card is named by what the caller gives (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or its visible title text).

keyboard.text: none by itself: Tab goes to the focusable parts inside (links, buttons in the header, content or footer); the card root takes none.

states.text: Default; clickable (`data-clickable`); each `variant`.
Disabled, loading, pressed, selected, focus: none of the card's own (see `Card#14`).

testApi: `Spectra.findCard(name)`: by the `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or visible text (title); `Spectra.queryCard(name)`: `null` when missing.

Parts: `getContainer()`, `getHeader()`, `getBody()`, `getTitleContainer()`, `getTitle()`, `getSubTitle()`, `getContent()`, `getFooter()` (each throws when not rendered); `hasHeader()`, `hasTitle()`, `hasSubTitle()`, `hasContent()`, `hasFooter()`.

Readers: `getTitleText()`, `getSubTitleText()`, `getVariant()`, `isClickable()` (clickable, button role or tab stop, and not disabled), `getTitleFontWeight()`, `isTitleBold()` (weight 600 or more), with polling `should*` forms.

Readers of caller-owned state: `isLoading()` (a loading Shimmer with `aria-busy` inside), `isDisabled()` (`aria-disabled`, `disabled` or `data-disabled` on the root), `isPressed()` (`aria-pressed="true"`).
`click({ force })`: clicks the root; `force: true` clicks a disabled one on purpose.

components.name: Checkbox

does.text: Clicking the box, the label text, or pressing Space on the focused box toggles it between checked and unchecked.
A checked box shows a filled primary-colour box with a white check mark drawn in; an unchecked box shows an empty outlined box with no mark.
`onChange` receives the new checked boolean (not a DOM event) on every toggle.
Uncontrolled (`defaultChecked`) keeps and flips its own state on each click.
Controlled (`checked`) shows only what the parent passes: a click calls `onChange` but the box stays as it was until the parent passes the new value.
With `label`, the label text is shown beside the box and is the accessible name; clicking it toggles the box.
With `description`, the secondary text is shown under the label and is linked to the box as its accessible description (`aria-describedby`).
Inside a `CheckboxGroup` the box is checked exactly when the group value contains this checkbox's `value`; a click adds or removes that `value` in the group.
Inside a `CheckboxGroup` the checkbox also gets the group's `name`, and is disabled or invalid when the group is.
`invalid` turns the box border, fill (when checked), label and description red and sets `aria-invalid="true"`.
A disabled box shows greyed colours, a not-allowed cursor, cannot be toggled by click, label click or Space, and does not call `onChange`.
Focusing the box with the keyboard shows a circular focus halo around it; clicking or tabbing away removes it.
The check mark animates in and out (about 0.15 s) when the state changes.

doesNot.text: No indeterminate or partial state (that is TriStateCheckbox); the check mark is never a dash.
Clicking the description text does not toggle the box (only the label and the box do).
Without `label` and `description` there is no visible text and no accessible name unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is given.
