No `required` prop: the box shows no required marker and is not natively required (only a passed `aria-required` is set on the input).
Enter does not toggle the box.
`size` changes the box size; the label and description text also step with it.
A disabled checkbox inside a non-disabled group stays disabled, and a non-disabled checkbox inside a disabled group is disabled too (the group wins; a child cannot opt out).
`checked` and `defaultChecked` on a checkbox inside a group are ignored; the group value decides.

defaults.text: Unchecked, enabled, valid, no label, no description.
`size` `xs` (16 px box); the other steps are `sm` 20 px, `md` 24 px, `lg` 28 px.
`aria-invalid` is rendered as `"false"` when not invalid.
A generated id is used when `id` is not given; the label's `for` and the description id follow it.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `label`: visible label text beside the box, and the accessible name.
`description`: secondary text under the label.
`checked` + `onChange`: controlled; `defaultChecked`: uncontrolled initial state.
`value`: the value the input submits in a form and the entry it adds to a `CheckboxGroup` array.
`name`: the form field name on the input (inside a group the group `name` wins when set).
`disabled`, `invalid`: the states in Does; `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, also per breakpoint.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`: replace the generated accessible name or description link.
`className`, `style`: applied to the outer wrapper when a label or description exists, else to the box itself.
`onClick`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `tabIndex`: passed to the input.

keyboard.text: Tab focuses the box, Shift+Tab leaves it; Space toggles it.
A disabled box is skipped by Tab.

states.text: Unchecked: empty outlined box, no check mark.
Checked: filled box with check mark.
Focused: halo around the box, shown for keyboard focus.
Hover and pressed: a faint circular halo appears around the box (primary colour, red when invalid), not when disabled.
Disabled: greyed box and text, checked or unchecked, not toggleable.
Invalid: red box border, red label and description; checked invalid fills the box red.

testApi: `Spectra.findCheckbox(name)`: by accessible name (label text or `aria-label`); `Spectra.queryCheckbox(name)`: `null` when missing.
`isChecked()` (`shouldBeChecked()`, `shouldNotBeChecked()`); `check()`, `uncheck()`, `toggle()`, `setChecked(bool)`.
`isDisabled()`, `isInvalid()` (`aria-invalid="true"`), `isRequired()` (native `required`; false because no such prop), `isFocused()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.
`getInput()`, `getBox()`, `getIcon()`, `getLabel()`, `getDescription()`, `getContainer()`.
`hasLabel()`, `hasDescription()`, `hasIcon()` (the icon is in the DOM whether or not checked); `getLabelText()`, `getDescriptionText()`.

components.name: CheckboxGroup

does.text: Renders its children stacked vertically in one wrapper with `role="group"`.
Each child `Checkbox` is checked exactly when its `value` is in the group array; clicking it adds the `value` to the array, clicking it again removes it.
`onChange` receives the whole next array of values (not an event); new values are appended at the end in click order.
Uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) keeps its own array; controlled (`value`) shows only what the parent passes and snaps back until the parent updates it.
Child checkboxes still call their own `onChange` with the new checked boolean.
`disabled` disables every child checkbox (greyed, not clickable); `invalid` makes every child invalid (red) and the group `aria-invalid="true"`.
`name` is put on every child input, so the set submits under one field name.
A child nested inside other elements (layout wrapper, tooltip) still belongs to the group.

doesNot.text: No visible legend or label: the group needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
No select-all or tri-state parent.
No min or max selection limit; any number including none may be selected.
A child cannot opt out of the group's `disabled` or `invalid`: the group state wins even if the child sets its own to false.
A child without `value` cannot be represented in the array (all such children share one undefined entry).
The group root itself has no `disabled` attribute; the disabled state shows only on the children.
No error or helper text (that is Field).

defaults.text: Empty selection, enabled, not invalid.
`aria-invalid` renders as `"false"` when not invalid.
Children stack in a column with a 10 px gap.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `value` + `onChange`: controlled; `defaultValue`: uncontrolled initial selection.
`disabled`, `invalid`: cascade to all children as above.
`name`: shared `name` on every child input.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `id`: set on the group wrapper.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling of the wrapper only.

keyboard.text: No group-level keys: Tab moves through the child checkboxes one by one, Space toggles the focused one.

states.text: Nothing selected / some selected / all selected: each child shows its own checked state.
Disabled: all children disabled.
Invalid: all children red, group `aria-invalid="true"`.

testApi: `Spectra.findCheckboxGroup(name)`: by `aria-label` or the Field label; `Spectra.queryCheckboxGroup(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getCheckbox(label)` / `queryCheckbox(label)` (inside the group), `getAllCheckboxes()`.
`getSelectedValues()` (checked inputs' `value` attributes), `getSelectedLabels()` (label texts of checked children).
`select(labels)`, `deselect(labels)` (string or array), `selectAll()`, `deselectAll()`.
`isDisabled()` (true when every child is disabled), `isInvalid()` (`aria-invalid="true"` or any child invalid), `getName()` (the first child's `name`), `getContainer()`.

components.name: CircularProgress

does.text: Single mode (`value`) draws a ring whose coloured arc covers `value` of `max` (`max` 100 by default), starting at the top and running clockwise over a grey track.
The arc covers the whole-number percentage, rounded and clamped to 0 to 100: a `value` above `max` shows a full ring, a negative `value` an empty one; `max` of 0 or less shows an empty ring.

The root is `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` the value on the `aria-valuemin` to `aria-valuemax` scale (`value`, kept inside 0 and `max`), `aria-valuemin` 0 and `aria-valuemax` the resolved `max`: `value` 75 with `max` 100 reads 75 and 100; `value` 25 with `max` 50 reads 25 and 50 and shows 50% (TC-0151).
Multi mode (`values`) draws each segment as a coloured arc, in order, end to end on one ring (layout `sequential`); segments with a value of 0 or less are left out of the ring and of the legend.
Multi mode `max` defaults to the larger of 100 and the sum of the segments, so segments summing below 100 leave the rest of the ring empty.
Sequential segments whose sum exceeds `max` are scaled down together to fit the ring (proportions stay, the absolute arc sizes no longer match the values).
Multi mode `aria-valuenow` is the sum of the segment values kept inside 0 and `max`; `aria-valuemax` is the resolved `max`.

Multi mode without `aria-valuetext` gets a spoken summary `<total>% total: <label>: <value>, <label>: <value>` (a segment without a text `label` reads `Segment`); `aria-valuetext` replaces it (TC-5017).

Layout `concentric` draws one ring per segment, nested, the first outermost, each with its own grey track and its arc covering its own value of `max`; a segment is not scaled when the sum exceeds `max` (TC-0154).
`gap` leaves that many pixels between segments on a sequential ring (only with two or more segments), or between nested rings in concentric layout.

Indeterminate mode (`indeterminate`) shows a spinning ring of a 70% arc with no track and no percentage; the root is `role="progressbar"` with `aria-busy="true"` and no `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` (TC-0155).
`showValueLabel` shows the percentage in the centre (`60%`; multi mode the total percentage) (TC-0152).
`labelContent` shows that node in the centre; it wins over `showValueLabel` and works in every mode (TC-0157).
`formatValue` replaces the centre text of `showValueLabel`: `(value, max)` in single mode, `(sum, max, values)` in multi mode, which receives every item including the zero ones (TC-0157).
Clicks on the empty part of the centre go through to what is under the ring; interactive content in `labelContent` stays clickable.
`showLegend` in multi mode shows a legend with one item per drawn segment: a colour dot, the `label` (omitted when there is none) and the raw `value` (`Apps` `40`) (TC-0153, TC-5017).

The legend sits at `legendPosition` of the ring: `bottom` below, `top` above, `right` beside it in a row, `left` to the left; `top` and `bottom` list items horizontally, `left` and `right` vertically, unless `legendOrientation` says otherwise (TC-0158).
The coloured arc moves with a 300 ms transition when the value changes.

doesNot.text: Does not show any percentage text unless `showValueLabel`, `labelContent` or `formatValue` with `showValueLabel` is set; by default there is no centre container (TC-0151).
Does not show a legend without `showLegend`, in single or indeterminate mode, or when no segment has a value above 0 (the ring is drawn without a legend wrapper).
Does not draw a value arc in indeterminate mode, nor an indeterminate arc in single mode (TC-0155).
Does not take input: not focusable, no click, no keyboard, no tooltip.
Does not set `aria-valuetext` in single mode unless the prop is passed.
Does not give the ring an accessible name by itself; without `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` it has none (so a finder cannot locate it) (TC-0156).
Does not colour multi-mode segments by the component `severity`; only a segment's own `severity` or `color`, else the position colour.

defaults.text: `size` `md` (48 px): `xs` 24, `sm` 32, `md` 48, `lg` 64, `xl` 96; a number is the diameter in px.
Stroke thickness by size: `xs` 2.5, `sm` 3.5, `md` 4.5, `lg` 6, `xl` 8 px; a numeric size gets 8% of it (at least 2 px); `thickness` overrides.
`strokeLinecap` `round`; `layout` `sequential`; `gap` 0; `showValueLabel` false; `showLegend` false; `legendPosition` `bottom`; `indeterminate` false.
Single and indeterminate arc colour `primary` (chart colour), track grey; multi segments take colours by position: primary, warning, success, danger, info, secondary, then repeating.
Centre text size follows the ring size (7, 9, 11, 14, 18 px for `xs` to `xl`).

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `severity` (`primary`, `secondary`, `danger`, `success`, `warning`, `info`): colours the arc of single and indeterminate mode.
`color` (single and indeterminate): a CSS colour (`#`, `rgb`, `hsl`, `var(`) paints the arc directly, anything else is added as a class.
A segment's `color`, `severity`, `key`, `pt`: its own arc and legend dot colour; the legend dot follows the same colour.
`trackColor`: colour of the grey track (CSS colour or class).
`strokeLinecap="flat"`: square arc ends instead of round.
`thickness`: stroke width in px.
`max`, `values`, `layout`, `gap`, `showLegend`, `legendPosition`, `legendOrientation`, `labelContent`, `showValueLabel`, `formatValue`, `aria-valuetext`: as in the lines above.
`className`: on the root, or on the legend wrapper when a legend is shown.

builtInText.text: `Segment`: the name used in the generated `aria-valuetext` for a segment without a text `label` (locale en, not translated).
No other built-in text; the percentage text is `<n>%`.

states.text: Single: `aria-valuenow` set, arc shown.
Multi: arcs per segment, optional legend.
Indeterminate: `aria-busy` true, spinning arc, no `aria-valuenow`.

testApi: `Spectra.findCircularProgress(name)` by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; `Spectra.queryCircularProgress(name)`: `null` when missing.

`getValue()` / `shouldHaveValue(n)`: reads `aria-valuenow`, the value on the `aria-valuemin` to `aria-valuemax` scale (CircularProgress#3); `null` when indeterminate. `getMax()`, `getMin()`, `getValueText()`.
`getPercentage()`: `(aria-valuenow - aria-valuemin) / (aria-valuemax - aria-valuemin)` rounded, kept in 0 to 100; right whatever `max` is.
`isIndeterminate()`; `hasCenterLabel()`, `getCenterLabelElement()`, `getCenterLabelText()`; `hasLegend()`, `getLegendElement()`, `getLegendItems()` (`{ label, value, element }`).
`getGraphicElement()`, `getTrackElement()`, `getValueTrackElement()` / `hasValueTrack()`, `getSegmentElements()`, `getIndeterminateTrackElement()` / `hasIndeterminateTrack()`.

components.name: ColorPairPicker

does.text: Shows a small button with the letter `A` in the saved foreground colour on the saved background colour; clicking it opens a floating panel below it.

The panel has the title `Color Picker`, a close button (`aria-label` `Close`), a `Foreground` / `Background` switch, a preview row (`Color`, circle and hex like `#000000`), a colour canvas, `H` and `A` sliders, the inputs `HEX`, `R`, `G`, `B`, a contrast panel, `Swap Colors` and `Save` buttons.
The `Foreground` tab is selected when the picker starts; switching tabs makes the preview, canvas, sliders and inputs edit the other colour of the pair.
Edits in the canvas, sliders, `HEX` and `R`/`G`/`B` change the draft colour of the selected tab only; the trigger button and `onChange` do not change until `Save`.

The contrast panel shows `Contrast ratio` and the draft pair's ratio with one decimal, like `21.0:1`, and two badges: `AA` (ratio 4.5 or more) and `AAA` (7 or more), each with a check icon when passed and a cross icon when failed.
`Save` commits the draft pair (`onChange` with `{ background, foreground }`) and closes the panel.
`Swap Colors` exchanges the draft foreground and background at once (contrast ratio stays the same, the edited colour shown follows the tab); it is saved by `Save`.
The close button, Escape and a click outside close the panel without saving; the draft goes back to the saved pair.

The `HEX` input accepts 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex digits with or without `#`; valid entries update the draft at once, invalid entries leave it unchanged and the field shows the current colour again when it loses focus.
`R`, `G`, `B` clamp to 0..255 and treat empty or non-numeric text as 0.

Presets are a list of swatch buttons showing `Aa` in the pair's colours under the heading `Color pairs`, named by their `label`; the swatch whose background and foreground both equal the draft pair (exact text match, case-sensitive) has `data-active="true"`.
Clicking a preset puts the whole pair in the draft (both colours and contrast update); it is saved only by `Save`, unless `closeOnSelect`.
When presets exist, a non-clickable `Aa` swatch after them shows the current draft pair.

The trigger has `aria-label` `Choose color pair` (or the given `aria-label`), `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; the panel is a `role="dialog"` named by `panelAriaLabel`; the presets sit in a toolbar named `Color pair presets`.
With no value the pair is white background `#FFFFFF` and black foreground `#000000` (`21.0:1`).

doesNot.text: Does not change the value or call `onChange` while only the draft is edited, nor when closed by the close button, Escape or an outside click.
Does not let `Save` commit a pair that fails AA: the button is disabled while the ratio is under 4.5:1; between 4.5 and 7 it stays enabled (AAA is only informational).
`closeOnSelect` does not check contrast: a preset is saved and the panel closes even if the pair fails AA.
Does not open when `readOnly` or `disabled`.
Does not keep an unsaved draft after closing: it returns to the saved pair; the selected tab is not reset.
Does not translate `Close`, `Hue`, `Alpha`, `HEX`, `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `H`, `A`, `R`, `G`, `B`, `AA`, `AAA`, `Aa` and the letter `A` on the trigger.
Does not normalise a hex typed in `HEX`: the pair keeps it as typed (for example `#fff`), while canvas and sliders write lowercase 6-digit hex.
Arrow keys in the swatch grid do not wrap vertically; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight wrap around the ends.

defaults.text: Closed at start; `closeOnSelect`, `presetsOnly`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `readOnly` all false; no presets; tab `Foreground` selected.
Tab labels `Foreground` and `Background` (English, in this order).

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `presets` (list of `{ label, value: { background, foreground } }`): shows the `Color pairs` section; none given, no section.

`presetsOnly`: hides the `Foreground`/`Background` switch, the preview row, canvas, sliders, inputs, contrast panel, `Swap Colors` and the custom `Aa` swatch; header, presets and `Save` stay (`Save` still needs the pair to pass AA).
`closeOnSelect`: clicking a preset saves that pair as the value and closes the panel.
`foregroundTabLabel`, `backgroundTabLabel`: replace the text of the two tabs.
`open` + `onOpenChange`: the app controls the panel; `defaultOpen` starts it open.
`readOnly`: shows the pair, can be focused, never opens, no `aria-haspopup`.
`disabled`: the trigger is disabled and out of the tab order.
`invalid` or `aria-invalid`: the trigger gets `data-invalid="true"`.
`panelAriaLabel`: the dialog's accessible name.

builtInText.text: English locale defaults: trigger `Choose color pair`, title `Color Picker`, `Color`, `Contrast ratio`, `Color pairs`, `Color pair presets`, `Swap Colors`, `Save`.
Fixed text: tabs `Foreground`, `Background`; `Close`; `Hue`, `Alpha`, `HEX`, `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`; badges `AA`, `AAA`; swatch text `Aa`; the trigger letter `A`.

keyboard.text: Enter or Space on the trigger opens the panel; Escape closes it.

Inside the swatch grid: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move to the next and previous swatch (wrapping), ArrowDown and ArrowUp move one row of 8, Home and End jump to the first and last swatch; one swatch is in the tab order (active, else first).

states.text: Closed: no panel; trigger `aria-expanded="false"`. Open: dialog in a portal, `aria-expanded="true"`.
Save disabled: draft pair under 4.5:1 (`ColorPairPicker#6`).
Contrast pass/fail: AA and AAA badges show pass or fail separately (`ColorPairPicker#5`).
Disabled, read-only, invalid: see `ColorPairPicker#32`, `ColorPairPicker#31`, `ColorPairPicker#33`. Loading, selected: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findColorPairPicker(label)` / `Spectra.queryColorPairPicker(label)`: finds the trigger by accessible name; `query` gives `null` when missing.

Panel: `open()` (sub-part getters open the panel first), `close({ method: 'clickOutside' | 'escape' | 'closeButton' })`, `isOpen()` (`shouldBeOpen()`, `shouldNotBeOpen()`), `getTrigger()`, `getPanel()`, `getContainer()`.
Header: `getHeader()`, `getTitle()`, `getTitleText()`, `getCloseButton()`, `hasCloseButton()`.
Tabs: `getViewSwitcher()`, `hasViewSwitcher()`, `getActiveTab()` (`'foreground'` or `'background'`), `switchTab(tab)`.

Preview, canvas, sliders, inputs: `getPreviewSection()`, `getPreviewCircle()`, `getPreviewHex()`, `hasPreview()`, `getCanvas()`, `getCanvasPointer()`, `hasCanvas()`, `getSliders()`, `getHueSlider()`, `getAlphaSlider()`, `hasSliders()`, `getInputsContainer()`, `getHexInput()`, `getRedInput()`, `getGreenInput()`, `getBlueInput()`, `setHexInput(hex)` (edits the selected tab), `setRgbaInput({ r, g, b })`, `hasInputs()`.
Contrast: `getContrastPanel()`, `hasContrastPanel()`, `getContrastScore()` (text like `21.0:1`), `getContrastRatio()` (number), `passesContrast('AA' | 'AAA')`.

Presets: `getPairsSection()`, `getSwatchGrid()`, `hasSwatchGrid()`, `getSwatches()`, `getSwatch(labelOrPair)`, `choosePreset(labelOrPair)`, `isPresetActive(labelOrPair)` (`shouldBePresetActive(...)`), `getCustomSwatchItem()`.
Footer: `getFooter()`, `hasFooter()`, `getSwapButton()`, `hasSwapButton()`, `swap()`, `getSaveButton()`, `hasSaveButton()`, `save()`.

Value: `getValue()` reads `{ background, foreground }` from the trigger's inline style (browser format, may be `rgb(...)`) [unverified]; `setValue({ foreground, background })` opens, types each hex on its tab, saves (fails to save when the pair is under 4.5:1).
State: `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`; `focus()`, `blur()` on the trigger.

components.name: ColorPicker

does.text: Shows a small square button filled with the saved colour; clicking it opens a floating panel below it (aligned to its left edge).

The panel has the title `Color Picker` and a close button (`aria-label` `Close`), a preview row (`Color`, a circle in the draft colour and its hex like `#3B82F6`), a colour canvas, `H` (hue) and `A` (alpha) sliders, the inputs `HEX`, `R`, `G`, `B`, and a `Save` button.
Everything the user does in the panel (canvas, sliders, inputs, preset click) changes a draft colour only: the preview updates, the trigger button and `onChange` do not.
`Save` commits the draft as the value (`onChange` fires with a hex like `#10b981`, lowercase, 6 digits, or 8 digits when the alpha slider is below full) and closes the panel.
The close button, Escape and a click outside close the panel without saving; the draft goes back to the saved value, so reopening shows the saved colour again (when a colour was saved).
Typing in the `HEX` input accepts 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex digits with or without `#`; a valid entry updates the preview and the `R`, `G`, `B` fields at once.
A `HEX` entry that is not valid leaves the colour unchanged; when the input loses focus it shows the current colour again (uppercase, no `#`).
The `HEX` input shows the draft colour uppercase without `#`, max 8 characters.
`R`, `G`, `B` take numbers; an empty or non-numeric entry becomes 0 and a number above 255 or below 0 is clamped to 255 or 0; the preview and `HEX` follow.
Each preset is a round swatch button named by its `label`; the swatch whose hex equals the draft colour (case-insensitive) is marked active (`data-active="true"`).
Clicking a preset puts its colour into the draft (preview, inputs and active mark update); it is saved only by `Save`, unless `closeOnSelect`.
The presets sit in a toolbar named `Color presets`; only one swatch is in the tab order (the active one, else the first).

The trigger is a button with `aria-label` `Choose color` (or the given `aria-label`), `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded` true while the panel is open; the panel is a `role="dialog"` named by `panelAriaLabel`.
Changing the value from outside (controlled `value`) repaints the trigger and, next time the panel opens, the draft.

doesNot.text: Does not change the value, trigger colour or call `onChange` while the user only edits the draft.
Does not save when closed by the close button, Escape or an outside click.
Does not accept colour names or `rgb()` text; only hex digits in `HEX`.
Does not open when `readOnly` or `disabled`.
Does not translate `Close`, `Hue`, `Alpha`, `HEX`, `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`, `H`, `A`, `R`, `G`, `B`; these are fixed English.
Does not show a text value on the trigger; the button is only a colour swatch.
Does not check contrast or restrict colours (that is ColorPairPicker).
Arrow keys in the swatch grid do not wrap vertically: ArrowDown on the last row and ArrowUp on the first row stay on the swatch; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight wrap around the ends.

defaults.text: Closed at start (`defaultOpen` not set); `closeOnSelect` false; `presetsOnly` false; `disabled`, `invalid`, `readOnly` false; no presets.
No value: the trigger is transparent and the draft opens as white (`#FFFFFF`).

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `presets` (list of `{ label, value }`): shows the `Color presets` swatch grid below the inputs; none given, no grid.
`presetsOnly`: hides the canvas, sliders and the `HEX`/`R`/`G`/`B` inputs; the header, preview row, presets and `Save` stay.
`closeOnSelect`: clicking a preset saves it as the value (`onChange` fires) and closes the panel at once.
`open` + `onOpenChange`: the app controls whether the panel is open; `defaultOpen` starts it open (uncontrolled).
`readOnly`: the trigger shows the colour and can be focused, but a click or key never opens the panel and `aria-haspopup` is removed.
`disabled`: the trigger is disabled and out of the tab order.
`invalid` or `aria-invalid`: the trigger gets `data-invalid="true"` (invalid styling).
`panelAriaLabel`: sets the dialog's `aria-label`; without it the dialog has no accessible name.

builtInText.text: English defaults (locale keys): trigger `Choose color`, panel title `Color Picker`, preview label `Color`, swatch toolbar `Color presets`, `Save`.
Fixed English, not translated: close button `Close`; slider rows `Hue`, `Alpha` with letters `H`, `A`; inputs `HEX`, `Red`, `Green`, `Blue` with letters `HEX`, `R`, `G`, `B`.

keyboard.text: Enter or Space on the trigger opens the panel (native button); Escape closes it.
Inside the swatch grid: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move to the next and previous swatch (wrapping), ArrowDown and ArrowUp move one row of 8, Home and End jump to the first and last swatch.
Tab goes through the panel controls; focus is on one swatch at a time (`ColorPicker#12`).

states.text: Closed: no panel in the page; trigger `aria-expanded="false"`.
Open: dialog in a portal; trigger `aria-expanded="true"`.
Focused: the trigger shows its focus style.
Disabled, read-only, invalid: see `ColorPicker#30`, `ColorPicker#29`, `ColorPicker#31`. Loading, selected: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findColorPicker(label)` / `Spectra.queryColorPicker(label)`: finds the trigger by its accessible name (`aria-label` or field label); `query` gives `null` when missing.

Panel: `open()` (clicks the trigger, and every sub-part getter opens the panel first if closed), `close({ method: 'clickOutside' | 'escape' | 'closeButton' })`, `isOpen()` (`shouldBeOpen()`, `shouldNotBeOpen()`), `getTrigger()`, `getPanel()`, `getContainer()`.

Header and preview: `getHeader()`, `getTitle()`, `getTitleText()`, `getCloseButton()`, `hasCloseButton()`, `getPreviewSection()`, `getPreviewCircle()`, `getPreviewHex()` (`shouldContainPreviewHex(hex)`), `hasPreview()`.
Canvas and sliders: `getCanvas()`, `getCanvasPointer()`, `hasCanvas()`, `getSliders()`, `getHueSlider()`, `getAlphaSlider()`, `hasSliders()`.
Inputs: `getInputsContainer()`, `getHexInput()`, `getRedInput()`, `getGreenInput()`, `getBlueInput()`, `setHexInput(hex)`, `setRgbaInput({ r, g, b })`, `hasInputs()`.
Presets: `getSwatchGrid()`, `hasSwatchGrid()`, `getSwatches()`, `getSwatch(labelOrHex)`, `choosePreset(labelOrHex)`, `isPresetActive(labelOrHex)` (`shouldBePresetActive(...)`).
Footer: `getFooter()`, `hasFooter()`, `getSaveButton()`, `hasSaveButton()`, `save()`.

Value: `getValue()` reads the saved colour from the trigger's inline `background-color` (the browser's own format, may be `rgb(...)` rather than hex) [unverified]; `setValue(hex)` opens, types the hex, saves.
State: `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()` (true when the trigger has no `aria-haspopup`), `isInvalid()`; `focus()`, `blur()` on the trigger.

components.name: ContextMenu

does.text: Right-clicking the target area (its single child, or anything inside it) opens a floating action list at the pointer: its top-left corner sits 8 px below and level with the click point, and the browser's own right-click menu does not appear.
Right-clicking again, elsewhere in the area, while it is open moves the list to the new pointer position.
The list is a Menu: items, icons, danger items, group headers, separators, hidden and disabled items, links and tooltips behave as in `Menu#2` to `Menu#12`.
The target area carries `data-contextmenu-state="open"` or `"closed"` (and `data-popover-state`, `aria-expanded`); the panel is not in the page while closed.
The panel renders inline in the page, right after the target area (no portal), so a clipping or scrolling ancestor can clip it.
Picking an enabled leaf item runs its `onClick` and closes the menu; picking an item that has sub-items does not (as in `PopupMenu#8`).
Sub-items open as flyout panels to the right of their parent item (as in `Menu#10`, `Menu#11` with `triggerFlyoutOn="hover"`); picking a sub-item closes the whole menu.
Escape closes the menu (`Popover#8`); a click outside the panel and the target area closes it (`Popover#7`).
A disabled item stays in the list and behaves as in `Menu#6`; clicking it does not close the menu.
The child's own `onContextMenu` handler still runs on each right-click that opens the menu.
`onOpenChange(open)` fires as in `Popover#11`.
With no (visible) items the panel shows the empty text (as in `Menu#16`).
`header`, `footer`, `ariaLabel`, `ariaLabelledby`, `tabIndex`, `emptyContent`, `flyoutDelay` and the other Menu props pass to the list.

doesNot.text: Does not open on left-click, hover or keyboard from the target area; only the right-click (context menu) event opens it, or `open` set by the caller.
Does not open when `disabled`: the browser's own right-click menu appears, the target carries `data-contextmenu-disabled`, and the child's own `onContextMenu` handler does not run either.
Does not move focus into the list on open: Arrow Down needs focus on the list first (Tab).
Does not close on item pick when `closeOnSelect` is false (as in `PopupMenu#16`).
Does not close on Escape when `closeOnEscape` is false.
A left-click inside the target area does not close the open menu (it is not an outside click).
Submenus are never inline (`expand`); `submenuMode` has no effect.
Does not need a trigger button and has no hover or click trigger mode.
Right-click on the open panel itself does not reposition it (the panel is not inside the target area).

defaults.text: Closed at start (`defaultOpen` false); `disabled` false; `closeOnEscape` true; `closeOnSelect` true; placement `bottom-start` with 8 px gap, flipping and shifting to stay in the viewport.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `disabled`: right-click does nothing (`ContextMenu#15`).
`open` and `onOpenChange`: controlled by the caller; `defaultOpen`: uncontrolled initial state. An open menu with no right-click yet anchors to the target area (bottom-left corner).
`closeOnEscape={false}`, `closeOnSelect={false}`: see `ContextMenu#18`, `ContextMenu#17`.
`triggerFlyoutOn="hover"` with `flyoutDelay`: hover-opened flyouts as in `Menu#11`.
`emptyContent`, `header`, `footer`: see Menu.

builtInText.text: `No options available` when `items` is empty or all hidden and no `emptyContent` is given (as in `Menu#37`); otherwise none.

keyboard.text: Escape closes it; with focus on the list, Arrow Down, Arrow Up, Home, End and Enter or Space work as in `Menu#13` and `Menu#39`.
An open panel sits right after the target area in the page, so Tab from the target reaches the list next.

states.text: Closed, open; target enabled or disabled; items as in `Menu#40`.
No loading or error state.

testApi: Finders: `Spectra.findContextMenu(label)` and `Spectra.queryContextMenu(label)` by the target area's accessible name.
Parts: `getTrigger` (the target area), `getContainer`, `getMenu`, `getList`, `getItems`, `getItem`, `getIcon`, `getSubmenu`, `getSubmenuIcon`, `getGroupHeaders`, `getGroupHeader`.

Readers (each with a polling `should*`): `isDisplayed`, `isOpen`, `isDisabled`, `getItemCount`, `getItemLabels`, `hasItem`, `getItemDestination`, `isItemDisabled`, `hasIcon`, `hasSubmenu`, `isSubmenuOpen`, `getGroupHeaderLabels`.
Actions: `open` (right-click), `close({ method })`, `clickItem`, `openSubmenu`, `closeSubmenu`.

components.name: CopyButton

does.text: Clicking copies the `text` prop to the clipboard (falls back to a hidden-textarea copy when the clipboard API is unavailable or refused).
After a successful copy it shows copied feedback: the icon changes from the copy icon to a check, the label becomes `Copied!`, the button turns secondary.
The feedback ends by itself after 2000 ms: label, icon and colour return to idle.
A second click during feedback restarts the 2000 ms countdown.
Icon-only button (no `label`): no label text before copying; `Copied!` appears as text after copying, then disappears again.
Labeled button: the label text is swapped for `Copied!` while copied, then the original label returns.
A failed copy (clipboard refused and fallback failed) shows no feedback and no error; the button stays idle (a failed click during feedback ends the running feedback at once).

doesNot.text: No tooltip on hover or focus.
No disabled or loading state (no such prop).
Does not copy anything but the `text` prop (not the label).
The `aria-label` does not change to `Copied!` for an icon-only button; it stays `Copy to clipboard` while the visible text changes.

defaults.text: Text variant button; copy icon `FileCopyLine`, copied icon `CheckLine`.
`resetDelay` 2000 ms; `copiedLabel` `Copied!`.
No visible label.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `label`: visible text next to the icon, and the accessible name becomes that text (no default `aria-label`).
`copiedLabel`: replaces `Copied!`; a string is passed through `t()`, a node renders as is.
`resetDelay: <ms>`: changes how long the copied feedback stays.
`icon` / `copiedIcon`: replace the copy / check icon.
`aria-label`: replaces the accessible name, labeled or icon-only.
`className`, `pt`: styling only.

builtInText.text: Default `aria-label` (icon-only, no `label`, no `aria-label`): `Copy to clipboard` (locale en; passed through `t()`).
Copied label: `Copied!` (locale en; passed through `t()` when it is a string).
A labeled button without `aria-label` has no `aria-label` attribute; its name is the label text.

keyboard.text: A native button: Tab focuses it, Enter or Space copies.

states.text: Idle: copy icon, original label (or none).
Copied: check icon, `Copied!` label, secondary colour, for `resetDelay`.
Focused: standard focus; blur on clicking elsewhere.
Disabled, loading: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findCopyButton(name)`: by the visible label or `aria-label` (icon-only: `Copy to clipboard`); `Spectra.queryCopyButton(name)`: `null` when missing.
`click()` / `copy()` (alias): triggers the copy; `{ force: true }` on `click()` clicks a disabled one.

`isCopied()` (`shouldBeCopied()`, `shouldNotBeCopied()`): true when the text matches `copied`/`shared` or the icon is the check; the copied state flips asynchronously after the clipboard write, so wait for the label before asserting.
`getText()`, `getLabelText()` (throws with no label), `getLabel()`, `hasLabel()`, `getIcon()`, `hasIcon()`.
`isDisabled()`, `isFocused()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.

components.name: CountUp

does.text: Shows a number that counts from `from` (0 by default) to `to` and stops on `to`, as soon as it is shown (TC-3024).
The counting is eased: fast first, slowing towards `to` (ease-out).
Every shown value is a whole number: each step is rounded, so a `to` with decimals ends on the rounded number (`to` 95.4 ends on `95`).
The animation lasts the smaller of `duration` and 15% of the distance in milliseconds (`|to - from| * 0.15`): `from` 0, `to` 1000 takes 150 ms even with `duration` 1200, and `to` 200 takes 30 ms.
Counts down when `to` is below `from` (`from` 60, `to` 0 ends on `0`) (TC-3029).
Negative numbers count as any others (`from` -50, `to` 50 ends on `50`) (TC-3034).
With `from` equal to `to`, shows that number at once with no animation (TC-3033).
Changing `to` while mounted counts again towards the new target and ends on it (100 to 200 ends on `200`) (TC-3030).
Changing `to` restarts the count from `from`, not from the number currently shown.
`format` turns every shown number into the text shown, during the count and at the end (`$48,320`, `95.0%`, `0s`) (TC-3027, TC-3028, TC-3029).
The root is a `span` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"`, so a screen reader announces the whole text when it changes (TC-3025).
Native span attributes (`aria-label`, `id`, `style`, `data-*`, handlers) go onto the root; a changed `aria-label` is the new accessible name at once (TC-3031).

doesNot.text: Does not group thousands or add any symbol by itself: the plain display of `1234` is `1234`, not `1,234` (use `format`).
Does not show decimals during or after the count (`format` receives whole numbers only).
Does not accept children; the only content is the number text.
Does not animate again when it re-renders with the same `from`, `to` and `duration`.
Does not announce each step: `aria-live` is polite, not assertive, and there is no `role`.
Does not have a label, tooltip, input or keyboard behaviour; it is display only.

defaults.text: `from` 0; `duration` omitted: the limit is 15% of the distance, at least 500 ms and at most 2000 ms, so the real length is 15% of the distance up to a distance of about 13,333, and 2000 ms beyond (TC-3032).
The display is the plain number text; the root is an inline-block span.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `from`: the start number.
`duration`: the upper limit of the animation in ms (CountUp#4).
`format(value)`: the shown text (CountUp#10).
`className`, `pt.root`: styling only.

states.text: Counting: the root text changes frame by frame.
Settled: the root text is the final number (or its `format`).

testApi: `Spectra.findCountUp(name)` by `aria-label` or visible text; `Spectra.queryCountUp(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getText()`: trimmed root text. `getValue()`: the number in the text (commas dropped; first `-?digits(.digits)?`), `null` when none; a `format` with other digits (`1.5s`) parses the first number.
`waitForValue(n, { timeout, interval })` / `shouldHaveValue(n)`: waits until the parsed value equals `n` (within 0.001).
`waitForText(textOrRegExp, { timeout })`: waits for the exact text or a match.
`isLive()` / `shouldBeLive()`: `aria-live` is `polite` or `assertive`; `isAtomic()`: `aria-atomic` is `true` or empty.
`getContainer()`: the root span.

components.name: CurrencyInput

does.text: Shows a currency button at the start (the symbol, for example `$`) and an amount field after it.
The amount is shown with thousand grouping and two decimals, formatted in the active locale (`1250` shows `1,250.00` in en-US and `1.250,00` in id-ID).
The number format follows the `locale` (the provider's active locale by default), not the selected currency: changing the currency from `$` to `€` keeps the same separators.
Clicking the currency button opens a searchable list of currencies; each row reads `<symbol> - <currency name>` (for example `$ - US Dollar`) with the name in the active locale.
Typing in the list's search field filters the currencies by that text; text that matches nothing shows `No results found.`.
Choosing a currency changes the button's symbol, calls `onCurrencyChange(code, currency)` and moves focus to the amount field.
Choosing a currency does not change the amount or its separators.
`min` and `max` clamp a typed value on blur or Enter and stepper clicks stay inside the range (as in `NumberInput#1`).
A typed value is formatted to two decimals on blur (`10.5` shows `10.50`); with `allowEmptyValue` false a cleared field returns to `min` (or `0`).
The value reported by `onChange` is a plain number, or `undefined` when the field is empty.
A currency code that is not in the list is shown by its code in place of a symbol [unverified].

doesNot.text: The currency list cannot be cleared: choosing the selected currency again keeps it, and no `onCurrencyChange` is called for a clear.
The selected currency is not part of the value: `onChange` reports only the amount, `onCurrencyChange` reports the currency.
No stepper buttons by default.
No currency conversion when the currency changes.
With `currencyPlacement` `start-addon`, `startAddon` is ignored and stepper buttons are always stacked at the end (`controlOrientation: 'horizontal'` has no effect).
With `currencyPlacement` `embedded` there is no currency button and no selector, and `enableCurrencySelector` / `currencyDisplayMode` have no effect.
No range error message and no invalid look for a value outside `min`/`max`.

defaults.text: Currency `USD` shown as `$`, placed as a start addon with a selector.
Two fraction digits, always (`minFractionDigits` and `maxFractionDigits` 2), thousand grouping on.
`allowEmptyValue` true: the field can be empty and then shows the placeholder.
`step` 1, no `min`, no `max`, `showControls` false, size `xs`, not disabled, not read-only, not invalid.
The currency list holds 155 built-in currencies (loaded on first need) when `currencyOptions` is not given.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `currencyCode`: the initial currency (for example `JPY` shows `¥`); changing the prop changes the selected currency.
`currencyDisplayMode: 'code'`: the button shows the ISO code (`USD`) instead of the symbol.
`enableCurrencySelector: false`: the symbol (or code) is plain text at the start, with no button and no list.
`currencyOptions`: the list shows only these currencies.
`currencyPlacement: 'embedded'`: no start currency; the formatted amount itself carries the currency symbol (`€100.00`, placed as the locale does) and `startAddon` is shown.

`showControls`: increment and decrement buttons, labelled `Increase value by {step}` and `Decrease value by {step}`; with embedded placement `controlOrientation: 'horizontal'` puts decrement at the start and increment at the end.

`step`, `min`, `max`, `allowEmptyValue`, `minFractionDigits`, `maxFractionDigits`, `useGrouping`, `padStart`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `autoResize`: as in the `NumberInput` contract (for example `padStart` 5 shows `00012.00`, `useGrouping: false` shows `1250000.00`, `prefix` and `suffix` surround the amount).
`placeholder`: replaces `Enter amount`.
`disabled`: input, currency button and steppers are disabled.
`readOnly`: the amount cannot be edited, steppers are disabled, the currency list cannot be opened and the currency button is skipped by Tab.
`invalid`: `aria-invalid="true"` on the input.
`startElement`, `endElement`, `endAddon`: extra content (the end element is replaced by stacked stepper buttons).

builtInText.text: Amount placeholder: `Enter amount` (locale en, passed through `t()`).
Currency button accessible name: `Select currency, <symbol> <code>` (for example `Select currency, $ USD`; literal, not translated).
Search field placeholder in the list: `Search Currency...` (literal, not translated).
Empty search result: `No results found.` (locale en, passed through `t()`).
Stepper buttons: `Increase value by 1` and `Decrease value by 1` for step 1 (literal, not translated).

keyboard.text: ArrowUp and ArrowDown change the amount by `step`; Home and End go to `min` and `max`; Escape closes the currency list (as in `NumberInput#38`, `NumberInput#39`).
The currency button is a combobox in the Tab order, except when read-only or disabled.

states.text: Currency list closed or open.
Empty (placeholder) or with an amount.
Disabled, read-only, invalid: as set by the props above.
Focused: the amount field (also right after choosing a currency).

testApi: `Spectra.findCurrencyInput(name)`: by the accessible name; `Spectra.queryCurrencyInput(name)`: `null` when missing.

`getValue()` (formatted text, `""` when empty), `setValue(number)`, `clearValue()`, `paste(text)`, `stepUp()` / `stepDown()`, `jumpToMin()` / `jumpToMax()`, `increment()` / `decrement()`, `getIncrementButton()`, `getDecrementButton()`.

`getCurrency()` (symbol or code on the button), `getCurrencyTrigger()`, `hasCurrencySelector()`, `getCurrencySelector()`, `selectCurrency(labelOrPattern)`, `openCurrencySelector()`, `closeCurrencySelector({ method })`, `isCurrencySelectorOpen()`.
`filterCurrency(q)`, `getCurrencyFilterValue()`, `clearCurrencyFilter()`, `getCurrencyFilterInput()`, `hasCurrencyFilterInput()`.

`getStartAddon()`, `getEndAddon()`, `getStartElement()`, `getEndElement()` with `has*`; `getContainer()`, `getInput()`, `getDescription()`, `getDescriptionText()`; `focus()`, `blur()`, `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`.

components.name: CustomColumn

does.text: Lists every defined column as one checklist row (drag handle, checkbox with the header text); checked rows are the columns shown in the table, in list order.
Menu mode (`type` `menu`): the checklist sits in a popover under the table's `Column Visibility` header button; clicking that button opens it and a second click closes it.
Flat mode (`type` `flat`): the same checklist is always on the page, with no popover, no `Setup Columns` entry and no dialog.
Menu popover and flat list: a checkbox change applies to the table at once (no Save) and is saved for the next visit.
Menu popover and flat list: dragging a row reorders the table's columns at once and is saved; there is no pin control in these two lists.
Clicking anywhere on a row, or Enter or Space on a focused row, toggles its checkbox.
The menu popover starts with a `Setup Columns` button; clicking it closes the popover and opens the Setup Columns dialog.

The Setup Columns dialog (modal) shows, top to bottom: a hint text, a column-name search, the checklist with drag handles and pin buttons, and a `Preview` heading over a live preview table; the footer has `Reset to Default` and `Save`.
Edits in the dialog (check, pin, reorder) are staged: the preview follows them, the real table and the saved layout do not change until `Save`.
`Save` applies the staged order, checked state and pins to the table, saves them, and closes the dialog.
Closing the dialog with Escape, the close X (`Close dialog`) or a click outside it discards the staged edits; the table is unchanged and focus returns to the menu's trigger.
`Reset to Default` (dialog) stages the default layout and keeps the dialog open; the table changes only after `Save`.

The default layout is the definition order with every column checked except those with `defaultChecked: false`, no runtime pins (author pins stay), and the `maxColumn` cap applied; `Reset to Default` and the first load with nothing saved give the same layout.
A curated column (`defaultChecked: false`) is listed unchecked and stays off the table until checked; `Reset to Default` returns it to unchecked and still listed.
A column with `visible: false` is not listed, not shown, cannot be shown by the user, and `Reset to Default` does not bring it back.
The dialog's search narrows the rows by column name (case-insensitive substring, leading and trailing spaces ignored); clearing it lists every row again; it never changes any checked state.
While the search holds text, no row can be dragged; every opening of the dialog starts with an empty search.
Last visible column: when only one row is checked, that row's checkbox is disabled and its drag handle hidden, so the table never has zero columns; checking another row frees it.

`maxColumn` cap: once that many rows are checked, every unchecked row's checkbox is disabled and its drag handle hidden; unchecking one frees them; a layout over the cap is trimmed to the first `maxColumn` checked rows.
A locked column (`alwaysVisible`, or author-pinned with `pinned`) is always checked with a disabled checkbox, whatever is saved; it still counts toward the `maxColumn` cap and is never trimmed.

A disabled checkbox has a hover tooltip saying why: `This column is always shown.` (locked), `At least one column must remain visible.` (last visible), `Maximum N columns can be shown at once.` then `Uncheck another column first.` on a second line (cap); an enabled row has none.

Pin (dialog only): clicking a row's pin button pins it to the leading edge (left), forces it checked and moves it to the end of the pinned group at the top of the list; clicking again unpins it and moves it below the pinned group; an unchecked row cannot be pinned while the `maxColumn` cap is reached (the click does nothing).

Max pinned: once `maxPinnedColumns` runtime pins exist, every unpinned row's pin button stays but is `aria-disabled`, with the hover tooltip `Maximum N columns can be pinned at once. Unpin another column first.`; unpinning one enables them again.
Author pins (`pinned` on the column) are locked: the pin button shows pressed and disabled, and they do not use up the `maxPinnedColumns` budget.
Unchecking a runtime-pinned row also unpins it.
A row with `draggable: false` cannot be dragged: its drag handle and its pin button are hidden; a column with `reorderable: false` is not listed at all.

A locked `alwaysVisible` column can still be dragged (among unpinned columns); a pinned row can be dragged only among rows pinned to the same side, and a row never crosses between the pinned and unpinned groups.
Columns sharing a `parentHeader` are one row labelled with the parent header; its checkbox, pin and position act on all children together; a locked child locks the whole row.
With a `dataView`, a column visibility or pin change made elsewhere (another control, the header menu) is reflected in the checklist, and a change here is written to the `dataView`.

The preview table in the dialog shows exactly the checked columns in staged order with staged pins, with the first row of `tableData` only (no rows when `tableData` is empty), no row menu, no paginator, no column-visibility button.

What survives a reload: per `tableId`, the checked state, column order and runtime pins of the last change (menu, flat or Save); a layout equal to the default is not stored, so the table follows the definitions again.

On reload the definitions win for author-owned flags: locked columns stay checked, `visible: false` columns stay removed, a column added later takes its `defaultChecked`, and a saved column that is no longer defined is dropped from the saved layout unless it was saved unchecked.

doesNot.text: Does not sort, filter, search rows, rename columns or change any cell value; it only changes which columns show, their order and pins.
Does not reorder by keyboard: the drag handle is a focusable button whose Enter and Space do nothing; reordering is mouse drag only.
The menu popover and flat list have no pin button, no `Reset to Default` and no Save; those exist only in the Setup Columns dialog.
The dialog has no Cancel button and no confirm step on discard or Save, and shows no success message.
Does not save the dialog's staged edits unless `Save` is pressed; `Reset to Default` alone changes nothing saved.
Does not save search text, scroll or the open state across a reload.
Does not pin to the right: the pin button only pins to the left; a right pin comes from the author (`pinned: 'right'`) or the table's header menu.
Does not read the table's rows; `tableData` only feeds the preview.

Does not render its own trigger in menu mode; it opens from the table's header button (or `ref.toggleMenu()`), so with the table's `showCustomColumn` off and no other trigger there is no way to open it.

defaults.text: `type` `menu`; `showSetupColumn` true; `maxPinnedColumns` 3; no `maxColumn` cap.
All columns checked in definition order, no runtime pins.
Dialog size is large and modal; its title is the `Setup Columns` text unless `setupDialogTitle` is set.
The checklist is a `listbox` named by `tableName` (no `role` and no name when `tableName` is absent); rows are `role="option"`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `type: 'flat'`: inline checklist, see CustomColumn#3.
`showSetupColumn: false`: no `Setup Columns` entry in the menu and no dialog.
`maxColumn: N`: cap, see CustomColumn#19.
`maxPinnedColumns: N`: pin cap, see CustomColumn#23.

`setupColumnText`, `setupDialogTitle`, `saveText`, `resetDefaultText`, `previewText`: replace the `Setup Columns` button text (also the dialog title unless `setupDialogTitle` is set), the dialog title, `Save`, `Reset to Default`, `Preview`.
`setupHint(maxColumn, maxPinnedColumns)`: replaces the dialog hint text; returning nothing removes it.
`defaultColumns` flags: `alwaysVisible`, `pinned`, `defaultChecked`, `visible`, `draggable`, `reorderable`, `parentHeader` as described above.
`dataView`: two-way binding, see CustomColumn#29; `onVisibleColumnsChange(columns)`: called with the checked columns after a change here.
`tableData`, `dataKey`, `tableName`: only feed the preview table and the checklist name.
`pt`: styling only.

builtInText.text: `Setup Columns` (menu entry and dialog title), `Save`, `Reset to Default`, `Preview` (locale en). The label `Save Column Setup` does not exist in the component; it is only a story name.
Dialog hint: `Drag and drop to rearrange the order and click the pin to freeze up to 3 columns.` (the number is `maxPinnedColumns`).
Search placeholder and aria-label: `Search column name...`.
Row aria-labels: drag handle `Drag to reorder`, pin button `Toggle column pin`; dialog close X `Close dialog`.
DataTable header button (menu trigger) aria-label and tooltip: `Column Visibility`.
Disabled-row tooltips: see CustomColumn#21 and #23.

keyboard.text: Each row is focusable (Tab); Enter or Space toggles its checkbox; Enter or Space on a pin button pins or unpins without toggling the checkbox.
Escape closes the open menu popover or the Setup dialog (discarding staged edits); the dialog traps focus while open.

states.text: Menu closed / open; dialog closed / open.
Row checked or unchecked (`aria-selected`); row disabled (`data-disabled`); row pinned (pin button `aria-pressed` true).
Row draggable / not draggable (`draggable`); loading and error states: none.

testApi: Finders: `Spectra.findCustomColumn(name)` / `queryCustomColumn(name)` by the `tableName`; in menu mode open the menu first (click the header button once); from a table use `table.getCustomColumn()` after `table.getColumnVisibilityButton()` click.

Reads: `getColumnLabels`, `getCheckedColumnLabels`, `getUncheckedColumnLabels`, `getColumnCount`, `getVisibleColumnCount`, `isOpen`, `getPreviewTable` (dialog open); assertions `shouldHaveColumnLabels`, `shouldHaveCheckedColumnLabels`, `shouldHaveUncheckedColumnLabels`.

Per column: `isColumnVisible`, `isColumnToggleDisabled`, `isColumnPinned`, `hasDragHandle`, `hasPinControl`, `isPinDisabled`, `getPinTooltip`, `getColumnToggleTooltip`; assertions `shouldBeColumnVisible`, `shouldBeColumnToggleDisabled`, `shouldBeColumnPinned`, `shouldHaveDragHandle`, `shouldHavePinControl`, `shouldBePinDisabled`, `shouldHavePinTooltip(text, label)`, `shouldHaveColumnToggleTooltip(text, label)`.
Actions: `toggleColumn`, `showColumn`, `hideColumn`, `pinColumn`, `unpinColumn`, `moveColumn(label, target)`, `hoverColumn`.
Dialog: `getSetupLabel`, `openSetup(label?)`, `isSetupOpen`, `searchSetup`, `getSetupSearchPlaceholder`, `saveSetup(label?)`, `cancelSetup` (Escape), `resetToDefault(label?)`.
Details: `packages/testing-library/src/components/customcolumn/README.md`.

components.name: DataTable

does.text: Shows one row per record of the current page; rows keep the data order until a column is sorted.
Clicking a sortable column header sorts ascending, a second click descending, a third click clears the sort (back to the data order).
A plain header click replaces the active sort; Shift+click adds the column as a further sort key (the key is `multiSortKey`, default Shift; Ctrl also matches Cmd when set to `ctrl`).
A numbered badge appears on the sorted headers only while two or more columns are sorted; with one sorted column there is no badge.
Rows with equal values in the sorted column keep their data order, in ascending and in descending.

Sorting compares cell values as text with numeric-aware collation: `Item 2` before `Item 10`, numbers by value, ISO date strings chronologically; an empty (null/undefined) value goes last in both directions.
A `currency` column sorts by its amount; a row with no amount sorts first ascending and last descending.
A client-side (data array) sort returns the table to page 1; a server-driven sort keeps the current page and refetches.
Selected rows stay selected after sorting, searching, filtering and page changes; page navigation never clears the selection.
The header select-all checkbox acts on the current page only: checking adds the page's selectable rows to the existing selection, unchecking removes the page's rows; other pages keep their selection.
The header checkbox is indeterminate while some, not all, selectable rows of the page are selected; clicking it in that state selects the whole page.
A disabled or not-selectable row (`isRowDisabled`, `isRowSelectable`) has a disabled checkbox and is skipped by header select-all.
Clicking a row selects it (clicking again deselects it) when selection is on; a click on the checkbox cell or the actions button does not toggle the row twice.
With no row after filtering or searching, shows the no-results block; with no row and no active search/filter, shows the no-data block.
On the first load (no rows yet) shows a loading animation in place of rows; while a refetch runs with rows on screen the rows stay (dimmed) and the table is `aria-busy`.
In the error state shows the error message and a retry button that refetches the view; the error block is not the empty block.
Every body row has an actions (`⋯`) button (aria-label `Action`) while `showRowOptions` is on.

The header `⋯` button (aria-label `Column Visibility`, present while `showCustomColumn` is on) opens a popover with a `Setup Columns` button and a checkbox per column; unchecking a column removes it from the table at once and the layout is saved to the user's column-layout store without a Save step.
A column with `visible: false` is not on the table and not in the column list; a column with `defaultChecked: false` is off the table but listed unchecked.

The `Setup Columns` button closes the popover and opens a modal dialog with a column-name search box (`Search column name...`), the column list (drag-reorder, pin toggle, checkbox), a `Preview` heading over a one-row preview table, and footer buttons `Reset to Default` and `Save`; edits are staged and reach the table only on `Save` (closing the dialog discards them), and `Reset to Default` stages the default layout (definition order, each column's `defaultChecked`, author pins only) which `Save` then commits and which clears the saved layout.
An id-keyed table (`id` / `persistenceKey`) restores its sort, page, page size and column layout after a remount in the same browser session.

With `usePaginator`, removing the last row of the last page moves the table to the new last page, one page back when one row was removed (the Paginator corrects the page when the record count shrinks, see Paginator#51); removing the only remaining row of the whole table keeps the stale page number with the no-data block (the page is not reset) and the report `No records`. The page is not clamped in `useDataView` (`setPage` only floors at 1).

Multi-sort cycle: Shift+click on a column not yet sorted appends it as `asc`; on a sorted key it goes asc, desc, then that key alone is removed (the other keys stay); with `enableSortingRemoval: false` desc goes back to asc. Which headers sort: only data columns with `sortable: true` (select, actions and custom columns never sort).
`initialState` seeds the first render (sort, page, filter, selection, ...); the dataView `reset()` returns to that seed, not to the unsorted data order.

Pattern: the table returns to page 1 after Search is submitted (Enter, also with an empty box) or collapsed, after `Apply` in the filter panel (also an emptied draft), after a column-header filter changes or `Clear filter`, after `Rows per page` changes, and after a client-side sort click.

Pattern: selected rows stay selected, as whole row objects, across page changes, `Rows per page`, sort, Search and filter, so the selection can hold rows that are not on screen; BulkActionButton counts all of them while the header checkbox, row checkboxes and `getSelectedRowCount` cover only the visible page.

Pattern: the `Select all {N} records` link selects every record matching the current search and filter and replaces the existing selection with that set (earlier selected rows outside the current search/filter are dropped, `maxSelected` still caps it); N is the total of the current search/filter minus rows that cannot be selected, and the link disappears once the selected count equals N.

Pattern: with a BulkActionButton sibling, the select-all button appears as soon as one row on any page is selected, reads `Select All (N records)` while the selected count is below N, selects every record of the current search/filter across pages when clicked (replacing the selection), and then reads `Unselect All (N records)`.
Pattern: clicking `Unselect All (N records)` or the `Clear selection` button clears the selection on every page and the BulkActionButton disappears (it renders nothing at zero selected).

Pattern: the header checkbox looks only at the current page's selectable rows (checked when all are selected, indeterminate when some, unchecked when none), whatever other pages hold; in the indeterminate state a click selects the rest of the page, in the checked state a click removes the page's rows from the selection and leaves other pages selected.

Pattern: after the last row of the last page is deleted (the `data` prop shrinks, or the server count shrinks after a refetch) the footer Paginator snaps to the new last page and, in a server table, that page is fetched; deleting a row that is not the last of its page changes nothing about the page.

Pattern: a client table applies filter first, then Search, then sort, then slices the page; a server table sends filter, search, sort, page and limit together in one query and the server decides the order.

Pattern: sort, filter and Search survive each other: clearing Search keeps the filter and the sort, clearing the filter keeps Search and the sort, a new sort keeps Search and the filter, and page changes keep all three; all filters on different columns apply together (a row must match each).

Pattern: sort cycle with a plain click is asc, desc, cleared (asc, desc with `enableSortingRemoval: false`); a plain click on a column replaces every other sort key, also when the clicked column is already one key of a multi-sort (only that column stays, in its next direction), while Shift+click keeps the other keys (see DataTable#92); a client table goes to page 1 after each click, a server table keeps its page.
Pattern: Search matches only the columns currently shown in the column list, so hiding a column removes it from the search while a term is active.

Pattern: table state with an `id`, `persistenceKey` or dataView `id` is written on every change and restored on the next mount: Search, sort, filter, page, page size (only with `usePaginator`), filter panel open, density and column sizing; with the default `showCustomColumn` the column visibility, order and pinning are kept in the user's column-layout store (saved at once from the column list and on `Save` from the dialog), not in `statePersistence`.

Pattern: with the default `statePersistence` `sessionStorage` the state survives a page refresh in the same tab and is gone in a new tab or after the tab is closed; `localStorage` keeps it across browser restarts; restored values replace the `initialState` values for the stored slices, and `reset()` returns to `initialState`, not to the stored state.

Pattern: the table has no dialog-specific state rule: a table inside a dialog is mounted and unmounted with the dialog and follows the same persistence rule, so with an `id` or `persistenceKey` it comes back with its stored Search, sort, filter, page and page size on every open, and without a key it starts from `initialState` (page 1, no sort, no filter, no selection) on every open; two tables with the same key share one stored state.

doesNot.text: Does not sort a column that lacks `sortable: true`: no sort icon, no `aria-sort`, no response to click or Enter.
Does not return to the `initialState.sort` when the third header click clears the sort; it returns to the data order.
Does not sort ties by any secondary key; no implicit tie-break by id or index.
Does not show a checkbox column or header select-all for `selectionType` `single` or `none`; single selects by row click only.
Does not show a paginator, page size or "Showing" report unless `usePaginator` is set; without it every row is rendered on one page.
Does not show a count of selected rows or a clear-selection control by itself; those come from a BulkActionButton sibling.
Does not export by itself; there is no Download button inside the table.
Does not show the "Select all N records" link on a partly selected page, nor once every selectable record is selected.
Does not let a header select-all exceed `maxSelected`; a capped select-all stores fewer rows and the header stays indeterminate, not checked.
Does not show a description under the no-data title unless `emptyStateDescription` is set; does not show a create button unless `emptyStateAction` is set.
Does not show the create CTA in the no-results block (only `noResultsAction`, when set).
Does not show a drag handle for row reorder while any column is sorted.
Does not show a tooltip on the header checkbox or the row checkbox, except the disabled-row reason and the `maxSelected` hint on a disabled row checkbox.
Does not fetch on its own: server rows, search and export come from the `dataView`.

Pattern: does not return to page 1 after a server-driven sort, a page change, a column show/hide/reorder/pin/resize, a row selection or a row expand; hiding a column from the column list or column menu keeps that column's filter, while a column that leaves the `columns` prop drops its filter (page 1) and its sort (page kept).

Pattern: does not clear the selection on page change, `Rows per page`, sort, Search, filter or when rows leave `data`; the selection is cleared only by the BulkActionButton clear and `Unselect All` buttons, by unchecking the header checkbox for the rows of the page shown, by `dataView.clearSelection()`, or by `reset()` (back to the `initialState` selection).

Pattern: does not clamp the page in the table or the view; only the footer Paginator corrects a page past the end, so with `cursorPagination`, `infiniteScroll` or no paginator a stale page number stays.

Pattern: does not search while typing; the SearchButton box applies its term on submit only, its clear button only empties the box without changing the table until submit, and the term is trimmed before it is applied.
Pattern: does not store the selection, expanded rows, row edits, row data or cursor in `statePersistence`, so a page refresh or a remount shows no selected rows unless `initialState` seeds them.
Pattern: does not show `Select all {N} records` on a page whose selectable rows are not all checked, and does not select across pages without that link or the BulkActionButton select-all button.

defaults.text: `selectionType` is `none`; `usePaginator` false; `showRowOptions` true; `showCustomColumn` true; `stickyHeader` true; `keyboardNavigation` true (role `grid`).
With `usePaginator`, `rowsPerPage` is 10 and `rowsPerPageOptions` is 10, 25, 50, 100.
Sorting cycle is tri-state (asc, desc, cleared); `enableSortingRemoval: false` makes it asc and desc only.
`resizableColumns` and `reorderableColumns` are off; `columnMenu` is off; `filterDisplay` is `menu`; `loadingVariant` is `lottie`; `skeletonRowCount` is 5.
`statePersistence` is `sessionStorage`, active only when an `id` or `persistenceKey` exists.
`maxSelectAllRecords` is 10000; an over-cap cross-page select-all is aborted unless `onSelectAllExceedsMax` resolves true.
An empty cell shows `-` (`emptyCellText`).

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `selectionType="multiple"`: a leading checkbox column and a header select-all appear; `aria-multiselectable` is set on the grid.
`selectionType="single"`: no checkbox column; clicking a row selects it and clicking it again deselects it, unless `keepSingleSelection`.
`selectOnRowClick={false}`: a row click no longer selects; only the checkbox does.

`maxSelected`: at the limit every unselected row's checkbox is disabled, and hovering it shows `You've reached the maximum selection of {limit} rows.` (`maxSelectedReachedHint`); deselecting a row re-enables the others.

`selectAllAcrossPages`: the link `Select all {N} records` appears under the header checkbox only after the whole page is checked, N = total records minus disabled rows; clicking it selects every record (header shows a spinner while it fetches) and the link disappears.
`usePaginator`: the footer paginator appears (aria-label `Table pagination`) with page links, jump-to-page input, report text and a `Rows per page` dropdown.

`cursorPagination`: a footer nav (aria-label `Table pagination`) with only `Previous page` and `Next page` buttons (no page numbers, jump input, report or rows-per-page), `Previous page` disabled on page 1 and `Next page` disabled when the view has no next page; `infiniteScroll`: no footer paginator, a `Load more` button after the rows that is shown only while more rows remain (it also loads by itself when scrolled into view and is disabled while loading), and it wins over `cursorPagination` and `usePaginator`.

BulkActionButton sibling bound to the same `dataView`: appears only while at least one row is selected, shows the count text, a `Bulk Action` menu and a clear-selection button; absent at zero selected.

BulkActionButton shows its select-all button (`Select All (N records)`, N = records of the current search/filter minus rows that cannot be selected) only while something is selected and records exist; once all selectable records are selected it reads `Unselect All (N records)` and clicking it clears the selection.
BulkActionButton clear-selection button clears the selection on every page, not only the visible one.
ExportButton sibling: its menu offers `Download as XLSX` and `Download as CSV` by default; `Download as PDF` and `Print` only when listed in its `formatOptions`.
`resizableColumns` (or `resizable` on a column): a drag handle on the header edge; double-click auto-fits; `columnResizeMode` default `onEnd` commits the width on release.
`pinned: 'left' | 'right'` on a column: it sticks to that edge while the body scrolls sideways, is always visible, and is not draggable across the pin boundary.

`columnMenu`: each data column header gets an options button (aria-label `Column options`) whose menu offers `Pin left` and `Pin right` on an unpinned column, `Pin right` and `Unpin` on a left-pinned one, `Pin left` and `Unpin` on a right-pinned one, then `Autosize`, `Hide column`, and `Filter` only for a filterable column with `filterDisplay` `menu`; `columnMenu` may be a feature list (`pin`, `autosize`, `hide`, `filter`) and a column's own `columnMenu` overrides the table's; a choice closes the menu and never sorts the column.
`filterDisplay` `menu` (default) with `filter` on a column: a filter trigger in that header (aria-label `Filter {column}`) with `Clear filter`; `row` shows an input row under the headers.
`maxColumn`: once that many columns are checked in the column list, the unchecked ones are disabled.
`alwaysVisible` column: its column-list checkbox is checked and disabled.
`reorderable` (row drag): a drag-handle column appears while no column is sorted.
`emptyStateDescription`, `emptyStateAction`, `noResultsAction`: the description or button appears in the matching empty block only.

`slots.loading`, `slots.error`, `slots.emptyState`, `slots.pagination`: replace the built-in block of that state; `slots.pagination` replaces the footer only together with `usePaginator` (and not with `infiniteScroll`).
`loadingVariant="skeleton"`: skeleton rows replace the rows on every load, including a refetch (no overlay).

`rowOptions` (an item list, or a function of the row evaluated only for the row whose menu is open): the row `⋯` button opens a menu (aria-label `Row action menu panel`) with those items, and clicking the same button again closes it; `isRowActionDisabled(row)` returning true disables that row's button, a non-empty string returned also disables it and shows the string as the hover tooltip instead of `Action`; without `rowOptions` the button is still present and the menu has no items.
`rowExpansion`, `treeData`, `groupRowsBy`: expand/collapse buttons (`Expand row` / `Collapse row`, `Expand group` / `Collapse group`); grouping and tree are client-side only.
`statePersistence: 'none'`: no state restored after remount.

Pattern: `selectAllAcrossPages` needs no `fetchAll` prop on the table: the link calls `dataView.fetchAll()`, which a client view answers with its filtered and searched rows and a server view answers with its `fetchAll` option or, without one, its `queryFn` called without `page` and `limit`.

Pattern: `statePersistence` `none`, or a table with no `id`, `persistenceKey` or dataView `id`, writes and restores nothing; `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and `url` choose where the state is kept; with `showCustomColumn` off the column visibility, order and pinning are kept by `statePersistence` too.

builtInText.text: Header checkbox aria-label `Table select all checkbox`; row checkbox aria-label `Row selection checkbox`.
Row actions button aria-label and tooltip `Action`; header column-visibility button aria-label and tooltip `Column Visibility`.
Empty, no filter: `No data available`. Empty with search/filter: `No results found` and `Try adjusting your search or filter.`
Error: `Something went wrong.` with retry button `Try Again`.

Paginator: report `Showing {first} to {last} of {totalRecords}`, `No records` at zero; `Rows per page`, `First Page`, `Previous Page`, `Next Page`, `Last Page`, `Page {page}`, `Jump to page`; nav aria-label `Table pagination`.
Cursor and load-more: `Previous page`, `Next page`, `Load more`.
Cross-page link: `Select all {totalRecords} records`.
Cap hint: `You've reached the maximum selection of {limit} rows.`
Column list dialog: `Setup Columns`, `Reset to Default`, `Save`, `Preview`; hint `Drag and drop to rearrange the order and click the pin to freeze up to 3 columns.`
Column menu: `Column options`, `Pin left`, `Pin right`, `Unpin`, `Autosize`, `Hide column`, `Filter`; filter: `Clear filter`, `All`, `Filter {column}`.
Live region: `{count} results`, `Sorted by {column} ascending`, `Sorted by {column} descending`, `Sorting cleared`, `Loading`.
Rows: `Expand row`, `Collapse row`, `Expand group`, `Collapse group`, `Save row`, `Cancel edit`; empty cell `-`.

BulkActionButton: `1 item selected` / `N items selected`; `Select All (N records)` / `Unselect All (N records)` (`1 record` when N is 1); aria-labels `Select all records`, `Unselect all records`, `Clear selection`; `Bulk Action`, `Apply`.
ExportButton: `Download as XLSX`, `Download as CSV`, `Download as PDF`, `Print`; tooltip and aria-label `Download`; busy text `Downloading...`.

keyboard.text: Tab enters the grid at one roving cell; arrow keys move one cell, Home / End, PageUp / PageDown jump (PageUp/PageDown jump by the page size).
Enter or Space on a focused sortable header sorts like a click; on a non-sortable header nothing happens.
Enter or Space on a focused body cell runs the row click and toggles the row selection (when `selectOnRowClick` is not false).
Escape leaves an open cell editor; Escape on a plain cell is not consumed by the table.

states.text: Loading: `aria-busy` on the table root; first load shows the animation block, refetch keeps rows.
Empty (no data / no results) and error are separate blocks; `isEmpty()` is false in the error state.
Selected row: `data-selected` true on the row and its checkbox checked; header checkbox checked / indeterminate / unchecked for all / some / none of the page's selectable rows.
Sorted header: `aria-sort` `ascending` or `descending`; sortable but unsorted `none`.
Disabled row: checkbox disabled, row still listed.

Pattern: BulkActionButton select-all states: absent at zero selected, `Select All (N records)` while the selected count differs from N, `Unselect All (N records)` when the selected count equals N (counts are compared, not rows, so after Search or a filter changes N the label can flip with the same selection), `1 record` when N is 1.

testApi: Finder: `Spectra.findDataTableById(id)` (preferred), `Spectra.findDataTable(name)`; `queryDataTable*` return null. Name lookup is slower; `find*` waits the implicit wait, `query*` waits `probeTimeout` (500ms).

Rows and cells: `getRowCount`, `getAllRows`, `getRow(i)`, `getRowByCellText(header, text)`, `getColumnTexts(header)`, `getCell`, `getCellText`; `shouldHaveRowCount(n)`, `shouldHaveCellText(text, header, row)`, `shouldHaveRowWithCellText`. Count covers the current page only; group and pinned rows are excluded.

Columns: `getColumnHeaderLabels`, `isColumnVisible`, `getColumnWidth`, `getColumnPinSide`, `openColumnMenu`, `hideColumn`, `pinColumn`, `unpinColumn`, `reorderColumn`, `getCustomColumn`, `getColumnVisibilityButton`; `shouldHaveColumnHeaderLabels([...])`.

Sort: `sortBy(header, dir?)` (waits for the rows), `getSortDirection` (reads the header), `isColumnSorted` / `hasColumnSorted` (reads the cell values; `shouldHaveColumnSorted`), `isColumnSortable`, `clickColumnHeader` (one click, no wait); `shouldHaveSortDirection(dir, header)`.

Selection: `selectRow`, `deselectRow`, `isRowSelected`, `selectAll`, `deselectAll`, `toggleSelectAll`, `isAllSelected`, `isSelectAllIndeterminate`, `selectAllAcrossPages`, `getSelectedRowCount`, `hasSelectionColumn`; `shouldBeRowSelected`, `shouldHaveSelectedRowCount(n)`, `shouldBeAllSelected`. Counts are for the current page. Row wrapper: `getCheckbox`, `getSelectionTooltipText`.

Pagination: `getPaginator`, `hasPaginator`, `goToPage`, `goToNextPage` / `goToPreviousPage` / `goToFirstPage` / `goToLastPage`, `setPageSize`, `getPaginationReport`, `loadMore`; each action returns once the table shows the result.

State: `isLoading`, `getSkeletonRowCount` (`shouldHaveSkeletonRowCount(n)`: the skeleton rows of `loadingVariant="skeleton"`, `skeletonRowCount` 5 by default, 0 when none), `isEmpty`, `getEmptyStateText`, `getEmptyStateDescription`, `hasError`, `getErrorMessage`, `retry`, `hasRetryButton`, `hasEmptyStateIllustration`; `shouldHave*` forms poll, plain readers wait `probeTimeout`.
Keyboard: `focusCell`, `navigateCell`, `getFocusedCell` need `keyboardNavigation` on.
Row sub-wrapper: `getRowOptionsButton`, `openRowOptions`, `clickRowOption(label)`, `getRowOptionsMenu`, `select` / `deselect`, `isSelected`, `isDisabled`, `expand` / `collapse`.
Siblings have their own wrappers: SearchButton, FilterContainer, BulkActionButton, ExportButton, CustomColumn.

components.name: DatePicker

does.text: Shows a read-only text field with a calendar icon at its end; clicking it opens a calendar panel below, left-aligned (bottom-start).
The field text follows the committed value, not the draft: with Apply/Cancel buttons, picking a day in the panel does not change the field until Apply.
Single mode shows the day formatted with the date format, e.g. `18/05/2026`.
Multiple mode shows every picked day formatted, joined by `, `.
Range mode shows `start - end` once both ends are picked; with only the start picked it shows the start alone.
In range mode, after the start is picked and the end is pending, days before the start are disabled in the panel.
Clicking Cancel, or clicking outside the panel, discards the draft; the field keeps the committed value.
Pressing Escape with the panel open closes it (Popover behaviour, closes the topmost layer first).
Apply commits the draft, calls `onChange` and `onDateSelect` (only if the draft is non-null), and closes the panel.
The clear button empties the value (`onChange` receives `null`) and does not open the panel.
Multiple mode: clicking a day adds it, clicking an already picked day removes it; the picked days are kept and shown in ascending date order.

Range mode: a click while no start is picked, or while both ends are picked, starts a new range (start only, end cleared); the click after the start picks the end; the end may be the start day itself (one-day range, shown `start - start`).
Apply with nothing picked and no initial value closes the panel and fires neither `onChange` nor `onDateSelect`; Apply is not disabled by an empty draft.
