While the field has a displayed value and the picker is neither disabled nor read-only, a clear button replaces the calendar icon (same size) and has no `showClear` switch; with no value the calendar icon shows. `clearIcon` replaces the default close icon (`CloseLine`).
`aria-describedby` passes through to the focusable field, so the text of the elements it names (a surrounding `Field`'s helper or error text) is its accessible description.

doesNot.text: No typing: the text field is always read-only; a date cannot be entered by keyboard text.
The placeholder does not change per mode: single, multiple and range all show the same default placeholder.
No Apply or Cancel button unless configured (see Only when configured); the clear button shows only while the field has a value (see `DatePicker#24`).
The panel does not open when the field is disabled or read-only (click, Enter, or the open prop's `onOpenChange` are ignored).
No error message text is rendered; `invalid` only sets `aria-invalid` and the invalid styling.
`onDateSelect` is never called with `null`.
Multiple mode never auto-closes the panel on selection.
`minDate` and `maxDate` only disable picks in the panel: a `value` outside them is not clamped, rejected or flagged, and is shown as given.
Pressing keys in the field (typing digits, Backspace, Delete) changes nothing: no value, no `onChange`, no invalid state.

defaults.text: `mode` is `single`, `dateFormat` is `dd/MM/yyyy`, `size` is `xs`.
`showButtons`, `showTime`, `invalid`, `disabled`, `defaultOpen` are all `false`; `closeOnSelect` is `true`.
Without a string `placeholder`, the placeholder is `Select date` (default locale).
An empty value shows an empty field text.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `showButtons`: Cancel and Apply buttons appear in the panel footer; the panel then never auto-closes on selection, `closeOnSelect` is ignored, and `onChange`/`onDateSelect` fire only on Apply.
`applyButtonLabel` / `cancelButtonLabel`: replace the `Apply` / `Cancel` footer labels (only visible with `showButtons`).
`closeOnSelect` true (default) without `showButtons`: single mode without `showTime` closes on the first pick; range mode without `showTime` closes once both start and end are picked.
`showTime`: single and range modes stay open after a pick, closing only by outside click or Escape; time controls appear in the panel.
`closeOnSelect={false}` (without `showButtons`): no mode auto-closes; the value is committed on every pick.
`minDate` / `maxDate`: days before the min or after the max (whole-day comparison) are disabled in the panel and cannot be picked; month and year cells outside the bounds are disabled too.
`disabledDate(date)` returning true: that day is disabled in the panel.
`dateFormat`: changes the field text format (rendered with `timeZone` when set).
`placeholder` as a string replaces `Select date`; a non-string placeholder is ignored and `Select date` is used.
`open` / `defaultOpen`: panel starts open (`defaultOpen`) or is controlled (`open` with `onOpenChange`).
`onDateSelect`: without `showButtons` called on each calendar pick with a non-null value.

builtInText.text: Placeholder `Select date` (default locale en).
Clear button `aria-label` and `title`: `Clear selection`.
Footer button labels: `Cancel`, `Apply`.
Calendar navigation `aria-label`s `Previous month`, `Next month`; time controls (`showTime`): `Previous Hour`, `Next Hour`, `Previous Minute`, `Next Minute`, `AM`, `PM`.

keyboard.text: Enter on the field toggles the panel (opens when closed, closes when open); ignored when disabled or read-only.
Space toggles the panel via the popover trigger on key release (the picker's own handler does not act on Space).
Escape closes an open panel.
No arrow-key day navigation: day cells are native buttons with no key handler, reached with Tab and activated with Enter or Space.

states.text: `disabled`: field text input is disabled, panel cannot open, footer buttons disabled, clear button not shown.
`readOnly`: field has `aria-readonly`, panel cannot open, clear button not shown, calendar cells and navigation are disabled.
`invalid`: `aria-invalid="true"` on the field (an explicit `aria-invalid` prop wins) and the group is styled invalid.
Controlled `value`: the field text and the draft follow the prop; with `onChange` only and no `value`, the picker holds its own value (uncontrolled).

testApi: Finders: `Spectra.findDatePicker(label, opts?)` waits for the component (default 1000ms); `Spectra.queryDatePicker(label, opts?)` returns `null` when absent.

Parts: `getContainer`, `getInput`, `getIcon`, `hasIcon`, `getPanel` (throws when closed), `getCalendar` (opens panel if needed), `getButtonBar`, `getApplyButton`, `getCancelButton`, `getClearButton` (throws without a value, or while disabled or read-only), `getAccessibleDescription` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits).
Readers: `getValue`, `getPlaceholder`, `isOpen`, `hasButtonBar`, `hasApplyButton`, `hasCancelButton`, `hasClearButton`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `isInvalid`.

Actions: `open`, `close({ method: 'clickOutside' | 'escape' })`, `selectDate(day)`, `selectMonth(month)`, `selectYear(year)`, `apply`, `cancel`, `clear`, `focus`, `blur`; selecting opens the panel automatically if closed.
Assertions seen in README: `shouldContainValue`, `shouldNotBeOpen`, `shouldHaveClearButton`, `shouldNotHaveClearButton` (plus the generated `should*` of each reader).

components.name: DayOfMonthPicker

does.text: Shows a read-only text field with a calendar icon at the end; clicking it opens a panel with the numbers 1 to 31 as buttons in a grid of 7 columns (5 rows, the last row has 3 numbers and 4 empty cells).
Selecting a number in single mode shows it in the field (for example `12`) and, by default, closes the panel.
Clicking the already selected number in single mode clears the selection (empty field) and keeps the panel open; `onDateSelect` still reports the clicked number.
In multiple mode each click adds or removes a number, the field shows the numbers ascending separated by `, `, and the panel stays open.

In range mode the first click sets the start (field shows `<start> - `), the second click completes the range with the lower number first and closes the panel; a click after a complete range starts a new range.
A range with equal start and end shows just that number; the numbers between start and end are marked in range and both ends are marked selected.
Days for which `disabledDay(day)` returns true are disabled and cannot be selected.
`panelHeader` and `panelFooter` content appear above and below the number grid in the panel.
Escape closes the open panel.
`onDateSelect` reports the number (single), the sorted list (multiple) or `[start, end]` (range), and `onChange` reports the new value (single: `null` when cleared).
`onPanelHide` is called each time the panel closes.

While the field has a displayed value and the picker is neither disabled nor read-only, a clear button replaces the calendar icon (same size); clicking it empties the value (`onChange(null)`) and leaves the panel as it is. With no value the calendar icon shows. `clearIcon` replaces the default close icon (`CloseLine`).
`aria-describedby` passes through to the focusable field, so the text of the elements it names (a surrounding `Field`'s helper or error text) is its accessible description.

doesNot.text: The field cannot be typed into; it is always read-only text.
Does not mark the current day of the month as today (no today highlight).
Has no weekday header, no month or year, and no real dates; 29, 30 and 31 are always offered.
Does not open or change value while disabled or read-only.
Does not close the panel after each click in multiple mode, and not after the first click of a range.
A value outside 1 to 31 is not shown in the field.

defaults.text: Mode `single`, `closeOnSelect` on, size `xs`, closed, not disabled, not invalid.
No value: empty field showing the placeholder.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `mode: 'multiple'` or `'range'`: see `DayOfMonthPicker#4`, `DayOfMonthPicker#5`.
`value` + `onChange` (controlled) or `defaultValue` (initial selection): the field shows the value.
`closeOnSelect: false`: the panel stays open after a selection.
`disabledDay`, `panelHeader`, `panelFooter`: see `DayOfMonthPicker#7`, `DayOfMonthPicker#8`.
`placeholder`: replaces the empty-field text; passed as given, not translated.
`open` + `onOpenChange` (controlled) or `defaultOpen`: panel opened from outside or initially.
`disabled`: field and number buttons disabled. `readOnly`: field has `aria-readonly` and the panel does not open.
`invalid` (or `aria-invalid`): invalid styling and `aria-invalid` on the field; `aria-invalid` wins when both are given.
`size`, `className`, `style`, `pt`: styling only.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `id`, `name`: set on the field.

builtInText.text: Default placeholder `Select day` (locale en; passed through `t()`).
Each number button has aria-label equal to its number (for example `15`).

keyboard.text: Enter on the field toggles the panel; Space (native trigger behavior) toggles it too.
Number buttons are Tab stops (disabled ones are skipped); Enter or Space activates the focused one.
Escape closes the panel.

states.text: Closed / open panel.
Number selected: `data-selected`, `aria-pressed` true; between range ends: `data-in-range`.
Number disabled: `data-disabled`, `aria-disabled`, button disabled.
Disabled, read-only, invalid picker: as in `DayOfMonthPicker#27`, `DayOfMonthPicker#28`.

testApi: `Spectra.findDayOfMonthPicker(label)`: by `aria-label`, label text or placeholder; `Spectra.queryDayOfMonthPicker(label)`: `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindDayOfMonthPicker(label)`.
`getInput()`, `getIcon()`, `hasIcon()`, `getValue()` / `shouldHaveValue(text)` (field text), `getPlaceholder()`.
`getPanel()`, `isOpen()`, `open()`, `close()` (with `Escape`).
`getDayButton(n)`, `getDayButtons()`, `selectDay(n)` (opens the panel if needed).
`getSelectedDays()`, `isDaySelected()`, `isDayInRange()`, `isDayDisabled()` with `should*` / `shouldNot*` forms; `isDayToday()` is always false (no today mark).
`getHeaderSlot()`, `hasHeaderSlot()`, `getFooterSlot()`, `hasFooterSlot()`.
`focus()`, `blur()`, `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`, `element`, `getContainer()`.

Clear button: `getClearButton` (throws without a value, or while disabled or read-only), `hasClearButton` (`shouldHaveClearButton()` / `shouldNotHaveClearButton()`), `clear()`; `getAccessibleDescription()` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits).

components.name: DayOfWeekPicker

does.text: Shows a read-only text field with a calendar icon at the end; clicking it opens a panel with 7 weekday buttons in the order Sunday to Saturday (index 0 to 6).
Selecting a weekday in single mode shows its label in the field and (by default) closes the panel.
Clicking the already selected weekday in single mode clears the selection (empty field) and keeps the panel open; `onDateSelect` still reports the clicked index.
In multiple mode each click adds or removes a weekday, the field shows the labels in week order separated by `, `, and the panel stays open.

In range mode the first click sets the start (field shows `<start> - `), the second click completes the range in week order (the lower index first) and closes the panel; a click after a complete range starts a new range.
A range with the same start and end shows just that one label; the days between start and end are marked in range and the ends marked first and last selected.
Weekdays for which `disabledDay(index)` returns true are disabled and cannot be selected.
`panelHeader` and `panelFooter` content appear above and below the weekday buttons in the panel.
Escape closes the open panel.
`onDateSelect` reports the selected index (single), the sorted list (multiple) or `[start, end]` (range), and `onChange` reports the new value (single: `null` when cleared).
`onPanelHide` is called each time the panel closes.
The field and the panel weekday buttons use `dayLabels` (index 0 is Sunday).

While the field has a displayed value and the picker is neither disabled nor read-only, a clear button replaces the calendar icon (same size); clicking it empties the value (`onChange(null)`) and leaves the panel as it is. With no value the calendar icon shows. `clearIcon` replaces the default close icon (`CloseLine`).
`aria-describedby` passes through to the focusable field, so the text of the elements it names (a surrounding `Field`'s helper or error text) is its accessible description.

doesNot.text: The field cannot be typed into; it is always read-only text.
Does not open or change value while disabled or read-only.
Has no week-start setting: the first button is always Sunday.
Does not close the panel after each click in multiple mode, and does not close after the first click of a range.
Does not show weekdays that are selected outside 0 to 6; such values show an empty field.

defaults.text: Mode `single`, `closeOnSelect` on, size `xs`, closed, not disabled, not invalid.
Labels are the long locale weekday names (`Sunday` ... `Saturday`, locale en).
No value: field empty.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `mode: 'multiple'` or `'range'`: see `DayOfWeekPicker#4`, `DayOfWeekPicker#5`.
`value` + `onChange` (controlled) or `defaultValue` (initial selection): the field shows the labels of the value.
`closeOnSelect: false`: the panel stays open after a selection (single and range).
`dayLabels`: replaces the 7 labels in field and panel (for example `Sun`...`Sat`).
`disabledDay`, `panelHeader`, `panelFooter`: see `DayOfWeekPicker#7`, `DayOfWeekPicker#8`.
`placeholder`: replaces the empty-field text; passed as given, not translated.
`open` + `onOpenChange` (controlled) or `defaultOpen`: panel opened from outside or initially.
`disabled`: field and weekday buttons disabled. `readOnly`: field has `aria-readonly` and the panel does not open.
`invalid` (or `aria-invalid`): invalid styling and `aria-invalid` on the field; `aria-invalid` wins when both are given.
`size`, `className`, `style`, `pt`: styling only.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `id`, `name`: set on the field.

builtInText.text: Default placeholder `Select day` (locale en; passed through `t()`).
Weekday button aria-label equals its label text (for example `Monday`).

keyboard.text: Enter on the field toggles the panel; Space (native trigger behavior) toggles it too.
Weekday buttons are Tab stops (disabled ones are skipped); Enter or Space selects the focused weekday.
Escape closes the panel.

states.text: Closed / open panel.
Weekday selected: `data-selected`, `aria-selected`; in range also `data-first-selected`, `data-last-selected`, `data-in-range`.
Weekday disabled: `data-disabled`, `aria-disabled`, button disabled.
Disabled, read-only, invalid picker: as in `DayOfWeekPicker#29`, `DayOfWeekPicker#30`.

testApi: `Spectra.findDayOfWeekPicker(label)`: by `aria-label`, label text or placeholder; `Spectra.queryDayOfWeekPicker(label)`: `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindDayOfWeekPicker(label)`.
`getInput()`, `getIcon()`, `hasIcon()`, `getValue()` / `shouldHaveValue(text)` (field text), `getPlaceholder()`.
`getPanel()`, `isOpen()`, `open()`, `close()` (with `Escape`).
`getDayButton(index | label)`, `getDayButtons()` / `shouldHaveDayButtonsCount(n)`, `selectDay(index | label)` (opens the panel if needed).

`getSelectedDays()` (labels), `shouldContainSelectedDays(label)`, `isDaySelected()`, `isDayInRange()`, `isDayFirstSelected()`, `isDayLastSelected()`, `isDayDisabled()` with `should*` / `shouldNot*` forms.
`getHeaderSlot()`, `hasHeaderSlot()`, `getFooterSlot()`, `hasFooterSlot()`.
`focus()`, `blur()`, `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`, `element`, `getContainer()`.

Clear button: `getClearButton` (throws without a value, or while disabled or read-only), `hasClearButton` (`shouldHaveClearButton()` / `shouldNotHaveClearButton()`), `clear()`; `getAccessibleDescription()` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits).

components.name: DayOfYearPicker

does.text: Shows a read-only text field with a calendar icon at the end; clicking it opens a panel with a month header and a grid of that month's day numbers (7 columns, no weekday row).
The panel opens on the month of the first selected date, otherwise on the current month, and re-opens on that month each time it opens.
The previous and next buttons move one month and the title shows the month name (`August`); `onMonthChange` reports the month index (0-11).
The previous button is disabled in January and the next button in December; there is no year and no wrap-around.
February always offers 29 days, April, June, September, November 30, the others 31 (the grid is year-agnostic, Feb 29 is selectable).
The field shows the value formatted with `dateFormat` (default `Jan 5` style, `MMM d`; month names in the locale).
In single mode picking a day shows it in the field and closes the panel; clicking the selected day clears the selection (empty field) and keeps the panel open.
In multiple mode each click adds or removes a month-day, the field lists them in calendar order separated by `, `, and the panel stays open.

In range mode the first click sets the start (field shows `<start> - `), the second click completes the range with the earlier day first (it may be in another month; navigate between clicks) and closes the panel; a click after a complete range starts a new range.
Range days between start and end are marked in range across months; the ends are marked selected. A range with the same start and end shows `Jan 1 - Jan 1`.
Days for which `disabledDay({ month, day })` returns true are disabled and cannot be selected.
`overlayMessage` text shows at the top of the panel, `overlayHeader` above the day grid and `overlayFooter` below it.
With `overlayValidatorFn`, `overlayValidatorMessage` shows under the grid while the function returns false for the current value (the function may be async; a throw counts as invalid).
Escape closes the open panel.
`onChange` reports the new value (single: `null` when cleared) and `onPanelHide` is called each time the panel closes.

While the field has a displayed value and the picker is neither disabled nor read-only, a clear button replaces the calendar icon (same size); clicking it empties the value (`onChange(null)`) and leaves the panel as it is. With no value the calendar icon shows. `clearIcon` replaces the default close icon (`CloseLine`).
`aria-describedby` passes through to the focusable field, so the text of the elements it names (a surrounding `Field`'s helper or error text) is its accessible description.

doesNot.text: The field cannot be typed into; it is always read-only text.
Has no year: the value is `{ month, day }` and never a date; no year navigation.
Does not mark today (no today highlight).
Has no `onDateSelect` and no `closeOnSelect`: it always closes after single selection and after completing a range, and never after a multiple click.
Does not open or change value while disabled or read-only.
Does not show the validator message unless both `overlayValidatorFn` and `overlayValidatorMessage` are given.
Does not collapse a same-day range unless `collapseSameDate` is on.

defaults.text: Mode `range` (not single), `dateFormat` `MMM d`, `collapseSameDate` off, size `xs`, closed, not disabled, not invalid.
No value: empty field showing the placeholder.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `mode: 'single'` or `'multiple'`: see `DayOfYearPicker#7`, `DayOfYearPicker#8`.
`value` + `onChange` (controlled) or `defaultValue`: the field shows the value.
`dateFormat`: tokens `MMMM`, `MMM`, `MM`, `M`, `dd`, `d` (for example `dd/MM`); other characters stay as is.
`collapseSameDate`: a range with the same start and end shows one date.
`disabledDay`, `overlayMessage`, `overlayHeader`, `overlayFooter`, `overlayValidatorFn`, `overlayValidatorMessage`: see `DayOfYearPicker#11` to `DayOfYearPicker#13`.
`placeholder`: replaces the empty-field text; passed as given, not translated.
`open` + `onOpenChange` (controlled) or `defaultOpen`.
`disabled`: field and all day and month buttons disabled. `readOnly`: field has `aria-readonly` and the panel does not open.
`invalid` (or `aria-invalid`): invalid styling and `aria-invalid` on the field; `aria-invalid` wins when both are given.
`size`, `className`, `style`, `pt`: styling only.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `id`, `name`: set on the field.

builtInText.text: Default placeholder `Select date` (locale en; passed through `t()`).
Month navigation aria-labels `Previous month` and `Next month` (locale en; passed through `t()`).
Each day button has aria-label equal to its day number (for example `15`).

keyboard.text: Enter or Space on the field toggles the panel.
Day buttons and month buttons are Tab stops (disabled ones are skipped); Enter or Space activates the focused one.
Escape closes the panel.

states.text: Closed / open panel.
Day selected: `data-selected`, `aria-pressed` true; between range ends: `data-in-range`.
Day disabled: `data-disabled`, `aria-disabled`, button disabled.
Disabled, read-only, invalid picker: as in `DayOfYearPicker#33`, `DayOfYearPicker#34`.

testApi: `Spectra.findDayOfYearPicker(label)`: by `aria-label`, label text or placeholder; `Spectra.queryDayOfYearPicker(label)`: `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindDayOfYearPicker(label)`.
`getInput()`, `getIcon()`, `hasIcon()`, `getValue()` / `shouldContainValue(text)` (field text), `getPlaceholder()`.
`getPanel()`, `isOpen()`, `open()`, `close()` (with `Escape`).
`getPreviousMonthButton()`, `getNextMonthButton()`, `getMonthTitle()`, `navPreviousMonth()`, `navNextMonth()`.
`getDayButton(day | { month, day })`, `getDayButtons()`, `selectDate(day | { month, day })`: with a `{ month, day }` object the wrapper navigates to that month first.
`isDateSelected()`, `isDateInRange()`, `isDateDisabled()` with `should*` / `shouldNot*` forms; `isDateToday()` is always false (no today mark).
`getOverlayMessage()`, `hasOverlayMessage()`, `getOverlayValidatorMessage()`, `hasOverlayValidatorMessage()`.
`getHeaderSlot()`, `hasHeaderSlot()`, `getFooterSlot()`, `hasFooterSlot()`.
`focus()`, `blur()`, `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`, `element`, `getContainer()`.

Clear button: `getClearButton` (throws without a value, or while disabled or read-only), `hasClearButton` (`shouldHaveClearButton()` / `shouldNotHaveClearButton()`), `clear()`; `getAccessibleDescription()` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits).

components.name: Dialog

does.text: Opens as a centered overlay over a dimmed backdrop; the page behind is blocked and its scroll is locked.
Header shows the `header` text as a heading, with the close button (✕) at the right end of the header row.

Escape closes a plain `Dialog` with default props (`closable` true, `closeOnEscape` true; no `footer`, no extra prop needed), only the topmost one when several are open; an open menu, multi-select list or filter panel inside it closes first, the dialog on the next Escape.
One click on the backdrop closes the dialog; a double click is not special.
Clicking the close button closes it.
Pressing a toast (its close button) over an open dialog does not close the dialog.
Every dismissal (Escape, backdrop, close button) only requests close through `onOpenChange(false)`; with a controlled `open` the dialog stays open until the app sets `open` false.
Focus is trapped inside: Tab and Shift+Tab cycle within the dialog and never reach the page behind (modal: the page behind is made inert).

On close, focus returns to the element that was focused when it opened (normally the opener button), the moment closing starts; when that element is gone by then (a menu item that closed its menu), set `returnFocus` or focus falls to the page behind.
Closing: the dialog fades and scales out for about 200 ms; from the first instant it is inert, `data-state="closed"`, no longer owns Escape or focus.
Content area scrolls vertically when taller than the dialog.
Container carries `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby` pointing at the header when a header is given.

Focus on open: if focus is not already inside, it moves to the first tabbable element in the dialog (the close button when `closable`, otherwise the first control of the body or footer); with nothing tabbable the container itself takes focus. A `DialogForm` without `autoFocusFirst` therefore lands on the close button, not on its first field.

doesNot.text: No built-in footer buttons (no OK/Cancel/Save): the footer renders only when `footer` is given.
No unsaved-changes confirmation (that is DialogForm with `discardConfirm`).
Escape does nothing when `closable` is false or `closeOnEscape` is false.
Escape is not blocked by `closeDisabled`; `closeDisabled` only disables the close button.
No header row when there is no `header` and `closable` is false.
No tooltip on the close button.

defaults.text: Closed (`defaultOpen` false).
`size` `md` (max width 600 px); `placement` `center`; `role` `dialog`.
`closable` true, `closeOnOverlayClick` true, `closeOnEscape` true, `trapFocus` true, `lockScroll` true, `modal` true.
Header title is rendered as `h2` when `header` is a string, in a `div` when it is any other node.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `size`: `sm` 400 px, `md` 600 px, `lg` 800 px, `cover` fills the viewport minus 24 px each side, `full` fills the viewport with square corners.
`closeOnOverlayClick: false`: a backdrop click does nothing and the dialog stays open.
`closeOnEscape: false`: Escape does nothing.
`closable: false`: no close button and no Escape close; the backdrop still closes unless `closeOnOverlayClick` is false.
`closeDisabled: true`: close button present but disabled.
`modal: false`: no backdrop mask is rendered; a click outside still closes it when `closeOnOverlayClick` is true.
`trapFocus: false`: the whole focus manager is off: no focus move on open, no trap, no focus return on close.
`lockScroll: false`: the page behind keeps scrolling.
`placement` other than `center`: the dialog sits at that viewport edge, 24 px from it.
`footer`: a footer section with that content; `header`: the header text.
`initialFocus` / `returnFocus`: choose the element focused on open / on close.
`as="form"`: the container is a `form` and `onSubmit` receives its submit.
`role="alertdialog"`: the container role changes.

Backdrop click: default `closeOnOverlayClick` true closes a plain `Dialog` (one click, via `onOpenChange(false)`); independent of `closeOnEscape` and `closable` (`closable: false` does not block it); a click on a toast over the dialog does not count.

`Modal` (confirm/alert, built on `Dialog` with `role="alertdialog"`) fixes `closable` false, `closeOnOverlayClick` false and `closeOnEscape` false on its `Dialog`: no close button, backdrop click does nothing. Its own `closeOnEscape` prop defaults to `false`, so Escape does nothing by default; with `closeOnEscape` true Escape acts as `Cancel` (`onCancel`, then close), except while its confirm is pending (loading).

`DialogForm` (a `Dialog` with `as="form"`) keeps the `Dialog` defaults: Escape and backdrop click close it. With `discardConfirm` set and the form dirty, Escape, backdrop and the close button do not close it; they open the discard confirm (a `Modal`), and the form closes only on its confirm. A clean form closes at once; while submitting, Escape/backdrop/close are ignored (the close button is disabled).

builtInText.text: Close button `aria-label`: `Close dialog` (locale en; passed through `t()`, a translated locale shows its translation).
No other built-in text; header, footer and body come from props.

keyboard.text: Escape: closes the topmost dialog (see `Dialog#3`, `Dialog#15`, `Dialog#25`).
Tab / Shift+Tab: cycle inside the dialog while `trapFocus` is on and it is open.
Escape is ignored while focus is inside a control that owns Escape (an element under `[data-ui-owns-escape]`, e.g. a badge being edited); that control handles it first.

states.text: Open: root `data-state="open"`.
Closing: root `data-state="closed"` and `inert`, on screen about 200 ms; `isOpen()` stays `true` until it leaves the page.
Close button disabled: only with `closeDisabled`.
The dialog itself has no loading, error or selected state; the state of buttons in its footer (disabled, loading) belongs to the caller.

testApi: `Spectra.findDialog(name)`: dialog by header text or `aria-label`; closing, gone or not-yet-shown names give a bound wrapper; throws only if the name belongs to a non-dialog. `Spectra.queryDialog(name)`: `null` when missing. `Spectra.shouldNotFindDialog(name?)`, `Spectra.shouldFindDialogCount(name?, n)`: web only, count open dialogs.

`isOpen()` (`shouldBeOpen()` waits for it to show; `shouldNotBeOpen()` asserts closed, counted only once the exit animation ended). `isSettled()` (`shouldBeSettled()`) waits for the open animation to finish.
`getContainer`, `getHeader`, `getCloseButton`, `getContent`, `getFooter`, `getMask`: sub-part elements, wait for the dialog like a find.
`clickBackdrop()`: one click outside the box; closes only when `closeOnOverlayClick`.
`close()`: clicks the close button or presses Escape, then waits until closed or another modal covers it.

`hasHeader`, `hasFooter`, `hasCloseButton`, `isModal`, `hasScrollableContent`, `isCloseButtonAtEnd`, `getHeaderText`, `isLoading`, `getSize` (`shouldHaveSize('md')`), `getFooterButtonLabels` (`shouldHaveFooterButtonLabels([..])`).
`isFocusWithin` (`shouldBeFocusWithin`, `shouldNotBeFocusWithin`), `getFocusedLabel` (`shouldHaveFocusedLabel(text)`).

components.name: DialogForm

does.text: Opens as a Dialog whose container is a `form`; the fields, header and footer are the ones the app passes.
Submitting runs validation; invalid: the dialog stays open and `onError` receives the errors; valid: `onSubmit(values)` runs, then the dialog closes.
While validation or `onSubmit` runs, the close button is disabled and Escape, backdrop click and the close button do nothing (the form stays open).
A clean form (no changed field) closes at once on Escape, the close button or the backdrop (when `closeOnOverlayClick` is on).
A successful submit closes the dialog without asking about unsaved changes.
After a whole-form reset or clear, focus moves to the first editable field (disabled, read-only and hidden fields are skipped).
All Dialog behaviours apply: Escape closes only the topmost dialog, focus trap, focus returns to the opener on close, backdrop click, scroll lock, close button `Close dialog`.
A `footer` function receives `{ control, isSubmitting, clear, close }`; `close()` goes through the same unsaved-changes guard as the close button; `clear()` empties the fields and never closes.
Submit is idempotent: a second submit (double click, or Enter then click) that arrives while the first is still running is ignored, so validation and `onSubmit` run once.

With `closeOnSubmit` true the second click of a double click lands on a dialog that is already closing (inert) or is ignored, so it never submits again; with `closeOnSubmit` false or a failed validation, a click after the first submit has settled submits again.
Submit never resets the form: with `closeOnSubmit` false the values stay and the form stays dirty, so a later Escape, close button or backdrop click with `discardConfirm` set asks.
Dirty is decided per field against its initial value: typing and then restoring the initial text makes the form clean again, and Escape then closes without asking.

The close button, Escape and backdrop click all end in the same guard (`Dialog#7`): clean closes, dirty with `discardConfirm` asks, submitting is ignored; a footer Cancel button asks only when it calls `footer` `close()`, one that sets the app's own `open` to false closes without asking.

doesNot.text: No built-in Save, Submit or Cancel buttons: the footer is whatever the app passes; Enter in a field does not replace a visible submit button.
No unsaved-changes confirmation unless `discardConfirm` is set (directly or through the provider's `dialogform` default props): a dirty form then closes like any dialog.

The unsaved-changes confirmation has no built-in header or message: `Unsaved Changes` and the message text appear only when the app supplies them in `discardConfirm` (only the button labels have fallbacks, see `DialogForm#32`).
The confirmation never appears for a successful submit, a clean form, a closed form, or a form mid-submit.
Cancel on the confirmation does not discard: values the user typed stay.
Backdrop click on the confirmation does not close it, and the confirmation has no close button.
No automatic focus of the first field on open (`autoFocusFirst` false): focus lands where `Dialog` puts it (the close button, see `Dialog#48`), and returns to the opener on close.

defaults.text: `closeOnSubmit` true: the dialog closes after a successful submit.
`autoFocusFirst` false; `focusOnReset` true; `warnOnUnload` true (applies only with `discardConfirm`).
Dialog defaults: `size` `md`, closable, Escape closes, backdrop click closes, focus trap on, scroll lock on.
Starts closed unless `open` or `defaultOpen` is set.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `discardConfirm`: when the form is dirty, Escape, the close button, a backdrop click or `footer` `close()` opens a confirmation (a Modal) instead of closing; `false` turns it off for one form.

Confirmation confirm button (labelled `Leave` in the existing specs, `Confirm` by default): resets the form to its initial values and closes the dialog. Cancel button: closes the confirmation only; the dialog stays open with its values.

Confirmation texts: `header`, `message`, `confirmLabel`, `cancelLabel` come from `discardConfirm`; string values are passed through `t()`. Unset labels fall back to `Confirm` and `Cancel`; unset header or message are not shown.

Confirmation Escape: does nothing by default; it acts as Cancel only when `closeOnEscape: true` is passed inside `discardConfirm` (forwarded to the `Modal` at runtime, though not listed in the declared `DialogFormDiscardConfirm` type).

Confirmation button focus: on open the Confirm button (the Leave action) is focused; Cancel when the confirm button is hidden (`showConfirmButton: false`, forwarded at runtime, not in the declared type).
With `discardConfirm` and a dirty open form: leaving the screen (breadcrumb, sidebar, browser Back inside a router) is held and asks through the same confirmation (Leave proceeds, Cancel stays).
With `discardConfirm` and `warnOnUnload` true: reloading or closing the tab while dirty shows the browser's own prompt; `warnOnUnload: false` turns it off.
`closeOnSubmit: false`: the dialog stays open after a successful submit.
`autoFocusFirst` (or `focusFirstField`) true: the first editable control is focused when the dialog opens; `initialFocus` overrides.
`focusOnReset: false`: focus stays where it is after reset or clear.
`closeOnOverlayClick: false`: backdrop click does nothing, clean or dirty.

The submit button is the caller's: the `footer` function receives `isSubmitting` (true while `onSubmit` runs), and any disabled or loading state of the submit button is set by the caller (project convention), not by `DialogForm`.

builtInText.text: Close button `aria-label`: `Close dialog` (locale en).
Confirmation fallbacks, only when `discardConfirm` omits them: `Confirm`, `Cancel` (locale en; `t()`-translated). Default confirmation severity `danger`, size `sm`.
Nothing else built in; `Unsaved Changes`, `You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to leave?`, `Leave` in the existing specs are supplied by the spec's `discardConfirm`, not by the component.

keyboard.text: Escape: closes a clean form; asks the confirmation for a dirty form with `discardConfirm`; ignored while submitting.
Escape on an open confirmation: ignored unless `discardConfirm.closeOnEscape` is true; after a Cancel the next Escape on the form asks again.
Tab / Shift+Tab stay inside the form dialog.

states.text: Submitting (while `onSubmit` runs): close button disabled (`isCloseDisabled()` true), dismissals ignored; `footer` function gets `isSubmitting` true for the caller to use (the submit button state is the caller's).
Dirty: any field differs from its initial values; only matters with `discardConfirm`.
Confirming discard: confirmation open over the form; the form stays open underneath.
Closing: as Dialog, about 200 ms, inert, `data-state="closed"`.

testApi: `Spectra.findDialogForm(name)` / `Spectra.queryDialogForm(name)` / `Spectra.shouldNotFindDialogForm(name)`: by header text or `aria-label`; closing, gone or not-yet-shown names give a bound wrapper; a closing form is never bound.
`isOpen()` (`shouldBeOpen()` waits to show, `shouldNotBeOpen()` asserts closed), `waitForClosed()` throws if still open at the timeout.

`getContainer` / `getForm`, `getHeader`, `getCloseButton`, `getContent`, `getFooter`, `getMask`, `getSubmitButton`, `hasSubmitButton`, `hasHeader`, `hasFooter`, `hasCloseButton`, `isModal`, `getHeaderText`, `getSize` (`shouldHaveSize`).
`submit()`: submits, then waits for close; a form that stays open (no `closeOnSubmit`, failed validation) is no error; waits for field checks to end first.
`close()`: clicks the close button or presses Escape, then waits until closed or its discard confirmation covers it.
`isCloseDisabled()` (`shouldBeCloseDisabled()`, `shouldNotBeCloseDisabled()`).
The discard confirmation is read with `Spectra.findModal('<header>')` (`shouldBeOpen`, `cancel()`, `confirm()`), see the Modal suite.

components.name: Divider

does.text: Draws a full-width horizontal line with 18px vertical margin above and below (`my-4.5`).
With `orientation="vertical"` it draws a vertical line that stretches to the parent's height (needs a parent that gives it height, e.g. a flex row) with 18px horizontal margin.
With a `label` the line is split in two segments with the label between them (text style label-small, 16px padding on the line side).
A horizontal divider with a label is centred by default; `labelPosition="left"` puts the label at the left end (left line hidden), `labelPosition="right"` at the right end (right line hidden).
A vertical divider with a label keeps the label horizontal (not rotated) in the middle of the line, with a line segment above and below it.
The line is solid, dashed or dotted according to `variant`.
The line thickness follows `size`: `xs` 1px, `sm` 2px, `md` 3px, `lg` 4px, `xl` 5px, or a number as that many pixels.
A non-decorative divider is a semantic separator (`role="separator"`); a vertical one also has `aria-orientation="vertical"`, a horizontal one has no `aria-orientation` attribute.
A decorative divider has `role="none"` and `aria-hidden="true"` and is skipped by assistive technology.
A `label` can be a node (for example a Badge) and is rendered inside the label part.
`size` accepts a responsive value (different thickness per breakpoint).

doesNot.text: Does not render a label part or second line when there is no `label` (one line only); `label={null}` or `undefined` counts as no label, but an empty string `""` still renders an empty label part.
Does not rotate the label of a vertical divider and does not apply `labelPosition` there (the label stays centred).
Is not interactive: no click, hover, focus or keyboard behaviour.
Does not give itself a height: a vertical divider in a parent without height collapses.
A decorative divider does not expose `role="separator"` or `aria-orientation`, even when vertical.
Does not render `children`: content goes in `label`.

defaults.text: `orientation` `horizontal`, `variant` `solid`, `size` `xs` (1px), `decorative` `false`, `labelPosition` `center`, no label.
Line colour is the outline-variant token at 50% opacity.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `label`: shows the label between two line segments (the label can be text or a node).
`labelPosition`: `left` / `right` move the label to that end; applies only to horizontal dividers with a label.
`orientation="vertical"`: vertical line.
`variant`: `dashed` / `dotted` line style.
`size`: thicker line (see `Divider#7`).
`decorative`: `role="none"` and `aria-hidden="true"` (see `Divider#9`).
The `size` prop styles the line only; it is not put on the root element as an attribute (a numeric `size` would otherwise show as `size="6"`).
`aria-label` (or any other attribute) is put on the root element, which is how tests find a divider by name.
`className`, `pt`: styling only (`pt` sections `root`, `line`, `label`).

keyboard.text: None: a divider is not focusable.

states.text: Only the configuration states (horizontal / vertical, with / without label, semantic / decorative); no hover, focus, disabled or loading state.

testApi: `Spectra.findDivider(name)`: by `aria-label` (the root carries `data-ui-section="divider.root"`); `Spectra.queryDivider(name)`: `null` when missing.
`Spectra.findDividerAt(index)` (also on a wrapper, `card.findDividerAt(0)`): the divider at that 0-based document position, for a divider with no accessible name; web only.
`getLabelText()`: trimmed label text, `null` without a label; `shouldHaveLabelText(text)`.
`getLabelElement()`: the label span, `null` without a label.
`getLineElements()`: the first and last span (one element without label, two with); `shouldHaveLineElementsCount(n)` / `shouldNotHaveLineElementsCount(n)`.
`hasLabel()` / `shouldHaveLabel()` / `shouldNotHaveLabel()`.
`getOrientation()`: `vertical` when `aria-orientation="vertical"` or the root class contains `flex-col`, else `horizontal`; `shouldHaveOrientation('horizontal' | 'vertical')`.
`isDecorative()`: true when `role="none"` or `aria-hidden="true"`; `shouldBeDecorative()` / `shouldNotBeDecorative()`.

components.name: EmptyState

does.text: Renders a block with an optional illustration, a title, a description and an action, in that order, each only when it has content.
The title is a paragraph showing the `title` prop; the description is a paragraph showing the `description` prop.
With no `title` (omitted, `undefined` or `null`) the title shows the default `No data`.
The `illustration` is shown in a wrapper above the title: an icon or element renders as given, an object with `src` plays as a Lottie animation.
The `action` node renders in a wrapper below the description, as given.
The block is centered in its container (max width 32rem) with centered text.

DataTable uses it for an empty body: with no data it shows `No data available` (prop `emptyStateMessage`) and a search icon; when a search or filter hid every row it shows `No results found` with the description `Try adjusting your search or filter.` and a search icon.
In the DataTable filtered case the create action (`emptyStateAction`) is not shown; only `noResultsAction` is.

doesNot.text: Renders no button, link or other interactive element of its own; an action exists only when `action` is passed.
No retry button, no `Try Again`, no error styling or error icon (that is `ErrorState`, which wraps it).
No default description, no default illustration and no default action.
No `role`, `aria-live` or `aria-label` of its own; it is a plain `div` with paragraphs, not announced when it appears.
An empty-string `title` renders no title paragraph, and the default `No data` is not used.
`description` and `action` that are `undefined`, `null`, `false` or an empty string render no paragraph or wrapper.
Does not decide on its own whether data is empty or loading; the parent mounts it.

defaults.text: `size` `md`, `align` `center`.
Title `No data` (locale en, passed through `t()`); no description, no illustration, no action.
Size scale (preset): `xs` icon 32 px, `sm` 40 px, `md` 48 px, `lg` 56 px; the title grows with the size.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `title`: replaces `No data`; shown as given (not passed through `t()`).
`description`: shows the description paragraph.
`illustration`: shows the illustration wrapper (`emptystate.illustration`, icon `emptystate.icon`); `null` shows none.
`action`: shows the action wrapper (`emptystate.action`) with that node.
`align="start"`: left-aligned content, not centered.
`size` `xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg`, or a responsive object: padding, gaps, icon and text sizes.
`className`, `style`, other props: applied on the root; `pt`: styling only.

`ErrorState` (same root, `data-ui-section` `emptystate.root`): title `Something went wrong` (not translated), `message` as description, `AlertLine` icon, and a link-variant `Try Again` button with a refresh icon only when `onRetry` is passed (`retryLabel` replaces the label, passed through `t()`); a given `action` or `illustration` replaces those defaults, `action={null}` hides the retry button.

builtInText.text: Default title `No data` (locale en, passed through `t()`).
`ErrorState` only: `Something went wrong`, `Try Again` (the latter passed through `t()`).

keyboard.text: None of its own; no focusable element unless the `action` node has one.

states.text: Shown with whichever parts have content; no loading, disabled, selected or hover states.

testApi: `Spectra.findEmptyState(title)`: by the title text or an `aria-label`; `Spectra.queryEmptyState(title)`: `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindEmptyState(title)`. Matches the root (`data-ui-section` `emptystate.root`), `ErrorState` included.

`getTitleText()` (`shouldHaveTitleText(text)`), `getDescriptionText()` (`shouldHaveDescriptionText(text)`), `getTitle()`, `getDescription()`, `getIllustration()`, `getIcon()`, `getAction()`, `getActionButton()`: each fails naming the part when it is not rendered.

`hasTitle()`, `hasDescription()` (`shouldHaveDescription()`), `hasIllustration()`, `hasIcon()`, `hasAction()`, `hasActionButton()`; `clickAction()`; `getIllustrationSize()` (`shouldHaveIllustrationSize({ width })`).

components.name: ExportButton

does.text: Renders one outlined success-coloured icon button with a download icon; hovering shows the tooltip `Download`.
With neither `format` nor `formatOptions` (single-table path), clicking opens a format menu instead of downloading.
Menu entries follow the order of `formatOptions`; default entries are `Download as XLSX` then `Download as CSV`.
Choosing an entry closes the menu and starts the export in that format.
While an export runs, the button area shows a loading overlay with `Downloading...` and a polite live region announces it; it returns to normal when the export ends or fails.
A failed export calls `onError(error)`, or logs `[ExportButton] export failed:` to the console when `onError` is absent; no toast or message is rendered.
`fileName` is saved as written with the extension added (`.xlsx`, `.csv`, `.pdf`); characters `\ / : * ? " < > |` and control characters become `-`, surrounding spaces and trailing dots are dropped.

The file has the same columns as the table shows: a column hidden through Column Visibility is left out, the rest follow the order the user arranged; columns with `visible: false` or `excluded` are never exported; the header text is `exportHeader`, else `header`, else `-`.
Cell values come from the column's `exportValue(row)` when set, else the raw `row[field]`; date and number presets are formatted as the table does.
Rows by `scope`: `all` as in ExportButton#15, `page` the rows of the current page, `selected` the view's selected rows.
`fileName` is a required prop; when it is left out anyway, a single-table export is saved as `export` plus the extension.
CSV: UTF-8 with a BOM, rows joined by CRLF, cells with a comma, quote or line break quoted; a cell text starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` (not a plain number, not a lone `-`) is prefixed with `'`.

doesNot.text: No disabled prop: the button is never disabled by the component, including while downloading and with an empty table (0 rows).

With 0 rows and scope `all`/`page`, a click still exports: no empty-table guard or message in the component, the payload resolver or the CSV/Excel/PDF writers; the file has the headers of the `columns` prop (the columns not hidden through Column Visibility) and no rows; with no `columns` prop the headers come from the first row, so with 0 rows the file has no headers either; the CSV is then the header line only. Only `scope="selected"` with no selection is skipped (ExportButton#32).
No visible text label unless `label` is set (icon only).
No menu when `format` is set, or on the `tables` / `dataConfigs` paths (without `formatOptions`); the click exports directly.
`tables` and `dataConfigs` paths always write an Excel workbook, whatever the format.
Without `dataView`, `tables`, `dataConfigs` or `serverExport`, a click downloads nothing (dev console errors only).
`print` produces no file download.
No success message is shown after an export.

defaults.text: `scope` is `all`: the rows come from `fetchAll` (the prop, else the view's own `fetchAll`) under the current filter, search and sort; with neither, the rows currently loaded in the view; `tableName` is `datatable`.
Direct export with no `format` falls back to Excel.
Trigger `aria-label` is `Download` when no `label`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `label`: visible button text; also the accessible name (the aria-label is dropped).
`format` (`excel` | `csv` | `pdf` | `print`): the click exports directly in that format, no menu.
`formatOptions`: the menu offers exactly those formats in that order; an empty array gives no menu and a direct export.

`serverExport`: choosing Excel calls `serverExport('xlsx')`, CSV calls `serverExport('csv')`; the returned blob is saved as the result `fileName` or `<fileName>.xlsx|csv`; PDF and print still run locally; the menu offers Excel and CSV only unless `formatOptions` names others.
`scope` (`all` | `page` | `selected`) and `fetchAll`: choose the exported rows (single-table path).
`tables` (refs) / `dataConfigs`: multi-sheet Excel workbook; `additionalTextBelowTable` adds text below.
`downloadingMessage`, `downloadTooltip`, `downloadIconAriaLabel`, `excelMenuLabel`, `csvMenuLabel`, `pdfMenuLabel`, `printMenuLabel`: override the built-in texts.
`columns` (via the hook): limits the exported columns.

builtInText.text: Tooltip `Download`; trigger aria-label `Download` (icon-only).
Menu labels: `Download as XLSX`, `Download as CSV`, `Download as PDF`, `Print` (English; not translated through locale constants).
Progress text: `Downloading...`.

keyboard.text: The trigger is a native button: Enter or Space activates it (opens the menu or exports); the component adds no key handling of its own.

states.text: Format-menu mode: trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` true or false; absent in direct mode.
Busy (single-table, multi-table or server export): overlay and live region text `Downloading...`; empty live region otherwise.
`scope="selected"` with nothing selected: nothing is exported and no file downloads; the export is skipped without a message.

testApi: Finders: `Spectra.findExportButton(name)` and `queryExportButton(name)`; the name is the `label`, or `Download` for the icon-only button.
Parts: `getContainer`, `getButton`, `getLabel`.

Menu: `hasFormatMenu`, `isMenuOpen`, `openMenu` (throws when no menu), `getFormatOptions` (empty when closed), `selectFormat(label)` (opens the menu, starts a download; throws when no menu or no such entry).
Direct: `download` (throws when the button opens a menu).
State: `isDownloading`; assertions `shouldHaveFormatMenu`, `shouldContainFormatOptions`, `shouldBeDownloading`.
Starting a download writes a file: tests suppress the download first (README recipe).

components.name: Field

does.text: Stacks, top to bottom: the label row, the control, then the error or the helper text.
Shows `label` above the control as a real `<label>` tied to the control, so the control's accessible name is the label text.
A required field shows `*` after the label, and its control (when it receives `fieldProps`) carries `aria-required="true"`.
A field with `name` inside a Form binds to the form: its value, touched and dirty state and its error resolve from the form state.
`required` adds a rule that rejects an empty value (empty or whitespace text, no value, empty list) with `Field is required`, unless `validators` already has its own Required rule.

The error text appears under the control only after validation fails (the rule's own trigger; the default Required rule runs when the form is submitted) and the control is marked `aria-invalid="true"`.
When an error shows, it replaces the helper text.
The error text is announced as an alert and the control's `aria-describedby` points at it; the helper text is linked the same way while shown.
An explicit `error` wins over the error from the form state; an explicit `invalid` marks the control invalid without any message.
While an async validator runs, its `pendingMessage` shows under the control in place of the helper text and the error.
While the form is submitting, a control that receives `fieldProps` is disabled.
A string `info` shows an information icon after the label; hovering or focusing it (it takes Tab focus, its accessible name is the info text) opens a tooltip with the text.
A non-string `info` node is shown as is after the label.
A function child receives `{ fieldProps, fieldState, fieldActions }`; spreading `fieldProps` onto the control wires value, change, blur, id, aria attributes and invalid.
On a failing submit, focus moves to the first invalid field (`focusOnError` default on).
A control that reads the field label (such as TreeSelect) takes the label as its accessible name even without `fieldProps`.

doesNot.text: Does not bind a bare element child: without a function child spreading `fieldProps`, the field neither validates nor submits that control.
Does not show the helper text while an error or a pending message shows.
Does not show an error before validation: no error on first render, and the default Required rule does not complain while the user types.
Does not show `*` and the optional mark together: the optional mark shows only when the field is not required.
Does not dim the label, marks or helper text when the form is submitting or the control is disabled; only the control is disabled.
Does not render the label row when `label` is empty, unless `preserveLabelLayout` is set.
Does not pass `size` to the control; set the same size on both.
Does not render any control of its own.

defaults.text: `required` false, `requiredMark` `*`, `invalid` false, `size` `xs`.
No optional mark, no info icon, no helper text.
`preserveOnUnmount` false: the field is unregistered when it unmounts and its value leaves the form payload.
`focusOnError` true.
`preserveLabelLayout` false: a field without label has no label row.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `label`: the label text; a string or any node.
`required`: the `*` mark, the required rule and `aria-required`.
`requiredMark`: replaces `*`.
`optionalMark` (for a field that is not required): shows that node after the label, for example `(optional)`.
`info`: the information icon described above.
`helperText`: hint under the control while there is no error and no pending check.
`error`: forces that message under the control and the invalid state.
`invalid`: marks the control invalid.
`validators`, `sanitizers`: rules and text clean-up (for example Trim, applied on blur and at submit).
`asyncValidator`: debounced check while typing; its `pendingMessage` shows while it runs and its message shows as the error.
`preserveLabelLayout`: with no label, an invisible placeholder keeps the row height so controls in a row stay aligned.
`preserveOnUnmount`: keeps the value when the field unmounts.
`size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md` or `lg` sets label and helper text size and spacing.
`className`, `pt`: styling only.

builtInText.text: Required message from `required`: `Field is required` (not localized).
Required mark: `*`.
No default optional mark, helper, info or pending text.

keyboard.text: No key handling of its own; the info icon is a Tab stop and its tooltip opens on focus.

states.text: Idle: label, control, helper text if any.
Invalid: error text in place of the helper text, control `aria-invalid`.
Pending: pending message shows while an async validator runs, helper and error hidden.
Submitting: the control is disabled.
Disabled, read-only: belong to the control; the field has no own prop for them.

testApi: `Spectra.findField(label)`: by the label text; `Spectra.queryField(label)`: `null` when missing.
`getContainer()`, `getControl()`, `getContent()`, `getInput()`.

`getLabelText()`, `getHelperText()`, `getErrorText()`, `getHelperElement()`, `getErrorElement()`, `getRequiredMarkText()`, `getOptionalMarkText()`, `getInfoText()`, `getInfoIcon()` (its Tooltip wrapper), `getSeverity()`.
`hasHelperText()`, `hasError()`, `isChecking()` (`shouldNotBeChecking()`), `hasRequiredMark()`, `hasOptionalMark()`, `hasInfo()`.
`getValue()`, `setValue(value)`, `clearValue()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.
`isRequired()`, `isDisabled()`, `isInvalid()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isFocused()`; `should*` for each reader.

components.name: FileUpload

does.text: Default (field) mode shows a text field with a `Browse` block at its start; clicking the block or the field opens the system file dialog.
The field text is read-only and shows the chosen file name; multiple files show names joined by `, `.
Choosing files runs validation: files that are too large or of the wrong type are dropped, the rest are kept.
Single mode: `onChange` receives the first valid file; selecting again replaces it.
Multiple mode: `onChange` receives the existing files plus the new valid ones.
A rejected file is reported only through `onReject` as `{ file, errors }` where `errors` holds `file-too-large`, `file-invalid-type`, `too-many-files`; the user sees no message.
The clear button (shown while a file is set, not read-only) empties the value (`onChange(null)`, or `[]` in multiple mode) and does not open the dialog.
The native file input is reset after each choice, so the same file can be chosen again.

doesNot.text: No rejection message, toast or error text is rendered for a file of the wrong type (`accept`), over `maxFileSize` or beyond `maxFiles`; the rejected file simply does not appear.
No upload, progress bar or percentage exists; the component only hands `File` objects to `onChange`.
No per-file remove button; the only removal is the clear-all button.
The component does not hold its own value: without a `value` prop the chosen file is not displayed.
Drag and drop works only in `dropzone` mode; the default field mode has no drop handling.
No clear button in dropzone mode.
Single mode never keeps more than one file; extra valid dropped or chosen files are ignored without a report (only `maxFiles` can still report the extras as `too-many-files`).
A file that fails both size and type gets one rejection with both errors.
Multiple mode does not remove duplicates: choosing or dropping the same file again appends it again.
In dropzone mode a click or drop on a `disabled` or `readOnly` dropzone does nothing and drag-over shows no highlight; only `disabled` sets `aria-disabled` on the dropzone.
With `trigger` the component renders no field, no clear button and no file name; showing the value and clearing it are up to the trigger content.

defaults.text: `dropzone`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `invalid`, `multiple` are all `false`.
Placeholder is `Select File`; start block label is `Browse`.
No `accept`, `maxFileSize`, `maxFiles` limits.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `accept`: files not matching are rejected with `file-invalid-type`. Tokens: `.ext` matches the name suffix (case-insensitive), `type/*` matches the MIME prefix, other tokens match the MIME exactly.
`maxFileSize` (bytes): files larger are rejected with `file-too-large`.
`maxFiles`: valid files beyond `maxFiles` minus current count (current count only in multiple mode) are rejected with `too-many-files`; earlier ones are kept.
`dropzone`: shows a drop area (role button, tab stop) instead of the field; drops and clicks add files; single mode takes only the first dropped file.
`dropzone` shows a hint line built from the configured limits (see Built-in text); with none configured the hint is `or click to browse`.
`trigger` (non-dropzone): replaces the field with the given content; the picker opens via `open()` of the trigger context.
`dropzonePlaceholder`: replaces the default dropzone content.
`chooseLabel` replaces `Browse`; `placeholder` replaces `Select File`.
`onReject`: called only when at least one file is rejected.
`multiple`: sets the native `multiple` on the file input so the system dialog allows several files; without it the dialog allows one.

builtInText.text: Field: placeholder `Select File`, start block `Browse`, clear button aria-label `Clear selection` (default locale en).
Field aria-label with no file: `Browse, Select File`; with a file: `Browse, selected: <file names>` (label and placeholder follow `chooseLabel` / `placeholder`).
Dropzone title: no file and limits set `Drag and drop files here, or click to browse`; no file, no limits `Drag and drop files here`; with files, the file names joined by `, `.
Dropzone description: no file `or click to browse` when no limits; with a file `Drag & drop or click to replace file`, followed by ` • ` and the limits if any.

Limits text parts joined by ` • `: `Supports {formats}`, `Max {size} per file`, `Up to 1 file` / `Up to {count} files`. Formats: `image/*` becomes `SVG, PNG, JPG, GIF`; `video/*` `MP4, MOV, AVI`; `audio/*` `MP3, WAV, AAC`; `.pdf` becomes `PDF` (any `.ext` becomes its upper-case extension); `application/pdf` `PDF`; `image/jpeg` `JPG`, `image/png` `PNG`, `image/webp` `WEBP`; deduped, comma-joined. Size formatted like `5MB`, `512KB` (1024-based, one decimal).

keyboard.text: Dropzone: Enter or Space opens the file dialog (ignored when disabled or read-only).
Field text input: Enter or Space opens the file dialog.

states.text: `disabled`: field and hidden input disabled, clicks and drops ignored, dropzone `aria-disabled` and not tabbable.
`readOnly`: clicks, keys and drops ignored; no clear button in field mode.
`invalid`: `aria-invalid` on field and hidden input, group styled invalid.

Dragging files over the dropzone turns its border and tint primary (accept); with `accept` set and a dragged item whose MIME type does not match, it turns danger instead (reject, no text); it returns to normal on drag leave or drop. An `accept` made of `.ext` tokens only never matches while dragging (the name is not known yet), so the zone shows reject for every drag, but the drop itself is validated by file name and a matching file is kept.

testApi: Finders: `Spectra.findFileUpload(label)` waits; `Spectra.queryFileUpload(label)` returns `null` when absent.
Parts: `getContainer`, `getFileInput` and `getHiddenInput` (native file input; `.upload(path)` supported), `getInputGroup`, `getTextInput`, `getDropzone`, `getDropzonePlaceholder`, `getClearButton`.
Actions: `dropFiles(paths)` (dropzone mode; a single-mode dropzone takes the first only).
Readers: `getValue` (shown file names), `hasClearButton`, `hasDropzone`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `isInvalid`; assertions `shouldHaveValue`, `shouldHaveClearButton`.

components.name: FilterContainer

does.text: The panel is on the page only while the table's filter panel is open (toggled by a FilterToggleButton or `toggleFilterPanel`); closed, it leaves the page after its exit animation and its fields, Apply and Clear Field cannot be found.
Values entered in fields are a DRAFT; the table, its rows and the filter dot do not change until Apply.
Apply commits all draft values as the table's filter model, returns the table to page 1 and fires `onApply(model)`; the panel stays open.
Fields left empty (empty text, no selection, empty range, no date) are dropped on Apply and do not narrow the result; Apply with every field empty removes all applied filters.
Clear Field empties every draft field only; the table keeps its applied filter until Apply is pressed, and the panel stays open.
Closing the panel without Apply discards the draft; reopening shows the last applied filters, as the table applies them.
An applied filter narrows the table's total, so a DataTable paginator's page count and `Showing X to Y of Z` follow it; a filter matching nothing shows the no-results empty state `No results found`.
After a reload or restore, the panel shows the persisted applied filters in its fields, and an immediate Apply re-commits them.
An open panel follows filters changed from outside (a screen calling `setFilter`, another writer): fields the user has not edited show the new applied value; an edited field keeps its draft.
Text field filters by case-insensitive, accent-insensitive substring (`contains`).
Select field filters rows whose value equals the chosen option (compared as text).

Multiselect field filters rows whose value is any of the chosen options; its list has a search input and no Select all; chips show the choices, overflow chips collapse to a `+N more` style summary when there is no room.
Number range field filters inclusively between min and max; an empty bound is open (min only = `>= min`, max only = `<= max`).
Date field is a range picker; without `showTime` the applied range is whole days, from 00:00:00.000 of the start day to 23:59:59.999 of the end day.
Tree field is a checkbox tree; the checked node keys filter rows whose value is one of them.
A select or multiselect with `fetchOptionFn` reloads its options each time its list is opened (a newly added option appears); the options already loaded stay shown meanwhile.
A selected multiselect value that a reloaded list no longer offers stays listed, under its last seen label, so it can be deselected.
Changing a field that other fields `dependsOn` empties those dependent fields, their draft values and their loaded options.
Fields are laid out in a grid of 4 per row; the Clear Field / Apply buttons sit in the last column of the last row.
Escape closes the panel when it is the topmost layer; an open select list or dialog above it takes Escape first.
The form is a `role="search"` landmark named `Filter data`.
Clear Field empties every typed text, selection, multiselect chip, number bound and date in the fields.
The panel is a `form` whose submit event runs Apply; both buttons are `type="button"`, so only native implicit submission (Enter inside a lone text input) can trigger it.

doesNot.text: No Reset button, no Close button and no applied-filter badges or counts in the panel; the only applied-filter signal is the dot on FilterToggleButton.
Apply does not close the panel; Clear Field does not apply and does not close it.
Clear Field does not touch the table's applied filter, the search term, sort or page.
No live filtering; no value reaches the table before Apply.
It never filters rows itself; it writes the filter model, the table (client) or the server filters.
No Select all in a multiselect field.
A field renders no label unless its `header` is set.
A closed panel is removed from the DOM once its exit animation (about 200 ms) ends; it is not hidden with `display:none`, so its fields, `Clear Field` and `Apply` cannot be found while closed.
A DataTable does not render a FilterContainer; the page places it and pairs it with the same `dataView`.
Apply does not reset the search term (SearchButton), only the page (to 1).
Closing the panel (toggle button or Escape, both run the same close) does not apply the draft: the table and its applied filters stay as they were.

defaults.text: Panel closed until opened.
`fieldsPerRow` 4; `tableName` `datatable`.
Match mode by field type: text `contains`, select `equals`, multiselect `in`, number range `between`, date `dateBetween`, tree `in`.
The panel state and applied filters persist with the table's state (`statePersistence`, default `'sessionStorage'`).
Button order: `Clear Field`, then `Apply` (Apply is the green/success button).
English text only; labels are component props, not locale constants.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `fields` decides which fields exist (types `text`, `select`, `multiselect`, `rangenumber`, `date`, `tree`); with no `fields` and no `children` the panel shows only the two buttons.
`field.visible: false` omits that field.
`field.header` renders the label above the control; wrappers address fields by this text.
`children(api)` render-prop adds custom controls (`setValue` / `getValue` / `clearValue` / `apply` / `clear`); they share the same draft and are remounted by Clear Field.
`syncFieldsWithColumns` hides a field whose bound column is hidden and removes that column's applied filter from the table; requires `dataView`.
`static` takes select/multiselect options from the table's loaded rows (unique values) instead of `fetchOptionFn`, loaded when the field's list is first opened; `fetchOnMount` is skipped.
`fetchOptionFn` loads options on open; `fetchOnMount: true` also loads them when the panel mounts (non-static).
`fetchOptionFn` rejecting leaves the field with no options and logs to the console.

Date field `selectionMode: 'single'` picks one day (applied as that whole day); `view: 'month'` picks whole months (first day 00:00 to last day 23:59:59.999, format `MMM yyyy`); `showTime` keeps the picked times instead of whole days.
`timezone` sets the zone whose midnight starts and ends the whole-day range (otherwise the browser's).
`fieldsPerRow` sets the number of grid columns.
`onApply(model)` fires on Apply with `{ [field]: { value, matchMode } }`.
`clearFieldLabel`, `applyLabel`, `filterPanelAriaLabel` rename the buttons and the panel name.
Without `dataView` nothing opens or applies (the panel never shows); `syncFieldsWithColumns` without it logs a dev console error.

builtInText.text: `Filter data` (panel aria-label).
`Clear Field` (button label).
`Apply` (button label).

keyboard.text: Escape closes the topmost open panel; the draft is discarded.
Buttons are native: Tab to focus, Enter or Space to activate.

states.text: Closed (not on the page) / open.
Draft differs from applied (table unchanged) / draft applied.
Field loading while its options are being fetched.
Empty applied model (no dot) / non-empty (dot on the toggle).

testApi: `Spectra.findFilterContainer(name)` / `queryFilterContainer(name)`: by `filterPanelAriaLabel` (default `Filter data`); finds only while the panel is open; `find*` throws when absent, `query*` returns `null`.
`isOpen()`: shouldBeOpen / shouldNotBeOpen.
`getFieldHeaders()`: shouldHaveFieldHeaders([...]) / shouldContainFieldHeaders; `hasField(header)`: shouldHaveField(header); `getField(header)`: the field wrapper element.
`getButtonLabels()`: shouldHaveButtonLabels([...]) (visible buttons in DOM order).
`setTextValue(header, value)` / `getTextValue(header)`: shouldHaveTextValue(value, header).
`selectOption(header, label)`: select and multiselect; opens the field's own list, scrolls a long list to the option, closes a multiselect list.
`getMultiSelect(header)`, `getDatePicker(header)`, `getRangeNumberInput(header)`: the field's control wrappers with their own readers and should*.
`setRange(header, min, max)`: sets both bounds and blurs (each clamped to its range).
`setDate(header, day)` (single), `setDateRange(header, start, end)`, `setMonthRange(header, start, end)`: a `Date` navigates to its month first.
`selectTreeNodes(header, labels)`: opens the dialog, checks the visible nodes, commits.
`apply(applyLabel?)`: clicks Apply; returns once the table shows the result.
`clearFields(clearLabel?)`: clicks Clear Field; table unchanged until `apply()`.
Wrappers resolve the panel again by name on each call, so they follow a reopened panel.

components.name: FilterToggleButton

does.text: Shows an icon-only button with a funnel icon; closed, the button is outlined with an outline funnel.
Clicking it opens the paired filter panel; the button turns filled with a filled funnel. Clicking again closes the panel and restores the outline look.
The open/closed state is the table's filter-panel state: opening or closing the panel from anywhere else (another toggle, Escape in the panel, a programmatic call) updates this button.
A small dot appears on the button's corner while at least one filter is applied (non-empty value), with the panel open or closed.
The dot reflects applied filters only; a value typed in the panel but not yet applied does not show it.
An applied range with only a minimum or only a maximum counts as applied (dot shown).
Clearing every field and applying removes the dot.
Hovering or focusing the button shows the tooltip `Filter` after a 300 ms open delay.
The panel is on the page only while open; the button's `aria-controls` names the panel id even while the panel is absent.

doesNot.text: No count or number of applied filters, only the dot.
The dot is aria-hidden and ignores clicks; it carries no text.
The accessible name does not change between open and closed (`Toggle filter` both ways).
It does not apply, clear or hold any filter value; it only shows or hides the panel.
No `active`/`defaultActive` prop; the pressed look cannot be forced from props when `dataView` is passed.
A DataTable does not render this button; the page places it and pairs it with the same `dataView`.

defaults.text: Panel starts closed (`isFilterPanelOpen` false) unless seeded or restored.
The open/closed state persists with the table's state (`statePersistence`, default `'sessionStorage'`) and survives a same-tab reload.
`tableName` defaults to `datatable`.
English text only; labels are component props, not locale constants.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `toggleLabel` renames the button's accessible name (default `Toggle filter`).
`filterTooltip` renames the tooltip (default `Filter`); `label` / `activeLabel` rename the inner icon aria-labels (defaults `Filter` / `Filter active`).
`onShowFilter(show)` fires on each click with the new state.
Without `dataView` the button flips on local state only, never reveals a panel, and logs a dev console error; the dot never shows.
`tableName` sets `aria-controls` to `filter-panel-<tableName>`; it must equal the panel's `tableName`.

builtInText.text: `Toggle filter` (button aria-label).
`Filter` (tooltip; icon aria-label while closed).
`Filter active` (icon aria-label while open).

keyboard.text: Native button: Tab to focus, Enter or Space toggles.

states.text: Closed: `aria-expanded="false"`, outlined.
Open: `aria-expanded="true"`, filled.
Dot present / absent, independent of open or closed.

testApi: `Spectra.findFilterToggleButton(name)` / `queryFilterToggleButton(name)`: by `toggleLabel` (default `Toggle filter`); `find*` throws when absent, `query*` returns `null`.
`isActive()`: shouldBeActive / shouldNotBeActive (panel open, from `aria-expanded`).
`hasFilterIndicator()`: shouldHaveFilterIndicator / shouldNotHaveFilterIndicator (the dot).
`toggle()`: clicks and waits for `aria-expanded` to flip; throws if it does not.
`open()` / `close()`: idempotent; wait for the target state.
`getFilterPanel()`: the FilterContainer wrapper through `aria-controls`, no name needed; while collapsed it reads not open (`shouldNotBeOpen()`) and follows the panel once opened.
`getButton()`, `getContainer()`: the button and the root wrapper elements.

components.name: Form

does.text: Renders a native `<form>` around its children and makes its `control` available to every Field inside, however deep.
Submitting (a submit button, or Enter in a text field) never reloads the page.
On submit every registered Field is validated (all rules run, whatever their own trigger), and the errors then show under their fields.
When every Field is valid, `onSubmit` is called once with the values as a plain object (sanitizers such as Trim already applied; a file field holds its `File`).
When any Field is invalid, `onSubmit` is not called and `onError` receives the map of field name to error message.
While `onSubmit` is running (an async handler is awaited), the form counts as submitting: a second submit is ignored and Fields' controls that receive `fieldProps` are disabled.
If an async check on a Field is still running at submit, nothing is submitted; fields with a failing rule show their error.
After `control.reset()` or `control.clear()` (for example a Reset to Default button the caller renders), focus moves to the first editable field: disabled, read-only and hidden fields are skipped.

With `discardConfirm`, leaving the screen in the app (a link, breadcrumb, sidebar or browser Back) while the form is dirty is held and a confirm dialog asks; Leave resets the form and goes on, Cancel stays with the typed values.
With `discardConfirm`, a reload or tab close of a dirty form asks the browser's own confirmation.
Fields that unmount are unregistered, so their values leave the submitted payload.
Passes native form attributes (`id`, `aria-label`, `className`, `noValidate`, `data-*`) to the `<form>`.

doesNot.text: Does not render layout, spacing, a title, buttons or any text of its own.
Does not call `onSubmit` for an invalid form.
Does not validate while the user types; each rule's own trigger decides, and submit runs all.
Does not hold navigation or ask about reload for a clean form, a form that is submitting, or without `discardConfirm`.
Does not hold a save that navigates away from inside `onSubmit`.
Does not move focus after a reset when `focusOnReset` is false.
Does not bind a control that is not inside a Field with `fieldProps` spread on it.
Does not render the dirty-confirm dialog without `discardConfirm`.

defaults.text: `autoFocusFirst` false: nothing is focused on mount.
`focusOnReset` true.
`submitOnEnter` true: Enter in a text field submits.
`warnOnUnload` true, effective only with `discardConfirm`.
No `discardConfirm`: leaving a dirty form is never held.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `autoFocusFirst`: on mount, focus goes once to the first visible, enabled, editable control.

`submitOnEnter: false`: Enter in a text input does nothing; the form submits only from its submit button; Enter in a textarea, on a button, or in a control's own Enter handling (Select list, autocomplete) is untouched.
`focusOnReset: false`: a reset leaves focus where it is.
`discardConfirm`: the leave-confirm dialog (header, message, labels from the given object; string copy translated); the dialog sits beside the form, so its buttons never submit it.
`warnOnUnload: false`: reload of a dirty form is not asked (only with `discardConfirm`).
`onError`: called with the error map when submit finds errors.

builtInText.text: Form has no built-in text; the confirm dialog texts come from `discardConfirm` (for example set once in the provider's `form` defaults), and the required-field error is `Field is required` from Field.

keyboard.text: Enter in a text input submits the form (unless `submitOnEnter` is false); Enter on a button activates that button only.
Tab order is the DOM order of the controls.

states.text: Idle: nothing shown beyond the fields.
Submitting: from the start of submit until `onSubmit` settles; controls spreading `fieldProps` are disabled.
Dirty (with `discardConfirm`): leaving asks; clean: leaving is free.
Disabled, read-only, invalid: none at form level; each Field or control owns them (the wrapper readers report them from the form element).

testApi: `Spectra.findForm(label)`: by the form's accessible name; `Spectra.queryForm(label)`: `null` when missing.
`getContainer()`, `getSubmitButton(label?)`, `getResetButton(label?)`, `hasSubmitButton(label?)`, `hasResetButton(label?)`.
`submitForm(label?)` clicks the submit button; `submitWithEnter()` presses Enter in the focused field; `resetForm(label?)` clicks the reset button.
`isDisabled()`, `isInvalid()`, `isReadOnly()`; `should*` for each reader.

components.name: Gallery
