does.text: Shows the active image of the `value` array large, with a thumbnail strip below it; the first item is active at start.
Renders nothing at all when `value` is missing or empty.
Inline (default, no `fullScreen`) it sits in the page as a region of 640 x 480 px (or `width` x `height`) and is always visible; it has no close button.
With `fullScreen` nothing is shown until opened with the imperative handle `show()`; it then opens as a modal dialog over the whole page on a dark backdrop, with a close button at the top right.
The fullscreen dialog closes with the close button, `hide()`, or Escape; the page behind cannot scroll while it is open and keyboard focus stays inside it.
Clicking a thumbnail makes that item the active one; the active thumbnail is full opacity with a ring, the others are dimmed, and the strip scrolls to centre the active one.
With more than one item, a previous and a next button sit on the left and right of the large image; clicking moves one item.
Without `loop`, previous is disabled on the first item and next is disabled on the last; with `loop`, next on the last goes to the first and previous on the first goes to the last.
Each thumbnail is a button named `<n> / <total>` (e.g. `2 / 5`); the active one has `aria-current="true"`.
Only the active thumbnail is in the Tab order; Tab reaches the strip once.
`onItemChange` fires with `{ index, item }` on every change of the active item (thumbnail click, buttons, keys, autoplay, handle `next`/`prev`/`setActiveIndex`).
`onShow` fires when the fullscreen dialog opens and `onHide` after it has closed (after its 150 ms fade); neither fires for the inline gallery.
`onItemError` fires with `{ index, item }` when the shown item's image fails to load; the gallery stays as it is.
The imperative handle offers `show`, `hide`, `next`, `prev`, `setActiveIndex(i)` (ignored when out of range), `startSlideShow`, `stopSlideShow`, `isAutoPlayActive`, `getElement`.
The content area carries `aria-live="polite"`, or `aria-live="off"` when the `autoPlay` prop is set.

doesNot.text: Does not zoom, rotate or pan the image.
Does not close on Escape in the inline gallery, and not in fullscreen when `closeOnEscape` is `false`.
Does not show previous and next buttons when there are 0 or 1 items.
Does not go past the ends without `loop`: next on the last and previous on the first do nothing (the buttons are disabled).
Does not move the active item with the Left/Right arrow keys unless focus is on a thumbnail; there is no arrow handling on the large image itself.
Does not show a source given as a `Blob` or one needing authentication with the default renderers (the image has no `src`); supply `item`/`thumbnail` render functions for those.
Does not render thumbnails when `showThumbnails` is `false`.
Does not render the dialog while closed (fullscreen); it is removed from the page after the close fade.
Does not change the active item through `activeIndex` alone when controlled: without the parent updating `activeIndex` from `onItemChange` the shown item does not move.

defaults.text: `activeIndex` 0, `autoPlay` `false`, `autoPlayInterval` 3000 ms, `loop` `false`, `showThumbnails` `true`, `fullScreen` `false`, `closeOnEscape` `true`, `baseZIndex` 0 (the fullscreen dialog uses z-index 1100 when 0).
Default `aria-label` `Gallery` (locale en) on the region (and on the fullscreen dialog).
The image is shown contained (whole image visible, no crop); thumbnails are cropped to a square 64 px (80 px from the small breakpoint up).

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `autoPlay`: advances to the next item every `autoPlayInterval` ms; without `loop` it stops on the last item, with `loop` it wraps to the first and keeps going.
`autoPlayInterval`: ms between automatic steps.
`loop`: see `Gallery#8`.
`activeIndex`: controlled active item (see `Gallery#24`); uncontrolled when omitted.

`item` / `thumbnail`: render function replacing the inner content of the large slide / each thumbnail; a falsy return falls back to the default ``; the outer elements and their focus and click behaviour stay.
`width` / `height` (px): size of the region; without them 640 x 480 inline, full viewport when fullscreen.
`closeAriaLabel` (default `Close`), `previousAriaLabel` (default `Previous`), `nextAriaLabel` (default `Next`): labels of those buttons, locale en.
`aria-label`: replaces `Gallery` as the name of the region and the dialog.
`className`, `style`, `id`, other div attributes go to the region; `pt` is styling only.

builtInText.text: `Gallery` (region and dialog name), `Close`, `Previous`, `Next` (locale en, each replaceable by its prop); thumbnails `<n> / <total>`; no other visible text.

keyboard.text: On a focused thumbnail: ArrowRight or ArrowDown activates the next item, ArrowLeft or ArrowUp the previous, wrapping around at both ends even without `loop`; Home activates the first, End the last; Enter or Space activates the focused one.
Focus follows the newly active thumbnail when focus was inside the strip.
Escape closes the fullscreen dialog (`closeOnEscape`).
The previous/next/close buttons are native buttons: Tab focuses them, Enter or Space presses them.

states.text: Active item, inactive items: thumbnail ring and full opacity versus dimmed.
At the first/last item without `loop`: previous/next disabled at 30 % opacity with a not-allowed cursor.
Fullscreen closed (nothing in the page) and open (dialog); inline always open.
Autoplay running or stopped (stops at the last item without `loop`); the wrapper reads it from `aria-live`, which follows the `autoPlay` prop, so it stays `off` after a no-loop run has stopped.
Clicking the dark backdrop outside the content closes the fullscreen dialog.
Autoplay with one item and `loop` keeps re-selecting item 0 every interval (and keeps calling `onItemChange`).

testApi: `Spectra.findGallery(label)` / `queryGallery(label)` (`null` when missing): by `aria-label` (default `Gallery`); matches the inline root or the fullscreen dialog mask.
`isAutoPlayActive()` (reads `aria-live="off"` of the content; follows the `autoPlay` prop), `shouldBeAutoPlayActive`-style assertions via the wrapper.
`hide()` clicks the close button; `next()` / `prev()` click the buttons; `setActiveIndex(i)` / `clickThumbnail(i)` click that thumbnail (throws when out of range).
`getActiveIndex()` (index of the thumbnail with `aria-current="true"`; 0 when there are no thumbnails), `getThumbnails()`, `getActiveThumbnail()`, `getThumbnailCount()`.
`navigateRight/Left/Up/Down()` press the arrow key on the current focus (so they only act on a focused thumbnail).
`getCloseButton()`, `getPreviousButton()`, `getNextButton()`: by the labels `Close`, `Previous`, `Next` (not by custom labels).
Opening the fullscreen gallery has no wrapper method; the page's own trigger (imperative `show()`) opens it.

components.name: GuidedTour

does.text: While open it shows one step at a time: a card (`role="dialog"`, named by the step title) anchored to the step's target, with the progress text, the title, the description, and a footer with `Skip`, `Back` (not on the first step) and `Next` (`Done` on the last).
The page is dimmed everywhere except a ring (the spotlight) around the target; the spotlight follows the target while the page scrolls, resizes or lays out late.
Each step scrolls its target into view (smooth, centred) and the card takes keyboard focus when the step shows.
`Next` goes to the next step; `Back` goes to the previous; the progress reads `Step <n> of <total>`.
`Done` on the last step closes the tour as completed: `onComplete` is called, `onOpenChange(false, 'complete')`.
`Skip`, Escape and a click on the dimmed page close the tour as skipped: `onSkip` is called, `onOpenChange(false, 'skip')`.
The spotlighted target stays clickable: a click on it reaches the target and leaves the tour open.
A window resize closes the tour without marking it seen: `onOpenChange(false, 'resize')`, neither `onComplete` nor `onSkip`.

With a `tourKey` the tour opens by itself on the first visit (at step 1); `Done`, `Skip`, Escape and a scrim click mark the key seen, so it does not open by itself again; a resize does not mark it seen.
A step whose `target` is missing centres the card in the viewport (a third from the top) under a plain full-page dim; a target that mounts later is found.
A selector `target` is searched inside `scope` only (when given); while the scope is not mounted it finds nothing.
A step with `when: false` is left out; the progress counts only the shown steps.
The step index is clamped between the first and last step.
The tour can be restarted at step 1 by the app's own button (`useGuidedTourState().start`), and `useGuidedTourState({ tourKey })` gives the first-visit opening and the seen flag.

doesNot.text: No help button by default: the app renders its own (`trigger` is deprecated and off).
A click on the dimmed page is not passed to the page behind it (it skips the tour instead); no click reaches anything but the target and the card.
A resize does not mark the tour seen and does not call `onSkip`.
Does not close by clicking outside the card (apart from the dimmed-page skip).
Nothing opens when `steps` is empty or all steps have `when: false`.
Web only: no React Native version.
A Back button is not shown on the first step.
Labels passed in `skipLabel`, `backLabel`, `nextLabel`, `doneLabel` and `triggerLabel` are shown as given, not translated.

defaults.text: Closed (`defaultOpen` false), step 0, progress shown, scrim on, `closeOnResize` true, `closeOnScrimClick` true, `trigger` false.
Card placed `bottom` of the target, 12 px away, with an arrow.
The spotlight has 4 px of room around the target.
The seen flag is kept in `localStorage` under `wangs-ui:guided-tour:<tourKey>`.
`Next` is the primary button; `Skip` and `Back` are secondary text buttons.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `open` / `onOpenChange` and `step` / `onStepChange` control it from outside; `defaultOpen` / `defaultStep` start it uncontrolled.
`step.placement`: where the card sits relative to the target.
`scrim: false`: no dim, no spotlight and no scrim; the page behind takes clicks.
`closeOnScrimClick: false`: the dimmed page takes clicks again (they reach the page) and the tour stays open.
`closeOnResize: false`: a resize leaves the tour open.
`showProgress: false`: no `Step n of total` text; `progressLabel`: the template with `{current}` and `{total}`.
`skipLabel`, `backLabel`, `nextLabel`, `doneLabel`: replace the button texts.
`seenStore`: another place to remember the seen flag (`getSeen` / `setSeen`).

`trigger: true` (deprecated): a round help button with a question-mark icon, named `Show guide` (or `triggerLabel`), with a tooltip of the same text; pressing it opens the tour at step 1; `triggerProps` restyles it.
`scope`: the root inside which selector targets are searched.

builtInText.text: Buttons `Skip`, `Back`, `Next`, `Done`; progress `Step {current} of {total}` (for example `Step 1 of 3`); help button `Show guide` (locale en; all passed through `t()`).

keyboard.text: The card is focused on every step; ArrowRight goes next (`Done` on the last), ArrowLeft goes back.
Enter on the card itself goes next; on a focused button Enter keeps that button's own action.
Escape skips the tour.
Keys act only while focus is inside the card.

states.text: Open: the card, the progress and the spotlight (or the plain scrim) are shown; closed: nothing of the tour is on the page (except the optional help button).
First step: no Back; last step: `Done` instead of `Next`; step without a target: card centred, plain dim.
Seen: the key is stored and the tour no longer opens by itself.

testApi: `Spectra.findGuidedTour(title)` by the active step's title; `Spectra.queryGuidedTour(title)`: `null` when missing; a closed tour found by title reads not open.

`getContainer()` (the card), `getTitle()`, `getDescription()`, `getProgress()` (`{ current, total }`; throws with `showProgress={false}`), `getProgressIndicator()` (a wrapper, `shouldBeAbove(title)`).
`getSkipButton()`, `getBackButton()` (throws on the first step), `getNextButton()` (Next, or Done on the last), `hasBack()`.
`next()`, `back()`, `skip()` (waits for the card to close), `clickScrim()` (skips; throws when the page takes no clicks).
`isOpen()` / `shouldBeOpen` / `shouldNotBeOpen`, `isHighlighting(target)` / `shouldBeHighlighting`, `hasScrim()`, and the common `shouldHaveFocusWithin()`.

components.name: Icon

does.text: An icon from `@wangs-ui/react-icons` (e.g. `MailLine`) draws a vector glyph about 1rem by 1rem (16px) that takes the surrounding text colour (`currentColor`).
Every library icon carries its own name as the `data-icon` attribute (`MailLine` shows `data-icon="MailLine"`), which is how tests find it.
The glyph is hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden="true"`) and has no accessible name.
An icon passed a `color` shows in that colour (inline `color` on the svg).
An icon passed `className` or `style` applies them on top of the `icon` class (size can be overridden).
An icon passed `accessibilityLabel` gets `aria-label` with that text and `role="img"`, but the svg keeps `aria-hidden="true"`.

doesNot.text: An icon is not interactive: no click, focus, hover or tooltip behaviour of its own.
An icon shows no text and no loading state; it renders synchronously, never asynchronously.
An icon does not change its look by itself with state (hover, disabled): the parent controls colour.
The `data-icon` name is not changed by `color`, `className` or `style`.

defaults.text: Size 1rem by 1rem, `viewBox` `0 0 24 24`, colour `currentColor`, no `aria-label`, no `role`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `color`: shows the glyph in that colour instead of the text colour.
`className`, `style`: styling only (for example a different size).
`accessibilityLabel`: sets `aria-label` to that text and `role="img"` (the `aria-hidden="true"` stays).
`testID`: sets `data-testid` on the glyph.

keyboard.text: Not focusable: Tab skips an icon.

states.text: Only one state: shown. No disabled, loading, focused or selected state.

testApi: `Spectra.findIcon(name)`: the first icon whose `data-icon` equals `name` exactly (e.g. `MailLine`); waits the implicit wait, throws when none appears. `queryIcon(name)`: `null` when missing (waits `probeTimeout`). Web only (mobile throws).
`card.findIcon(name)` / `card.queryIcon(name)` on a wrapper: searches only inside that wrapper.
`getName()`: the icon name from `data-icon`; `shouldHaveName(name)` polls it.
`Spectra.shouldNotFindIcon(name)`: asserts nothing with that name is on the page.
Visibility and containment assertions: `shouldBeVisible()`, `shouldBeWithin(wrapper)`, `shouldNotBeWithin(wrapper)`.

components.name: ImageCarousel

does.text: Shows one image at a time from `value` (each `{ src, alt }`); the slides sit side by side and slide horizontally (about 300 ms) when the active one changes.
Renders nothing when `value` is missing or empty.
With more than one slide, a row of small round indicator dots sits under the images; the dot of the active slide is highlighted.
Each indicator is a tab named `Slide <n> of <total>` with `aria-selected` `true` on the active one; clicking one shows that slide.
Autoplay (on by default, more than one slide) advances to the next slide every 3000 ms; at the last slide it wraps to the first with `loop` (default), otherwise it stops there.
Any manual change (indicator click, key, handle `next`/`prev`/`goTo`) restarts the autoplay countdown from that moment when `autoPlay` is on.

The slide track has `aria-live="off"` while autoplay is running and `aria-live="polite"` when it is not (autoplay off, single slide, stopped at the last slide without `loop`, or paused by the preview).
Hovering a slide darkens it and shows an eye icon; clicking it (or pressing Enter or Space on the focused slide overlay) opens the full-screen preview on that slide.

Opening the preview stops the carousel's autoplay and makes that slide active; the preview is the `Gallery` dialog (`Gallery#4`) with thumbnails, previous/next, close, and it starts at that slide and uses the same `loop`, `autoPlay` and `autoPlayInterval`.
Changing the slide inside the preview also changes the carousel's active slide behind it.
Closing the preview returns focus to the slide overlay that opened it and restarts the autoplay when `autoPlay` is on.
`onActiveIndexChange` fires with `{ index, item }` on every change of the active slide (indicator, keys, autoplay, handle, opening the preview, changing slide inside the preview).

`onError` fires with `{ index, item, error }` when a slide image fails to load (native failure: the event; `getImageUrl` failure: the Error), and also for failures inside the preview; that slide shows the error fallback (`Image#6`).
A slide without `src` shows the placeholder (`Image#7`).
The root is a region named `Image Carousel` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`.
A new `value` array resets the active slide to the first.

The imperative handle offers `next`, `prev`, `goTo(i)`, `startAutoPlay`, `stopAutoPlay`, `isAutoPlayActive`, `getElement`; `startAutoPlay` does nothing unless `autoPlay` is on and there is more than one slide; `next`/`prev` at the ends do nothing without `loop`; `goTo` ignores an out-of-range or current index.

doesNot.text: Does not show previous/next arrow buttons on the carousel (indicators, keys and the handle are the only ways to move).
Does not show indicators for a single slide, and does not autoplay a single slide.
Does not have a play/pause button; pausing needs the caller's own control through the handle.
Does not pause autoplay on hover or focus (only opening the preview pauses it).
Does not open the preview when `preview` is `false`: no overlay buttons, no dialog.
Does not support swipe or drag on the slides.
Does not move with ArrowUp or ArrowDown (only ArrowLeft and ArrowRight on the indicators).
Does not go past the last slide without `loop`: autoplay stops there and ArrowRight stays on it.
Does not resolve a thumbnail or preview image with different content than the slide; all use the same `value` and `getImageUrl` (the preview thumbnails ask for a width of 100 px).

defaults.text: `autoPlay` `true`, `autoPlayInterval` 3000 ms, `loop` `true`, `fit` `cover`, `rounded` `lg`, `loading` `lazy`, `preview` `true`.
Without `width`/`height` the slide track is 125 x 125 px.
Indicator label `Slide <n> of <total>`; region name `Image Carousel` (locale en).

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `autoPlay={false}`: no automatic movement; `aria-live` stays `polite`; the preview does not autoplay either.
`autoPlayInterval` (ms) and `loop`: interval of automatic steps; whether the carousel, its keys, autoplay and the preview wrap.
`width` / `height` (px): size of the slide track.
`fit` (`fill`, `contain`, `cover`, `none`, `scale-down`), `rounded` (`none`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `full`), `loading` (`eager`, `lazy`): applied to every slide image.
`preview={false}`: removes the hover overlay and the full-screen preview.
`placeholder`, `errorFallback`: content for a slide without `src` / one that failed to load (string as text, node as is), as `Image#33`, `Image#34`.
`indicatorAriaLabel(index, total)`: replaces the indicator labels (e.g. `Gambar 1 dari 3`).
`getImageUrl`: resolves private or relative sources for slides, preview image and preview thumbnails (`Image#9`).
`aria-label`: replaces `Image Carousel` as the region name; `className`, `style`, other div attributes go to the root; `pt` is styling only.

builtInText.text: Region `Image Carousel`; indicators `Slide <n> of <total>` (both locale en, replaceable); the preview adds `Gallery`, `Close`, `Previous`, `Next` and thumbnails `<n> / <total>` (`Gallery#37`); the preview overlay on a slide has no accessible name.

keyboard.text: Only the active indicator and the active slide's preview overlay are in the Tab order (roving tabindex 0 / -1).

On a focused indicator: ArrowRight shows the next slide and focuses its indicator, ArrowLeft the previous, wrapping with `loop` and stopping at the ends without it; Enter or Space shows the focused one.
On the focused slide overlay: Enter or Space opens the preview; Escape closes the preview (`Gallery#5`).

states.text: Autoplaying (`aria-live="off"`) versus not autoplaying (`polite`).
Active slide / active indicator (`aria-selected="true"`, primary colour dot) versus inactive.
Preview open (dialog over the page, carousel autoplay paused) versus closed.
Per slide: loaded, placeholder, error (`Image#44`, `Image#46`, `Image#47`).
The full-screen preview's own slideshow timer runs only while the preview is open; while it is closed only the carousel advances its slides, one active-index change per interval.

testApi: `Spectra.findImageCarousel(label)` / `queryImageCarousel(label)` (`null` when missing): by the region `aria-label` (default `Image Carousel`).
`getActiveIndex()` (the indicator with `aria-selected="true"`; 0 when none), `getIndicatorCount()`, `getIndicatorButton(i)`, `getIndicatorsContainer()` (only with more than one slide).
`isAutoPlayActive()`: reads `aria-live="off"` of the slide track (the real running state).

`goTo(i)` clicks indicator i; `next()` / `prev()` click the following / preceding indicator and always wrap around (even without `loop`); `focusIndicator(i)`; `pressArrowRight/Left/Up/Down()` press the key on the current focus (Up/Down do nothing).

`openGallery(index?)` clicks that slide's overlay (default the active slide); `getGalleryActiveIndex()` (-1 when no preview is open), `isGalleryIndexSynced(i)`, `isAutoplaySynced()` read the open `Gallery` preview.

components.name: Image

does.text: Shows one picture from `src` inside a fixed box (125 x 125 px by default) with rounded corners and a thin outline; the picture fills the box and is fitted by `fit`.
Renders the `alt` text on the picture; `alt=""` marks it decorative (no name, no `aria-label`).

With `preview` on (default) and a loaded picture, a transparent button covers the whole image; hovering or focusing it darkens the image and shows an eye icon; click, Enter or Space opens the full-size view.

The full-size view is a modal dialog named `Gallery` with the single picture shown large, a `Close` button, no thumbnails and no previous/next buttons; Escape or the close button closes it and focus returns to the preview button.
While the source is being resolved (async `getImageUrl`) the box shows a shimmer block, the root has `data-loading`, and the screen-reader status text is `Loading image...`.

When the picture cannot be loaded (native load failure, or `getImageUrl` rejected or threw) the box shows the error fallback, the status text is `Image failed to load`, and `onError` is called once: with the load event for a native failure, with the Error for a resolver failure.
When `src` is missing or empty the box shows the placeholder (`placeholder`), not the error fallback; there is no preview button.
An absolute `http(s)://` URL or a `data:image/...;base64,` URI is shown as is; `getImageUrl` is not called for it.
A relative string `src` with `getImageUrl` is shown from the resolved value (called with `src`, `width`, `height`); without `getImageUrl` it is used as is.
With `getImageUrl` and a relative `src`, the full-size view loads the full resolution by calling `getImageUrl(src)` without width and height; otherwise it shows the same address as the small image.
A `Blob` `src` is shown through a temporary object URL (revoked on change and unmount); `getImageUrl` is not called for it.
A new `src` clears a previous error and loads again.
Extra HTML attributes (`id`, `data-*`, handlers) and `aria-label` go to the root `<span>`.

doesNot.text: Does not show the preview button or open the full-size view while loading, while in the error state, with no `src`, or when `preview={false}`.
Does not make the root focusable or a button; only the preview button is focusable.
Does not offer zoom, rotate, pan, or a multi-image preview (single picture).
Does not fill its parent by itself: the box is fixed at 125 x 125 px unless `width`/`height`/`style`/`className` change it.
Does not keep the aspect ratio when only `width` or only `height` is given: the other side stays 125 px.
Does not call `getImageUrl` for a `Blob`, an absolute URL or a data URI source (full-size view included).
Does not retry by itself after an error; only a changed `src` loads again.
Does not treat a string `placeholder` or `errorFallback` as an image address: it is shown as plain text, centred in the box.
Does not show anything (empty box) when `getImageUrl` resolves to an empty value without an error.
Does not distinguish the two empty states in the screen-reader status text: a missing `src` also announces `Image failed to load`.

defaults.text: `rounded` `lg`, `fit` `contain`, `preview` `true`, `loading` `lazy` (native lazy loading).
Default placeholder and default error fallback look the same: a landscape picture (sun and hills) filling the box on a light grey background.
Preview button label `Click to preview full-size image`; with `alt` it becomes `Click to preview full-size image: <alt>` (locale en).
Preview dialog name `Gallery`, close button `Close` (locale en; from Gallery, `Gallery#26`, `Gallery#34`).

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `width` / `height` (px): size of the box (see `Image#18`).
`rounded`: `none`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `full` (full on a non-square box gives an ellipse).
`fit`: `fill`, `contain`, `cover`, `none`, `scale-down` (CSS `object-fit`).
`preview={false}`: no preview button and no full-size view.
`previewButton`: render function replacing the default button; it receives `onClick` (opens the full-size view) and the default `aria-label`.
`placeholder`: replaces the missing-`src` content; a string shows as text, a node as is.
`errorFallback`: replaces the failed-load content in the same way; setting one leaves the other at its default.
`loading="eager"`: native eager loading.
`loadingLabel`, `errorLabel`, `previewLabel`: replace the status texts and the preview button label (locale en defaults above).
`getImageUrl`: async resolver for private or relative sources (see `Image#9`, `Image#10`).
`onError`: notification only (see `Image#6`); it does not change the fallback.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling only; `style` can override the box size.

builtInText.text: `Loading image...` (status while resolving), `Image failed to load` (status on error), `Click to preview full-size image` (preview button name), `Gallery` and `Close` (preview dialog), all locale en and replaceable; the status texts are visually hidden (screen reader only).
The fallback and placeholder pictures have no text.

keyboard.text: The preview button is a native button: Tab focuses it (the dim mask and icon appear on focus), Enter or Space opens the full-size view.
In the full-size view Escape closes it and focus returns to the preview button; Tab stays inside the dialog.

states.text: Loading: shimmer, `data-loading`, `Loading image...`; no ``, no preview.
Loaded: `` with the preview button on top (when `preview` is on).
Placeholder (no `src`): placeholder content, no ``, no preview button.
Error: error fallback, no ``, no preview button, `Image failed to load`.
Preview open: modal dialog `Gallery` over the page; closed: not in the page.
Focused and hovered preview button: image darkened with the eye icon (otherwise the button is invisible).

testApi: `Spectra.findImage(label)` / `queryImage(label)` (`null` when missing): by the root `aria-label`, or by the `alt` text of the picture.
`getImageElement()` (the ``), `getPlaceholderElement()` (placeholder or fallback box), `getPreviewButton()` (the button named `Click to preview...`), `getContainer()`.

`hasImageElement()`, `hasPlaceholder()`, `hasPreviewButton()`, `isLoading()` (`data-loading` present), `hasError()` (no `` and a placeholder box present: true for the missing-`src` placeholder too), with polling `should*` forms.
`openPreview()` clicks the preview button; `closePreview()` presses Escape on the open preview dialog (throws when none is open).

components.name: ImageCropper

does.text: Open (`open` or `defaultOpen`) it shows a modal dialog titled `Adjust photo` with the crop area for `imageSrc` and a footer of controls; closed it renders nothing (`Dialog#19`).
The crop area mounts about 250 ms after the dialog opens; `Apply` stays disabled until the cropper reports the image loaded (`ImagePicker#72`).

The footer toolbar has, in order: aspect ratio segments (`Free`, `1:1`, `4:3`, `16:9`), four icon buttons (`Rotate left`, `Rotate right`, `Flip horizontal`, `Flip vertical`), a `Zoom` slider with its percentage, a `Quality` slider with its percentage, the original file size, the expected output size, and `Restore`; the action row has `Cancel`, `Change`, `Apply` (`ImagePicker#19`).
Choosing an aspect ratio segment locks the crop box to that ratio (`Free` unlocks it); the active segment is shown pressed (`aria-pressed="true"`).
Rotate buttons turn the image 90 degrees left or right; flip buttons mirror it horizontally or vertically.
The `Zoom` slider ranges from the smallest zoom that still covers the crop box up to 300 % and shows its percentage; dragging the image or crop box also moves it, and zoom is capped at 300 %.
The `Quality` slider ranges 1 to 100 % in steps of 1, starts at `compressionQuality` (default 80 %), and shows its percentage.

After every control change (aspect ratio, rotate, flip, zoom, quality, restore, end of a crop-box drag) and once after the image loads, the expected output size is recomputed: a spinner shows while computing, then the size as `<n> KB` (counting up from the previous value over about 300 ms).
`onExpectedSizeChange(bytes)` fires with the expected output size after each recompute and with `null` when the dialog closes; it is informational and never blocks Apply.
The original size text shows when `fileSize` (bytes) is given: `<n> KB` below 100 KB, otherwise `<x.y> MB` (one decimal).

`Apply` encodes the crop in `fileType` at the quality on the slider and calls `onApply(payload)` once, then closes the dialog; the output pixel size is the crop size times the quality (minimum 0.1), as in `ImagePicker#17`.

The payload has `compressed` (`objectUrl`, `fileName`, `file` (a `File`), `size` as rounded kilobytes in the form `<n>KB` with no space, `type` as `image/<fileType>`), `canvas`, `message` `File has been compressed.`, `cropperState`, `aspectRatio` (number or `null` for free) and `compressionQuality` (0 to 1) at the moment of Apply.

The output file keeps the source `fileName` base name: `photo.png` applied as `jpeg` is `photo.jpeg`, an already matching extension (`jpg`/`jpeg` count as one) stays, a path part is dropped, a name with no extension gets the format added; without `fileName` the file is named with a timestamp and the format (e.g. `1794525466237.webp`).

With `maxOutputFileSize` (bytes) Apply never exceeds it when reachable: quality goes down in steps of 10 points to a floor of 50 %, then the dimensions shrink until it fits; the quality slider moves to the fitted quality and the expected size shows the fitted result, with no error or message.
`Cancel` calls `onCancel` and closes the dialog; no `onApply`.
`Change` only calls `onChangeImage`; the dialog stays open (the caller swaps `imageSrc`, `ImagePicker#23`).
`Restore` resets the crop, zoom, rotation and flips to the initial image framing, the aspect ratio to `Free` (`1:1` when circular), and the quality to `compressionQuality`.
When the image cannot be decoded, a message `The image could not be read` (role `alert`) shows next to the buttons and `Apply` stays disabled (`ImagePicker#22`).
`defaultState` restores the crop position, zoom, rotation and flip when the cropper is ready, and `aspectRatio` restores the aspect segment (re-edit after a previous Apply).
A new `imageSrc` while open reloads the cropper and (without `defaultState`) resets ratio, quality and zoom to the starting values.
Closing the dialog resets zoom, quality, aspect ratio and the expected size to their starting values for the next opening.
Escape, a backdrop click and the dialog's own close button (`Close dialog`) close it through `onOpenChange(false)` (`Dialog#3` to `Dialog#5`, `Dialog#7`, `Dialog#36`); they do not call `onCancel`.

doesNot.text: Does not pick, validate or reject files (type and size checks are the caller's, `ImagePicker#18`).
Does not call `onApply` and keeps the dialog open when the crop is empty (no canvas, zero width or height) or encoding fails; the failure is only logged to the console, with no on-screen message.
Does not close on `Change`.
Does not call `onApply` on raw crop interaction; only after `Apply`.
Does not show the aspect ratio segments when `shape` is `circular` (1:1 locked).
Does not revoke the payload `objectUrl`; the caller does.
Does not show the original size text without `fileSize`.
Does not translate the segment labels `Free`, `1:1`, `4:3`, `16:9`, nor `Quality`/`Zoom` percentages (the percent sign and `KB`/`MB` units are fixed text).
Does not apply an `aspectRatio` prop when `shape` is `circular` (always 1:1).

defaults.text: Closed (`defaultOpen` false), `shape` `square`, `fileType` `webp`, `compressionQuality` 0.8, no `maxOutputFileSize`, aspect ratio free unless `aspectRatio` (or circular).
Zoom 100 % on open.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `open` + `onOpenChange` (controlled) or `defaultOpen` (uncontrolled); a controlled dialog stays open until the app sets `open` false (`Dialog#7`).
`shape="circular"`: circular crop box, ratio locked at 1:1, no aspect segments.
`fileType`: `webp`, `jpeg` or `jpg`: output mime and file extension.
`compressionQuality` (0 to 1): initial quality and quality after Restore.
`fileName`: base name of the output file (`ImageCropper#13`).
`fileSize`, `maxOutputFileSize`, `aspectRatio`, `defaultState`: see `ImageCropper#10`, `ImageCropper#14`, `ImageCropper#19`.

`cropDialogHeader`, `cancelCropLabel`, `changeImageLabel`, `applyCropLabel`, `zoomLabel`, `qualityLabel`, `restoreLabel`, `imageUnreadableLabel`: replace the matching built-in text (the button labels are also their accessible names) (`ImagePicker#58`).
`pt`: styling only.

builtInText.text: Dialog title `Adjust photo`; buttons `Cancel`, `Change`, `Apply`, `Restore`; labels `Zoom`, `Quality` (visible label and slider `aria-label`); error `The image could not be read` (locale en; each replaceable by its prop; passed through the locale).
Icon button `aria-label`s `Rotate left`, `Rotate right`, `Flip horizontal`, `Flip vertical` (locale en, translated through the locale; no prop replaces them).
Segments `Free`, `1:1`, `4:3`, `16:9`; payload message `File has been compressed.`; dialog close button `Close dialog` (from `Dialog#36`).

keyboard.text: Escape closes the dialog (`Dialog#3`); Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside it (`Dialog#8`).
The sliders respond to arrow keys; each change recomputes the expected size.
The footer controls are native buttons (Enter or Space presses them).

states.text: Closed (nothing in the page) and open.
Cropper loading: `Apply` disabled; ready: `Apply` enabled.
Computing size: spinner replaces the expected size; settled: `<n> KB`.
Unreadable image: alert text shown and `Apply` disabled.
Circular: no aspect segments; square: segments with the current one pressed.

testApi: `Spectra.findImageCropper(label)` / `queryImageCropper(label)` (`null` when missing): the dialog, by its header text (default `Adjust photo`); a cropper closed and gone still resolves and reads closed with `find`.
`clickRotateLeft/Right()`, `clickFlipHorizontal/Vertical()` (by their aria-labels), `clickRestore()`, `clickCancel()`, `clickChangeImage()`, `clickApply()` (waits for Apply to be enabled).
`setAspectRatio('16:9')` (segment label; throws for circular), `setZoom(n)`, `setQuality(n)` (slider values: zoom as a ratio such as 1 to 3, quality 1 to 100).
`getOriginalSize()` (text, needs `fileSize`), `getCompressedSize()` (waits out the spinner), `isComputingSize()`, `isOpen()`, `getContainer()`.
Labels customised by props change the accessible names these helpers look for (`Cancel`/`Apply`/`Change`, `Zoom`, `Quality`, `Restore`).

components.name: ImagePicker

does.text: A picker with no image shows one upload trigger button, 125x125 px (30x30 px for `type="inline-table"`) unless `width`/`height` are set; the trigger holds an icon, the title and the requirements text
Picking or dropping a valid image opens the crop dialog titled `Adjust photo`; the thumbnail appears only after `Apply`
`Cancel` or closing the crop dialog adds nothing for a new image and keeps the previous image when editing one
`Apply` puts the compressed image in the thumbnail and calls `onChange`: with the payload (single) or the full array of payloads (multiple)
Single mode: while an image is shown there is no upload trigger; the user replaces it with Edit; deleting it brings the trigger back
Multiple mode: the trigger stays beside the thumbnails after each image until `maxImages` is reached, then it disappears
Several files picked at once open the crop dialog one file at a time, in order
Edit on an image that came from `imagePreviewUrl` or `value` of a server URL (not a blob from this picker) opens the file chooser; the crop dialog opens after a file is chosen
Edit on an image already cropped in this picker reopens the crop dialog on the original file with the earlier crop, ratio and quality restored
Delete removes that thumbnail at once (no built-in confirmation) and calls `onChange`: `null` (single) or the array without it (multiple); the next upload adds beside the rest
`type="normal"`: Edit, Delete and the eye button sit in an overlay over the thumbnail that shows on hover or when a button inside has focus; the buttons are in the DOM while it is hidden
`type="inline-table"`: Edit and Delete are always visible beside the thumbnail (no overlay)
The eye button opens a full-size lightbox of the image
The first image shows the Default badge in multiple mode; the badge fades out while the thumbnail is hovered or focused
Multiple mode with 2 or more images: dragging a thumbnail onto another moves it there (the others shift); the first position is the default image; `onReorder` and `onChange` (full array) fire

The compressed file keeps the source file's base name: `photo.png` becomes `photo.webp`; the extension is kept only when it already matches the output format (`jpg` and `jpeg` count as the same); a name without a dot gets `.<fileType>` added; a source with no name is named `<timestamp>.<fileType>`; a path prefix is dropped
The output pixel size is the crop size multiplied by the quality (minimum 0.1), so lowering `Quality` also shrinks the image

Rejection: a file not matching `accept` (default `image/*`) is rejected as `file-invalid-type`; a file larger than `maxFileSize` (default 1048576 bytes, equal passes) as `file-too-large`; valid files beyond the allowed count as `too-many-files` (single mode allows 1; replacing an image frees its slot); one `onReject` call lists them all and the other valid files still open the crop dialog

Crop dialog footer: aspect ratio segments, rotate and flip buttons, `Zoom` and `Quality` sliders with percentages, the original file size, the expected output size, `Restore`, `Cancel`, `Change`, `Apply`
Original size readout uses 1024: under 100 KB (102400 bytes) it reads `<n> KB` rounded, otherwise `<n.n> MB` with one decimal (bytes / 1048576)
Expected output size readout is `<n> KB`, bytes / 1024 rounded; a loader shows while it is computed
`Apply` stays disabled until the cropper has loaded the image; an undecodable file shows `The image could not be read` (role alert) and `Apply` stays disabled
`Change` inside the crop dialog opens the file chooser to swap the file being cropped (single file)

`Restore` resets crop, quality and ratio to the starting values: the ratio returns to the one the dialog opened with (the ratio saved from an earlier apply of that image, 1:1 for a circular picker), and to `Free` for a first crop.
The payload's `compressed.size` is a string `<n>KB` using 1000 (bytes / 1000 rounded), unlike the readouts in `ImagePicker#20`/`#21` which use 1024

The crop dialog ALWAYS opens after a valid file is picked or dropped; no prop (no skip-crop, no auto-apply) bypasses it, and the thumbnail and `onChange` come only after `Apply`. Same for each queued file in a multi-pick (`ImagePicker#7`) and for `Change` inside the dialog.

doesNot.text: No visible rejection message anywhere, for an oversized file or a wrong type alike (no toast, no inline text, no `aria-live` text, no `invalid` styling); a rejected file is reported only through `onReject(rejections)`, where each entry is `{ file, errors }` and `errors` holds the codes `file-too-large` / `file-invalid-type` / `too-many-files` (a file both oversized and of a wrong type gets both codes in one entry), and no crop dialog opens for it. The codes are not translated and no built-in rejection text exists in any locale
No confirmation dialog on Delete unless the app answers `onBeforeDelete`

No Edit/Delete/eye overlay while `disabled`, or for an empty picker; in `type="normal"` also none while an image is still resolving through `getImageUrl` or has failed to load (in `inline-table` the Edit/Delete buttons stay beside the thumbnail unless `disabled`)
No image counter and no "limit reached" text when `maxImages` is hit; the trigger just disappears
No keyboard reordering; reorder is drag only
Single mode ignores `maxImages`, `reorderable`, `onReorder` and shows no Default badge unless `showDefaultBadge`/`showPrimaryBadge` is true
Dropping a file works only on the upload trigger; dropping on a thumbnail does nothing
The default requirements text does not follow `maxFileSize`; it always reads the built-in `Max. 1 MB` unless `requirements` is passed
No upload to a server and no progress; output is only handed to `onChange`
The default `requirements` are `Image` and `Max. 1 MB` and the default `placeholder` title is `Select or drop` (the texts in Built-in text)

defaults.text: `multiple` false, `type` `normal`, `accept` `image/*`, `maxFileSize` 1048576, `fileType` `webp`, `compressionQuality` 0.8 (slider starts at 80%), `fit` `contain`, `loading` `lazy`, `preview` true, `useDeleteButton` true, `showInfo` true, `disabled` false, `invalid` false, `name` `imageInput`
Thumbnail corners: `lg`, or `xs` for `inline-table`
Default badge: shown in multiple mode, not in single
`reorderable` true in multiple mode

Default `maxFileSize` 1048576 bytes (1 MB, binary): a file of exactly 1048576 bytes passes, 1048577 is rejected `file-too-large`. The default text `Max. 1 MB` is only the requirements line (`ImagePicker#33`); it is not an error message and does not change with `maxFileSize`. A number passed as `maxFileSize` replaces the limit.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `multiple`: several images, the trigger stays, Default badge, reorder; without it only one image
`maxImages` (multiple only): trigger disappears at that count; extra picked files are rejected `too-many-files`
`reorderable={false}`: no thumbnail dragging; `disabled` also turns reorder off
`showDefaultBadge` / `showPrimaryBadge` true: Default badge on the first image in single mode too; false: none in multiple mode (`showPrimaryBadge` wins over `showDefaultBadge`)
`defaultBadgeLabel` / `primaryBadgeLabel`: replaces `Default` in the badge (`primaryBadgeLabel` wins)
`preview={false}`: hides the eye button and the lightbox only; Edit and Delete stay; in `inline-table` it also removes the thumbnail's own preview button
`useDeleteButton={false}`: no Delete button
`disabled`: trigger and file input disabled, drop ignored, no Edit/Delete/eye on existing thumbnails
`type="inline-table"`: the trigger shows only the icon (no title, no requirements text) and Edit/Delete sit beside the thumbnail

`placeholder` string: replaces the title `Select or drop`; a ReactNode replaces the whole trigger content; with a custom placeholder and no explicit `requirements`/`showInfo`, the requirements text is not shown

`requirements` (string array): replaces the default two strings; joined with `, ` as one description line; `showInfo={false}` or an empty array hides it. It is visible only in `type="normal"` and only while the trigger is shown (so not in single mode once an image exists)
`rounded="full"`: circular thumbnail and a circular 1:1 crop, with the aspect ratio segments hidden

`maxOutputFileSize`: on Apply the output is lowered in quality down to 50%, then in dimensions, until it fits; no error or rejection; the `Quality` slider and expected size show the fitted result; independent of `maxFileSize`
`onBeforeDelete`: Delete runs only when it returns (or resolves) exactly `true`

`getImageUrl(src, width, height)`: called for each source that is not an absolute `http(s)` URL or a data URI (a `blob:` thumbnail of this picker also goes through it); while its promise is pending the thumbnail shows a shimmer block with no eye button or Edit/Delete overlay; a rejection shows the error fallback (`errorFallback`, else the default placeholder picture) and calls `onError` with an `Error`; an image that fails to load in the browser does the same with `onError` receiving the event
`imagePreviewUrl` / `value`: shows existing images at first render
`fileType` `jpeg` / `jpg`: output and file extension use it
`invalid`: the file input gets `aria-invalid="true"`
Label props (`editLabel`, `deleteLabel`, `cropDialogHeader`, `cancelCropLabel`, `changeImageLabel`, `applyCropLabel`): replace the matching built-in text
Inside a loading `Shimmer`: the trigger is an empty block with no icon or text, and the pointer cannot reach it

builtInText.text: Trigger title `Select or drop`; description `Image, Max. 1 MB` (the two default requirements joined with `, `)
aria-label `Upload image` on both the trigger button and the hidden file input (unless `aria-label` is passed, which replaces the file input's)
Badge `Default`
Edit and Delete buttons are icon only, with aria-labels `Edit` and `Delete`
Eye button aria-label `Click to preview full-size image` (not translated)

Crop dialog: header `Adjust photo`; buttons `Cancel`, `Change`, `Apply`, `Restore`; segments `Free`, `1:1`, `4:3`, `16:9`; aria-labels `Rotate left`, `Rotate right`, `Flip horizontal`, `Flip vertical`, `Zoom`, `Quality`; error `The image could not be read`
Hidden live-region texts of a thumbnail: `Loading image...` while resolving, `Image failed to load` on error (not translated)
Payload `message` is `File has been compressed.`

keyboard.text: The trigger, Edit, Delete and eye buttons are native buttons: Tab reaches them, Enter or Space activates; the overlay shows while one has focus
No keyboard reorder (`ImagePicker#30`)

states.text: Empty, with images, disabled, invalid, crop dialog open
Dragging files over the trigger sets a drag-active, accept or reject styling only; the check uses `accept`
Crop dialog content mounts about 250 ms after it opens; `Apply` enables only once the cropper reports ready

testApi: `Spectra.findImagePicker(label, options?)` / `Spectra.queryImagePicker(label, options?)`: match the hidden file input by accessible name; with no `aria-label` the name is `Upload image`, so pass `aria-label` or a Field label. `find` waits the implicit wait; `query` returns null when absent.
`getFileInput()`: the hidden file input; `(await picker.getFileInput()).upload(file)` or `setValue(path)` starts the crop flow. Then `Spectra.findImageCropper('Adjust photo')` and `clickApply()`.
`getUploadTrigger(options?)`, `hasUploadTrigger(options?)` / `shouldHaveUploadTrigger()`
`getEditButton(options?)`, `hasEditButton(options?)` / `shouldHaveEditButton()` / `shouldNotHaveEditButton()`: only over a preview image
`getDeleteButton(options?)`, `hasDeleteButton(options?)` / `shouldHaveDeleteButton()`
`clickEdit(options?)`, `clickDelete(options?)`: act on the first image; `deleteImage(index, options?)` deletes at `index` (an `onBeforeDelete` confirm still has to be answered)
`reorderThumbnails(from, to, options?)`; `setDefaultImage(index, options?)` (= `reorderThumbnails(index, 0)`, needs `reorderable`)
`getImageSources(options?)` / `shouldHaveImageSources([...])`: each `src` in display order, default first
`getThumbnails(options?)`, `getThumbnail(index, options?)`, `getPreviewImages(options?)`, `getPreviewCount()` / `shouldHavePreviewCount(n)`, `shouldHaveThumbnailsCount(n)`
`getDefaultBadge(options?)`, `hasDefaultBadge(options?)` / `shouldHaveDefaultBadge()`
`isDisabled()` / `shouldBeDisabled()`, `isInvalid()` / `shouldBeInvalid()`
`getContainer(options?)`, `element`
`find*` and sub-part lookups wait the implicit wait; `query*` and `is*`/`has*` readers wait `probeTimeout` (500 ms); pass `{ timeout }` for async surfaces (crop dialog, `getImageUrl`).

components.name: Input

does.text: Renders a single-line native text field; typed text appears and `onChange` receives the new string directly.

`maxLength` is passed to the native `<input maxlength>` (Input adds no length logic): typing and pasting stop at the limit, nothing is shown (no error, no counter, `aria-invalid` unchanged); a paste longer than the room left is cut to fit.
`draftFilter(text)` rewrites typed or pasted text before it is shown and before `onChange`; the caret stays after the preceding text.
`invalid` sets `aria-invalid` on the field and on its group and styles it invalid.
Placeholder text is shown while the value is empty.

doesNot.text: No character counter is rendered, ever.
No error message or helper text is rendered by Input; a surrounding Field supplies it (exposed via the field's accessible description).
Reaching `maxLength` shows no error; typing simply stops.
The value is not trimmed on blur or on change; surrounding spaces are kept.
No clear button is built in.
`type` cannot be `password`, `search`, `number` or `tel`; only `text`, `email`, `url`.
No format or length validation runs inside Input (`email`/`url` only set the native type).

defaults.text: `type` is `text`, `size` is `xs`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `readOnly` are `false`.
Uncontrolled value starts as an empty string (or `defaultValue`).
No placeholder, no `maxLength`, no addons or elements.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `startAddon` / `endAddon`: a bordered block before / after the field in the group.
`startElement` / `endElement`: inline content inside the field box at the start / end.
`maxLength`: limits typed and pasted length.
`draftFilter`: rewrites input as typed.
`placeholder`, `name`, `autoComplete`, `autoFocus`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`: passed to the native field.
`value` + `onChange`: controlled; without `value`, the Input holds its own text.
`size` (`xs` | `sm` | `md` | `lg`, or responsive).

Length is counted by the browser in UTF-16 code units (`string.length`), not characters: Input does not count with spread, `Array.from` or `Intl.Segmenter`. `𝒜` (U+1D49C) counts as 2. With `maxLength` 3 (Chromium, verified): at `ab` (max-1) typing `𝒜` is refused whole (value stays `ab`); at `a` it fits (`a𝒜`, length 3); pasting `a𝒜𝒜` keeps `a𝒜` (the second pair is dropped whole, never split). There is no counter, so nothing else changes on screen.

builtInText.text: none; no built-in literal text or aria-labels.

keyboard.text: Native text field keys only; Input adds no key handling and exposes `onKeyDown` / `onKeyUp` passthrough.

states.text: `disabled`: native field is disabled, text dimmed, group has `aria-disabled`.
`readOnly`: native `readOnly`, focusable and selectable but not editable; group has `aria-readonly`.
`invalid`: `aria-invalid="true"` on field and group; the wrapper `getSeverity()` reads `danger`.

testApi: Finders: `Spectra.findInput(label)` waits and throws if absent; `Spectra.queryInput(label, { timeout })` returns `null` when absent.
Value: `getValue`, `setValue` (clears, then types), `clearValue`, `paste(text)`; assertions `shouldHaveValue(v)`.
Focus: `focus`, `blur`, `isFocused`.

State readers: `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `isInvalid`, `getSeverity` (`shouldHaveSeverity('danger')` waits), `getType`, `getPlaceholder`, `getAccessibleDescription` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits), `getBorderColor` (`#RRGGBB`, `shouldHaveBorderColor` waits).

Parts: `element`, `getInputElement`, `getContainer`, `getStartAddon`, `getEndAddon`, `getStartElement`, `getEndElement`, `getStartAddonText`, `getEndAddonText`, `hasStartAddon`, `hasEndAddon`, `hasStartElement`, `hasEndElement`.

components.name: InputGroup

does.text: Shows the wrapped control in one bordered row, full width, with the control filling the space left by the addons and elements.
`startAddon` and `endAddon` render as filled blocks outside the field, at its left and right edge, with a border shared with the field.
`startElement` and `endElement` render inside the field (for example an icon), before and after the control.
A plain addon (text or a non-interactive element) is shown inside a wrapper block.

An interactive addon (a `button`, `a`, `select` or `input` element, or any element with `role="button"`, a `tabIndex` or an `onClick`) is shown as itself with the group's addon look, not inside an extra wrapper, and stays clickable and focusable.
With neither addons nor elements, the single child is shown directly, with the group look added to the child itself and no extra wrapper element.
The focus outline appears around the field part (elements and control) when the control is focused, and around an addon when it has focus.
Invalid shows the border and the focus outline in the danger colour.
Disabled shows the group and its addons with the 12% disabled background and 38% faded text.
The group root carries `aria-disabled`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-readonly` with the props' values (`true` or `false`).

doesNot.text: Does not disable, make read-only or mark invalid the wrapped control itself; `disabled`, `readOnly`, `invalid` on the group only change the group's look and aria attributes, so the control needs its own props.
Does not render an empty element slot: no `startElement` or `endElement` span is present when it is not given.
Does not accept zero or several children when no addon or element is given.
Does not render any text, label or error message of its own.
Does not take more than one addon or element per side; each slot is a single node.

defaults.text: `disabled`, `invalid`, `readOnly` are all false.
No addon and no element.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `startAddon` / `endAddon`: the addon block at that edge, outside the field; the field loses its rounded corner on that side.
`startElement` / `endElement`: the element inside the field at that side.
`disabled`, `invalid`, `readOnly`: see the aria attributes and the look above.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling; in the no-addon mode they land on the child.

keyboard.text: No key handling of its own; Tab moves through an interactive addon and the control in DOM order.

states.text: Idle: bordered row with the surface background.
Focused: primary outline around the field part, or around the focused addon.
Invalid: danger border and outline.
Disabled: disabled background and faded text; the wrapped control is disabled only if it has its own `disabled`.
Read-only: only `aria-readonly` on the group; no visual change.

testApi: `Spectra.findInputGroup(label)`: by the accessible name; `Spectra.queryInputGroup(label)`: `null` when missing.
`getContainer()`, `getContent()` (falls back to the group element in the no-addon mode), `getInput()`, `getElementWrapper()`.
`getStartAddon()`, `getEndAddon()`, `getStartElement()`, `getEndElement()`, `getStartAddonText()`, `getEndAddonText()`.
`hasStartAddon()`, `hasEndAddon()`, `hasStartElement()`, `hasEndElement()`.
`getValue()`, `setValue(value)`, `clearValue()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.
`isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`; `should*` for each reader.

components.name: Inventory

does.text: Lists each Wangs UI component on the page as an entry (component kind, accessible name), reading the names from `aria-label`, `title`, `aria-labelledby` and the innermost visible text of the page.

An entry is kept only when the component's own `query<Component>(name)` really finds it by that name and the element it finds is the name's own element, the nearest component root above it, or the control it labels (TC-6100).

A container is not listed under a name that belongs to a control inside it: the names of a Field and its Input list as `Field "Brand Name"` and `Input "Brand Name"` and no wrapper around them (TC-6100).

One name can list several components that a finder resolves on the same element (`Field` and `Input` for `Brand Name`; `Dialog` and `DialogForm`); each lists, and the entry's `alternatives` holds all of them.

Reports how many components of one kind carry a name (`occurrences`): the places inside the one resolved component count once, every other enclosing component of the same family adds one; `Button "Clear Field"` twice (one hidden, one visible) reads 2 (TC-6100).
Marks an entry `hidden` when the resolved component is not rendered visibly, and still lists it (TC-6100).

Reports where a name comes from (`nameFrom`: the component's own attribute, or text inside it), the `data-ui-section` of the resolved element, its `id`, and the component families around it (`within`, `datatable` for the buttons of its paginator).
Drops a component resolved inside another element of its own kind (an icon of the same component), so only the outer one lists.
Lists as `elements` the elements that name themselves (`aria-label`, or an `id`) but that no finder claims, as `~name` or `#id`; the page's own mount point is left out.

`inventoryOverlays` opens, one at a time, the triggers the page marks with `aria-haspopup` or `aria-expanded="false"` (a row's action menu, a bulk action, an export menu, a filter panel), lists the components each one adds under the trigger's name, and puts the page back (the trigger clicked again when it stays expanded, then Escape) (TC-6101).
`inventoryOverlays` reports only what an opened overlay adds: a component already in the base inventory is not repeated, and a trigger that adds nothing is not listed (TC-6101).

The overlay walk takes one trigger per kind (its section and name with digits folded, so one row action per row counts once), skips triggers that are hidden or disabled, and finds each trigger again before clicking since a re-render replaces it.

`inventoryReport()` gives the readers `getComponents()` (each as `Component "name"`), `getComponentsNamed(name)` (sorted kinds for a name), `getOccurrences(component, name)` (0 when none) and `getOpenedBy(trigger)` (names added by that trigger), with a polling `should*` for each; every read inventories the page afresh (TC-6100, TC-6101).

doesNot.text: Does not list a name longer than 120 characters or an empty name; a trailing required `*` is dropped and whitespace is collapsed before matching.
Does not read `script`, `style`, `svg` and `path` elements as names.
Does not list a name for a component whose finder does not resolve it (a name nothing can find is not an entry).
Does not count the same text in another kind of component (a column header) as a repeat of the name.
Does not change the page: it only reads, except `inventoryOverlays`, which opens and closes triggers and leaves the page as it found it (TC-6101).
Does not stop at one failing finder: a finder that throws is skipped; only a page that stops answering (a timeout from a native dialog or navigation) ends the overlay walk.
Does not leave its marker attributes (`data-wangs-inventory`, `data-wangs-inventory-trigger`) on the page.

defaults.text: `inventoryComponents` asks each finder with a 30 ms timeout.
`inventoryOverlays` waits 500 ms after each click (`settle`) and opens at most 20 triggers (`limit`).

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `inventoryComponents({ timeout })`: the time each finder is given; `skipNames`: names not asked again (the overlay walk passes the base page's names).
`inventoryOverlays(base, { timeout, settle, limit })`: finder time, wait after each click, and the number of triggers opened.

keyboard.text: After opening a trigger, `inventoryOverlays` presses Escape to close what it opened.

states.text: An entry is either visible or `hidden`; a name is either `attribute` (the component's own `aria-label` or `title`) or `text`.

testApi: `inventoryComponents(options?)`: `{ components, elements }`; a component is `{ component, name, section, id, alternatives, occurrences, hidden, element, nameFrom, within }`.
`inventoryOverlays(base, options?)`: `[{ trigger, triggerSection, components }]` per trigger that adds components.

`inventoryReport()`: `getComponents()` with `shouldContainComponents(part)` / `shouldHaveComponentsCount(n)`; `getComponentsNamed(name)` with `shouldHaveComponentsNamed([kinds], name)`; `getOccurrences(component, name)` with `shouldHaveOccurrences(n, component, name)`; `getOpenedBy(trigger)` with `shouldContainOpenedBy(name, trigger)`.

components.name: Label

does.text: Shows its text inline as a small rounded chip on one line (no wrapping).

The colours follow `severity` and `variant`: `light` is a tinted background with matching text, `filled` a solid background with contrasting text, `outline` a transparent background with a border and text in the severity colour.
`backgroundColor` and `color` replace the severity colours with the given CSS colours.
Any native span attribute passed (`id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `onClick`) lands on the chip.

doesNot.text: Does not label a form control: it renders a plain `span`, not a `<label>`, so it gives no accessible name to any input.
Not interactive: no focus, hover, press or disabled state of its own.
Does not truncate, remove or edit its text; long text stays on one line.
Does not render an icon, a close button or a tooltip.

defaults.text: Severity `neutral`, variant `light`, size `xs`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `severity`: `primary`, `secondary`, `danger`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, `contrast` or `neutral` sets the colour meaning.
`variant`: `light`, `filled` or `outline`.
`size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md` or `lg` sets padding and text size.
`backgroundColor` / `color`: custom colours, overriding the severity colours.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling only.

keyboard.text: None; the chip is not focusable.

states.text: Only the static look of the chosen severity, variant and size; no hover, focus, disabled or loading state.

testApi: `Spectra.findLabel(label)`: by the accessible name (an `aria-label` the caller sets); `Spectra.queryLabel(label)`: `null` when missing.
`getContainer()`, `getText()`.

components.name: LanguageSwitcher

does.text: Shows a compact, borderless dropdown trigger with the selected language's flag image and its upper-case ISO code (for example `EN`), and a down-arrow at the end.
Clicking the trigger opens a floating list panel of the languages; Escape, clicking outside or clicking the trigger again closes it.
Each option row shows the language's flag, its name and its upper-case code in brackets, for example `English (EN)`.
Clicking an option selects it, shows its code in the trigger and closes the panel.
The selected option is marked selected and set in bolder text in the list.
Only languages with `is_active: true` are listed; inactive ones are never shown.
The panel has a search box on top (placeholder `Search`); typing narrows the list to languages whose name contains the text, case-insensitively.
When the search matches nothing the panel shows `No languages found.`.
With an empty `options` list the panel shows `No languages available.`.
A flag image is shown only for a language whose `flag` is a non-empty string; otherwise that language shows text only.
Each flag image has the language code as its `alt` text.
A selected code that is not among the active options is shown in the trigger as its upper-case code, without flag or name.
Uncontrolled (`defaultValue`): it keeps its own selection and shows each new pick.
Controlled (`value`): it shows the `value` it is given; a pick only calls `onChange`, and the trigger changes only when the parent passes the new `value`.
Choosing a language calls `onChange` with the language code and the language object.
`onChange` is called once per pick, never a second time with the code alone.

doesNot.text: Does not change the app language itself; it only reports the pick through `onChange`.
Does not load or fetch languages; the list is whatever `options` holds.
Does not clear the selection: clicking the selected language again only closes the panel, and there is no clear button.
The search matches the language name only, not the code (typing `id` does not find `Bahasa Indonesia` by its code).
Does not call `onChange` for a pick that has no language object.
A disabled switcher does not open its panel and cannot be changed.
Does not show a loading spinner, an invalid style, a read-only mode or a visible label (no such props).
Does not show inactive languages even when one of them is the current `value`'s language (the trigger then shows the bare upper-case code).

defaults.text: `filter` is on: the search box shows in the panel.
Trigger shows the flag as a circle plus the code only (`showTriggerFlag` `circle`, `showTriggerCodeName` `code_only`).
Options show the circle flag plus name and code (`showOptionFlag` `circle`, `showOptionCodeName` `both`).
`size` is `md` (24 px trigger flag).
`panelWidth` is `content`: the panel is as wide as its content (at least the preset minimum), not tied to the trigger.
Closed (`defaultOpen` false), enabled, no value selected unless `value` or `defaultValue` is given.
With no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` the trigger's accessible name is the placeholder `Select an option` (locale en).
With no value the trigger shows the placeholder `Select an option`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `showTriggerFlag` / `showOptionFlag`: `circle`, `rect` (square-cornered flag) or `none` (no flag image).
`showTriggerCodeName`: `code_only`, `name_only` (name without code) or `both` (name then code).
`showOptionCodeName`: `code_only` (only `(EN)`), `name_only` (only the name) or `both`.
`filter: false`: no search box in the panel.
`filterPlaceholder`, `emptyFilterMessage`, `emptyMessage`: replace `Search`, `No languages found.`, `No languages available.`.
`disabled`: greyed trigger, panel cannot be opened.
`size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` scale the trigger, flag, text and arrow; a responsive value is accepted.
`panelWidth`: `trigger` (same width as the trigger), `content`, a number of px, or a CSS width.
`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`: control or start the panel open and report each open or close.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`: the trigger's accessible name.
`id`, `className`, `style`, `pt`: root id and styling only.

builtInText.text: Search placeholder `Search`, no-match `No languages found.`, empty list `No languages available.` (locale en, passed through `t()`).
Fallback placeholder and trigger name `Select an option` (locale en, from the Select it is built on).
The names and codes come from `options`; the component adds no language names of its own.

keyboard.text: Tab focuses the trigger; Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens the panel; Escape closes it.
ArrowDown / ArrowUp move the highlight in the list and Enter picks the highlighted language, as in Select.
With the search box, typing filters at once and Enter picks the first match.
A disabled switcher is skipped by Tab.

states.text: Closed / open (the trigger reports expanded when open).
Disabled: dimmed, no panel.
Selected option: bold text in the list; highlighted option: standard list highlight.
Loading, invalid, read-only: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findLanguageSwitcher(label)` finds by the trigger's accessible name (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`); `Spectra.queryLanguageSwitcher(label)` returns `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindLanguageSwitcher(label)`.
`selectLanguage(labelOrPattern)` / `selectOption(...)`: opens the panel, picks the option whose text matches (the language name), closes it.
`getValue()` (`shouldHaveValue(text)`): the trigger text, by default the upper-case code (`EN`), not the language name. `getPlaceholder()`.
`clearValue()`: clicks the selected option; the value stays because deselect is not supported.
`open()`, `close({ method: 'clickOutside' | 'escape' | 'trigger' })`, `toggle()`, `isOpen()` (`shouldBeOpen()`, `shouldNotBeOpen()`).
`getOptions()` (`shouldHaveOptionsCount(n)`), `getOption(label)`, `hasOption(label)` (`shouldHaveOption(label)`).
`getPanel()` / `getContent()`, `getList()`, `getTrigger()`, `getContainer()`.

`getFilterInput()`, `hasFilterInput()` (`shouldHaveFilterInput()`), `getFilterValue()` (`shouldHaveFilterValue(text)`), `setFilter(query)` (`setFilter('')` clears; `clearFilter()` does not clear headless), `getFilterIcon()`, `hasFilterIcon()`.
`getEmptyMessage()`, `hasEmptyMessage()` (`shouldHaveEmptyMessage()`).

`getArrow()`, `hasArrow()`, `getLoader()`, `hasLoader()` (always absent), `getStartAddon()`, `getEndAddon()`, `getStartElement()`, `getEndElement()` and their `has*` forms; the arrow sits inside the end element, no start or end addon is rendered.
`isDisabled()`, `focus()`, `blur()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`, `isLoading()` (the last three are always false).

components.name: Link

does.text: Shows its children as a link (`<a>`) to `href`; clicking it follows the link.
Looks like a link: small body text in the brand colour, with an underline appearing on hover (offset 4 units) and a pointer cursor.
Its children may be plain text, a `Text`, or text beside an icon; the visible text is the sum of them.
`onClick` runs on click and may stop the navigation with `preventDefault`.
`external` opens it in a new tab (`target="_blank"`), sets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and shows a small box-and-arrow icon after the children.
`as` draws the link through another component, such as a router link; the same look and `href`, `target`, `rel` are passed to it.

doesNot.text: Does not navigate in-app on its own: a plain `<a>` reloads the page unless the app handles the click or uses `as` with a router link.
Does not check the address: `external` is the caller's word, an off-site `href` without it still opens in the same tab.
Does not translate its text: it shows the children as given.
The external icon is not hidden from assistive tech and has no text label.
Without `href` it is an `<a>` with no `href`, which is not a link for the keyboard or for the test finder.

defaults.text: `variant` `bodySmall`, `color` `primary`, `underline` `hover`, `external` false, element `a`.
With no `target`, none is set; with `external` and no `rel`, `rel` is `noopener noreferrer`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `underline`: `always` keeps the underline on, `none` removes it, `hover` (default) shows it on hover.
`variant`, `color`: change the text style and colour from the typography and colour tokens.
`hoverColor`: the text takes this colour on hover.
`target` / `rel`: set as given; `external` overrides `target` with `_blank` and keeps a given `rel`.
`external`: see `Link#5`.
`className` is added after the built-in classes.

builtInText.text: none; the text is the children.

keyboard.text: Tab focuses it and Enter follows it, as any native link with `href`; Space does not.

states.text: Hover: underline (by default) and the hover colour if `hoverColor` is set.
External: `target="_blank"` and the arrow icon.

testApi: `Spectra.findLink(label)` / `queryLink(label)`: finds an `<a>` that has an `href`, by accessible name (`aria-label` or visible text, also when the text sits in a nested `Text` beside an icon); `queryLink` gives `null`. Also chained from a container (`(await Spectra.findPopover('...')).findLink('...')`).
`getText()`: trimmed visible text; `shouldHaveText(text)`.
`getHref()`: the `href` as written or `null`; `shouldHaveHref(href)`.
`isExternal()`: true when `target="_blank"`; `shouldBeExternal()` / `shouldNotBeExternal()`.
`click()`, `hover()` and the common assertions come from the base wrapper.

components.name: LoadingOverlay

does.text: While `isLoading` is true it covers the viewport (fixed, full width and height) with a semi-transparent surface backdrop (75% opacity, 2 px blur), the animation centered and the message below it
Mouse clicks on the area it covers do not reach the page behind it
It fades in over 0.2 s; when `isLoading` turns false it fades out over 0.2 s and is then removed from the DOM (0 s with reduced-motion; `findLoadingOverlay` no longer matches)
The animation is the built-in loading animation (a Lottie player), played automatically in a loop
The message renders as a paragraph under the animation, centered

doesNot.text: No built-in text: no default message, no `Loading...`
No `role`, `aria-live`, `aria-busy` or `aria-label` of its own; an accessible name exists only from the `aria-label` prop
Does not make the content behind it inert, trap focus, move focus or lock scroll: Tab still reaches controls underneath
No cancel or close control, no timeout, no progress value; it leaves only when the app sets `isLoading` false
Renders nothing at all while `isLoading` is false
The content behind stays in the page, dimmed and blurred through the 75% backdrop; it is not hidden, removed or disabled, but mouse clicks cannot reach it (`LoadingOverlay#2`).
No minimum display time and no delay: it appears the moment `isLoading` turns true and starts leaving the moment it turns false, however short the load.

defaults.text: `isLoading` false (nothing shown), `contained` false (viewport cover), no message, built-in animation

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `isLoading`: true shows the overlay

`contained`: covers only the nearest positioned ancestor (absolute, `inset-0`, full size of it) instead of the viewport; with no positioned ancestor it is placed against the page start instead of the intended container
`message`: text (or node) shown under the animation; an empty string still renders an empty paragraph; `undefined` or `null` renders none
`src`: plays that Lottie file instead of the built-in animation
`animation`: renders that node instead; wins over `src`
`aria-label`: names the overlay (for one without a message)
`className`, `style`, other props: applied on the root

keyboard.text: None; it has no focusable element and does not block the keyboard (`LoadingOverlay#8`)

states.text: Shown (`isLoading` true) or absent from the DOM; fading in or out lasts 0.2 s

testApi: `Spectra.findLoadingOverlay(label, options?)` / `Spectra.queryLoadingOverlay(label, options?)`: match the root (`data-ui-section` `loadingoverlay.root`) by message text or `aria-label`. `find` waits the implicit wait (default 1000 ms) and throws; `query` returns null when absent.
`getContainer(options?)`, `element`; after loading ends, `element.shouldNotExist()`.
`isDisplayed(options?)` / `shouldBeDisplayed()`
`getMessage(options?)`; `getMessageText(options?)` / `shouldHaveMessageText(text)`; `hasMessage(options?)` / `shouldHaveMessage()` (true when the paragraph has non-blank text)
`getAnimation(options?)`; `hasAnimation(options?)` / `shouldHaveAnimation()`: looks for a `dotlottie-player`, `lottie-player`, `canvas` or `svg` inside the overlay
`is*`/`has*` readers wait `probeTimeout` (500 ms); the sub-part getters wait the implicit wait.

components.name: Menu

does.text: Shows a permanent, always-visible vertical list of the items given in `items`, in order, as a rounded panel with a shadow that scrolls when taller than 90% of the viewport.
An item is a button with its label; an item with `href` is a link (`<a>`) with that `href` and `target`; both have `role="menuitem"` and the list has `role="menu"`.
Clicking an enabled item calls its `onClick`; Enter or Space on a focused item does the same.
An item with `icon` shows the icon before its label; an item with a string label also gets that label as its `aria-label`, a non-string label gets no `aria-label`.
An item with `danger: true` shows in the danger colour (red text, red-tinted hover background) and carries `data-danger="true"`.
A disabled item is dimmed, cannot be clicked (its `onClick` never runs), has `aria-disabled="true"` (a button item also has the `disabled` attribute), and is skipped by Tab and the arrow keys.
An item with `visible: false` (also a separator or group header) is not in the page at all; when every entry is hidden the empty text shows.

`{ type: 'group', label }` shows a small uppercase section header (`role="none"`, not focusable); `{ type: 'separator' }` shows a thin divider line (`role="presentation"`); both are entries in the same flat list, not parents of the items after them.

An item with `items` shows a chevron after its label and `aria-haspopup="true"`; in the default `expand` mode clicking it unfolds the sub-items inline under it (chevron turns upside down, `aria-expanded` true) and clicking again folds them, each parent independent of the others.

With `submenuMode="flyout"` a parent item shows a right chevron and clicking it opens its sub-items in a floating panel to the right of the item (`aria-expanded` true); a second click, Escape or a click outside closes it.

With `submenuMode="flyout"` and `triggerFlyoutOn="hover"` the flyout opens when the pointer rests on the parent item (after `flyoutDelay.open`, 100 ms if not set) and moving onto another item of the same list closes it; a click on the parent opens nothing.
An item with `tooltip` shows that plain text in a tooltip on hover or keyboard focus, also on a disabled item.

Arrow Down and Arrow Up move focus to the next and previous enabled item of the list the focus is in and wrap around at the ends; Home and End jump to the first and last enabled item; focus on the list itself enters at the first item (Down) or the last (Up).
Only one item is a Tab stop (the first enabled root item until an item has had focus, then the last focused one); the list itself is also focusable.
`header` and `footer` show in the panel above and below the list, separated by a thin line.
With no (visible) items it shows one line of empty text instead of items; the line is not a menu item.
`ariaLabel` or `ariaLabelledby` names the list; `onFocus` and `onBlur` fire when focus enters and leaves the list or any item in it.
An item's `className` and `style` apply to its row.

doesNot.text: Has no open or close state and no trigger: it is always rendered, and nothing closes it (Escape and outside clicks do nothing).
Holds no selected, checked or active value: clicking an item runs `onClick` only and leaves no mark on it.
A disabled item's tooltip still opens, but its `onClick` and `href` navigation do not run.
Arrow Right and Arrow Left do not open or close a submenu, and typing letters does not jump to an item (no type-ahead).
In `expand` mode Arrow Down and Arrow Up in the root list do not enter the unfolded sub-items; they move only among the root items.
A collapsed `expand` submenu is not removed from the page: its items stay in the DOM with zero height and are invisible.
Does not close anything by itself on item click (no `closeOnSelect`); that belongs to PopupMenu and ContextMenu.
Does not filter or search.
`triggerFlyoutOn="hover"` has no effect in `expand` mode.

defaults.text: `items` empty; `submenuMode` `expand`; `triggerFlyoutOn` `click`; list `tabIndex` 0; `focusOnMount` off; `flyoutDelay` open 100 ms in hover mode.
Every item is an action item (`type` `item`), visible, enabled, not danger; flyout opens to the right, aligned to the item top, with no gap.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `submenuMode="flyout"`: sub-items float instead of unfolding (`Menu#10`).
`triggerFlyoutOn="hover"` with `flyoutDelay` (number, or `{ open, close }`): hover opens flyouts (`Menu#11`).
`emptyContent`: replaces the empty text, string or any node.
