`focusOnMount`: the list takes focus when it appears, so Arrow Down reaches the first item.
`tabIndex`: sets the tab index of the list.
`header`, `footer`: show those slots (`Menu#15`).
Per item: `icon`, `tooltip`, `href` and `target`, `disabled`, `danger`, `visible`, `items`, `id`, `className`, `style`.

builtInText.text: Empty text `No options available` (English; a string `emptyContent` goes through the app translation, any other node is shown as given). It is the same text the empty menu of ContextMenu and PopupMenu shows.
No other built-in text: labels, group headers and tooltips are the caller's.

keyboard.text: Tab: list, then the Tab-stop item; Arrow Down, Arrow Up, Home, End as in `Menu#13`; Enter and Space activate the focused item; Escape does nothing in a plain Menu.

states.text: Item states: enabled, disabled (`Menu#6`), danger, focused (the list and the item show focus), submenu open or closed (`aria-expanded`, chevron direction).
Menu states: with items, empty (`Menu#16`); no loading or error state.

testApi: Finders: `Spectra.findMenu(label)` and `Spectra.queryMenu(label)` by the list's accessible name (`ariaLabel` or `ariaLabelledby`).
Parts: `getContainer`, `getList`, `getItems`, `getItem(indexOrLabel)`, `getIcon`, `getSubmenuIcon`, `getSubmenu`, `getGroupHeaders`, `getGroupHeader`, `getEmptyElement`.

Readers (each has a polling `should*`, e.g. `shouldBeItemDisabled`): `isDisplayed`, `getItemCount`, `getItemLabels`, `hasItem`, `getItemDestination`, `getItemTooltip` (hovers to open it), `hasIcon`, `getIconName`, `hasSubmenu`, `isSubmenuOpen`, `getGroupHeaderLabels`, `hasEmptyElement`, `getEmptyText`, `isEmpty`, `isItemDisabled`, `isItemDanger`, `getItemSeverity`, `isAnchoredTo(trigger)`, `isFocused`, `getFocusedItemLabel`.
Actions: `clickItem`, `openSubmenu`, `closeSubmenu`, `focus`, `blur`.
`getItems` and `getGroupHeaders` return only the current level; read a submenu through `getSubmenu()`.

components.name: Modal

does.text: Opens as a centered `alertdialog` with a header row (severity icon, then the `header` title), the `message` as body and a footer with the buttons; backdrop, page blocking and scroll lock as in `Dialog#1`.
The `message` is the modal's accessible description, so a screen reader reads it with the header on open (an explicit `aria-describedby` wins).
Clicking `Confirm` runs `onConfirm`, then closes the modal; clicking `Cancel` runs `onCancel`, then closes it.
While an async `onConfirm` is pending, the confirm button shows loading, the cancel button is disabled, and a second confirm click does nothing.
When `onConfirm` throws or rejects, `onError` receives the error and the modal stays open (the confirm button returns to normal).
Every close request goes through `onOpenChange(false)`; with a controlled `open` the modal stays open until the app sets `open` false.
Focus moves to the confirm button when the modal opens (to the cancel button when there is no confirm button), on the next animation frame.
Focus is trapped inside as in `Dialog#8`; Tab and Shift+Tab cycle between the footer buttons.
A closing modal fades out and is inert as in `Dialog#10`, then leaves the page.
Root carries `data-severity` with the modal's severity.
A message with a bulleted list reads each item as `• <name>`; a long list scrolls inside the message.

Imperative `useModals()` under `ModalsProvider`: `confirm(options)` opens a Cancel and Confirm modal, `alert(options)` opens one with a single `OK` button, `close()` closes the topmost; several can be open at once, each removed from the page after its exit animation.

doesNot.text: No close (✕) button in the header (`closable` is fixed off, as in `Dialog#46`).
By default a click on the backdrop does nothing; the modal stays open (`closeOnOverlayClick` is off, as in `Dialog#46`).
Escape does nothing by default.
Escape does not cancel while the confirm is pending.
Confirm does not call `onCancel`; cancel does not call `onConfirm`.
No form fields or arbitrary layout in the footer: only the Cancel and Confirm buttons (use `Dialog` or `DialogForm` for that).
`closeOnOverlayClick` given in `useModals()` options works as on `Modal` (`Modal#48`); without it the backdrop does nothing.
A closed `Modal` is not kept in the page after its exit animation (removed, not hidden).
No built-in unsaved-changes logic and no async work of its own: it only awaits what `onConfirm` returns.

defaults.text: Closed (`defaultOpen` false); `size` `sm` (400 px); `severity` `danger`.
Header icon by severity: `InformationLine` for `primary` and `info`, `ErrorWarningLine` for `danger` and `warning`, `CheckboxCircleLine` for `success`; its `aria-label` is `Header Icon`.
Confirm button: label `Confirm`, colour follows `severity`; cancel button: label `Cancel`, `contrast` colour, `text` variant.
Both buttons shown; `closeOnEscape` false; `role` `alertdialog`.
`useModals().alert` default severity `warning`, button label `OK` (in the cancel slot, no confirm button); `useModals().confirm` keeps the Modal defaults.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `severity`: header icon, its colour and the default confirm colour change.
`icon`: replaces the severity icon; `icon: false` shows no icon.
`confirmSeverity`: confirm colour independent of `severity`; `cancelSeverity` / `cancelVariant` restyle the cancel button.
`confirmLabel` / `cancelLabel`: replace the button texts (translated through `t()`).
`showConfirmButton: false` or `showCancelButton: false`: that button is not rendered; with one button left the footer holds only it (an alert's `OK`).
`confirmDisabled: true`: the confirm button is disabled and a click does nothing.
`closeOnEscape: true`: Escape acts as `Cancel` (`onCancel`, then close), only the topmost modal reacts and a dialog underneath does not see the key.
`closeOnOverlayClick: true`: a click on the backdrop acts as `Cancel` (`onCancel`, then close) unless the confirm is pending.
`size`: `sm` 400 px, `md` 600 px, `lg` 800 px as in `Dialog#23`; a responsive object picks per breakpoint.
`header`: a string is translated through `t()`; any other node renders as given; without `header` there is no title.
`aria-label`, `aria-describedby`, `id`, `className`, `pt`: accessible name, description target, container id, styling.

builtInText.text: Default button labels `Confirm` and `Cancel` (locale en; passed through `t()`).
Default header icon `aria-label` `Header Icon` (locale en).
`useModals().alert` button default `OK`.
No other built-in text; header and message come from props.

keyboard.text: Tab / Shift+Tab cycle inside the modal only (`Dialog#39`).
Enter or Space on a focused footer button activates it (native buttons).
Escape: nothing by default; with `closeOnEscape` it cancels unless the confirm is pending.

states.text: Open and closing: root `data-state`, inert and `isOpen()` as in `Dialog#41` and `Dialog#42`.
Confirming (async `onConfirm` pending): confirm loading, cancel disabled.
Confirm disabled: only with `confirmDisabled`.
The modal has no selected or error state of its own; an error from `onConfirm` is only reported to `onError`.

testApi: `Spectra.findModal(name)`: by header title or accessible name (found while open, closing or gone); `Spectra.queryModal(name)`: `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindModal(label)` for a modal never shown.
`getHeaderTitleText()` / `getHeaderTitle()` / `hasHeaderTitle()`, `getHeaderIcon()` / `hasHeaderIcon()`, `getSeverity()`, `getRole()` (`alertdialog`), `getSize()`.
`getMessageText()` / `getMessage()` / `hasMessage()`, `getAccessibleDescription()`, `getMessageListItems()`, `hasMessageListItemIcon(label)`, `getMessageGroupItems(label)`.
`hasScrollableMessage()`, `hasScrollableMessageList(index)`, `getScrollableMessageLists()`, `scrollMessage('start'|'end')`, `getMessageScroll()`.

`getConfirmButton()` / `hasConfirmButton()` (a lone footer button counts as the confirm), `getCancelButton()` / `hasCancelButton()`, `getFooterButtonLabels()`, `isConfirmDisabled()`, `isConfirmLoading()`.
`confirm()` / `cancel()`: click then wait until the modal is gone; `clickBackdrop()` (modal stays open).
`isOpen()`, `isDisplayed()`, `isFocusWithin()`, `getFocusedLabel()`, `getContainer()`.

`shouldBeOpen()` / `shouldNotBeOpen()`, `shouldHaveRole`, `shouldHaveSize`, `shouldHaveAccessibleDescription`, `shouldHaveMessageListItems` / `...Count`, `shouldHaveMessageListItemIcon` / `shouldNotHave...`, `shouldHaveScrollableMessage`, `shouldHaveMessageScroll`, `shouldHaveFooterButtonLabels` / `...Count`, `shouldBeFocusWithin`, `shouldHaveFocusedLabel`.

components.name: MultiSelect

does.text: Clicking a closed field opens the option list; clicking an option toggles it and the list stays open (it does not close after a pick). It closes on Escape or a click outside (Popover `closeOnClickOutside`); a second click on the already open field closes the list (the Popover click toggle; read from the code, not run in a browser).
Each selected value shows as a chip with the option's label (a value with no matching option shows `String(value)`); chips appear in the order selected.
Every chip has a remove button (accessible name `Remove badge`) that is not in the Tab order (`tabIndex=-1`) but takes focus by click or by `focus()`.
Clicking a chip's remove button removes that chip and does not open or toggle the list.
Enter or Space on a focused chip remove button removes that chip and does not open or toggle the list (the field's own key handling skips events from the remove button).
Removing the last chip leaves the placeholder text visible.
Chip remove while the field is `disabled` or `readOnly`: the remove button is still drawn and clickable but nothing is removed.

A chip is removable whatever its option's state: a selected option that is `optionDisabled` still has a removable chip. There is no prop for a locked (non-removable) chip and no chip looks different; a custom chip comes only from `renderChip(option, remove)`.

Select all (header checkbox): checking selects every visible, non-disabled option not yet selected; unchecking deselects only the visible, non-disabled options (selected values outside the current search stay). It is checked only when every visible non-disabled option is selected, and unchecked when there are none.

Search (`filter`): a text field in the header; typing keeps options whose label contains the text, case-insensitive; the first enabled match is highlighted so Enter picks it. The typed text is not cleared when the list closes.
Opening a list with `filter` moves focus to the search field; closing returns focus to the field when focus was lost to the page body.
Empty list: a row `No options available` when there are no options to show (also when `hideSelectedOptions` hid them all); `No results found.` when a search matches nothing.

While `loading` the field is inert and shows the loader icon in place of the arrow; an empty field shows `Loading...` as its placeholder; an open list with no options shows only a `Loading...` row, never the empty message (options already present stay listed).

`onChange(values, options)` fires on every toggle, remove and select-all with the full array of selected values (the option's value, or the option itself when no `optionValue`), in selection order; `options` is the original option array.

Overflow: with `maxVisibleChips: N` only the first N chips show, followed by one non-removable overflow chip `+{hidden count} more`; the hidden labels are in `data-overflow-labels` (JSON), so `getSelectedValues()` returns them without opening the list.
`maxVisibleChips: 'responsive'`: as many chips as fit the field width (at least one), the rest in the overflow chip; it re-fits when the width or the selection changes.
`maxValues`: once the selection count reaches it, every unselected option is disabled (`aria-disabled`) and a click does nothing; deselecting re-enables them; select all stops at `maxValues`.
`aria-describedby` passes through to the focusable field, so the text of the elements it names (a surrounding `Field`'s helper or error text) is its accessible description.

doesNot.text: No chip limit by default: all chips show and the field scrolls sideways (the wheel scrolls it horizontally) when they do not fit; `hasHorizontalScroll()` reads that.
The list does not close after choosing an option.
No range, count or error message of its own: no message when `maxValues` is reached; the only status text is the strings in Built-in text.
The Select all checkbox has no visible text label and no `aria-label` (the locale string `Select all` is not used here).
No search field unless `filter` is set; never a highlight of matches in option text and never a "create new option" row.
A disabled option cannot be toggled by click, Enter or Space and is skipped by select all; its checkbox is disabled.
No default `aria-label`: the accessible name is `ariaLabel` / `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` or a surrounding Field label; the placeholder `Select options` is not the name.
`maxVisibleChips` and `overflowLabel` do nothing with `display="comma"`.

defaults.text: `filter` false; `showSelectAll` true; `hideSelectedOptions` false; `display` `chips`; `loading`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `invalid` false; `defaultOpen` false; `scrollHeight` 300; `panelWidth` `trigger`; `size` `xs`; value `[]` when uncontrolled.
No `maxValues`, no `maxVisibleChips` (every chip shows).
Header (the row above the list) shows only when `filter` or `showSelectAll` is on; with both off it is absent.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `filter`, `filterPlaceholder` (string: replaces the search placeholder and aria-label), `filterFunction(query, option)` replaces the label match.
`showSelectAll={false}`: no Select all checkbox. `hideSelectedOptions`: selected options leave the list.
`maxValues`, `maxVisibleChips`, `overflowLabel` (node, or a function of the hidden options), see `MultiSelect#15` to `MultiSelect#17`.
`display="comma"`: no chips; the labels show as one comma-separated text (`A, B`), with no remove buttons.
`placeholder`, `loadingPlaceholder`, `emptyMessage`, `emptyFilterMessage`: replace the matching built-in text (nodes render as given; no `t()` applied by the component).
`optionLabel`, `optionValue`, `optionDisabled`, `dataKey` (identity of object values): map the option shape.
`readOnly`: the list still opens but shows only the selected options, without checkboxes and without Select all; clicking changes nothing; chips cannot be removed.

`renderTrigger`, `renderOption`, `renderChip`, `startElement`, `endElement`, `startAddon`, `endAddon`, `panelWidth` (`trigger`, `content` = 12rem, a number in px, or a CSS size), `virtualScrollerOptions`: layout and custom render only.
`invalid`: marks `aria-invalid="true"` and the invalid look; no message.

builtInText.text: Placeholder: `Select options` (locale en; through `t()`).
Loading: `Loading...` (placeholder while empty and loading, and the list row while loading).
Search field: `Search` as both placeholder and `aria-label` (role `searchbox`), unless `filterPlaceholder` is a string.
Empty list: `No options available`; empty search: `No results found.`
Overflow chip: `+{count} more`, for example `+3 more`.
Chip remove button `aria-label`: `Remove badge`.
Select all checkbox: no text.

keyboard.text: The field is a `combobox` with `tabIndex=0` (`-1` when disabled): Tab focuses it. Enter, Space or ArrowDown on the closed field opens the list.

In an open list: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the highlight (first ArrowDown starts at the top); Enter or Space toggles the highlighted option; Escape closes and returns focus to the field. Home and End are not handled.

With `filter`: Tab (without Shift) from the open field moves focus to the search field and Tab or Shift+Tab inside it returns to the field; Space types in the search unless an option was highlighted by the arrow keys; Enter picks the highlighted (or first) match.
The chip remove button: Enter or Space removes the chip (`MultiSelect#5`).
`disabled` or `loading`: the field does not open by key or click.

states.text: Closed, no selection: placeholder text. Closed with selection: chips (or the comma text).
Open: list and header visible; option `aria-selected` true for chosen options; the keyboard-highlighted option carries `data-focused`.
Disabled: inert, `tabIndex=-1`, no open, no change. Loading: `MultiSelect#13`. Read-only: `MultiSelect#35`. Invalid: `MultiSelect#37`.
Option disabled by `optionDisabled` or by `maxValues`: `aria-disabled`, disabled checkbox.

testApi: `Spectra.findMultiSelect(name)`: by the accessible name (`aria-label` or the Field label); `Spectra.queryMultiSelect(name)`: `null` when missing.
`open()`, `close()`, `isOpen()` (`shouldBeOpen()`, `shouldNotBeOpen()`).
`selectOption(label)`, `deselectOption(label)`, `toggleOption(label)`: open the list, find the option (scrolls a virtual list) and click it.
`selectAll()`, `deselectAll()`, `isAllSelected()`, `hasSelectAll()`.
`filter(keyword)`, `clearFilter()`, `hasFilter()`, `getFilterInput()`.
`getChips()`, `getChipLabels()` (visible chips only), `getSelectedValues()` (chips plus the `+N more` values, never opens the list), `getOverflowText()`, `hasHorizontalScroll()`.
`getChip(label)`: wrapper with `getLabel()`, `getAccessibleName()`, `isInvalid()`, `getRemoveButton()`, `isRemoveButtonFocused()`, `remove()` and their `should*`; `removeChip(labelOrIndex)`.
`getPlaceholder()`, `getTrigger()`, `getPanel()`, `getList()`, `getItems()`, `getItemLabels()`, `getItem(label)`, `getHighlightedOption()` (`shouldHaveHighlightedOption(label)`).
`isOptionSelected(label)`, `isOptionDisabled(label)`, `hasEmptyMessage()`, `getEmptyMessageText()`.
`isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`, `isLoading()`.
`getAccessibleDescription()` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits).

components.name: NumberInput

does.text: `min` and `max` are a range, not a typing filter: while typing, a value outside the range stays as typed (typing `-7` with `min` 0 shows `-7`); on blur or Enter it is clamped to the nearest bound (`-7` becomes `0`, above `max` becomes `max`). The clamp is never per character.
A typed minus (`-`) alone stays on screen while typing, with no value yet; on blur it is gone (empty, or the bound when `allowEmptyValue` is false).
The Enter key clamps the typed value to the range like blur; the field keeps focus.
A controlled `value` outside the range is shown clamped to the range.
Characters that are not digits (or the sign, or the decimal separator where decimals are allowed) are dropped as typed; a field that gets only such characters stays empty, also after blur.

With `maxFractionDigits` 0 (default) typing the decimal separator after digits leaves the text unchanged (`2` then `.` stays `2`), so typing `2`, `.`, `5` key by key gives `25`. With `maxFractionDigits` above 0 a trailing separator or zero (`1.`, `1.0`) stays as typed until blur, which formats it; display is rounded to `maxFractionDigits` and padded to `minFractionDigits`.
A separator typed with no digit before it reads as `0.` (`.5` becomes `0.5`) when `minFractionDigits` is 0.
Empty: clearing the field gives no value (`onChange(undefined)`), the field is empty and shows the placeholder.

`onChange(value)` carries only the number (or `undefined`); it fires while typing with the typed number as is (`-7` before blur), again on blur or Enter with the clamped number when clamping changed it, and on every step.
A value outside the safe integer range, or a step too small for the value, is not emitted and the field keeps the last safe value.

Stepper buttons (only with `showControls`): increment adds `step`, decrement subtracts `step`, result clamped to the range and rounded to `maxFractionDigits`; from an empty field the start is `min`, else 0. The buttons are not disabled at the bounds; a click at the bound leaves the value at the bound.
`Home` sets the value to `min` and `End` to `max` (only when that bound is set; no key effect otherwise).

`prefix`, `suffix`, `padStart` (zero padding of the integer part), `useGrouping`, `locale`, `formatterOptions` format the displayed text; the caret cannot move into the prefix or suffix and deleting them is blocked.
With `allowEmptyValue={false}` a cleared field becomes `min` (0 with no `min`) at once and `defaultValue` falls back to `min` or 0.
`aria-describedby` passes through to the focusable field, so the text of the elements it names (a surrounding `Field`'s helper or error text) is its accessible description.

doesNot.text: No range error message and no invalid state for a value outside `min`/`max`: nothing in the UI reports it, it is only clamped.
Typing does not clamp per character: no keystroke is refused for being below `min` or above `max`.
No stepper buttons by default.
Stepper buttons and arrow keys do not go outside the range.
No string value mode: the value is a `number` (a decimal as a JS number), never a string or bigint.
Alt+Arrow (0.1 times `step`) changes nothing while `maxFractionDigits` is 0 (the result is rounded back to the integer).
The stepper `aria-label`s are not translated (not passed through `t()`).
No value change on a read-only field: the input is read-only, steppers are disabled, and the step and Home/End keys do nothing.
No default `aria-label` on the input.

defaults.text: `allowEmptyValue` true, `showControls` false, `controlOrientation` `stacked`, `step` 1, `minFractionDigits` 0, `maxFractionDigits` 0, `useGrouping` false, `size` `xs`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `readOnly`, `autoResize` false.
`locale` is the provider's active locale; no `min`, no `max`, no prefix or suffix.
The input is `type="text"` with `inputMode` `numeric` (`decimal` when `maxFractionDigits` is above 0); `min`, `max`, `step` are also set as attributes.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `showControls`: stacked (default) shows increment above decrement at the end of the field; `controlOrientation="horizontal"` shows decrement as the start addon (minus icon) and increment as the end addon (plus icon). Both are disabled when `disabled` or `readOnly`.
`min`, `max`: `NumberInput#1`; `step`: stepper and arrow size.
`minFractionDigits`, `maxFractionDigits`: `NumberInput#6`; a `minFractionDigits` above `maxFractionDigits` is reset to 0 and 0 with a console error.
`allowEmptyValue={false}`: `NumberInput#14`.
`autoResize`: the field grows with its text and the placeholder becomes `...` (a custom `placeholder` is ignored).
`startElement`, `endElement`, `startAddon`, `endAddon`: extra content; with `showControls`, stacked steppers replace `endElement`, horizontal steppers replace `startAddon` and `endAddon`.
`readOnly`: the input is read-only; steppers disabled; value unchanged by keys. `disabled`: the input and steppers are disabled. `invalid`: `aria-invalid="true"` and the invalid look; no message.
`placeholder`: replaces `Enter number` (not with `autoResize`). `aria-label`, `aria-describedby`, `name`, `autoFocus`, `autoComplete`: passed to the input.

builtInText.text: Placeholder: `Enter number` (locale en; through `t()`); with `autoResize` the placeholder is always `...`.
Increment button `aria-label`: `Increase value by {step}` (for example `Increase value by 1`); decrement: `Decrease value by {step}`; English literal in the code, not translated.
No range or error text.

keyboard.text: ArrowUp and ArrowDown change the value by `step`; Shift by 10 times `step`; Alt by 0.1 times `step` (rounded to `maxFractionDigits`); results stay inside the range. The default action is prevented.
`Home` goes to `min`, `End` to `max` (when set); Enter and Tab or blur clamp a typed value.

Backspace and Delete cannot remove the decimal separator, group separator, prefix, suffix or padding, and cannot delete the value that already equals `min` one digit at a time; selecting the whole text and deleting clears the field (when `allowEmptyValue`).
A second `-` is ignored; a decimal separator typed where one is shown moves the caret past it.
Stepper buttons are native buttons (Tab, Enter or Space).

states.text: Empty: no text, placeholder visible. With a value: formatted text.
Typing (focused, out-of-range value allowed): shows the typed text; blur or Enter: clamped (`NumberInput#1`).
Disabled, read-only, invalid: `NumberInput#33`. Focused: standard focus; blur commits.

testApi: `Spectra.findNumberInput(name)`: by the accessible name; `Spectra.queryNumberInput(name)`: `null` when missing.

`getValue()`: the formatted text of the input, `""` when empty (`shouldHaveValue(text)`, which polls); `setValue(number)`: clears and types the number; `clearValue()`; `paste(text)` (`shouldHaveValue(...)`).
`focus()`, `blur()`: `blur()` is the step that clamps a typed value.
`stepUp({ magnitude })`, `stepDown({ magnitude })` (`standard` ArrowUp, `large` Shift+ArrowUp, `fine` Alt+ArrowUp); `jumpToMin()`, `jumpToMax()` (Home, End).
`increment()`, `decrement()`, `getIncrementButton()`, `getDecrementButton()`: the stepper buttons (exist only with `showControls`).
`getInput()`, `getContainer()`; `hasStartAddon()`, `hasEndAddon()`, `hasStartElement()`, `hasEndElement()` and their `get*`.
`isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`; `getDescription()`, `hasDescription()`, `getDescriptionText()`.
`getAccessibleDescription()` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits).

components.name: Paginator

does.text: Shows icon-only First, Previous, Next and Last buttons around a window of numbered page buttons; the active page is a filled button with `aria-current="page"`, the others plain.
The window holds 5 page buttons (`pageLinkSize`), keeping the current page centered where possible and pinned to the ends near the first or last page; fewer pages show fewer buttons.
Clicking a page button, First, Previous, Next or Last emits the new page; Previous and First are disabled on page 1, Next and Last are disabled on the last page.
The rows-per-page dropdown lists `rowsPerPageOptions` in the order given, plus the current page size appended at the end if it is not among them; choosing a size returns to page 1.
With no `rowsPerPageOptions` the dropdown offers only the current page size.
With zero records, or `rows` omitted/0, every button, the jump field and the rows-per-page dropdown are disabled, and there are no page buttons.
When the record count shrinks so the current page no longer exists (offset at or past the total), it moves to the new last page by emitting a page change; it does not do this on first render.

When the record count drops to 0, no page correction is emitted (the correction target would be below page 1, which is ignored): a DataTable keeps its stale page number, shows no rows and the report `No records`.

The jump-to-page field commits on Enter or on blur: a page past the last goes to the last page, a page below 1 goes to page 1, a decimal is truncated, an empty field reverts to the current page; the field shows the current page number as its placeholder and value.

Jump field as coded: `0`, `-1` and any value below 1 commit as page 1 (nothing is emitted when already on page 1, the field resets to the current page); a value above the total commits as the last page; the target is `trunc(value)` clamped to 1..totalPages, and with 0 total pages nothing is emitted. A letter or other non-numeric character typed in the field is not accepted (NumberInput ignores input that does not parse; the previous digits stay); a lone `-` counts as empty and reverts to the current page.

After the last row of the last page is removed (client or server), the record count shrinks, the Paginator emits a page change to the new last page and the DataTable then shows that page (a fall back of one page; not an empty page) as long as at least one record remains; the correction is an effect after the render, so one render with the empty page can precede it. Code: `useUpdateEffect` on `totalRecords` in `Paginator.tsx` with `resolveOutOfRangeFirst`; DataTable and `useDataView` have no clamp of their own.
Inside a DataTable (`usePaginator`), the layout is First, Previous, page buttons, jump field, Next, Last, page report, rows-per-page dropdown.
Inside a DataTable the report reads `Showing {first} to {last} of {totalRecords}` (e.g. `Showing 1 to 10 of 95`, last clamped to the total) and `No records` when the (filtered) total is 0.
Inside a DataTable the total follows the active search and filters (client: the filtered count; server: the reported total), and a new search or Apply returns to page 1.
Inside a DataTable, changing the page size resets to page 1 and the paginator is named `Table pagination`.
Inside a DataTable the default page size is 10 and the default options are 10, 25, 50, 100.

DataTable report values: `{first}` is the 1-based first record of the page and `{last}` the last, clamped to the total; page 2 at 10 per page of 95 reads `Showing 11 to 20 of 95`, the last page `Showing 91 to 95 of 95`, one record `Showing 1 to 1 of 1`.

doesNot.text: No tooltips on any button or the dropdown.
The standalone Paginator never moves by itself: it is controlled, nothing changes until the parent feeds `first` and `rows` back from `onPageChange`.
The rows-per-page dropdown shows no visible `Rows per page` text, and the page buttons show only numbers; the labels are aria-labels.
Previous/Next/First/Last at an end emit nothing (disabled; out-of-range targets are ignored).
No ellipsis or "..." between page buttons, no total-pages text unless the report template includes it.
A DataTable's cursor mode, infinite scroll or `slots.pagination` replaces this paginator; cursor mode has only `Previous page` / `Next page` and no page numbers, total, jump or rows-per-page.
The report's `{first}` and `{last}` never exceed the total records (clamped), and `{first}` is 0 when the total is 0.

defaults.text: Standalone layout: First, Previous, page buttons, Next, Last, rows-per-page dropdown; no report, no jump field.
`alwaysShow` true: renders even with one page or none.
`pageLinkSize` 5; `totalRecords` 0, `rows` 0, `first` 0 (so a bare Paginator is empty and disabled).
Page change events carry zero-based `page` and `first`; DataTable converts to its 1-based page.
English text only; labels are component props, not locale constants.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `template` decides which parts exist: tokens `FirstPageLink PrevPageLink PageLinks NextPageLink LastPageLink RowsPerPageDropdown CurrentPageReport JumpToPageInput`; a part absent from the token string is not rendered (the report and jump field are off by default).
`alwaysShow={false}` renders nothing when there is at most one page.

`currentPageReportTemplate` sets the report text (placeholders `{currentPage}`, `{totalPages}`, `{first}`, `{last}`, `{rows}`, `{totalRecords}`; each replaced once); default `({currentPage} of {totalPages})`, only visible when `CurrentPageReport` is in the template.
`rowsPerPageOptions` adds the page-size choices (see Paginator#4, #5).
`pageLinkSize` changes the page-button window size.
`leftContent` / `rightContent` render extra content at the left / right end of the bar.
`firstPageLinkIcon`, `prevPageLinkIcon`, `nextPageLinkIcon`, `lastPageLinkIcon` replace the nav icons; per-part template overrides replace whole parts.
`firstPageLabel`, `prevPageLabel`, `nextPageLabel`, `lastPageLabel`, `rowsPerPageLabel`, `pageLinkAriaLabel`, `jumpToPageLabel` rename the accessible names.
`aria-label` names the `nav` (none by default; a DataTable sets `Table pagination`).
A DataTable shows the paginator only with `usePaginator`; its `rowsPerPage`, `rowsPerPageOptions`, `paginationReportFound` and `paginationReportNotFound` set the page size, options and report texts.

builtInText.text: `First Page`, `Previous Page`, `Next Page`, `Last Page` (nav button aria-labels).
`Page {page}` (page button aria-label, e.g. `Page 3`).
`Rows per page` (dropdown aria-label); `Jump to page` (jump field aria-label).
`Showing {first} to {last} of {totalRecords}` and `No records` (DataTable report, locale en).
`({currentPage} of {totalPages})` (standalone report template, only when in the layout).
`Table pagination` (DataTable paginator name).
Rows-per-page option texts are the bare numbers (`10`, `25`, `50`, `100` in a DataTable) with no suffix; the closed dropdown shows the current page size.

keyboard.text: Nav and page buttons are native buttons: Tab to focus, Enter or Space to activate; disabled buttons are skipped.
In the jump field, Enter or blur commits the typed page.
In the rows-per-page list, Escape closes it.

states.text: First page: First and Previous disabled. Last page: Next and Last disabled.
Empty (0 records): all controls disabled, no page buttons.
Active page: `aria-current="page"`, filled.
Rows-per-page list open / closed.

testApi: `Spectra.findPaginator(name)` / `queryPaginator(name)`: by `aria-label` (DataTable: `Table pagination`); `find*` throws when absent, `query*` returns `null`.
`getPage()`: shouldHavePage(n), 1-based, from the active button; throws without an active page.
`getPageButtons()`: shouldHavePageButtonsCount(n); `goToPage(n)` clicks a button in the current window (throws when off-window).
`goToFirst/Prev/Next/Last(label?)`: click the nav button; return once the table shows the result; throw when the button is not in the layout.
`isPrevDisabled()` / `isNextDisabled()`: shouldBePrevDisabled / shouldBeNextDisabled and negations.
`getRowsPerPage()`: shouldHaveRowsPerPage(n); reads without opening, also when disabled.

`setRowsPerPage(n)`: opens and picks; `openRowsPerPage()`, `closeRowsPerPage()` (Escape), `isRowsPerPageOpen()` (shouldBeRowsPerPageOpen waits), `getRowsPerPageOptions()` (list closed again), `hasRowsPerPage()`.
`getSummary()`: shouldHaveSummary(text), the report verbatim; `hasSummary()`; `getTotalRecords()`: shouldHaveTotalRecords(n), the last number in the report (throws on `No records`).
`jumpToPage(page, label?)`: types and commits (any text accepted); waits for the field to show the active page first; returns once the table shows the result; `hasJumpToPage()`: shouldHaveJumpToPage.
Sub-parts absent from the layout (report, jump) make their methods throw; guard with `hasSummary()` / `hasJumpToPage()`.

components.name: PasswordInput

does.text: Typed characters are masked (shown as dots) by default.
Clicking the eye toggle shows the typed text in plain text; clicking it again masks it again.
Pressing Enter on the focused toggle shows the text, like a click.
The toggle icon changes with the state: eye-off icon while masked, eye icon while shown.
The toggle's accessible name follows the state: `Show password` while masked, `Hide password` while shown.
The shown or masked state stays while the user keeps typing and when the field loses focus [unverified].
The field is a plain-value control: the value change callback receives the new text, and the field starts empty when no value is given.
With a `Field` around it, the Field's error or helper text is the input's accessible description.

doesNot.text: No default placeholder text.
No strength meter, no rule checklist and no validation message of its own (that belongs to `Field`).
No clear button.
No tooltip on the toggle unless `withVisibilityToggleTooltip` is set.
Disabled or read-only fields cannot be revealed: the toggle is not clickable [unverified].
Changing `visibilityToggleIcon` does not change the toggle's accessible name.

defaults.text: Starts masked (`type="password"`).
Size `xs`; not disabled, not read-only, not invalid.
The visibility toggle is shown at the end of the field.
Empty value when neither `value` nor `defaultValue` is given.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `withVisibilityToggle: false`: no toggle button; the text can never be revealed.
`withVisibilityToggleTooltip`: hovering or focusing the toggle shows its name (`Show password` / `Hide password`) as a tooltip.
`visibilityToggleIcon(visible)`: replaces the eye icons with what the function returns for the current state.
`startAddon` / `endAddon`: a filled block before / after the field.
`startElement` / `endElement`: plain content inside the field before / after the text; the end element is placed after the toggle.
`disabled`: field and toggle are disabled, text dimmed.
`readOnly`: the text cannot be edited and the toggle is disabled.
`invalid` (or `aria-invalid`): the field is marked invalid.
`placeholder`: shown while the field is empty.
`maxLength`, `autoComplete`, `autoFocus`, `name`: passed to the native input.
`size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, or responsive): changes height, padding and text size.

builtInText.text: Toggle accessible name while masked: `Show password` (literal, not translated).
Toggle accessible name while shown: `Hide password` (literal, not translated).

keyboard.text: Tab from the field moves to the toggle, then to the next control.
Enter or Space on the focused toggle switches masked and shown (native button) [unverified].

states.text: Masked: `type="password"`, eye-off icon.
Shown: `type="text"`, eye icon.
Disabled, read-only, invalid: as set by the props above.
Focused: standard focus ring on the input or on the toggle.

testApi: `Spectra.findPasswordInput(label)`: by `aria-label`, visible label text or `aria-labelledby`; waits and throws when missing. `Spectra.queryPasswordInput(label)`: `null` when missing.
`getValue()`, `setValue(v)`, `clearValue()`, `paste(text)`, `getPlaceholder()` (`shouldHavePlaceholder`), `getAccessibleDescription()` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription`).
`toggleVisibility()`, `isPasswordVisible()` (true = plain text), `getToggleButton()`, `hasToggleButton()`.
`getStartAddon()`, `getEndAddon()`, `getStartElement()`, `getEndElement()`, `getStartAddonText()`, `getEndAddonText()`, `hasStartAddon()`, `hasEndAddon()`, `hasStartElement()`, `hasEndElement()`.
`getContainer()`, `getContent()`, `getInput()`.
`focus()`, `blur()`, `isFocused()`, `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`.

components.name: PhoneInput

does.text: Shows a dial code button (for example `+62`) at the start and a phone number field after it.
The value is one E.164 string: dial code plus national number with no space or separator (for example `+628123456789`).
Only digits can be typed: every non-digit character typed or pasted is removed.
The number of digits is limited per selected country from phone metadata (the longest valid national length); digits beyond the limit are dropped.
Clicking the dial code button opens a list of countries; each row shows the flag, the country name and the dial code in brackets, for example `(+62)`.
The list has a search field that filters by country name, dial code or country code; matching ignores case.
Choosing a country changes the dial code, keeps the typed digits (cut to the new country's limit) and moves focus to the phone number field.
Choosing a country cannot be undone by choosing it again: the selected country stays selected (no deselect).
Pasting text that starts with `+` fills both parts: the dial code and country are taken from the pasted number and the rest becomes the digits (cut to the limit).
Clearing the digits keeps the selected dial code; the value becomes empty.
A controlled `value` pushed from outside updates the dial code and the digits shown.
Leaving the number field reports the E.164 value, or nothing when the number is empty.

doesNot.text: Letters, spaces, dashes and brackets are never shown in the number field.
The value is empty (not just the dial code) when no digits are entered: the dial code alone is never reported as a value.
No formatting or grouping of the digits while typing.
No validation message of its own; an incomplete or invalid number is not marked invalid (that belongs to `Field`).
No clear button.
The dial code cannot be typed into a field: it is only changed by the list or a pasted `+` number.

defaults.text: Dial code `+62` (Indonesia) with an empty number, unless the browser time zone maps to another country [unverified].
The country list is searchable.
Size `xs`; not disabled, not read-only, not invalid.
Number field type `tel`, numeric keyboard.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `value` / `defaultValue`: an E.164 string sets the dial code, country and digits.
`maxDigit`: replaces the per-country digit limit with this number.
`filter: false`: the country list has no search field.
`filterPlaceholder`: replaces the placeholder of the list's search field.
`placeholder`: replaces the number field placeholder.
`aria-label`: replaces the number field's accessible name.
`disabled`: dial code button and number field are disabled.
`readOnly`: the number cannot be edited and the country list cannot be opened; the dial code button is skipped by Tab.
`invalid` (or `aria-invalid`): the field is marked invalid.
`size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, or responsive): changes the field size and the width of the country list.

builtInText.text: Number field placeholder: `Enter phone number` (locale en, passed through `t()`).
Number field accessible name when no `aria-label`: `Phone number` (locale en, passed through `t()`).
Country list search placeholder: `Search` (locale en, passed through `t()`).
Country names are English region names.

keyboard.text: Tab moves from the dial code button to the number field; the dial code button is a combobox.

states.text: Dial code list closed or open.
Disabled, read-only, invalid: as set by the props above.
Focused: standard focus on the number field or the dial code button.

testApi: `Spectra.findPhoneInput(label)`: by the number field's accessible name; `Spectra.queryPhoneInput(label)`: `null` when missing.
`getValue()`: dial code plus number (E.164); `getPhoneNumberValue()`: digits only; `getDialCode()`: for example `+62`; `setValue(v)` (non-digits stripped), `clearValue()`.
`getDialCodeButton()`, `hasDialCodeButton()`, `openDialCodeDropdown()`, `isDialCodeDropdownOpen()`, `getPanel()`, `selectDialCode(dialCodeOrCountry)`.
`filterDialCode(q)`, `getDialCodeFilterValue()`, `clearDialCodeFilter()`, `getDialCodeFilterInput()`, `hasDialCodeFilterInput()`.
`getContainer()`, `getContent()`, `getInput()`, `focus()`, `blur()`, `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`.

components.name: Popover

does.text: Clicking the trigger opens a floating panel with the `children` under it, left-aligned (`bottom-start`) with an 8 px gap; clicking the trigger again closes it.
The panel is a rounded surface with a shadow, sized to its content, and holds any content (text, forms, lists, buttons) that stays interactive.
The panel is not in the page while closed; it fades and moves in and out over about 150 ms and is still in the page during the exit.

The trigger carries `data-popover-state="open"` or `"closed"`, `aria-expanded` true or false, and `data-popover-controls` equal to the `data-popover-id` of its own panel (two open popovers never read each other's panel).
The panel renders on `document.body` (a portal), above sibling content and outside any clipping ancestor.
When there is no room on the preferred side the panel flips to the opposite side and shifts to stay inside the viewport (8 px margin); it follows the trigger when the page scrolls or resizes.
Clicking outside the panel and the trigger closes it; a click on an element marked `data-ignore-click-outside` does not.
Escape closes it; when the popover sits in a Dialog, Escape closes the popover first and the Dialog on the next press.
The page behind stays usable: no backdrop, no scroll lock, focus is not trapped and not moved into the panel on open.
Nested popovers: clicking or pressing inside an inner popover's panel does not close the outer one.
`onOpenChange(open)` fires whenever the popover asks to open or close (trigger, outside click, Escape, hover).
Passing `trigger` props (such as `onClick`, `aria-label`, or a ref) through is kept: the trigger's own handlers still run.

doesNot.text: Has no `role` (not `dialog`, not `tooltip`), no `aria-modal`, and no `aria-haspopup` on the trigger.
Does not dim or block the page and does not trap focus (use Dialog for that).
Is not a tooltip: it takes rich, interactive content, and a hover-opened popover stays open while the pointer moves onto the panel.
Does not open on keyboard focus of the trigger in `hover` mode (only on pointer hover).
Does not close on outside click when `closeOnClickOutside` is false, nor on Escape when `closeOnEscape` is false.
Does not have a `disabled` prop; a disabled trigger (a disabled button) simply cannot open it.
With `triggerOn="none"` neither click nor hover on the trigger opens it.
A click on the trigger while open is not an outside click: it toggles closed once.
Does not show an arrow unless `arrow` is set.

defaults.text: Closed at start (`defaultOpen` false); `triggerOn` `click`; `placement` `bottom-start`; `offset` 8 px; `closeOnClickOutside` true; `closeOnEscape` true; `arrow` false; `panelWidth` `content`; `portal` true.
Hover delays when `triggerOn="hover"`: opens after 100 ms, closes 150 ms after the pointer leaves trigger and panel.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `triggerOn="hover"`: opens on pointer hover instead of click, and clicking the trigger does not toggle it; `delay` (number, or `{ open, close }` in ms) changes the delays.
`triggerOn="none"`: the caller drives `open`; the component is a positioned container.
`open` with `onOpenChange`: controlled; the popover opens and closes only as the caller sets `open`.
`placement`: 12 values (`top`, `top-start`, `top-end`, `bottom`, ..., `right-end`).
`offset`: gap in px between trigger and panel.
`arrow`: a small pointer from the panel to the trigger in the panel colour; `arrowPosition` (`start`, `center`, `end` or px) and `arrowOffset` (minimum px from the panel edge) move it.
`panelWidth`: `trigger` makes the panel as wide as the trigger; a number is px; a string is any CSS width (`15rem`, `max-content`).
`portal={false}`: the panel renders inline next to the trigger; `portalRoot`: the panel renders into that element instead of `document.body`.
`positionReference`: a virtual element the panel anchors to instead of the trigger.
`className`: added to the panel.
`closeOnClickOutside={false}` and `closeOnEscape={false}`: see `Popover#17`.

builtInText.text: None: the panel shows only the `children`.

keyboard.text: Enter or Space on a trigger that is not a native button toggles it (a native button toggles through its click); Escape closes it; Tab is not trapped and moves on in page order.

states.text: Closed, open (trigger `data-popover-state`); during the exit animation the panel is still mounted while the state reads closed.
No loading, error or disabled state of its own.

testApi: Finders: `Spectra.findPopover(label)` and `Spectra.queryPopover(label)` by the trigger's accessible name.
Parts: `getTrigger`, `getContent` (the panel; throws when closed), `getArrow` (throws when absent), `getContainer` (panel if open, else trigger).
Readers (each with a polling `should*`): `isOpen`, `hasArrow`, `isDisabled` (the trigger).
Actions: `open`, `close({ method: 'clickOutside' | 'escape' | 'trigger' })`, `toggle`, `hover`, `unhover` (for `triggerOn="hover"`), `focus`, `blur` (the trigger).

components.name: PopupMenu

does.text: Clicking the trigger (its single child) opens a floating action list under it, left-aligned (`bottom-start`) with an 8 px gap; clicking the trigger again closes it.
The list is a Menu: items, icons, danger items, group headers, separators, hidden and disabled items, links and tooltips behave as in `Menu#2` to `Menu#12`.
Panel mounting and the fade and move over about 150 ms are as in `Popover#3`.
The panel renders on `document.body` as in `Popover#5`, so it sits above an AppLayout side panel and is not clipped by a scrolling parent.
When there is no room the panel flips and shifts as in `Popover#6`.
The trigger carries `data-popupmenu-state` `open` or `closed`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="menu"` (a value the child already sets is kept), plus `data-popover-state` as in `Popover#4`.
A trigger that is `disabled` or `aria-disabled` carries `data-popupmenu-disabled`; a disabled button trigger does not open the menu.
Picking an enabled leaf item runs its `onClick` and closes the menu; picking an item that has sub-items does not close it.
Clicking outside the panel and the trigger closes the menu (as in `Popover#7`).
Escape closes the menu (as in `Popover#8`).
Opened by click, the menu list takes focus, so Arrow Down reaches the first item at once; closing by Escape or by picking an item gives focus back to the element that held it before.
Sub-items always open as flyout panels to the right of their parent item (as in `Menu#10`); picking a sub-item closes the whole menu.
A disabled item stays in the list and behaves as in `Menu#6`; clicking it does not close the menu.
`onOpenChange(open)` fires as in `Popover#11`, also on an item pick.
`header`, `footer`, `emptyContent`, `ariaLabel`, `ariaLabelledby`, `tabIndex` and the other Menu props pass to the list.

doesNot.text: Does not close on item pick when `closeOnSelect` is false.
No imperative show/hide handle: to open it from elsewhere the caller passes `open`.
Does not trap focus and does not block the page behind it (`Popover#9`, `Popover#14`); a click there closes the menu.
Does not render submenus inline (`expand`); the `submenuMode` prop has no effect.
Does not open from Arrow Down or Arrow Up on the trigger; Enter or Space on a button trigger opens it like a click.
`closeOnEscape={false}` keeps the menu open when Escape is pressed; an item pick or an outside click still closes it.
Clicking the trigger while the menu is open toggles it closed once (as in `Popover#20`).
A child that is not a single element (text, fragment) gets no trigger behaviour.
A menu opened by hover does not take focus and does not return focus on close (unless `focusOnOpen`).

defaults.text: Defaults as in `Popover#22`, `Popover#23`, with `portal` true and `closeOnSelect` true; closed at start (`defaultOpen` false); `focusOnOpen` true when `triggerOn` is `click`, else false.
Outside click always closes; there is no prop to turn it off.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `triggerOn="hover"`: as in `Popover#24`; moving onto the panel keeps it open.
`triggerOn="none"`: as in `Popover#19`; only `open` opens it.
`open` and `onOpenChange`: controlled (`Popover#26`); `defaultOpen`: uncontrolled initial state.
`placement` (12 values), `offset`: as in `Popover#27`, `Popover#28`.
`positionReference`: as in `Popover#32`.
`portal={false}`: as in `Popover#31`.
`closeOnSelect={false}`: item picks leave the menu open (`PopupMenu#16`).
`focusOnOpen`: forces the focus handling of `PopupMenu#11` on or off whatever `triggerOn` is.
`triggerFlyoutOn="hover"` and `flyoutDelay`: as in `Menu#11`.

builtInText.text: `No options available` when `items` is empty or all hidden (as in `Menu#37`); otherwise none.

keyboard.text: Enter or Space on a button trigger opens it; Tab and Shift+Tab move on to the list and its Tab-stop item.
In the open list: Arrow Down, Arrow Up, Home, End, Enter and Space as in `Menu#13` and `Menu#39`; Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.

states.text: Closed, open; trigger enabled or disabled; items as in `Menu#40`.
No loading or error state.

testApi: Finders: `Spectra.findPopupMenu(label)` and `Spectra.queryPopupMenu(label)` by the trigger's accessible name.
Parts: `getTrigger`, `getContainer`, `getMenu`, `getList`, `getItems`, `getItem`, `getIcon`, `getSubmenu`, `getSubmenuIcon`, `getGroupHeaders`, `getGroupHeader`.

Readers (each with a polling `should*`): `isDisplayed`, `isOpen`, `isDisabled`, `getItemCount`, `getItemLabels`, `hasItem`, `getItemDestination`, `isItemDisabled`, `isItemDanger`, `hasIcon`, `hasSubmenu`, `isSubmenuOpen`, `getGroupHeaderLabels`.
Actions: `open`, `close({ method })`, `toggle`, `hover`, `unhover`, `focus`, `blur`, `clickItem`, `openSubmenu`, `closeSubmenu`.
The panel is portalled (`portal` true); the wrapper finds it through the trigger's `data-popover-controls`.

components.name: ProgressBar

does.text: Shows a track with a fill whose width is the percentage of `value` against `max` (the unrounded percentage, e.g. `33.333333333333336%`), clamped to 0-100%
The percentage text is `<n>%` with n rounded to a whole number (`Math.round`: 33.4 reads `33%`, 33.5 reads `34%`)
`value` above `max` shows a full bar and `100%`; a negative `value` shows an empty bar and `0%`
A missing or NaN `value` counts as 0; a `max` that is missing, 0, negative or NaN counts as 100

The track has `role="progressbar"`, `aria-label="Progress"`, `aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` always 100 (not `max`), `aria-valuenow` = the rounded percentage (not the raw `value`), `aria-valuetext` = the percentage text (or `<n>%` when `formatValue` returns a non-string)

Indeterminate: the fill is an animated sliding segment, no width, no percentage text; the track has `role="progressbar"` and `aria-label="Progress"` but no `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` or `aria-valuetext`
The root carries `data-severity`, the severity name
Changing `value` moves the fill with a 300 ms width transition

doesNot.text: No percentage text by default (`valuePosition` is `none`)
No label prop and no visible caption; the only name on the track is the fixed `Progress`; an accessible name for the finder comes from `aria-label` on the root
No file sizes, bytes, units or speed: it shows a percentage only (nothing uses 1024 or 1000)
No "Complete" text, color change or event at 100%
Indeterminate mode never shows text, even with `valuePosition` set, and ignores `striped`
`aria-valuemax` does not follow `max`; `ProgressBar#5`
`animated` alone does nothing: the stripe movement runs only when `striped` is also on
No `aria-live` region: a changing value is not announced by itself; assistive tech reads `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` only when it queries the bar.
`value` is ignored in indeterminate mode (no width, no `aria-valuenow`).
No built-in upload or file handling: for an upload the app passes the percentage as `value`; the bar never reads bytes or files itself.

defaults.text: `max` 100, `mode` `determinate`, `severity` `primary`, `size` `md` (track 8 px high), `striped` false, `animated` false, `rounded` false (track `rounded-lg`, square fill), `valuePosition` `none`
Track heights by size: `sm` 6 px, `md` 8 px, `lg` 10 px, `xl` 12 px

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `valuePosition="left"` / `"right"`: the percentage text sits before / after the track on one row (`progressbar.valueText`)
`valuePosition="inside"`: the text is rendered inside the fill (`progressbar.inlineValue`), not as `valueText`

`formatValue(value, percentage)`: its result replaces the percentage text; it receives the raw `value` (0 when missing) and the unrounded clamped percentage; a string result is also used as `aria-valuetext`
`mode="indeterminate"`: see `ProgressBar#6`, `ProgressBar#13`
`severity` `primary` | `secondary` | `danger` | `success` | `warning` | `info`: fill color and `data-severity`
`striped`: diagonal stripes on the fill; with `animated` they move
`rounded`: fully rounded track and fill
`size` `sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`: track height and value text size (`lg`/`xl` use the larger label size)
`max`: sets the scale the percentage is computed against

builtInText.text: `Progress` (aria-label of the track, fixed English, not translated)

states.text: Determinate (`aria-valuenow` present) or indeterminate (absent)
Empty (0%) and full (100%) are plain values; no extra visual state

testApi: `Spectra.findProgressBar(label, options?)` / `Spectra.queryProgressBar(label, options?)`: match the root or the track div by accessible name. `find` waits the implicit wait and throws; `query` returns null when absent.
`getContainer(options?)`, `getTrackElement(options?)`, `getFillElement(options?)`, `element`
`getValueTextElement(options?)` / `getInlineValueElement(options?)`: element or null
`hasValueText(options?)` / `shouldHaveValueText()` / `shouldNotHaveValueText()`; `hasInlineValue(options?)` / `shouldHaveInlineValue()` / `shouldNotHaveInlineValue()`
`getValueText(options?)` / `shouldHaveValueText('80%')`: text of the side value, else the inside value, else null
`getValue()` / `shouldHaveValue(n)`: reads `aria-valuenow` (the rounded percentage; null when indeterminate)
`getMin()` / `shouldHaveMin(n)`, `getMax()` / `shouldHaveMax(n)`: read `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` (0 and 100)
`getAriaValueText()` / `shouldHaveAriaValueText(s)`
`getPercentage()` / `shouldHavePercentage(n)`: computed from the aria values, rounded, clamped; null when indeterminate
`getSeverity(options?)` / `shouldHaveSeverity(s)`: root `data-severity`
`isIndeterminate()` / `shouldBeIndeterminate()` / `shouldNotBeIndeterminate()`
`is*`/`has*` readers wait `probeTimeout` (500 ms); sub-part getters wait the implicit wait.

components.name: Radio

does.text: Clicking an unselected radio (its circle or its label text) selects it: a filled primary dot appears inside the circle and the radio the group had selected before is cleared.
A radio is checked exactly when its `value` equals the `RadioGroup` value; the group holds the selection, the radio does not.
The radio's `onChange` receives the browser change event, and the group's `onChange` receives this radio's `value`; both fire only when an unselected radio is picked.
With `label`, the label text is shown beside the circle and is the accessible name; clicking it selects the radio.
With `description`, the secondary text is shown under the label and linked as the accessible description (`aria-describedby`).
The group's `name` is put on the input, so the options submit as one field.
A radio is disabled when its own `disabled` or the group's `disabled` is set; it greys out, shows a not-allowed cursor, and cannot be selected.
Invalid (own `invalid` or the group's) turns the circle border and dot red; own `invalid` also turns the label and description red.
Keyboard focus shows a circular halo around the circle; blurring removes it.
The dot scales in and out (about 0.2 s) when the checked state changes.

doesNot.text: A radio cannot be deselected by clicking it again; only picking another radio in the group changes the selection.
Outside a `RadioGroup` a radio is never checked and selecting it has no visible effect.
The radio input itself carries no `aria-invalid`; the invalid state is exposed only on the group (`aria-invalid="true"` on the `radiogroup`).
The group's `invalid` does not turn the label and description red, only the circle and dot.
Clicking the description text does not select the radio.
A disabled radio does not call `onChange` or the group's `onChange`.
Without `label` and `description` there is no visible text and no accessible name unless `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is given.
A radio cannot opt out of the group's `disabled` or `invalid` (the group state wins).

defaults.text: Unchecked, enabled, valid, no label, no description.
`size` `xs` (16 px circle, 8 px dot); `sm` 20 px, `md` 24 px, `lg` 28 px.
A generated id is used when `id` is not given; the label's `for` and the description id follow it.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `value` (required): the string this radio stands for.
`label`: visible label text; `description`: secondary text under it.
`disabled`, `invalid`: per-item state as above.
`size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, also per breakpoint; the label and description text step with it.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `id`, `tabIndex`: passed to the input; `aria-describedby` replaces the description link.
`className`, `style`: applied to the outer wrapper when a label or description exists, else to the circle.
`onChange`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onClick`: handlers on the input.

keyboard.text: Tab moves focus into the radio set and Shift+Tab out; Space selects the focused radio.
With a group `name`, the Arrow keys move focus and selection between the radios of the group; without `name` each radio is its own tab stop.
A disabled radio is skipped by Tab.

states.text: Unchecked: empty circle, dot scaled to zero.
Checked: primary border, filled dot.
Focused: halo around the circle.
Hover and pressed: faint halo around the circle (primary, red when invalid), not when disabled.
Disabled: grey border, dot and text (38 % opacity), checked or not.
Invalid: red border and dot; red label and description only when the radio itself is `invalid`.

testApi: `Spectra.findRadio(name)`: by label text or `aria-label`; `Spectra.queryRadio(name)`: `null` when missing.
`select()` (clicks the input; throws `WangsUITestingError` when disabled), `isChecked()` (`shouldBeChecked()`, `shouldNotBeChecked()`), `getValue()` (the `value` attribute).

`isDisabled()`, `isInvalid()` (true from the input's `aria-invalid`, its container, or the enclosing `radiogroup`'s `aria-invalid="true"`; a radio's own `invalid` prop alone is not seen), `focus()`, `blur()`.
`getInput()`, `getBox()`, `getIcon()`, `getContainer()`, `hasIcon()`.
`getLabel()`, `getLabelText()`, `hasLabel()`, `getDescription()`, `getDescriptionText()`, `hasDescription()`.

components.name: RadioGroup

does.text: Renders a `role="radiogroup"` container holding its `Radio` children; it adds no visible border, label or text of its own.
Exactly one child `Radio` is checked: the one whose `value` equals the group value.
Clicking an unchecked `Radio` checks it and unchecks the previously checked one.
Clicking a `Radio` calls the group `onChange` with the new string value (not an event), and the `Radio`'s own `onChange` first.
With `defaultValue` the group keeps its own selection: the initial `Radio` is checked and later clicks move the check.
With `value` (controlled) the checked `Radio` follows the prop; a click only reports through `onChange` and the check moves only when the parent passes the new `value`.
Group `disabled` disables every child `Radio`: none can be checked by clicking.
Group `invalid` shows every child `Radio` in its invalid (danger) style and sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the container.
`name` is applied to every child radio input, so the inputs share one native radio group and submit with the form.

Spreads other attributes (`id`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `onClick`, `data-*`) onto the container, so the container is found by its accessible name and read by its description.

doesNot.text: Does not render a label, helper text or error text itself; those come from a surrounding `Field` or the caller.
Does not allow selecting more than one option.
Clicking the already checked `Radio` does not uncheck it and does not call `onChange`.
A value that matches no child `Radio` checks nothing and shows no error.
A child `Radio` cannot opt back in when the group is `disabled`; its own `disabled` prop only adds to the group state (it never overrides it).
Does not set `aria-disabled` or `disabled` on the container; disabled shows only on the child inputs.
Does not select a `Radio` by default: with no `value` and no `defaultValue` nothing is checked.

defaults.text: `orientation` is `vertical`: options stacked in a column with a gap of 16px.
`disabled` is false and `invalid` is false.
Container carries `aria-invalid="false"` while valid (it is always present, not only when invalid).
Nothing is checked and no `name` is set.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `orientation: 'horizontal'`: options sit in one row and wrap to the next line when the width runs out.
`disabled`: every option is greyed out, shows a not-allowed cursor and cannot be changed.
`invalid`: every option turns danger coloured; an explicit `aria-invalid` replaces the value taken from `invalid`.
`name`: the same `name` on every child input (native form submission).
`value` / `defaultValue`: which option is checked first; `value` makes the group controlled.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling of the container only.

keyboard.text: Tab moves focus onto the checked radio (or the first one when none is checked), and the focus ring shows on that option.
With a shared `name` the arrow keys move focus and the selection between enabled options, and Space checks the focused option.
Without `name` the inputs are not one native group, so arrow keys do not move the selection.

states.text: Unchecked option: empty circle with a neutral outline; checked option: filled dot in the primary colour.
Disabled: dimmed circle and label, no hover or press halo, no change on click.
Invalid: danger-coloured circle, dot and label; hover and focus halos in the danger colour.
Focused option: focus halo around the circle only for keyboard focus.
Loading, readonly: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findRadioGroup(label)` finds the container by accessible name (`aria-label`, label text); `Spectra.queryRadioGroup(label)` returns `null` when missing.
`getContainer()`: the `role="radiogroup"` element (the root itself or its closest ancestor).
`getValue()`: value of the checked radio, `undefined` when none is checked.

`getSelectedRadio()`: the checked `Radio` wrapper (throws when none is checked); `getRadio(value)`: a `Radio` wrapper by `value` (throws when missing); `getAllRadios()`: every `Radio` wrapper in order.
`select(value)`: checks the radio with that value (throws when missing or when the group is disabled).
`isDisabled()` (`shouldBeDisabled()`): true when the container has `aria-disabled="true"` or `disabled`, or every radio input is disabled.
`isInvalid()` (`shouldBeInvalid()`): true when the container has `aria-invalid="true"`.

`getDescription()`, `hasDescription()` (`shouldHaveDescription()`), `getDescriptionText()`: the element named by the container's `aria-describedby` (a caller's hint, or a `Field`'s helper/error text).

components.name: RangeNumberInput

does.text: Shows two number fields, the lower bound first and the upper bound second, with a minus (dash) icon between them.
The value is a pair `[lower, upper]`; each side may be empty (`undefined`).
`onChange` fires with the whole pair every time either field changes.
The upper field cannot go below the lower field: a value typed below the lower value is raised to it when the upper field loses focus.
The lower field cannot go above the upper field: a value typed above the upper value is lowered to it when the lower field loses focus [unverified].
After the lower field is cleared, the upper field's floor goes back to the component's own `min` (typing `-3` in the upper field with `min` 0 shows `0` after blur).
The `min` and `max` props apply to both fields (clamp on blur or Enter, as in `NumberInput#1`).
A decimal typed or pasted into an integer range (the default) is shown rounded to a whole number (`2.5` shows `3`) and stays after leaving the field.
`step`, `showControls`, `controlOrientation`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `padStart`, `useGrouping`, `minFractionDigits`, `maxFractionDigits`, `locale`, `size` apply to both fields alike.
`onClick`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp` come from the outer wrapper, so focus moving from one field to the other also fires `onBlur` then `onFocus` [unverified].

doesNot.text: No error message, no invalid look when the lower value is above the upper value: the other side is clamped instead.
The two fields cannot be given different `step`, `min`, `max`, size or format.
No addons or elements around the fields (`startAddon`, `endAddon`, `startElement`, `endElement` do not exist here).
No default `aria-label` on the two fields; the name is on the wrapper only.
No slider or draggable handles.

defaults.text: Both fields empty, whole numbers (`minFractionDigits` and `maxFractionDigits` 0), no thousand grouping.
Locale `en-US` (not the provider's active locale).
`allowEmptyValue` true, `step` 1, no stepper buttons, size `xs`, not disabled, not read-only, not invalid.
Both fields show the placeholder `Enter number` when empty.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `value` / `defaultValue`: a pair that fills the two fields.
`minPlaceholder` / `maxPlaceholder`: placeholder of that field; `placeholder`: for both when the specific one is not set.
`allowEmptyValue: false`: a cleared field falls back to a number at once (lower field to `min` or 0, upper field to `max` or 0) [unverified].
`showControls`: increment and decrement buttons on each field; `controlOrientation: 'horizontal'` puts decrement before and increment after each field.
`minName` / `maxName`, `minId` / `maxId`: name and id of the lower and upper field; there is no fallback from name to id.
`autoFocus`: the lower field gets focus on mount.
`disabled`: both fields and their steppers are disabled.
`readOnly`: both fields are read-only and their steppers disabled.
`invalid`: both fields are marked invalid (`aria-invalid`).
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `id`: set on the wrapper.

builtInText.text: Placeholder of each empty field: `Enter number` (locale en, passed through `t()`).
Stepper buttons: `Increase value by {step}` and `Decrease value by {step}` (literal, not translated).

keyboard.text: Tab moves from the lower field to the upper field; each field follows `NumberInput#38` to `NumberInput#42` (arrows by `step`, Home and End to `min` and `max`, Enter clamps).

states.text: Both empty, one filled, both filled.
Disabled, read-only, invalid: as set by the props above.
Focused: standard focus ring on the field in use.

testApi: `Spectra.findRangeNumberInput(name)`: by the accessible name (wrapper `aria-label`, or a label linked to `minId` / `maxId`); `Spectra.queryRangeNumberInput(name)`: `null` when missing.

`getValue()` (both), `getMinValue()`, `getMaxValue()` (formatted text, `""` when empty); `setValue({min,max})`, `setMinValue(n)`, `setMaxValue(n)`, `clearValue()`, `clearMinValue()`, `clearMaxValue()`.
`getMinInput()`, `getMaxInput()` (`NumberInput` wrappers), `getMinInputElement()`, `getMaxInputElement()`, `getContainer()`, `getSeparatorIcon()`, `hasSeparatorIcon()`.
`focus(target?)`, `blur(target?)` with `'min'` or `'max'`: `blur()` is the step that clamps.

`incrementMin()`, `decrementMin()`, `incrementMax()`, `decrementMax()`, `getMinIncrementButton()`, `getMinDecrementButton()`, `getMaxIncrementButton()`, `getMaxDecrementButton()` (only with `showControls`).
`stepUpMin()`, `stepDownMin()`, `stepUpMax()`, `stepDownMax()` (`standard`, `large`, `fine`), `jumpToMin()`, `jumpToMax()`.
`isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`.

components.name: RangeSlider

does.text: Shows a track with two round handles and a filled bar between them; the value is always a pair `[start, end]` and `onChange` receives the whole pair.
The handles are `role="slider"`: the first has `aria-label` `Start`, the second `End` (English); with an `aria-label` on the slider they read `<label> (Start)` and `<label> (End)`.
The slider root is `role="group"` carrying the `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` given to the component.

Each handle exposes `aria-valuenow`; the start handle has `aria-valuemin` = `min` and `aria-valuemax` = the current end value, the end handle has `aria-valuemin` = the current start value and `aria-valuemax` = `max`.

Clicking the track (not a handle) moves the handle nearest to the click to that spot at once and starts dragging it; when both are equally near, a click below the start value moves the start handle, any other click moves the end handle.
Pressing on a handle only starts dragging it; the value does not jump on press.
While dragging, the handle follows the pointer and `onChange` fires continuously on every move; there is no separate commit callback.
Every value snaps to `step` counted from `min` and stays inside `min`..`max`; dragging past either end stops at the end.
The two handles never cross: the start handle stops at the end value, the end handle stops at the start value, and with `minRange` they stop that distance apart.
Handles are focusable with Tab; the start handle comes first.

A handle that is hovered, focused or being dragged shows a tooltip with its value (`String(value)`, or the `formatTooltip` result) with no delay, and the tooltip closes at once when hover, focus and drag end.
The filled bar and the handle positions move with the values; they animate over 150 ms except while dragging.
A pair set from outside (controlled `value`) moves both handles and the bar; an empty controlled value spans the whole `min`..`max` range.
Vertical sliders put `min` at the bottom and `max` at the top.

doesNot.text: Does not accept one number: the value is a pair, and it is not a single-value slider (that is `Slider`).
Does not swap or reorder the handles when one is dragged past the other.
Does not let the user type exact numbers; no input box.
Does not change the value when `disabled`: pointer, track click and keys are ignored and the handles cannot be reached with Tab.
Does not draw tick lines; `marks` shows labels only, and clicking a mark label does nothing.
Does not snap marks to the step; a mark sits at its own `value` position.
Does not show any visible change for `invalid`; it only sets `aria-invalid` on both handles.
Does not translate the `marks` labels or the `formatTooltip` text; they show exactly as given.
Does not scroll the page on touch drags (the control disables touch panning on itself).
Keyboard keys other than the ones listed under Keyboard do nothing and are not stopped (no `preventDefault`).

defaults.text: `min` 0, `max` 100, `step` 1, `minRange` 0, `size` `sm`, `orientation` `horizontal`, `showTooltip` true, `tooltipAlwaysOn` false, `disabled` false, `invalid` false, no marks.
Uncontrolled with no `defaultValue`: starts as `[min, max]`, the full range.
Sizes: `xs` track 4 px and handle 12 px, `sm` track 8 px and handle 16 px, `md` track 12 px and handle 20 px.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `min`, `max`, `step`: set the range and the grid the handles snap to.
`minRange`: the handles cannot get closer than this distance; start at 20 and end at 40 with `minRange` 20 means ArrowRight on the start handle and ArrowLeft on the end handle change nothing.
`orientation: 'vertical'`: both handles get `aria-orientation="vertical"` and the slider stands up; `horizontal` handles get `aria-orientation="horizontal"`.
`marks`: shows a label under (horizontal) or right of (vertical) the track at each mark `value`; the label is the mark's `label`, or its `value` when no `label`.
`showTooltip: false`: no tooltip at all, and `tooltipAlwaysOn` then has no effect.
`tooltipAlwaysOn: true`: both tooltips stay open whether or not a handle is hovered, focused or dragged.
`formatTooltip`: the tooltip text is the returned string for each handle's value.
`disabled: true`: handles and bar turn to the muted disabled colours, the root and handles get `aria-disabled="true"`, tab order is removed from the handles, and the pointer is ignored.
`invalid: true`: both handles get `aria-invalid="true"`.
`size`: accepts a responsive value (different size per breakpoint).
The slider itself ignores `id` and `aria-describedby` (it only uses `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`).

builtInText.text: Handle names `Start` and `End` (English; translated through the locale), joined to the slider's `aria-label` as `<label> (Start)` / `<label> (End)`.
No visible text of its own; tooltip text is the value number, mark text is the `marks` label or number.

keyboard.text: On a focused handle ArrowRight or ArrowUp adds one `step`; ArrowLeft or ArrowDown subtracts one `step`, in either orientation.
PageUp adds 10 steps and PageDown subtracts 10 steps.
Home sets the handle to `min` and End to `max`, each stopped by the other handle (and `minRange`); Home on the start handle reaches `min`, End on the end handle reaches `max`.
Handled keys do not scroll the page; each key moves only the focused handle.
Tab moves from the start handle to the end handle.

states.text: Default: both handles enabled with the full-range or given values.
Dragging: the pressed handle has `data-dragging` and scales up slightly; its tooltip is open.
Focused handle: shows a focus ring when focused with the keyboard (`:focus-visible`).
Disabled: see `RangeSlider#35` and `RangeSlider#18`.
Invalid: see `RangeSlider#36`. Loading, selected, read-only states: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findRangeSlider(label)` / `Spectra.queryRangeSlider(label)`: finds by the root's accessible name (`aria-label`, or the label text named by `aria-labelledby`); `query` gives `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindRangeSlider(label)`.
`getValue()` (`shouldHaveValue([start, end])`) reads both handles' `aria-valuenow`; `setValue([start, end])` moves each handle with keyboard steps (works on step grids, one key press per step).
`getStartHandle()`, `getEndHandle()`: the two `role="slider"` elements; `getContainer()`: the root.
`stepUp(n?)`, `stepDown(n?)`: ArrowRight / ArrowLeft n times on the END handle only; `jumpToMin()`: Home on the START handle; `jumpToMax()`: End on the END handle.
`isDisabled()` (`shouldBeDisabled()`): true when both handles have `aria-disabled="true"`; `isInvalid()` (`shouldBeInvalid()`); `hasMarks()` (`shouldHaveMarks()`).
`focus()` focuses the start handle; `blur()`.

components.name: ScrollArea

does.text: Content taller than the area's height limit (`height` / `maxHeight`) scrolls vertically inside the area; the native scrollbar is hidden and a custom rounded thumb is drawn instead.
The thumb shows only when the content overflows along a scrollable axis; without overflow there is no thumb.
With the default `variant="hover"` the thumb is visible only while the pointer is over the area or focus is inside it; with `variant="always"` it is always visible while content overflows.
Dragging the thumb scrolls the content in proportion; the thumb moves while scrolling by wheel, keyboard or script.

`orientation` selects the scrollable axis: `vertical` only vertical, `horizontal` only horizontal, `both` both axes with an own thumb for each (the thumbs leave room for each other in the corner). Only the matching axis scrolls; the other axis is hidden.
The scrollable viewport is a focusable region (`role="region"`, `tabIndex` 0) that carries `data-orientation`, `data-size` and `data-variant`.
Scrolling is contained: wheel or touch scrolling at an edge does not scroll the page behind (`overscroll-behavior: contain`).

Dimension props (`width`, `height`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight`) are applied to the outer frame; a number or digit string means pixels, other strings (`50%`, `20rem`, `calc(...)`) pass through.

Spacing props (`m*`) apply to the outer frame, padding props (`p*`) to the viewport (padding scrolls with the content), `bg` and `radius` to the frame; the frame clips its content (`overflow-hidden`).

With `scrollShadows`, content fades out at an edge where more content is hidden: at the top only the bottom edge fades, in the middle both, at the end only the top (1.5rem fade); the viewport reads `data-shadow-top` / `data-shadow-bottom` `true` or `false` accordingly (and `data-shadow-left` / `data-shadow-right` for horizontal).
Shadows are removed again when `scrollShadows` is switched off, and are never shown when the content does not overflow.

doesNot.text: It does not scroll when the content fits; it does not draw a thumb then.
It does not show the browser's native scrollbar.
It does not virtualize: all children stay in the DOM (use DataTable or a virtualised primitive for large lists).
It does not set an accessible name by itself: without `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` the region is unnamed.
Clicking the thumb does not scroll or jump the content (only dragging it does).
In `vertical` mode horizontal overflow is clipped and no horizontal thumb exists (and vice versa).
It does not show a focus outline on the viewport (`focus:outline-none`); with `variant="hover"` the thumb appearing is the focus cue.

defaults.text: `orientation` `vertical`, `size` `sm` (6px thumb), `variant` `hover`, `overscrollBehavior` `contain`, `scrollShadows` off, `tabIndex` 0, `role` `region`.
Thumb thickness by `size`: `xs` 4px, `sm` 6px, `md` 8px, `lg` 12px; minimum thumb length 24px.
