onlyWhenConfigured.text: `scrollShadows`: edge fades and `data-scroll-shadows` on the viewport (the attribute exists only when on); see `ScrollArea#10`.
`orientation="horizontal"` / `"both"`: horizontal scrolling (`both` scrolls either way).
`size`: thumb thickness (accepts a responsive value).
`variant="always"`: thumb always visible when content overflows.
`overscrollBehavior` `auto` / `none`: lets scroll chain to the page (`auto`) or also blocks the bounce (`none`).
`tabIndex`, `role`: replace the viewport's defaults; `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` name the region.
`testID`: `data-testid` on the viewport.
`flex`, `grow`, `shrink`, `fullWidth`, `fullHeight`: sizing inside a flex parent (`fullWidth` 100% wide, `fullHeight` 100% tall).

keyboard.text: Tab focuses the viewport (it is in the tab order, `tabIndex` 0); a focused scroller scrolls with arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home/End and Space (browser default).

states.text: Overflowing / not overflowing (thumb shown or hidden).
Scroll position: at top, middle, at bottom (with `scrollShadows` the fades and `data-shadow-*` follow it).
Focused: standard focus, thumb visible under `variant="hover"`; hovered: thumb visible under `variant="hover"` and a darker thumb on thumb hover.
Disabled, loading: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findScrollArea(name)`: the viewport (`role="region"` with `data-orientation`) found by `aria-label`; `Spectra.queryScrollArea(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getOrientation()`: `vertical` / `horizontal` / `both` from `data-orientation`; `shouldHaveOrientation`.

`hasScrollShadows()`: true when `data-scroll-shadows` exists; `hasTopShadow()` / `hasBottomShadow()`: `data-shadow-top` / `data-shadow-bottom` is `true` (and `should*` forms); there is no wrapper reader for left/right shadows.
`isScrollable()`: scrollHeight > clientHeight or scrollWidth > clientWidth; `shouldBeScrollable()`.
`getScrollTop()`: current `scrollTop`; `shouldHaveScrollTop(n)` / `shouldNotHaveScrollTop(n)`.
`scrollToTop()` / `scrollToBottom()`: set `scrollTop` and fire a `scroll` event (web only; mobile throws not implemented).
`scrollTo(label)`: finds the inner item by its accessible name or text and scrolls it into view; returns the element; throws when absent.

components.name: SearchButton

does.text: Collapsed, it shows only an icon-only search button; no input is visible.
Clicking the search button expands an inline box (back arrow, text input, clear X) in its place and puts focus in the input.
Typing alone changes nothing in the table; the search is applied only on Enter.
Enter applies the query trimmed of leading/trailing spaces and returns the table to page 1.

A row matches when one of its values contains the whole query as a case-insensitive substring, or when every whitespace-separated word of the query appears somewhere in the row's values (any order, words may sit in different columns).
Numbers, booleans and dates are matched as text (a `Date` value as its ISO text, e.g. `2025-01-31T00:00:00.000Z`; a date already stored as a string is matched as that string).
Only columns currently visible in the table are searched; a hidden column's values never match.
Enter with an empty or whitespace-only input clears the table search and returns to page 1.
The input keeps exactly what was typed, spaces included; only the applied term is trimmed.
The clear X empties the input text only, keeps the box open and returns focus to the input; the table stays filtered by the last applied query until Enter or collapse.
The clear X is invisible while the input is empty (still in the DOM), visible once the input has text.
The back arrow collapses the box, empties the input, clears the table search and returns to page 1.

When the search matches no row, a DataTable shows the empty state `No results found` with the description `Try adjusting your search or filter.` (not the no-data state); with `usePaginator` its paginator report reads `No records`.
When the table's search is set elsewhere (state restored on load), the box opens pre-filled with that term, without taking focus.
When the table's search is cleared elsewhere (a Reset), the input empties but the box stays open.
Hovering or focusing the collapsed search button shows the tooltip `Search` after a 300 ms open delay.
The root is a `role="search"` landmark named `Search`.

doesNot.text: No live (as-you-type) search; no debounce in this component.
No Escape handling; Escape does not collapse or clear the box.
No accent folding: `e` does not match `é` (the filter panel's text field does fold accents, search does not).
No regex, quotes, operators or column prefixes; every character is literal.
Property names are never matched, only values.
No result count, loading indicator or match highlight inside the box.
No tooltip on the back arrow or the clear X; only the collapsed search button has one.
The clear X does not refilter the table.
A DataTable does not render a SearchButton; the page places it and pairs it with the same `dataView`.

defaults.text: Starts collapsed unless the table already has a search term.
The input placeholder is `Search`; the placeholder is not an accessible name.
Applying or collapsing always goes to page 1.
The committed search persists with the table's state (`statePersistence`, default `'sessionStorage'`); the box reopens pre-filled after a same-tab reload.
English text only; the labels are component props, not locale constants.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `searchLabel` renames the landmark and the search button's accessible name (default `Search`).
`searchPlaceholder`, `collapseLabel`, `clearLabel`, `searchTooltip` rename the placeholder, back-arrow name, clear-X name and tooltip.
`onSearch(query)` fires on Enter (trimmed query, or `undefined` when empty) and on collapse (`undefined`); `onCollapsed` fires on collapse only.
Without `dataView` nothing is filtered (the box still opens and `onSearch` still fires); the dev console logs an error.
`tableName` sets the form id `search-button-form-<tableName>` that the search button's `aria-controls` names (default `datatable`).
`statePersistence: 'none'` on the table: a reload starts collapsed and empty.
A server-driven table (`useDataView` with a fetch) refetches on submit, debounced by the hook's `debounceMs` (default 0); the visible-column list is sent with the search.

builtInText.text: `Search` (collapsed button aria-label, landmark aria-label, tooltip, input placeholder).
`Collapse search` (back arrow aria-label).
`Clear search` (clear X aria-label).
`No results found` / `Try adjusting your search or filter.` (DataTable empty state when search is active, locale en).

keyboard.text: Enter in the input submits the search (via a hidden submit button, aria-hidden, tabIndex -1, skipped by Tab).
The search button, back arrow and clear X are native buttons: Tab to reach, Enter or Space to activate.

states.text: Collapsed: search button with `aria-expanded="false"` and `aria-controls` of the form id; no input.
Open and empty: input shown, clear X invisible.
Open with text: clear X visible.
Open with a committed search: table filtered; box pre-filled if restored.

testApi: `Spectra.findSearchButton(name)` / `querySearchButton(name)`: by `searchLabel` (default `Search`); `find*` throws when absent, `query*` returns `null`. Also chainable from `findTableToolbar(...)`. A page with several boxes named `Search` returns the first.
`isOpen()`: shouldBeOpen / shouldNotBeOpen.
`isClearVisible(clearLabel?)`: shouldBeClearVisible / shouldNotBeClearVisible (open and holding text).
`getQuery()`: shouldHaveQuery(text); `''` while collapsed.
`getInput()`: input element (throws while collapsed); `getInputWidth()` px (throws while collapsed).
`getContainer()`: the search landmark.
`open(searchLabel?)`: idempotent; waits for the input.
`collapse(collapseLabel?)`: idempotent; waits for the input to leave.
`typeQuery(query, searchLabel?)`: opens, types over existing text, does not submit; types again if the screen writes the previous search back meanwhile.
`search(query, searchLabel?)`: opens, types, Enter; returns once the paired table shows the result.
`clear(clearLabel?)`: clicks the clear X (box stays open; throws if absent).
`collapseLabel` / `clearLabel` params default to `Collapse search` / `Clear search`; pass overrides when props are customized.

components.name: SegmentedControl

does.text: Shows one button (segment) per option, side by side in a bordered bar, with a coloured indicator behind the active segment (TC-1302).
Exactly one segment is active at a time; clicking another makes it active, moves the indicator to it with a short slide (150 ms) and calls `onChange(value)` with that option's `value` (TC-1302).
Uncontrolled with neither `value` nor `defaultValue`: the first option is active on mount, even when it is disabled (TC-1302).
Controlled (`value`): the active segment is the one the parent passes; a click only calls `onChange` and the segment changes when the parent passes the new `value`.
Each segment is a `button` with `aria-pressed` `true` on the active one and `false` on the others (TC-5151).
Clicking the already active segment keeps it active and calls `onChange` again with the same value.
A segment's own `onClick` runs on a click of that segment (also the one already active), not on a disabled one.
An option's `label` is the segment text; any node is accepted; `leftIcon` and `rightIcon` sit before and after it; an option with `icon` and no `label` shows only that icon (TC-5151).

ArrowRight or ArrowDown selects the next enabled segment, ArrowLeft or ArrowUp the previous one, wrapping from the last to the first and the first to the last; the selection changes at once (`onChange` and the option's `onClick` run) and focus moves to it (TC-5151).
Arrow keys skip disabled segments.
Only the active segment is a tab stop (the others are `tabindex="-1"`): Tab enters the control on the active segment and the next Tab leaves it.
The indicator follows the active segment when the size, orientation, `fullWidth`, `rounded` or the container width changes.
The indicator is hidden when no option matches the value (a controlled `value` that is not an option's).
Native button attributes on an option (`aria-label`, `title`, `data-*`, `id`) go onto that segment's button.

doesNot.text: Does not allow no selection by a click: there is no way to deselect the active segment by clicking it.
Does not allow several active segments (a multiple choice is a CheckboxGroup).
Does not select a disabled segment by click or by arrow keys, and does not call its `onClick` (TC-5151).
Does not select on Home, End or typing: only the four arrow keys move the selection; Enter and Space on a focused segment click it as a button does.
Does not move on arrow keys while the whole control is `disabled`.

Does not give the container a `role` or `aria-label` of its own beyond the props passed to it; the segments carry the state, and the container carries `aria-disabled="true"` only while the whole control is `disabled` (`SegmentedControl#26`).
Does not give an icon-only segment a text name: pass `aria-label` on that option; the icons themselves are `aria-hidden`.
Does not show a tooltip.

defaults.text: `orientation` `horizontal`; `size` `xs`; `rounded` false (square corners); `fullWidth` false (the bar is as wide as its segments).
The active segment is the first option when `value` and `defaultValue` are omitted (SegmentedControl#3).
`disabled` false.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `disabled`: every segment is disabled, the bar is dimmed with a not-allowed cursor, keys are ignored and the indicator turns neutral grey and the active segment text stays in the on-primary colour.
An option's `disabled`: only that segment is disabled (native disabled button with `aria-disabled="true"`), dimmed text.
`fullWidth`: the bar fills its container and the segments share the width equally.
`orientation="vertical"`: segments stack in a column, each as wide as the bar; Down and Up arrows still move the selection (Right and Left too).
`rounded`: the bar and the first and last segment have fully round ends (pill).
`size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, or a responsive object): the segment height, padding and text size.
`value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `options`: as above; `className`, `style`, `pt`: styling; other HTML attributes (`aria-label`, `id`, `data-*`) go onto the container.

keyboard.text: Tab focuses the active segment; ArrowRight and ArrowDown select and focus the next enabled segment, ArrowLeft and ArrowUp the previous, with wrap-around (SegmentedControl#9).
Enter or Space on the focused segment activates it (button click).

states.text: Active: `aria-pressed="true"`, indicator behind it, text in the on-primary colour (TC-5151).
Inactive: `aria-pressed="false"`, text in the accent colour on the track.
Disabled segment: native `disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"`, dimmed text (TC-5151).
Focused: a focus-visible tint over the segment, no outline.

testApi: `Spectra.findSegmentedControl(name)` by the container's `aria-label`; `Spectra.querySegmentedControl(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getValue()`: the label text of the active segment (not the option `value`), `""` when none; `shouldHaveValue` / `getActiveLabel()` read it. `setValue(value)`: clicks the segment.
`getSegment(label)`, `getActiveSegment()`, `getAllSegments()`, `getSegmentCount()` / `shouldHaveSegmentCount(n)`, `hasSegment(label)`, `hasActiveSegment()`, `getIndicator()`.
`clickSegment(label)`, `selectNext()` / `selectPrevious()` (focus, then ArrowRight or ArrowLeft), `focus()` / `blur()` (the `tabindex="0"` segment).
`isSegmentActive(label)`, `isSegmentDisabled(label)`, `isDisabled()` (reads the container's `aria-disabled`, set while the whole control is `disabled`).

components.name: SegmentedInput

does.text: Shows one box (slot) per character, `length` of them (4 by default), or several groups of boxes when `groups` is set.
Typing fills the boxes from the first; the value is one string.
Typing on a filled box overwrites that character instead of inserting; typing past the last box is ignored.
The active box (where the caret is) shows a blinking caret and a focus ring while the field is focused.
Clicking a box, a group or a separator focuses the field and puts the caret on that box, but never past the first empty box (no gaps).
Clicking the field outside the boxes puts the caret on the first empty box, or on the last box when full.
Backspace removes the character before the caret, Delete the one at the caret, and a selected range is removed as a whole; the following characters shift left.
Pasting inserts the text at the caret (replacing a selection, or overwriting from the caret on a filled position); characters the `pattern` rejects are dropped and the text is cut to the free length.
The `pattern` filters every typed or pasted character one by one (for digits only, `a` is dropped from `12a4`, leaving `124`).
`transform` `uppercase` or `lowercase` changes the case of typed and pasted characters.
Reaching full length calls `onComplete(value)`.
Dropping text onto the field does nothing (the drop is blocked).
The separator text (for example `-`) is removed from pasted text before it is filled in.
Turning `invalid` on shakes the field once (400 ms); a field that mounts invalid also shakes; `data-shaken` is present on the root while it shakes.
`aria-describedby` passes through to the focusable field, so the text of the elements it names (a surrounding `Field`'s helper or error text) is its accessible description.

doesNot.text: No gaps: characters can only be added at the end or over an existing character.
The value is never longer than the number of boxes.
No shake under reduced motion, and none when `shakeOnInvalid` is false.
`onComplete` is not called while the field is not full.
The boxes themselves are not read by screen readers (`aria-hidden`); only the hidden input is.
No separator is drawn when `groups` is not set, nor after the last group.
Not a form-submit field: Enter is blocked while the code is incomplete or when `onComplete` is set.

defaults.text: 4 boxes, empty, text type, size `md`.
Empty boxes show nothing (`placeholderChar` is empty).
Characters are shown as typed (no mask), case unchanged, no `pattern` (any character).
`groupVariant` `segmented`: every box has its own border.
`invalid` false, `shakeOnInvalid` true, not disabled, not read-only.
The hidden input has `autoComplete` `one-time-code` and `inputMode` `text`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `length`: number of boxes (a non-positive value falls back to 4).
`groups: [4, 4, 4]`: boxes divided into groups of those sizes (12 boxes).
`separator` (with `groups`): that text between groups.
`groupVariant: 'grouped'` (with `groups`): one border around each group, plain boxes inside.
`mask`: filled boxes show `•` instead of the character.
`placeholderChar`: shown in empty boxes (not in the box holding the caret).
`type: 'password'`: the hidden input is a password input.
`inputMode`, `enterKeyHint`, `autoComplete`, `name`, `autoFocus`: passed to the hidden input.
`disabled`: boxes are not clickable, the hidden input is disabled, no caret or focus ring.
`readOnly`: the hidden input is read-only, controlled or not; typed keys, Backspace, Delete and paste change nothing and fire no `onChange` (the field still takes focus and shows its value).
`invalid`: `aria-invalid="true"` and the invalid look; does not stop editing.
`value` / `defaultValue`: the value is cut to the box count and passed through `pattern` and `transform`.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `id`: set on the hidden input.

builtInText.text: Mask character: `•`.
No built-in labels or messages (a missing accessible name only logs a development console error).

keyboard.text: Tab focuses the hidden input; ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home and End move the caret between boxes.
A printable key types, Backspace and Delete remove, Enter is blocked while incomplete or with `onComplete`.
Shift, Ctrl, Alt or Meta combinations keep the browser's default handling (select, copy, paste).

states.text: Idle (no caret) or focused (caret and ring on the active box); a selection across boxes highlights those boxes instead of showing a caret.
Empty, partly filled, full.
Disabled, read-only, invalid (shaking once), masked.

testApi: `Spectra.findSegmentedInput(name)`: by the accessible name; `Spectra.querySegmentedInput(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getValue()`, `setValue(text)`, `clearValue()`, `paste(text, slotIndex?)`, `getLength()` (number of boxes).
`getInput()` (hidden input), `getContainer()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.

`getSlots()`, `getSlot(i)`, `getSlotText(i)`, `clickSlot(i)`, `getSlotRowCount()`; `getGroups()`, `getGroup(i)`, `clickGroup(i)`; `getSeparators()`, `getSeparator(i)`, `getSeparatorText(i)`, `hasSeparators()`, `clickSeparator(i)` (indexes 0-based).
`getActiveSlotIndex()` (`null` while no caret), `hasFocusRing()`, `isMasked()`, `isInvalid()`, `hasShaken()` (`shouldHaveShaken()`), `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`.
`getAccessibleDescription()` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits).

components.name: Select

does.text: Shows a combobox trigger with the selected option's label, or the placeholder when nothing is selected, and a down-arrow at the end.
Clicking the trigger opens a floating list panel under it; clicking the trigger again, clicking outside, or pressing Escape closes it.
Clicking an enabled option selects it, shows its label in the trigger, and closes the panel at once.
The selected option is marked selected (`aria-selected="true"`) in the list; the list opens scrolled to it.
`onChange` receives the option's value (not an event) and the whole option object as second argument.
Disabled options (`optionDisabled` or a `disabled` field) are greyed, marked `aria-disabled`, and cannot be picked by click or Enter.
The list is virtualized: only the rows near the scroll position are in the DOM; `scrollHeight` (300 px) caps the panel height.
A value that matches no option is shown as its own text in the trigger.
With no options, the panel shows `No options available`.
`loading` swaps the arrow for a spinner, shows `Loading...` in place of the placeholder when nothing is selected, and the panel cannot be opened.
`disabled` greys the control, removes it from the tab order, and the panel cannot be opened.
`readOnly` shows the current value but the panel cannot be opened and the value cannot change.

With `filter`, a search box (placeholder `Search`, magnifier icon) is shown at the top of the panel and receives focus when the panel opens; typing narrows the list to options whose label contains the text, case-insensitively.
With `filter`, typing highlights the first enabled match, so Enter selects it; a query that contains a space can be typed (Space types into the search).
With `filter`, no match shows `No results found.` in the panel.
Closing the panel by Escape returns focus to the trigger.
An invalid select shows the invalid (red) style and `aria-invalid="true"` on the trigger.
`aria-describedby` passes through to the focusable field, so the text of the elements it names (a surrounding `Field`'s helper or error text) is its accessible description.

doesNot.text: Only one value can be selected; picking another replaces it (that is MultiSelect elsewhere).

Picking the already-selected option clears it (the value becomes `undefined`, `onChange(undefined)`, the placeholder returns) and closes the panel; with `allowDeselect={false}` the value stays and only the panel closes.
No clear (x) button.
No option groups or headers, and no creating new options by typing.
The search box is not shown without `filter`; typing on the closed trigger does not jump to an option.
Disabled options are not skipped by the arrow keys; they get the highlight but Enter does nothing on them.
No visible label, required marker or error text: those come from the wrapping Field.
The panel stays closed when the trigger is clicked while `loading`, `disabled` or `readOnly`.
No Home, End, PageUp or PageDown navigation.

defaults.text: Placeholder `Select an option` (locale en); it is also the trigger's accessible name when no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is given.
Closed, no value, no filter, deselect on, enabled, not read-only, not loading, not invalid.
`size` `xs`; row heights 28, 32, 36, 40 px for `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`.
`panelWidth` `trigger`: the panel is as wide as the trigger.
`scrollHeight` 300 px.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `options`: strings or objects; `optionLabel`, `optionValue`, `optionDisabled` name the object fields (defaults `label`, the object itself as value, `disabled`).
`value` + `onChange`: controlled; `defaultValue`: uncontrolled initial value.
`placeholder`: replaces `Select an option`.
`filter`, `filterPlaceholder`, `filterFunction`: search box, its placeholder, and a custom match rule instead of case-insensitive label contains.
`emptyMessage`, `emptyFilterMessage`: replace the two built-in empty texts.
`allowDeselect={false}`: clicking the selected option (or Enter on it) keeps the value, calls no `onChange`, and only closes the panel. `allowDeselect` is `true` by default.
`dataKey`: options and values are matched by that field (for object values) instead of by deep equality.
`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`: control or start the panel open; `defaultOpen` does not move focus into the search on page load.
`panelWidth`: `content` (minimum 12 rem), a number of px, or a CSS width.
`startAddon`, `endAddon`, `startElement`, `endElement`: extra content around or inside the trigger.
`renderOption`, `renderValue`, `renderTrigger`: custom option rows, trigger value text, or the whole trigger.
`virtualScrollerOptions`: row height estimate, overscan and paddings of the list.
`size`, `invalid`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `loading`: per Does.
`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-required`: set on the trigger; `aria-required="true"` is set only when passed (a required Field passes it).

builtInText.text: Placeholder `Select an option`; loading `Loading...`; filter placeholder `Search`; no match `No results found.`; no options `No options available` (locale en, passed through `t()`).

keyboard.text: Tab focuses the trigger; Enter, Space or ArrowDown on the closed trigger opens the panel.
ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the highlight through the options (first press starts at the selected option, or the top); the highlight stops at the first and last option.
Enter, or Space (without `filter`), selects the highlighted option and closes the panel.
Escape closes the panel and keeps focus on the trigger.
With `filter` and the panel open, Tab moves focus into the search box; Tab in the search box returns to the trigger.
With `filter`, after an arrow key has highlighted an option, Space in the search picks it; otherwise Space types.

states.text: Closed / open (`aria-expanded` false / true).
No value (placeholder) / has value.
Disabled, read-only, loading: panel cannot open; disabled also leaves the tab order.
Invalid: red style, `aria-invalid="true"`.
Option states: selected, highlighted, disabled.

testApi: `Spectra.findSelect(name)`: by the trigger's accessible name (label, `aria-label`, or placeholder); `Spectra.querySelect(name)`: `null` when missing.

`selectOption(label | RegExp | { value })` (opens, picks; `{ value }` for two options that read the same), `clearValue()` (needs `allowDeselect`, on by default; throws when nothing is selected), `getValue()`, `getPlaceholder()`.
`open()`, `close({ via })` (`'clickOutside'` default, `'escape'`, `'trigger'`), `toggle()`, `isOpen()`.
`getOptions()` (only the rendered rows), `getOption(...)`, `hasOption(...)` (scrolls the virtual list), `getPanel()`, `getContent()`, `getList()`, `getTrigger()`, `getContainer()`.
`getFilterInput()`, `hasFilterInput()`, `getFilterValue()`, `setFilter(q)`, `clearFilter()`, `getFilterIcon()`, `hasFilterIcon()`.
`getEmptyMessage()`, `hasEmptyMessage()`, `getArrow()`, `hasArrow()`, `getLoader()`, `hasLoader()`.
`getStartAddon()` / `getEndAddon()` / `getStartElement()` / `getEndElement()` and their `has*`.
`isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isInvalid()`, `isLoading()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.
`getDescription()`, `hasDescription()`, `getDescriptionText()` (the `aria-describedby` target, e.g. a Field's helper text).
`getAccessibleDescription()` of the trigger (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits).

components.name: Shimmer

does.text: While loading, the wrapped content stays in the page and keeps its text, but each innermost element is drawn as an animated grey placeholder block and its text is invisible

While loading, icons (svg) and images are drawn as placeholder blocks, input placeholder text is invisible, a textarea cannot be resized, a select loses its arrow, a divider (`hr`) is drawn as a 2 px bar, an input group is drawn as one block with its content hidden
While loading, nothing inside reacts to the mouse (clicks do not reach controls, text cannot be selected)
The wrapper draws no box of its own (`display: contents`): the layout is that of its children
The loading wrapper carries `aria-busy="true"`
The page leaves the state only when the parent sets `loading` to false: the placeholders and `aria-busy` go at once and the real content shows; there is no timer or internal exit

Descendants read the loading state: an ImagePicker's empty upload trigger becomes an empty block (no icon, no `Select or drop`, no requirements text); an Avatar draws its photo or fallback as a shimmer block
While loading, containers lose their own background, border, outline, focus ring and shadow, and all text is transparent; only the innermost elements show the animated grey blocks (2 s linear loop).
Avatar also wraps its own picture in a Shimmer while the image loads, so a loading Avatar reports `aria-busy="true"` without a parent Shimmer.

doesNot.text: No spinner, text, label or role of its own
Does not unmount, disable or make inert its children: nothing sets `disabled`, `inert` or `tabindex`, so Tab still reaches buttons and inputs inside and Enter or Space still activates them
Not loading: no `data-ui-section="shimmer.root"` on the root and no `aria-busy`, so `findShimmer` no longer matches it
Does not block the rest of the page; it is not an overlay
No minimum display time and no delay: the placeholders appear the moment `loading` is true and disappear the moment it is false, however short the load.
The `aria-busy` attribute is the only accessibility signal: no `aria-label`, `aria-live` or text like `Loading` is added, so a screen reader hears nothing about loading.

defaults.text: `loading` is true: `<Shimmer>` with no props is already shimmering
The wrapper element is a `div`

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `loading={false}`: shows the content normally (see `Shimmer#10`)
`as`: renders the wrapper as that element or component instead of `div`

`className`, `pt.root`, or extra props such as `aria-label`: merged onto the wrapper; an accessible name exists only if one is given this way (the wrapper has none otherwise, so `findShimmer(label)` matches by the wrapped text)

keyboard.text: None of its own; focus order and key handling of the wrapped controls are unchanged while loading (`Shimmer#9`)

states.text: Loading (`aria-busy="true"`, `data-ui-section="shimmer.root"`, class `shimmer active`)
Loaded (no `aria-busy`, no `data-ui-section`, no placeholder styling)

testApi: `Spectra.findShimmer(label, options?)` / `Spectra.queryShimmer(label, options?)`: match the root with `data-ui-section="shimmer.root"` and the accessible name or wrapped text; only a loading Shimmer has that attribute. `find` waits the implicit wait; `query` returns null when absent.
`getContainer(options?)`: the shimmer root element (nearest `shimmer.root` or `aria-busy="true"` ancestor).

`isLoading(options?)` / `shouldBeLoading()` / `shouldNotBeLoading()`: true when the container has `aria-busy="true"` or `shimmer.root`. A held wrapper whose Shimmer has finished loading reports not loading.
`isDisplayed(options?)` / `shouldBeDisplayed()`: the root is `display: contents`; assert visibility on a child (`Spectra.get('[data-ui-section~="shimmer.root"] span').shouldBeVisible()`, TC-5154).
`getText(options?)` / `shouldHaveText(text)` / `shouldContainText(text)`: the wrapped text (still in the DOM while loading).
`element`: raw root element; `Spectra.shouldNotFindShimmer(label)`.
A find for a control inside a loading Shimmer keeps polling until the control appears outside one (testing-library README); to test the skeleton itself chain from inside it.

components.name: Sidebar

does.text: Renders a vertical navigation panel (`aside` with a `nav` and a menu list) from `items`: plain links, accordion submenus and labelled sections, with an optional `header` above and `footer` below the scrolling list.
An item whose `value` (or `href`) equals `value` is the active item: highlighted, `aria-current="page"`, `data-active="true"`; a submenu holding the active item reads active too.
Clicking a link item runs its `onClick`, then `onValueChange(value)`; an item with `href` also follows its link.
Clicking a submenu trigger opens or closes its nested items (the arrow turns, `aria-expanded` flips); several submenus can be open at once.
A section (group item without `value`) shows its label as a small uppercase header over its items; a section is not clickable.
An item with `badge` shows the badge text at the right of its row; a submenu with a badged descendant item shows a dot in the rail.
Items with `visible: false` are not rendered; a submenu or section whose items are all hidden is not rendered either.
A disabled item is dimmed, has `aria-disabled="true"`, and a click does nothing (no `onClick`, no `onValueChange`).

Rail collapse (`collapsed` true, `collapseMode` `rail`): the panel narrows to icon-only; labels, badges, arrows and section headers disappear, a badge shows as a red dot on the icon, and an item or submenu without an `icon` is not rendered.
In the collapsed rail, clicking a submenu icon expands the sidebar and opens that submenu.

In the collapsed rail with `hoverExpand` on, hovering it (after 50 ms) floats the full panel over the page content; leaving it (after 100 ms) folds it back; clicking an item while peeking closes the peek.
Offcanvas collapse (`collapsed` true, `collapseMode` `offcanvas`): the panel shrinks to zero width and is invisible.
Only one item in the menu is a tab stop (the focused one, else the active one, else the first); arrow keys move focus between visible items.
With `renderLink`, link items are rendered by that function (spreading `href`, `aria-current`, `data-active`, `role="menuitem"`).

The expanded state and the collapsed state are each controllable (`expandedValues` / `collapsed`) or uncontrolled (`defaultExpandedValues` / `defaultCollapsed`); changes call `onExpandedValuesChange` / `onCollapsedChange`.

doesNot.text: No built-in collapse toggle button: the app renders it (for example in the navbar) and drives `collapsed`.
`value` is not changed by the sidebar itself: the active item follows the `value` prop (a controlled sidebar keeps the old one until the app updates it).
Clicking a section header does nothing.
No `aria-label` prop: the landmark has no accessible name unless the app sets `pt.root['aria-label']`.
Does not close a submenu when another opens (no accordion exclusivity).
In the rail with `hoverExpand` false there is no hover peek; hovering shows a tooltip with the item label instead.
No loading, empty or error state, and no search.
`side` does not move the sidebar in the layout; the app places it.

defaults.text: Expanded (`collapsed` false), `collapseMode` `rail`, `hoverExpand` true, `expandMode` `push`, `side` `left`.
No submenu open (`expandedValues` empty); expanded panel 240 px wide, rail 64 px wide.
Every row is 32 px high, with or without an icon.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `collapsed`: true narrows to the rail (or hides, in `offcanvas`).
`collapseMode: 'offcanvas'`: collapsing hides the whole panel; no rail, no hover peek (`hoverExpand` has no effect).
`hoverExpand: false` (rail): no peek; each rail icon shows a tooltip with its label on the opposite side of `side`.
`expandMode: 'overlay'` (rail): the rail keeps its 64 px in the layout and the expanded panel floats above the content, driven by `collapsed` alone.
`side: 'right'`: tooltips open to the left; a floating (hover or overlay) panel anchors to the right edge.
`header` / `footer`: sticky content above and below the list; a function receives `{ collapsed, hovering, collapseMode }`.
`item.icon`: shown before the label and stays in the rail.
`item.href`: the item is an anchor; `value` can match this `href` instead of the item `value`.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling; `pt.root['aria-label']` names the landmark.

keyboard.text: ArrowDown / ArrowUp: focus the next / previous visible, enabled item, wrapping around.
Home / End: focus the first / last item of the current level.
ArrowRight on a closed submenu trigger opens it; on an open one it focuses its first child.
ArrowLeft on an open submenu trigger closes it; on a nested item it focuses the parent trigger.
Enter on the focused item clicks it.
Sidebar keys do not bubble out of the menu (propagation stopped).

states.text: Expanded: labels visible, `data-collapsed="false"`; collapsed: `data-collapsed="true"` (rail icons only, or offcanvas hidden).
Peeking (rail, hover): `data-hovering="true"` and the panel floats over the content.
Active item: `aria-current="page"`; disabled item: `aria-disabled="true"`; submenu trigger: `aria-expanded` true or false.
Focused item: visible focus ring.

testApi: `Spectra.findSidebar(name)` by the root `aria-label` (set through `pt.root['aria-label']`); `Spectra.querySidebar(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getItemLabels()` / `shouldHaveItemLabels([...])`: labels shown now (nested items only while their submenu is open; none in a rail).
`getItem(label)`, `hasItem(label)` / `shouldHaveItem` / `shouldNotHaveItem`, `clickItem(label)`.
`isItemActive(label)` / `shouldBeItemActive` / `shouldNotBeItemActive`.
`isSubmenuOpen(label)` / `shouldBeSubmenuOpen`, `openSubmenu(label)`.
`isCollapsed()` / `shouldBeCollapsed` / `shouldNotBeCollapsed`, `getContainer()` (the `aside`).

components.name: Slider

does.text: Shows a track with a filled range from the minimum up to a round handle positioned at the current value.
ArrowRight or ArrowUp raises the value by one `step`; ArrowLeft or ArrowDown lowers it by one `step`; each key press changes the value at once.
Home sets the value to the minimum and End sets it to the maximum.
PageUp raises the value by 10 steps and PageDown lowers it by 10 steps.
The value never goes below `min` or above `max`; a key press at a limit leaves the value unchanged.
Pressing or dragging on the slider moves the handle to the pointer position, snapped to the nearest step and clamped to the range, and the handle follows the pointer while dragging.
The change is reported (`onChange`, and the exposed value `aria-valuenow`) when the pointer is released, not while dragging; the exposed value stays at the old value during the drag.
A vertical slider has its minimum at the bottom and maximum at the top; pointer position is measured from the bottom.
A tooltip with the current value appears above the handle while hovering the handle, dragging, or while the slider has keyboard focus.
The tooltip text is the plain number of the value being shown (it follows the handle during a drag).
Each entry of `marks` shows its label under (horizontal) or beside (vertical) the track at the position of its value.
Decimal steps (for example 0.1) give clean values without floating-point residue (rounded to 4 decimals).
The slider is a single focusable control with role `slider`; `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow` reflect `min`, `max` and the committed value, and `aria-orientation` the orientation.

doesNot.text: Has no numeric text input, no step buttons, and no visible value label besides the tooltip.
Has no range (two-handle) mode; a range is the RangeSlider component.
Does not change the value on keyboard or pointer input while disabled, and a disabled slider is not reachable by Tab.
Does not show tick marks or mark labels unless `marks` is given; marks are not generated from `step`.
Does not show a tooltip when `showTooltip` is false, even while dragging or focused.
Does not constrain `defaultValue` or `value` to `min`/`max`/`step`; the handle position is clamped visually but the exposed value is what was given.
Mouse wheel does not change the value.
Marks are not buttons: pressing on a mark label moves the handle like pressing anywhere else, and the handle does not snap to the mark.

defaults.text: `min` 0, `max` 100, `step` 1.
`defaultValue` is the `min` (0 unless `min` is set).
`orientation` horizontal, `size` `sm`.
`showTooltip` on, `tooltipAlwaysOn` off.
Not disabled, not invalid; no marks.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `value` + `onChange`: controlled; the handle only moves when the caller changes `value`.
`defaultValue`: initial value for the uncontrolled slider.
`min`, `max`, `step`: change the range and the increment of keys and pointer snapping.
`marks`: shows the labels (label text, or the number when `label` is missing).
`orientation: 'vertical'`: vertical track, handle moves bottom to top.
`size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, or responsive): changes track and handle thickness.
`showTooltip: false`: no tooltip at all.
`tooltipAlwaysOn`: the tooltip stays visible without hover, drag or focus.
`formatTooltip(value)`: replaces the tooltip text (for example `26%`).
`disabled`: dimmed, `aria-disabled` true, no interaction, tabIndex -1.
`invalid` (or `aria-invalid`): `aria-invalid` true on the slider; `aria-invalid` wins when both are given.
`aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`: the accessible name; without them the slider has no accessible name.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling only.

keyboard.text: Tab focuses the slider (one tab stop); a disabled slider is skipped.
ArrowRight/ArrowUp +1 step, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown -1 step, Home min, End max, PageUp +10 steps, PageDown -10 steps (also in vertical orientation: Up/Right still raise, Down/Left lower).
Other keys do nothing and are not prevented.
Focusing the slider shows the tooltip; blurring hides it (unless `tooltipAlwaysOn`).

states.text: Default: handle at the value, tooltip hidden until hover, drag or focus.
Dragging: tooltip visible, handle marked dragging, filled range follows without animation.
Focused: focus ring on the handle and tooltip visible.
Disabled: track, range, handle and mark labels dimmed; ignores pointer and keys.
Invalid: `aria-invalid` true (no separate visual change in the preset).

testApi: `Spectra.findSlider(label)`: by the `aria-label` on the root; `Spectra.querySlider(label)`: `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindSlider(label)`.
`getValue()` reads `aria-valuenow`; `shouldHaveValue(n)` polls it.
`setValue(n)`: focuses, presses Home, probes the step with one ArrowRight, Home again, then presses ArrowRight until `n` (keyboard only, min-based).
`stepUp()` / `stepDown()`: focus then ArrowRight / ArrowLeft.
`jumpToMin()` / `jumpToMax()`: focus then Home / End.
`getHandle()`: the root element itself (the root carries role `slider`); `getTrack(options?)`: the track part.
`isDisabled()` / `shouldBeDisabled()`: `aria-disabled` is `true`.
`isInvalid()`: `aria-invalid` is `true`.
`hasMarks()` / `shouldHaveMarks()`: the marks container exists.
`getOrientation()` / `shouldHaveOrientation('horizontal'|'vertical')`: `aria-orientation`.
`focus()`, `blur()`.
`element`, `getContainer(options?)`: the root element.

components.name: Stepper

does.text: Shows the `steps` as an ordered row of numbered circles, each with its title (and description when given), joined by connector lines between neighbours.
Each circle shows its 1-based number (step 1 shows `1`), or the step's own `icon` when it has one.
The step at `activeStep` is highlighted as the current step and carries `aria-current="step"` on its trigger; the steps before it are completed.
A completed step shows a check icon in its circle instead of its number or custom icon, with the hidden screen-reader text `Step N Completed` (N is the 1-based position).
Steps after the active one are pending: their number (or custom icon) shows in a neutral circle and they have no `aria-current`.
A connector is highlighted (completed colour) when the step before it is completed, otherwise it stays neutral.
Each step title may carry a description, shown under the title in a smaller secondary style.
Long titles and descriptions are cut with an ellipsis instead of wrapping.
With `onStepClick`, every step is a button; clicking an enabled step calls `onStepClick(index)` with the 0-based index.
With `onStepClick`, the enabled steps are the completed ones and the active one; clicking the active step also calls `onStepClick` with its own index.
`activeStep` is fully controlled: clicking a step only calls `onStepClick`, the highlighted step moves only when the parent passes a new `activeStep`.

A step with `disabled: true` is dimmed, shows its number (or custom icon) in a neutral circle, is neither active nor completed (no `aria-current`, no check), and its connector to the next step stays neutral.
`activeStep` at or beyond the number of steps shows every step as completed and none as current.
The root has `role="list"`, each step `role="listitem"`, and the root's accessible name is its `aria-label`.
`orientation: 'vertical'` stacks the steps in a column with vertical connectors; the root reports its orientation as `data-orientation="horizontal"` or `"vertical"`.
The sizes `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` give 20, 24, 28, 32 px circles with matching title text and icon sizes.

doesNot.text: Does not advance, go back or change `activeStep` by itself, and does not render any step content or panel.
Without `onStepClick` no step is a button and no step is focusable or clickable; steps are plain read-only elements.
Without `allowClickAhead`, a pending step after the active one is not clickable and `onStepClick` is not called for it.
A disabled step never calls `onStepClick`, with or without `allowClickAhead`.
A disabled step does not show the completed check or the `Step N Completed` text, even when it is before `activeStep`.
A custom `icon` on a step is not shown once that step is completed: the check (or `completedStepIcon`) replaces it.
The `Step N Completed` text is not translated (always English) and is not visible on screen.
The connectors are decorative: no role, no label, not clickable.
No arrow-key navigation between steps, no tooltip, no percentage.
`aria-labelledby` is not supported on the root; only `aria-label`.
A step marked `disabled` in a read-only stepper (no `onStepClick`) is dimmed but has no `disabled` attribute.

defaults.text: `steps` is empty: an empty list is shown (the root still renders).
`activeStep` is `0`: the first step is current and all others pending.
`orientation` is `horizontal`.
`size` is `xs` (20 px circles).
`allowClickAhead` is off.
`showConnector` is on: a connector sits between each adjacent pair of steps, none after the last step.
The completed icon is the check icon `CheckLine`.
A string entry in `steps` is a step with that title only.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `onStepClick`: turns the steps into buttons (see Does).
`allowClickAhead`: with `onStepClick`, pending steps after the active one also become clickable; disabled steps still are not.
`showConnector: false`: no connector is rendered in either orientation.
`completedStepIcon`: replaces the check icon in completed circles (the `Step N Completed` text stays).
Step `icon`: shows in the circle of that step while it is active or pending (or disabled).
Step `description`: see Does; an entry that is `null` or `undefined` shows no description line.
`size` accepts a responsive value (per breakpoint).
`aria-label`: replaces the default root name.
`id`: sets the root `id`; `className`, `pt`: styling only.

builtInText.text: Default root `aria-label`: `Progress steps` (locale en; passed through `t()`).
Completed marker per finished step: `Step 1 Completed`, `Step 2 Completed`, ... (hidden text, English only).

keyboard.text: With `onStepClick`, Tab moves focus through the enabled step buttons in order and Shift+Tab back; a focus ring shows on the focused step.
Enter or Space on a focused step calls `onStepClick(index)` (native button).
Disabled and not-clickable steps are skipped by Tab; a read-only stepper has no tab stops.

states.text: Completed: filled primary circle with check, normal title colour, primary connector after it.
Active: tinted primary circle with number or icon, accent title, `aria-current="step"`.
Pending: neutral circle, muted title, neutral connector.
Disabled: half-transparent, not-allowed cursor, neutral circle.
Clickable steps show a pointer cursor; non-clickable ones do not.
Focused: ring around the step button.
Loading, invalid, hover tooltips: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findStepper(label)` finds by the root `aria-label` (default `Progress steps`); `Spectra.queryStepper(label)` returns `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindStepper(label?)`, `Spectra.shouldFindStepperCount(label?, count)`.
`getContainer()` is the root (`data-ui-section="stepper.root"`).
`getSteps()` returns every step wrapper in order (empty array when there are none; it waits for the first step).
`getStep(title)` finds a step by exact title text; throws when missing. `hasStep(title)` is the boolean form.
`getActiveStep()` returns the step with `aria-current="step"`; throws when none is active (for example `activeStep` past the end).
`getOrientation()` reads `data-orientation`: `'horizontal'` or `'vertical'`.
A step wrapper (see StepperStep) gives `getTitle()`, `getDescription()`, `isActive()`, `isCompleted()`, `isDisabled()`, `click()`.

components.name: StepperStep

does.text: Shows a circle with the step's 1-based position number (or its custom `icon`), and next to it the title and, when given, the description under it.
The step whose position equals `activeStep` is current: tinted circle, accent title, `aria-current="step"` on its trigger.
A step before `activeStep` is completed: its circle shows a check icon (replacing number and custom icon) and a hidden `Step N Completed` text, N being its 1-based position.
A step after `activeStep` is pending: neutral circle with its number or icon, muted title, no `aria-current`.
In a Stepper with `onStepClick`, the step is a button; an enabled one calls `onStepClick(index)` with its 0-based position when clicked.
Completed steps and the current step are enabled; a pending step is enabled only when the Stepper has `allowClickAhead`.
A step with `disabled: true` is dimmed, shows number or icon in a neutral circle, is neither current nor completed, and its trigger is a disabled button.
The step is a list item (`role="listitem"`) of the Stepper's list.
The title and the description are each cut with an ellipsis when too long.

doesNot.text: Does not become current or completed by being clicked; only the parent's new `activeStep` changes that.
In a Stepper without `onStepClick` the step is not a button, cannot be focused or clicked, and has no `disabled` attribute even when `disabled: true` (it is only dimmed).
A disabled step never calls `onStepClick`, even with `allowClickAhead`.
A disabled step shows no check and no `Step N Completed` text, even before `activeStep`.
A completed step does not show its custom `icon` or its number.
The `Step N Completed` text is hidden on screen and not translated (English only).
Shows no description line when `description` is `null` or `undefined`, or when the step is given as a plain string.
Has no tooltip, no badge, no error or warning state.

defaults.text: A plain string entry means `{ title: <string> }`: number, title, no description, not disabled.
`disabled` is false.
No custom icon: the 1-based number is shown.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `description`: secondary text under the title.
`icon`: replaces the number in the circle while the step is current, pending or disabled.
`disabled: true`: see Does.
Parent `completedStepIcon`: replaces the check icon in completed circles.
Parent `onStepClick`, `allowClickAhead`: make the step clickable as described above.

builtInText.text: Hidden completed marker `Step 1 Completed`, `Step 2 Completed`, ... (English).
Title and description are the caller's text; no built-in labels.

keyboard.text: In a clickable Stepper an enabled step is a tab stop and Enter or Space activates it (native button).
A disabled or not-clickable step is skipped by Tab; a read-only Stepper has no tab stops.

states.text: Completed: filled circle with check.
Current: tinted circle, `aria-current="step"`.
Pending: neutral circle, muted title.
Disabled: half-transparent, not-allowed cursor.
Focused: ring around the step button.

testApi: Reached through the parent: `stepper.getStep(title)` (exact title, throws when missing), `stepper.getSteps()` (in order), `stepper.getActiveStep()`, `stepper.hasStep(title)`; there is no `Spectra.findStepperStep`.
`getTitle()` (title text), `getDescription()` (text or `null` when the step has none).
`isActive()` (`shouldBeActive()`, `shouldNotBeActive()`): `aria-current="step"` on the trigger.
`isCompleted()` (`shouldBeCompleted()`, `shouldNotBeCompleted()`): the circle contains the `Completed` marker text.

`isDisabled()` (`shouldBeDisabled()`): reads the native `disabled` attribute (or `aria-disabled="true"`) of the trigger; true for any step a clickable Stepper cannot click (disabled, or pending without `allowClickAhead`), false for every step of a read-only Stepper.
`click()`: clicks the trigger; throws when the trigger is disabled or hidden; in a read-only Stepper it clicks the non-interactive trigger and nothing happens.
`getContainer()`: the step item (`data-ui-section="stepper.stepItem"`).

components.name: Switch

does.text: Renders a track with a round thumb; unchecked shows the thumb on the left, checked shows it on the right (thumb slides across with a short spring animation).
Clicking the track or thumb flips it between unchecked and checked and calls `onChange` with the new boolean (not an event).
Clicking the visible `label` text flips it too (the label is bound to the input).
Uncontrolled (`defaultChecked`): it keeps its own state and flips on every click.
Controlled (`checked`): it shows what `checked` says; a click only calls `onChange` and the thumb moves only when the parent passes the new `checked`.
With `label` the text sits next to the track, and the accessible name is that text.
With `description` the secondary text shows under the label; it is the control's `aria-describedby` target.
`trackContent` and `thumbContent` render inside the track and thumb; a function form receives `{ checked }` and is re-evaluated on every flip.
The input carries `role="switch"` and `aria-checked` equal to the state.
`invalid` shows a danger-coloured track, label and description and sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the input.
`onFocus` and `onBlur` fire when the input gains or loses focus.

doesNot.text: Does not call `onChange` and does not flip while `disabled` or `loading`.
Does not render a label or description element when `label` and `description` are absent.
`aria-label` is dropped from the input whenever a `label` is given (the visible label wins); a `description` alone does not drop it.

Does not use the `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-required` or `value` props from a surrounding `Field` (it uses `inputId` and the `description` prop instead); a Field's helper or error text is not linked to the input through `aria-describedby`.
Does not show a tooltip itself; a tooltip comes only from a wrapping `Tooltip`.
Does not show `thumbContent` while `loading`: the spinner replaces it, and the thumb keeps its on or off position.

defaults.text: Unchecked (`defaultChecked` false), enabled, not loading, not invalid.
`size` is `xs`: a 32 by 16 px track and a 12 px thumb.
`labelPosition` is `after`: the label is to the right of the track.
`role` is `switch`.
No label, no description, no track or thumb content.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `label`: visible text; hides `aria-label`.
`labelPosition: 'before'`: label and description to the left of the track.
`description`: secondary text under the label, in the label column.
`size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`: larger track (40x20, 48x24, 56x28 px), thumb and text; also accepts a responsive value.
`disabled`: greyed track, thumb and text, no pointer events on the control, input disabled.
`loading`: a spinner shows on the thumb, the input is disabled and nothing can be toggled.
`invalid`: see Does.
`trackContent`, `thumbContent`: content inside the track or thumb.
`inputId`: the `id` of the native input (default is a generated id).
`role`: replaces `role="switch"` on the input.
`tabIndex`: tab order of the input.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: root styling only.

keyboard.text: Tab moves focus to the input; a focus halo appears around the thumb for keyboard focus.
Space flips the focused switch (native checkbox behaviour); Enter does not.
A disabled or loading switch is skipped by Tab (the native input is disabled).

states.text: Unchecked: transparent track with a neutral border, grey thumb on the left.
Checked: primary-filled track, light thumb on the right.
Invalid: danger border (unchecked) or danger fill (checked), danger label and description.
Disabled: dimmed track, thumb and text at reduced opacity; checked and unchecked remain distinguishable.
Loading: spinner in the thumb, controls disabled.
Focused: halo around the thumb.
Hover and pressed: a faint halo around the thumb in the primary (or danger when invalid) colour; none when disabled.

testApi: `Spectra.findSwitch(label)` finds by `aria-label` or label text; `Spectra.querySwitch(label)` returns `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindSwitch(label)`.
`getContainer()` (root `data-ui-name="switch"`), `getInput()` (the `input[role="switch"]`), `getTrack()`, `getThumb()`.
`toggle()` clicks the input (falls back to the track); `check()` / `uncheck()` flip only when the state differs.

`click()` clicks the input that fills the visible track, so it toggles a labelled switch (label before or after) like a user click; `click()` / `hover()`: on a disabled switch the action lands on the wrapping Tooltip trigger (`[data-tooltip-state]`) when the switch refuses it.
`isChecked()` (`shouldBeChecked()`, `shouldNotBeChecked()`): the input is selected or `aria-checked="true"`.
`isDisabled()` (`shouldBeDisabled()`): the input is not enabled; true while loading as well.
`isLoading()` (`shouldBeLoading()`): the spinner is in the thumb.
`isInvalid()` (`shouldBeInvalid()`): `aria-invalid="true"` on the input.
`isFocused()`, `focus()`, `blur()` on the input.
`getTrackText()` (`shouldHaveTrackText(text)`), `hasTrackText()`.
`getLabel()`, `getLabelText()` (`shouldHaveLabelText(text)`), `hasLabel()`.
`getDescription()`, `getDescriptionText()` (`shouldHaveDescriptionText(text)`), `hasDescription()`.
`getLoadingIcon()`, `hasLoadingIcon()`.
`getTooltipText()` (`shouldHaveTooltipText(text)`): hovers the wrapping Tooltip trigger and reads its text; throws when no tooltip opens.

components.name: TabItem

does.text: One tab in a Tabs bar: shows its `label`, an optional icon before it and an optional count badge after it.
Is identified by its `value`; clicking it makes it active (`aria-selected="true"`) and the previously active one inactive.
With `href` it is a link (`<a href role="tab">` inside an `<li role="presentation">`); the `href` is on the link.
Without `href` it is the `<li role="tab">` itself and no link is rendered.
A string or number `badge` is shown as a small count badge next to the label; a badge config object is shown with that config.
With Tabs' `renderLink`, an item with `href` is shown through the app's link component, which still gets the tab role, `aria-selected` and click handling.
Its label stays readable text, separate from the badge text, so the tab is found by its label alone.

doesNot.text: Has no separate component or finder: it exists only inside Tabs, reached through `getTab`, `getTabs` or `getActiveTab`.
A disabled item cannot be activated: click, Enter and Space do nothing and no link is followed.
An item without `href` has no `href` (reads `null`).
Does not translate its label: it shows `label` exactly as given.
Does not render a badge unless `badge` is given; an item without `icon` has no icon part.

defaults.text: `disabled` false; no icon, no badge, no `href`.
A badge given as a string or number is `secondary`, size `xs`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `icon`: an icon shows before the label.
`badge`: a count badge shows after the label.
`href`: the item is a link (see `TabItem#3`).
`disabled: true`: dimmed, `aria-disabled="true"`, not clickable, skipped by arrow keys, `tabindex="-1"`.

builtInText.text: none; the text is the `label`.

keyboard.text: Enter or Space activates the focused item; arrow keys, Home and End move focus between enabled items (see Tabs).

states.text: Active: `aria-selected="true"`; inactive: `aria-selected="false"`.
Disabled: `aria-disabled="true"`.
Only the active enabled item has `tabindex="0"`; all others `-1`.

testApi: Reached from the Tabs wrapper: `tabs.getTab(label)` / `queryTab(label)` / `getTabs()` / `getActiveTab()`; no `findTabItem`.
`isActive()`: `shouldBeActive()` / `shouldNotBeActive()` (reads `aria-selected` on the `role="tab"` element, also for link items).
`isDisabled()`: `shouldBeDisabled()` / `shouldNotBeDisabled()`.
`hasIcon()`: `shouldHaveIcon()` / `shouldNotHaveIcon()`. `hasBadge()`: `shouldHaveBadge()` / `shouldNotHaveBadge()`.
`getBadgeElement()`: the badge element (throws without a badge).
`select()`: clicks the tab.
`getHref()`: the `href` attribute or `null`; `shouldHaveHref(href)`.
`getContainer()`, `element`: the `<li>` item.

components.name: TableCell

does.text: A column with no `preset` shows the value as written on one line, as wide as its content, never cut, with no tooltip; a blank value (`null`, `undefined`, empty or spaces) shows `-` (DataTable#43).
An empty value shows `-` as plain text in every preset; a `link`, `avatar`, `number` or `badge` cell never shows an empty value as a link or badge.

A `link` preset cell shows the value (or `label`) as a link in the normal text colour with no underline, turning primary on hover, with a pointer cursor; with `href` it is a real anchor, without `href` a focusable button that runs `onClick` on click or Enter.
A `link` with `href` and `onClick`: a plain click runs `onClick` (no page load), Ctrl / Cmd / Shift / Alt or middle click follows `href` (a new tab).
A `link` with `href` and `external`: primary colour, the external-link icon, opens in a new tab.
A `link` with `disabled` (or a row function returning true) shows the text as plain text, not a link, and no greyed link (a tooltip, when set, still shows).
Clicking a link cell's link runs its handler and does not select the row or open an editor.
Focusing the cell with the grid keys (or `focusCell`) does not activate its link; only a click or Enter on the link does (TC-6412).

A `date` preset cell shows the value as a date `dd/mm/yyyy` (locale `en-gb`, two-digit day and month), with `showTime` also `hh:mm`; the table's or the provider's `dateFormatOptions` change it; a value that is not a date shows as written.

A `date` with `relative` shows, for a date in the last 7 days, the time since with a capital first letter (`5 minutes ago`, `Yesterday` as the locale words it); an older or a future date shows the absolute date.
A `date` with `tooltip` shows it on hover and focus (TC-6118).
A `badge` preset cell shows the value (or `label`) as a Badge with the preset's `severity` and `variant`; a `severity` function returning `null` for a row shows that row's label as plain text.
A `badge` with `textOverflow` shortens a long label and shows the full label on hover and on cell keyboard focus (TC-6413).
A `badges` preset cell shows the array as a BadgeGroup: the first `limit` badges, then a `+N more` button that opens a dialog with every value (TC-6115, TC-6127).
A `textList` preset cell shows the first `limit` values joined by `, `, then `+N more` that opens a dialog listing every value; `+2 more` for three values and limit 1 (TC-6127).
A `textList` or `badges` cell with no value shows `emptyLabel` (`textList` only) or `-`.
A `labels` preset cell shows each label in its stored background and foreground colours, side by side; a label whose colours are not hex is skipped; none left shows `-` (TC-6123).
An `avatar` preset cell shows an Avatar (the picture, or the name's initials without `src`) with the name beside it; the name is a link when `onClick` or `href` is set, as in TableCell#3.
A `gallery` preset cell shows a link `View photo` (or `label`) that opens the photos full screen; no image shows `-` (TC-6122).

A `file` preset cell shows the file name as a link to `href`: an image file (by the URL extension, or `image`) opens the full-screen gallery on the page, another file opens in a new tab as an external link; with no URL the name is plain text (TC-6122).
A `file` image that cannot be loaded closes the gallery, then runs `onError` with the row (TC-6283).
A `number` preset cell shows the value formatted in the active locale with thousands grouping and no decimals; `0` is a value, only no value shows `-`; a value that is not a number shows as written.
A `number` with `onClick` is a link (also at 0); with `emphasis` the number is bold in that colour, as text, not a badge.
A `number` with `prefix` / `suffix` writes them around the number (`#1234 pcs`); with `unit` the locale writes the unit (`3 days`) (TC-6128).
A `currency` preset cell shows `{ currency, value }` as money in the active locale with two decimals (`$12.50`); anything else shows `-` (TC-6128).
A `progress` preset cell shows a bar and `done / total (percent%)` (`3 / 10 (30%)`, percent rounded); a row without both numbers shows `-`; a total of 0 shows the text with `0%` and no bar (TC-6124).
A `breakdown` preset cell shows the total, then one muted line per part `label amount` with a colour marker; with `ring` also a ring of the parts to the left (TC-6130).
A `breakdown` with total 0 shows just the formatted 0 without parts; no value shows `-`.
An `icon` preset cell shows its icons in primary, each with its label as tooltip and accessible name (`role="img"`); none shows `emptyLabel` muted, else `-` (TC-6126).
An `image` preset cell shows the URL as a thumbnail (32 px by default); an empty or broken URL shows the Image placeholder, not `-` (TC-6121).
A `code` preset cell shows the value in capitals (`some-uniq-id` becomes `SOME-UNIQ-ID`) (TC-6134).
A `color` preset cell shows a swatch of the stored colour, then its `#RRGGBB` in capitals (`ff0000` and `f00` read `#FF0000`); a value that is not a hex colour shows `-` (TC-6129).
A `longText` preset cell shows at most two lines then an ellipsis, in a column at most 500 px wide unless the column sets its own width; the full text shows on hover only while it is cut (TC-6174).

A `userName` preset cell shows `[First Name] [Last Initial]` (`Budi S`); a one-word name shows whole; the full name shows on hover always, and while the cell holds keyboard focus (also its `aria-description`) (TC-6129).
A `switch` preset cell shows a Switch (`aria-label` `Row switch`) that flips at once and then runs `onSwitch`; a `false` or rejected result puts it back (TC-6125, TC-6368).
A `switch` with `tristate` shows a TriStateSwitch: a click cycles neutral, on, off, neutral (see TriStateSwitch#2, TriStateSwitch#3 for the control itself) (TC-6125).
A `checkbox` preset cell shows a Checkbox (`aria-label` `Row checkbox`) that toggles at once and then runs `onCheck`; a `false` or rejected result puts it back (TC-6368).
A toggle cell with `tooltip` shows it on hover (and on focus while enabled); on a disabled Switch it still shows, on a disabled Checkbox it does not (the checkbox swallows hover).

A column with `trailing` shows its items after the value, outside the value's click target: a `badge`, an `icon` (`role="img"`, label as tooltip and name; with `onClick` an icon button with that `aria-label`) or `text`; they wrap below the value in a narrow column (TC-6119, TC-6132).

A `field` preset cell shows a form input in the cell (`text`, `textarea`, `number`, `currency`, `phone`, `date`, `file`, `select`, `multiselect`, `treeselect`) bound to the surrounding Form; typing or choosing changes the form value (TC-6131).
Pressing Enter or Space on a focused cell runs the row click (DataTable#84).

With `cellEditing` on, a `editable` cell shows an inline editor on double-click (`singleClick` or Enter only per `editTrigger`): text `Row editable input`, number `Row editable numberinput`, select `Row editable select`, date `Row editable datepicker`, checkbox `Row editable checkbox`, or the column's `editor`.
Enter or leaving a text or number editor commits the value; a select, date or checkbox editor commits when a value is chosen; Escape cancels; Tab commits and opens the next editable cell.
While the row is in row edit mode, its editable cells show editors, and preset toggles in that row are inert.

doesNot.text: Does not show a tooltip on a plain cell, a `code` cell or a `number` cell; the cells with a tooltip are `date`, `badge`, `link`, `icon`, `userName`, `longText`, a toggle with `tooltip`, and `trailing` badges and icons (TC-6174).
Does not show a `longText` tooltip while its text is shown whole (TC-6174).
Does not cut or ellipse a plain cell's text.
Does not underline a link cell's link, at rest or on hover (TC-6175).
Does not show a `link` preset with `disabled` as a link: no anchor, no button, no pointer cursor (TC-6117).
Does not make a `trailing` item part of a link value; a link value stays the only link.
Does not sort an `image` column unless it sets `sortable` (DataTable#23).
Does not show the empty text for a `currency` value of 0 or a `number` value of 0; 0 is shown.
Does not add a translated word through `prefix` / `suffix`; the locale writes units through `unit`.
Does not open an editor on a cell without `editable`, nor without `cellEditing` on the table.

defaults.text: Empty cell text `-` (`emptyCellText`) (DataTable#43).
Boolean `booleanValue` columns show `Yes` / `No` (`trueText` / `falseText`).

`link`: `target` `_self`, not external, not disabled; `date`: no time, absolute; `number`: grouping on, 0 decimals, `unitDisplay` `long`; `textList`: `limit` 1; `gallery`: label `View photo`; `image`: size 32; `color`: shape `square`; `progress`: severity primary; `breakdown`: no ring, 0 decimals.
Cell editing: trigger double-click; Enter does not move to the cell below.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `preset.type`: chooses the cell type (TableCell#3 to TableCell#40); `cell(value, row, index)` replaces the preset.
`trailing(row)`: items after the value (TableCell#39).

`tooltip` on `link`, `date`, `badge`; `severity`, `variant`, `label`, `textOverflow` on `badge`; `limit`, `dialogHeader`, `dialogContent` on `badges` and `textList`: as described in their lines above.
`editable`, `editor`, `cellEditing`, `editTrigger`, `enterCommitAdvance`: single-cell edit (TableCell#42, TableCell#43).
`dateFormatOptions` on a column (also without a `date` preset): formats that column's values as dates.

builtInText.text: `-` empty cell; `View photo` gallery link; `+N more` overflow link and dialog header `All Items` (locale en, through `t()`; the dialog header is the BadgeGroup default, `dialogHeader` replaces it); `Yes` / `No` boolean (DataTable#79).
Toggle `aria-label`s `Row switch`, `Row checkbox`; editor `aria-label`s `Row editable input`, `Row editable numberinput`, `Row editable select`, `Row editable datepicker`, `Row editable checkbox`.

keyboard.text: Arrow keys, Home, End, PageUp and PageDown move between cells; Enter or Space on a focused cell runs the row click (DataTable#82, DataTable#84); the cell has a focus ring while focused (TC-6175 for a link).
Tab reaches the next link of a link cell and shows its focus ring (TC-6175, TC-6265).
Enter on a focused `button` link or gallery link runs it; Escape leaves an open cell editor, and Escape on a plain cell is not consumed (DataTable#85).

states.text: Link: rest and hover differ in colour (hover primary), never underlined; focused: a focus ring (TC-6175).
Truncated (`longText` cut, or a shortened badge): its tooltip is enabled; shown whole: no tooltip (TC-6174).
Selected (cell selection on): `aria-selected` true on the cell; focused: it holds the roving grid focus.
Editing: the editor replaces the display; committed or cancelled: the display returns.
Toggle cell disabled (`disabled` boolean or row function): the Switch or Checkbox is disabled and does not flip.

testApi: Resolve through the table or a row: `table.getCell(header, row)`, `row.getCell(header)`, `table.getFocusedCell()`.
`getContainer()`, `getText()` / `shouldHaveText`, `getField()` (the column field key).
`click()`, `doubleClick()`, `focus()`, `isFocused()`, `isSelected()`.

Link: `hasLink()`, `getLinkHref()`, `clickLink()`, `hoverLink()`, `focusLink()`, `isLinkFocused()` / `shouldBeLinkFocused()`, `getLinkColor()`, `getLinkTextDecoration()`, `getLinkLabel()`, `hasFocusRing()`, `getCursor()`.
Text: `getTextColor()`, `isBold()` / `shouldBeBold()` / `shouldNotBeBold()`, `isTruncated()` / `shouldNotBeTruncated()`.
Tooltip: `hasTooltip()` / `shouldHaveTooltip()`, `getTooltip()` (Tooltip wrapper), `getTooltipText()` (hovers once).
Badges: `getBadge()`, `getBadges()`, `getBadgeGroup()` (a `badges` cell); `getMoreText()`, `openOverflow()`, `getOverflowItems()` (`textList` and `badges`), `getTextListItems()`.
Media: `getAvatar()`, `hasAvatar()`, `getImage()`, `hasImage()`, `openGallery()` (a Gallery wrapper), `getLabels()`, `getColorHex()`.
Numbers: `getProgressBar()`, `getBreakdownTotal()`, `getBreakdownParts()`, `hasBreakdownRing()`.
Toggles: `getSwitch()`, `getTriStateSwitch()`, `getCheckbox()`.
Icons and trailing: `getIconLabels()`, `getIconTooltip(label)`, `clickTrailingAction(label)`.
Field: `getFieldInput()`, `getFieldSelect()`, `getFieldMultiSelect()`, `getFieldTreeSelect()`, `getFieldDatePicker()`.
Editing: `startEdit()`, `getEditor()`, `setEditorValue(value)`, `commit()`, `cancel()`.

components.name: TableRow

does.text: Shows one body row per record of the current page, its cells in column order, one cell per visible column (DataTable#1, DataTable#19).
A cell with no value shows `-` (DataTable#43); what each cell shows by column type is TableCell#1 and following.
Clicking the row selects it (clicking again deselects it) when selection is on; a click on the checkbox cell or the actions button does not toggle it twice (DataTable#13, DataTable#45, DataTable#46).
With `selectionType` `multiple` the row starts with a checkbox cell (aria-label `Row selection checkbox`); checking it selects the row (DataTable#44, DataTable#68).
A row that `isRowDisabled` or `isRowSelectable` rejects has a disabled checkbox, is skipped by header select-all, and stays listed (DataTable#12, DataTable#90).

Hovering the checkbox cell of a disabled row shows the reason `isRowDisabled` returned; hovering an unselected row at the `maxSelected` limit shows `You've reached the maximum selection of {limit} rows.` (DataTable#35, DataTable#47, DataTable#75).
With `showRowOptions` on, the row ends with an actions button (aria-label and tooltip `Action`) that opens the row's menu; clicking it again closes it (DataTable#17, DataTable#65, DataTable#69).
A `rowOptions` item chosen in the menu runs for that row only (DataTable#65).
With `isRowActionDisabled(row)` returning true, only that row's actions button is disabled; a non-empty string returned shows as its hover tooltip instead of `Action` (DataTable#65).

With `rowExpansion` or `treeData` the row has an expand button (`Expand row` / `Collapse row`) that shows or hides the nested detail or child rows; a tree row has `aria-level` and `aria-expanded` (DataTable#66, DataTable#79).
Rows of one line of text have the same height; a row with a cell whose text wraps is taller than them (proved by TC-6173).
A row in a `groupRowsBy` table sits under its group row, which has its own `Expand group` / `Collapse group` button (DataTable#66, DataTable#79).

doesNot.text: Does not show a checkbox cell for `selectionType` `single` or `none`; a single-select row selects by clicking the row (DataTable#26).
Does not select on a row click when `selectOnRowClick` is `false`; only its checkbox does (DataTable#46).
Does not carry a `data-selected` state when `selectionType` is `none`.
Does not show an actions button when `showRowOptions` is off (DataTable#37).
Does not show a tooltip on its checkbox, except the disabled-row reason and the `maxSelected` hint (DataTable#35).
Does not show a drag handle while any column is sorted, and only with `reorderable` (DataTable#34, DataTable#61).

defaults.text: Not selected; no checkbox cell (`selectionType` `none`); `showRowOptions` on (DataTable#37).
The row's identity is its `dataKey` / `getRowId` value, readable as the row id (wrapper `getRowId`); `null` when none is set.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `selectionType`, `selectOnRowClick`, `maxSelected`, `isRowDisabled`, `isRowSelectable`: as in DataTable#44 to DataTable#47.
`rowOptions`, `isRowActionDisabled`, `actionDisabledHint`, `actionTooltip`: the actions menu items, the per-row disabling and its hover text (DataTable#65).
`rowExpansion`, `treeData`, `groupRowsBy`, `reorderable`: expand button, tree rows, group rows, drag handle (DataTable#61, DataTable#66).
`onRowClick` / `onRowDoubleClick` / `onRowContextMenu`: the handler runs with the row's record on that gesture (DataTable#84).
`rowHeight` (`fixed`, `auto`, a number, a string, or a function of the row): sets the row height instead of the default.

builtInText.text: Checkbox `Row selection checkbox`; actions button `Action`; expand `Expand row` / `Collapse row`; group `Expand group` / `Collapse group`; edit `Save row` / `Cancel edit`; menu panel `Row action menu panel` (DataTable#68, DataTable#69, DataTable#79; locale en, through `t()`).
Cap hint `You've reached the maximum selection of {limit} rows.` (DataTable#75).

keyboard.text: Arrow keys move between cells of the grid, Enter or Space on a focused cell runs the row click and toggles the row selection (DataTable#82, DataTable#84).

states.text: Selected: `data-selected` true on the row and its checkbox checked (DataTable#88).

Disabled by `isRowDisabled` or `disableAllRows`: only the selection checkbox is disabled; the row has no `aria-disabled`, its own actions (single action, row options) stay clickable, and it stays listed (DataTable#90).
Expanded / collapsed: the expand button `aria-expanded` true / false.
Actions menu open: the actions button `aria-expanded` true while that row's menu is open.

testApi: Resolve through the table: `getRow(i)`, `getAllRows()`, `getRowByCellText(header, text)`, `getSelectedRows()`.
`getContainer()`: the row element. `getRowId()`: its id or `null`. `getHeight()` / `shouldHaveHeight(px)`: rendered height in px.
`getCell(header)`: a TableCell wrapper; `getCellText(header)` / `shouldHaveCellText(text, header)`.
`getCheckbox()`, `hasCheckbox()` / `shouldHaveCheckbox()` / `shouldNotHaveCheckbox()`; throws when the row has no checkbox.
`getSelectionTooltipText()` / `shouldHaveSelectionTooltipText(text)`: hovers the selection cell once; `''` when none.
`select()`, `deselect()` (no-op when already so; a single-select table clicks the row), `isSelected()` / `shouldBeSelected()` / `shouldNotBeSelected()`.
`getExpandButton()`, `hasExpandButton()`, `expand()`, `collapse()`, `isExpanded()`.

`getRowOptionsButton()`, `getRowOptionsLabel()` / `shouldHaveRowOptionsLabel(text)`, `hasRowOptions()` / `shouldHaveRowOptions()` / `shouldNotHaveRowOptions()`, `openRowOptions()`, `getRowOptionsMenu()` (a Menu wrapper), `clickRowOption(label)`.
`isDisabled()` / `shouldBeDisabled()`: true when the row's selection checkbox is disabled.

components.name: TableToolbar

does.text: Renders one row (`role="group"`, named by its `aria-label` when given) with the bulk-action area on the left and the extra, tools and primary-action slots in a right-aligned group.
Fixed order inside the right group: `extra`, then `tools`, then `primaryAction` (rightmost).
The bulk-action area is always in the DOM and is hidden while it holds nothing, so the right group stays at the right edge; it shows when `bulkAction` renders content.
A `bulkAction` element that itself renders nothing (a BulkActionButton with no selection) leaves the area hidden.
The `extra`, `tools` and `primaryAction` containers exist only when their prop is truthy; an omitted, `null`, `false` or empty-string slot is not rendered at all.
Tools sit side by side with a small gap; `primaryAction` does not shrink.

doesNot.text: Does not render any button, search, filter or export control of its own; every control is supplied by the slots.
Does not know the table: no selection, search or data state; it never shows or hides the bulk area from a selection.
`extra` is not a left-side slot; it stays in the right group before `tools`.
Does not wrap, collapse or hide slots at narrow widths; it is one flex line.
Has no accessible name of its own when `aria-label` is omitted; it is found by a slotted control's name instead.

defaults.text: No slot is filled, no `aria-label`; the root is a full-width row with the two areas split to the ends.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `aria-label`: names the group (needed to tell several toolbars on one page apart).
`bulkAction`: content on the left; the area is visible only when it has content.
