`extra`: a container before `tools` in the right group.
`tools`: a container for auxiliary controls (search, filter, export, column menu).
`primaryAction`: a container as the rightmost element.

states.text: Bulk area: hidden (no content) or visible (content); it is the only part that toggles. The other slots are present or absent.

testApi: Finder: `Spectra.findTableToolbar(label)` / `queryTableToolbar(label)`; `label` is the toolbar's `aria-label` or the accessible name of a control in any slot (the finder walks up to the row). With several toolbars give each an `aria-label`; the first toolbar containing a control name wins.
Containers: `getContainer`, `getBulkAction` (always resolves), `getActionsGroup` (always resolves), `getExtra`, `getTools`, `getPrimaryAction` (these three throw when the slot is not rendered).
Presence: `hasBulkAction` (reads visibility, not DOM presence), `hasExtra`, `hasTools`, `hasPrimaryAction`; `shouldHave*` / `shouldNotHave*` poll.
Layout: `isToolsRightAligned` (`shouldBeToolsRightAligned`).
Scoped lookup: `findTool(label)`, `queryTool(label)`, `hasTool(label)`, `getButtonLabels()` (visible buttons in DOM order; `shouldHaveButtonLabels([...])`).
Readers other than `find*` wait `probeTimeout` (500ms); `hasBulkAction` depends on the built presets (`empty:hidden`).

components.name: Tabs

does.text: Shows one horizontal bar of tabs, one per entry in `items`, in order, with exactly one tab marked active (`aria-selected="true"`, the others `aria-selected="false"`).
Clicking an enabled tab makes it the active tab, and the active look moves to it.
Enter or Space on a focused tab activates it, same as a click.
A tab with `href` is drawn as a link (`<a href>` with `role="tab"`, inside an `<li role="presentation">`); a tab without `href` is the `<li role="tab">` itself, with no link inside.
Clicking a tab with `href` makes it active and also follows the link; with `renderLink` the app's own link component is shown instead of the plain `<a>`.
A tab can show an icon before its label and a count badge after it.
A bar wider than its box scrolls sideways with no scrollbar and no scroll buttons, and the active tab is scrolled into view when it changes.
When the box is resized, the bar keeps the active tab in view and (for `line`) realigns the underline.
Only the active, enabled tab is in the Tab key order (`tabindex="0"`); every other tab has `tabindex="-1"`.
Controlled: with `value`, the active tab follows `value`, a click only calls `onValueChange` and the highlight moves when the app passes the new value.

doesNot.text: Does not render the section content under a tab: the app shows its own panel (no `tabpanel`, no `aria-controls`).
Does not read or match the URL: a tab with `href` is not made active by the current route, the app keeps `value` in step.
Clicking or pressing Enter/Space on a disabled tab does nothing: it does not become active, `onValueChange` is not called and its `href` is not followed.
Arrow keys only move focus; they do not activate the tab they land on (Enter, Space or click does).
Does not call `onValueChange` when the clicked tab is already the active one.
Does not translate tab labels: they show exactly as given in `label`.
The bar's accessible name cannot be set by the app: no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` prop is accepted.
A tab without `href` shows no link element; a tab with `href` that is `disabled` still draws the link but cannot be activated.
Does not wrap tabs onto a second row or shrink them: label text is cut with an ellipsis and the bar scrolls.

defaults.text: `variant` `line`; `grow` false; the first tab in `items` is active when neither `value` nor `defaultValue` is given.
With no items nothing is active and the bar is empty.
A string or number `badge` shows a small `secondary` badge (size `xs`) with that text.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `variant="line"`: a bottom border runs under the bar and a sliding underline sits under the active tab; no other variant draws it.
`variant="pill"`: tabs are rounded pills, the active one with a filled background.
`variant="plain"`: text only, the active tab differs by colour, with no underline and no pill.
`grow: true`: tabs share the full width equally; off, each tab is as wide as its content.
`value` + `onValueChange`: controlled; `defaultValue` alone: uncontrolled, starting on that tab.
`item.disabled`: that tab is dimmed, `aria-disabled="true"`, takes no pointer events, `tabindex="-1"` and is skipped by arrow, Home and End keys.
`item.badge` as a badge config object: the badge shows with those settings (size defaults to `xs`).
`className` is added to the root `<nav>`.

builtInText.text: The root `<nav>` has `aria-label` `Tabs` (English; passed through the app's translation).

keyboard.text: Right and Left Arrow move focus to the next or previous enabled tab and wrap around at the ends; Home and End move to the first and last enabled tab.
Enter or Space activates the focused tab; Space does not scroll the page.
Tab reaches the active tab only, and leaves the bar on the next Tab press.

states.text: Active: `aria-selected="true"`, active colour (and underline or pill fill by variant).
Disabled: `aria-disabled="true"`, reduced opacity, not-allowed cursor, not clickable.
Inactive enabled tab: hover changes its colour or pill fill; keyboard focus shows a primary focus ring.

testApi: `Spectra.findTabs(label)` / `queryTabs(label)`: finds the tab bar (`<nav>`); `label` is the accessible name or one of its tab labels (all specs find it by a tab label); `queryTabs` gives `null` when absent. Also chained from a container.
`getContainer()`, `element`: the root `<nav>`.
`getTab(label)` / `queryTab(label)`: the `TabItem` wrapper whose label text matches (a count badge beside it is ignored); `getTab` throws, `queryTab` gives `null`.
`getTabs()`: every tab as a wrapper, in order. `getActiveTab()`: the active tab, or `null`.
`selectTab(label)`: finds and clicks the tab. `hasTab(label)`: boolean; `shouldHaveTab(label)` / `shouldNotHaveTab(label)`.
`getTabLabels()`: labels in order; `shouldHaveTabLabels([...])`. `getActiveTabLabel()`: label or `null`; `shouldHaveActiveTabLabel(label)`.
`scrollTabs('start' | 'end')`: scrolls an overflowing bar. `getVisibleTabLabels()`: labels of tabs wholly in view; `shouldHaveVisibleTabLabels([...])`.
TabItem wrapper: see TabItem contract.

components.name: Textarea

does.text: Renders a native multi-line text box that shows the typed text, wraps long lines and scrolls once the text exceeds its height.
Typing updates the text and calls `onChange` with the new full string (not an event).
Enter inserts a new line; line breaks are kept in the value.
Uncontrolled (`defaultValue`): the box starts with that text and keeps whatever the user types.
Controlled (`value`): the box shows `value`; typing calls `onChange`, and the shown text changes only when the parent passes the new `value`.
`placeholder` shows in a faded colour while the box is empty and disappears as soon as there is text.
`maxLength` stops the user from typing more characters than the limit.
`invalid` draws a danger-coloured outline and sets `aria-invalid="true"`.
Focus switches the outline to the primary colour and thickens it; blur restores the neutral outline.
`onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onClick`, `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp` fire with the native event.
The user can resize the box vertically by dragging its corner handle (default `resize` is `vertical`).
`aria-describedby` passes through to the focusable field, so the text of the elements it names (a surrounding `Field`'s helper or error text) is its accessible description.

doesNot.text: Does not render a label, helper text, error text, counter or required mark; those come from a surrounding `Field`.
Does not trim, filter or validate the text.
Does not accept typing, and does not call `onChange`, while `disabled` or `readOnly`.
A `readOnly` box still takes focus and its text can be selected and copied.
Does not offer prefix or suffix addons or rich text formatting.
Does not grow with the content unless `autoResize` is set; by default a fixed height of `rows` lines with an internal scrollbar.
`cols` does not narrow the box in the design system: the box stays as wide as its container (full width) unless `autoResize` or a horizontal or both resize is set.
`autoResize` removes the drag handle: the `resize` prop is ignored while it is on.
`autoResize` has no maximum height: the box grows without limit unless the caller sets a `max-height`.

defaults.text: Empty text, 5 visible rows, enabled, editable, valid.
`size` is `xs`: 28 px minimum height, 16 px horizontal and 6 px vertical padding, small body text.
`resize` is `vertical`; `autoResize` is false.
Full width of the parent.
`aria-invalid` is always present on the box, `"false"` while valid.
No placeholder, no `maxLength`, no `name`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `rows`: how many lines tall the box is at first (the minimum height with `autoResize`).
`autoResize`: the box grows and shrinks to fit its text on every value change, without a scrollbar, and shrink-wraps its width (`w-fit`) instead of full width.
`resize: 'none' | 'horizontal' | 'both'`: removes the handle or lets the user drag horizontally or both ways; horizontal and both also shrink-wrap the width.
`size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` (also responsive): minimum heights 32, 40, 48 px with larger text and padding.
`disabled`: greyed background, dimmed text, not-allowed cursor, no focus, no typing.
`readOnly`: normal look with a default cursor, no typing.
`invalid`: see Does; an explicit `aria-invalid` replaces the value taken from `invalid`.
`maxLength`, `placeholder`, `name`, `autoFocus`, `cols`: the native attribute of the same name.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling of the box itself.

keyboard.text: Tab moves focus into and out of the box; Tab does not insert a tab character.
Enter adds a line break and does not submit a form.
Typed keys can be observed through `onKeyDown` and `onKeyUp`.

states.text: Default: neutral outline, light background.
Focused: thicker primary outline.
Invalid: danger outline, also while focused.
Disabled: greyed background and text, not-allowed cursor.
Read-only: default cursor, otherwise as default.
Filled and empty differ only by the placeholder showing.
Loading: none (no such prop).

testApi: `Spectra.findTextarea(label)` by `aria-label` or the associated label text; `Spectra.queryTextarea(label)` is `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindTextarea(label)`.
`getValue()` (`shouldHaveValue(text)`); `setValue(text)` clears, then types (line breaks kept); `clearValue()` selects all and presses Backspace.
`focus()`, `blur()`.
`isDisabled()` (`shouldBeDisabled()`): disabled attribute, `aria-disabled` on the box or the container.
`isReadOnly()` (`shouldBeReadOnly()`), `isInvalid()` (`shouldBeInvalid()`: `aria-invalid="true"` on the box or its container).
`getPlaceholder()` (`shouldHavePlaceholder(text)`), `getRows()` (`shouldHaveRows(n)`; 5 when the attribute is missing), `getMaxLength()` (`shouldHaveMaxLength(n)`; `null` when none).
`getContainer()`: the nearest `textarea.root` or `field.root` ancestor, else the box itself.
`getAccessibleDescription()` (`shouldHaveAccessibleDescription(text)` waits).

components.name: ThemeSwitcher

does.text: Shows a small pill switch with a round thumb; the thumb is on the left with a sun icon in light mode and on the right with a moon icon in dark mode.
Shows a text label inside the track: `Light` in light mode, `Dark` in dark mode.
Clicking it flips between light and dark; the label and thumb icon follow.
It is a switch: `role="switch"` and `aria-checked="true"` while dark, `"false"` while light.
Inside `WangsUiProvider`, with no `mode`, `defaultMode` or `onModeChange`, it shows the app's current mode and flips the whole app theme between light and dark when clicked.
With `defaultMode`, it starts in that mode and keeps its own state afterwards, independent of the app theme.
With `mode` (controlled), it always shows `mode`; a click only calls `onModeChange` with the new mode, and the switch changes only when the parent passes the new `mode`.
`onModeChange` receives `'dark'` when switched on and `'light'` when switched off.
`loading` shows a spinner on the thumb in place of the sun or moon icon, and the switch cannot be flipped.

doesNot.text: Does not flip and does not call `onModeChange` while `disabled` or `loading`.
With `onModeChange` given (and no `mode`), a click does not change the app theme itself; the parent must apply it, and until the app theme changes the switch does not move.
With `defaultMode` or `mode`, a click does not change the app theme unless the parent does it in `onModeChange`.
Offers only light and dark: no System or third option.
Does not show a visible text label next to the switch (only the label inside the track).
Does not store the chosen mode anywhere (no persistence of its own).
Without a surrounding provider it cannot change any theme: it stays in `light` (or its `defaultMode`/`mode`).

defaults.text: Accessible name (`aria-label`): `Toggle theme mode`.
`showTrackLabel` is on; labels `Dark` and `Light`.
Icons: moon (`MoonFill`) for dark, sun (`SunLine`) for light.
Not disabled, not loading.
Switch size `md`; the pill is 50 by 24 px with a 20 px thumb.
With no `defaultMode`, the starting mode is the app's current mode, or `light` when there is no provider.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `showTrackLabel: false`: no text in the track.
`darkLabel`, `lightLabel`: replace `Dark` and `Light`; a node is rendered as is.
`darkIcon`, `lightIcon`: replace the moon and sun icon.
`mode`, `defaultMode`, `onModeChange`: see Does.
`disabled`: dimmed, cannot be flipped, removed from the tab order.
`loading`: see Does.
`aria-label`: replaces `Toggle theme mode`.

Other Switch props (`label`, `description`, `labelPosition`, `invalid`, `inputId`, `className`, `style`) pass through to the Switch; `label` makes the label the accessible name and hides `aria-label`.

builtInText.text: Accessible name `Toggle theme mode`; track labels `Dark` and `Light` (fixed English strings, not translated).

keyboard.text: Tab focuses the switch; Space flips it, as a native switch.
A disabled or loading switcher is skipped by Tab.

states.text: Light: light track, left thumb, sun icon, `Light` label.
Dark: inverted (dark) track, right thumb, moon icon, `Dark` label.
Disabled: dimmed and not clickable.
Loading: spinner on the thumb, not clickable.
Focused: focus halo around the thumb, as the Switch.

testApi: `Spectra.findThemeSwitcher(label)` finds by `aria-label` (`Toggle theme mode` by default); `Spectra.queryThemeSwitcher(label)` returns `null` when missing.
`getMode()` (`shouldHaveMode('light' | 'dark')`): `'dark'` while checked.
`setMode(mode)`: flips only when the switcher shows the other mode (setting the current mode again changes nothing).

Every Switch reader applies: `isChecked()` (`shouldBeChecked()`), `isDisabled()` (`shouldBeDisabled()`), `isLoading()`, `getTrackText()` (`shouldHaveTrackText('Light')`), `toggle()`, `check()`, `uncheck()`, `focus()`, `blur()`, `isFocused()`.

components.name: Timeline

does.text: Renders one event row per item of `events`, in exactly the array order given; nothing is sorted and timestamps are not validated.

`direction="bottom-up"` (default) stacks the rows in reverse, so the last item of `events` appears at the top; `direction="top-down"` shows the first item at the top. `direction` changes only the visual order, not the data order.
A thin vertical connector line joins each marker to the next one; the bottom-most row has no connector below it (in `top-down` the last item, in `bottom-up` the first item).
The root is named by `aria-label` (a plain container with no role); that name is what finds it.

`collapsible` (default on) is one switch for the whole list: with it on, only events that have `detail` get a chevron toggle and start collapsed; with it off every event's detail is always visible (see `TimelineEvent#5`, `TimelineEvent#8`).
Expansion is kept per event inside the Timeline and each toggle changes only its own event (`TimelineEvent#10`).
`defaultExpanded` expands all events that have detail at first render (`TimelineEvent#21`).
The Timeline grows to fit all its rows (shows all events); it has no height limit or scrolling of its own.
An empty `events` array (or none) renders an empty container with no rows.

doesNot.text: Does not sort `events` by timestamp, and `direction` does not reverse the data.
Does not offer a controlled expansion: after first render the expanded set cannot be set from outside (`defaultExpanded` seeds it once).
Does not support `aria-labelledby` (only `aria-label` reaches the root).
Does not show an empty state, loading state or "no events" text.
Does not page, group by date or load more.
Does not scroll or cap its height (put overflow on a parent, e.g. a ScrollArea).
Does not expand events that are added after first render because of `defaultExpanded`.
Does not pin a locale: dates use the runtime default locale unless `formatDate` or `renderDate` is given.

defaults.text: `direction` `bottom-up`, `collapsible` `true`, `defaultExpanded` `false`, `events` `[]`.
Date text `DD Mon YYYY` in the runtime locale (day 2-digit, month short, year numeric).

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `direction="top-down"`: first item on top.
`collapsible={false}`: all details visible, no toggles.
`defaultExpanded`: initially expanded details (only with `collapsible`).
`formatDate`: custom date text; `renderDate`: replaces the whole timestamp area (wins over `formatDate`).
`renderMarker`, `renderAction`, `renderUser`, `renderDetail`: custom marker / action / user / detail per event (`TimelineEvent#11`, `TimelineEvent#12`).
`aria-label`: the accessible name of the root.

`className`, `pt`: styling only (`pt` sections include `root`, `event`, `separator`, `connector`, `marker`, `markerToggle`, `markerChevron`, `markerDot`, `content`, `header`, `action`, `user`, `timestamp`, `detail`, `detailContentRow`, `detailContentKey`, `detailContentValue`, `avatar`).

builtInText.text: Toggle labels `Expand detail` / `Collapse detail` and the detail row key format `<key>:` (see `TimelineEvent#26`, `TimelineEvent#27`).
No other built-in text.

keyboard.text: Tab moves through the chevron toggles in visual order of the rows; Enter or Space toggles (`TimelineEvent#28`).

states.text: Per event: collapsed, expanded, non-interactive (`TimelineEvent#30`, `TimelineEvent#31`, `TimelineEvent#32`).
Disabled, loading, empty, error: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findTimeline(name)` by `aria-label` of the root (`data-ui-section="timeline.root"`); `Spectra.queryTimeline(name)`: `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindTimeline(name)`.
`getContainer()`: the root element.
`getEvents()`: array of event wrappers in DOM order (with `bottom-up` the DOM order is array order, displayed reversed); `[]` when none; `shouldHaveEventsCount(n)`.
`getEvent(index)`: the event at that 0-based DOM position; throws `Timeline event at index N not found. Total events: M.` when out of range.
`getEventCount()` / `shouldHaveEventCount(n)`: number of event rows.
Event wrapper (`TimelineEvent`): see the TimelineEvent contract.

components.name: TimelineEvent

does.text: Each event row shows a marker on the timeline axis and, beside it, a header with the action text, the user (if any) and the timestamp, and below the header the detail (if shown).
The action text is `event.action`; text between backticks is rendered bold (`` Updated `invoice-42` `` shows `invoice-42` in bold), the backticks themselves are not shown.
The timestamp is shown formatted by the runtime locale as day, abbreviated month, year (e.g. `02 Jan 2024` in `en`); a value that cannot be parsed as a date is shown as given.

An event with a `user` shows a small avatar with the person's name beside the header; with `firstName` and `lastName` the name reads first name plus the last name's initial (`John D`), otherwise the full name.
When the Timeline is collapsible and the event has `detail`, the marker is a small round chevron toggle button; the detail is hidden until it is clicked.
Clicking the toggle (or pressing Enter or Space on it) expands the detail with a short (0.2 s) height and fade animation and rotates the chevron; clicking again collapses it.
The expanded detail is a region (`role="region"`) listing every `detail` entry as a row `key:` then value; an object value is shown as JSON text, other values as their text.

An event without `detail`, or any event when the Timeline is not collapsible, has a plain round dot marker that does nothing when clicked; with the Timeline not collapsible the detail (when present) is always shown.
The toggle exposes `aria-expanded` (`true` when expanded, `false` when collapsed) and `aria-controls` pointing at the detail region (`id` `timeline-detail-<event id>`).
Each event expands and collapses independently of the others.

A custom `renderMarker` result replaces the dot or chevron; when the event is interactive that marker becomes `role="button"` with `tabIndex` 0, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and toggles on click, Enter or Space. A `renderMarker` that returns `null` or `undefined` falls back to the default marker.

`renderAction`, `renderUser`, `renderDate` and `renderDetail` replace the action text, the user part, the timestamp and the detail rows; `renderDate` wins over `formatDate`; `formatDate` replaces the default date text.

doesNot.text: A non-interactive event's marker has no button role, no `tabIndex`, no `aria-expanded`, no `aria-controls`.
An event without `user` shows no avatar and no name.
An event with an empty `detail` object ({}) and collapsible Timeline still counts as having detail: the toggle shows, and the expanded region is empty (no rows).
An event cannot be collapsed individually when the Timeline is not collapsible (no per-event `collapsible` setting exists).
The toggle does not move or reorder events, and does not change the other events' expansion.
The timestamp is not relative (`2 hours ago`): it is a formatted date; no time of day is shown by default.

defaults.text: Collapsed on first render (Timeline `defaultExpanded` false).
Marker is a dot, or a chevron toggle when the Timeline is collapsible (default true) and `detail` is present.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `defaultExpanded` (Timeline prop): expands every event that has detail at first render; only events present at mount are expanded.
`collapsible: false` (Timeline prop): details permanently visible, dot markers, `defaultExpanded` ignored.
`user` on the event: shows the avatar and name (see `TimelineEvent#4`).
`detail` on the event: gives the event expandable or visible detail rows.
`formatDate` / `renderDate` / `renderAction` / `renderUser` / `renderDetail` / `renderMarker` (Timeline props): see `TimelineEvent#11` and `TimelineEvent#12`.

builtInText.text: Toggle `aria-label`: `Expand detail` when collapsed, `Collapse detail` when expanded (English, not translated through `t()`).
Detail row key is the entry's key followed by a colon (`Environment:`).

keyboard.text: The chevron toggle is a native button: Tab focuses it (it shows a focus ring), Enter or Space toggles the detail.
A non-interactive dot is not in the tab order.

states.text: Collapsed: chevron points down, `aria-expanded="false"`, no detail region.
Expanded: chevron rotated 180 degrees, `aria-expanded="true"`, the detail region is shown.
Non-interactive: dot marker, detail visible when present and the Timeline is not collapsible.
Disabled, loading, selected: none.

testApi: `timeline.getEvent(index)` / `timeline.getEvents()`: event wrappers (see the Timeline contract); there is no top-level `findTimelineEvent`.
`getContainer()`: the event row root (`data-ui-section="timeline.event"`).
`getAction()` / `shouldHaveAction(text)` / `shouldNotHaveAction(text)`: the action text; throws when the action element is missing.
`getTimestamp()` / `shouldHaveTimestamp(text)`: the timestamp text as displayed.
`isInteractive()` / `shouldBeInteractive()` / `shouldNotBeInteractive()`: true when the marker is the chevron toggle or a custom marker with `role="button"`.
`isExpanded()` / `shouldBeExpanded()` / `shouldNotBeExpanded()`: `aria-expanded` of the marker when interactive; for a non-interactive event true when a detail region is present.
`toggle()`: clicks the marker; throws `Cannot toggle an event that is not interactive.` when it is not interactive.

components.name: Toast

does.text: A toast shown with `show()` appears in the toast viewport and disappears by itself after 4000 ms.
Every severity (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`) auto-dismisses the same way; no severity persists on its own.
Resting the cursor on a toast pauses its dismissal timer; moving off resumes it with the time that was left (not a fresh 4000 ms).
Clicking the close button removes that toast only; other toasts stay.
Clicking a toast anywhere except a button calls `onClick(message)` and does not dismiss it.
New toasts are added after the existing ones, in the order they were shown; all stack (no limit).
The severity icon follows severity: success shows `CheckboxCircleLine`, danger `CloseCircleLine`, warning `ErrorWarningLine`, info and unset `InformationLine`.
Each toast is `role="alert"` with `aria-live="assertive"`, `aria-atomic="true"` and `data-severity`.
Title shows above the message text; each is rendered only when given.
A toast leaves with a 200 ms fade-out animation; it is still in the page during it.

`clear()` removes all toasts at once; `replace()` removes all current toasts and shows the new ones; `remove()` removes the given ones by `id` (a message without an `id` is ignored; `show()` assigns `toast_<n>` ids when none is given).

doesNot.text: No built-in action buttons (Undo, Retry, etc.): the only built-in button is the close button.
No progress bar or countdown indicator.
No pause on keyboard focus; only hover pauses the timer.
No limit on visible toasts unless `maxVisible` is set; no de-duplication of identical messages.
A persistent (`sticky`) toast has no countdown and never closes by itself.
No severity text: `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` change only the icon, colour, close-button colour and `data-severity`; no `Success`/`Error` word is added to the toast.
Showing another toast does not restart or extend the timer of a toast already shown; each toast counts its own `life` from its own `show()`.

defaults.text: Viewport position `bottom-right`, 16 px from the bottom and right edges.
Duration (`life`) 4000 ms per toast; `sticky` false.
`closable` true, so the close button is shown.
Severity `info` for the icon and `data-severity`; the preset colours a toast only for an explicit severity (unset severity gets the info icon but no coloured background or border).
Viewport z-index 1500, rendered in `document.body`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `sticky: true` on the message: it stays until closed by the close button or `clear()`/`replace()`/`remove()`.
`life: <ms>` on the message: changes its auto-dismiss time.
`closable: false` on the message: no close button; with `sticky` it cannot be dismissed by the user.
`maxVisible: n` on `<Toast>`: showing a toast past `n` drops the oldest ones at once (`onRemove` fires for each); `1` keeps one slot each new toast takes over.
`position`: moves the viewport to `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, `bottom-right` or `center`.

`message.content` (node or function): replaces the title/message/icon layout; the toast keeps `role="alert"` and hover pause but has no close button (add your own button inside `content` for actions).
`<Toast content>` (prop on the viewport): renders every message with that content only, with no `role="alert"`, no close button and no hover pause; the life timer still runs.
`message.icon` / `message.closeIcon`: replace the severity icon / close icon.

`onShow` fires on each `show()`/`replace()`; `onHide` fires when the last toast is removed or on `clear()`; `onRemove(message)` on each timed, closed, `remove()`d or `maxVisible`-dropped toast, but not on `clear()` or `replace()`.

builtInText.text: Close button `aria-label`: `Close Button` (exact case, not translated, any locale).
No other built-in text; title and message come only from the shown message.

keyboard.text: No key handling: Escape does not dismiss a toast; the close button is a normal button reachable by Tab and activated by Enter/Space.

states.text: Shown: in the viewport, auto-dismiss timer running (unless sticky).
Hovered: timer paused.
Closing: fading out for about 200 ms, then removed from the page.

testApi: `Spectra.findToast(name)`: finds the toast carrying the title or message text; a toast that is closing, gone or not shown yet gives a wrapper bound to that name; throws only if the name belongs to a non-toast element. `Spectra.queryToast(name)`: `null` when missing.

`Spectra.shouldNotFindToast(name)`: a toast never shown. `Spectra.shouldFindToastCount(name, n)`: exactly `n` shown toasts of that name (no name: any). `Spectra.shouldHaveVisibleToastCount(n, { severity? })` / `Spectra.getVisibleToastCount({ severity? })`: web only.

Readers and their should*: `getText`, `getTitleText`, `getMessageText`, `getTitle`, `getMessage`, `getIcon`, `getCloseButton`, `hasTitle`, `hasMessage`, `hasIcon`, `hasCloseButton` (`shouldHaveTitle`, `shouldHaveTitleText(t)`, `shouldHaveMessage`, `shouldContainMessageText(t)`, `shouldHaveIcon`, `shouldHaveCloseButton`).
`getActionButtons` / `hasActionButtons`: every button except the close button (`shouldHaveActionButtonsCount(n)`, `shouldNotHaveActionButtons`).
`getIconName` (`shouldHaveIconName(name)`), `getSeverity` (`shouldHaveSeverity(s)`), `getPosition` (`shouldHavePosition(p)`), `isClosable`.
`hover()` pauses, `unhover()` resumes.

`isDisplayed()` is `false` while closing or gone (`shouldNotBeDisplayed()` asserts a closed toast; `shouldBeDisplayed()` waits for it to show). `isDismissed()` is `!isDisplayed()`; `shouldBeDismissed()` polls 6 s (default life 4 s plus margin), `{ timeout }` for longer.
`close()`: clicks the close button, then waits until the toast is closed.
All other methods wait like a find and throw if the toast never appears.

components.name: Tooltip

does.text: Hovering the trigger opens the tooltip after 300 ms; moving the cursor off closes it after 100 ms.
Keyboard focus on the trigger (`:focus-visible`) opens it with no delay; blur closes it. Focus from a mouse click does not open it.
Escape closes an open tooltip and the same keypress still reaches the dialog or menu the trigger sits in, which closes on that press too.
Shows plain text only (`content` is a string) in a floating panel with `role="tooltip"`, placed above the trigger, with a pointing arrow.
The trigger carries `data-tooltip-state="open"` or `"closed"`.
Wrapping a disabled control still opens on hover: a span wrapper (`data-tooltip-disabled-trigger`) becomes the hover target.
The panel fades and moves in over 150 ms and out over 100 ms; it is still in the page during the exit.
A parent's props (click handler, `aria-*`, ref from PopupMenu or Popover) are passed on to the trigger, so a menu around a tooltip still opens.

Truncation-only tooltips (open only when the text is actually cut): Avatar display name (when the shown name differs from the full name), Badge (when `textOverflow` shortens the label, or `tooltip` is set), DataTable `longText` cell (only when the line clamp cuts it), TreeNode label (only when clipped; opens on hover after 300 ms, or on keyboard focus after 300 ms, and closes on blur).

Always-on tooltips, shown on any hover regardless of truncation: DataTable `userName` cell (full name, also on grid-cell keyboard focus), DataTable column `preset.tooltip` toggles and row-selection hints (only for rows that have a hint text), Menu item with `tooltip`, DataTable header with `headerTooltip`, Field `info` (the info icon is focusable, so keyboard focus opens it too), SearchButton, FilterToggleButton, ExportButton, DataTable column visibility button, DataTable `icon` and trailing action labels.

The panel ignores the pointer (`pointer-events: none`): moving the cursor from the trigger onto the panel does not keep it open, it closes 100 ms after leaving the trigger, and it cannot be hovered or clicked.
While open, the trigger has `aria-describedby` pointing at the panel (a description, not the accessible name); closed, no `aria-describedby`.
The panel text is at most 400 px wide (90vw on narrow screens), keeps line breaks in `content`, and wraps long words.
Hover and focus open it independently; the trigger event delays apply only to hover (`openDelay`), focus has none.
Slider and RangeSlider handle tooltips show the value with no delay while dragging or focused (and on hover), unless the slider's `showTooltip` is false; `tooltipAlwaysOn` keeps it open.

doesNot.text: Not interactive: it holds no focus, and no rich content (use Popover).
Click does not open it unless `events` includes `click`.
Does not open on hover or focus when `disabled`.
Does not follow the cursor (`move` off); anchored to the trigger.
A tooltip whose text is shown whole (not truncated) does not appear in the truncation-only components of `Tooltip#9`.
CopyButton has no tooltip.
PasswordInput's visibility toggle has no tooltip unless `withVisibilityToggleTooltip` is set.
A disabled control cannot be focused, so its tooltip opens on hover only.
The text is not translated by Tooltip: it shows `content` exactly as given.
An empty `content` string still opens an empty panel (nothing hides it).

defaults.text: `placement` `top`; `openDelay` 300; `closeDelay` 100; `arrow` true; `disabled` false; `events` `['hover', 'focus']`; closed at start (`defaultOpen` false); offset 8 px.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `disabled: true`: the trigger renders alone with `data-tooltip-disabled` and `data-tooltip-state="closed"`; no tooltip ever.
`events`: removes or adds triggers; `['hover']` ignores focus; adding `click` toggles it on click.
`openDelay` / `closeDelay`: change the hover delays; focus has no delay.
`open` + `onOpenChange`: controlled; the app decides when it shows.
`arrow: false`: no arrow; `arrowPosition`, `arrowOffset` move it.
`placement`: 12 values (`top`, `top-start`, `top-end`, `bottom`, ..., `right-end`); flips or shifts when no room.
The disabled-control wrapper appears only when the trigger has `disabled={true}`; with the Tooltip itself `disabled` there is no wrapper (`Tooltip#19`).

builtInText.text: None: text is the `content` prop. Built-in defaults of callers (English): SearchButton `Search` (`searchTooltip`), FilterToggleButton `Filter` (`filterTooltip`), ExportButton `Download`, DataTable action `Action`, column visibility `Column Visibility`.

keyboard.text: Tab to the trigger shows it; Tab away hides it; Escape hides it.
Enter and Space do nothing to the tooltip itself (unless `events` has `click`, which toggles it).

states.text: Closed: no panel in the page.
Open: panel in a portal with `role="tooltip"`.
Disabled: renders trigger only (`Tooltip#19`).
Loading, selected states: none.

testApi: `Spectra.findTooltip(triggerName)`: finds by the trigger's accessible name (`aria-label`, label text); `Spectra.queryTooltip(name)` returns `null` when missing. DataTable row selection tooltips: `row.shouldHaveSelectionTooltipText(text)`.
`hover()`, `unhover()`, `focus()`, `blur()`, `click()` act on the trigger; a raw element `hover()` only opens a tooltip on the element that holds it.

`isOpen()` (`shouldBeOpen()`, `shouldNotBeOpen()`), `getContent()` (`shouldHaveContent(text)`), `isDisabled()`, `hasArrow()` (`shouldHaveArrow()`), `getArrow()`, `getFloatingPanel()` (fails naming the missing panel when closed), `getContainer()` (panel if open, else trigger).
`waitUntilOpen(timeout?)`, `waitUntilClosed(timeout?)`.

components.name: Tree

does.text: Shows `data` as a nested list: each node is a row with an indent per level; a branch (a node with `children`) has a chevron, a leaf has none; branches start collapsed unless listed in `defaultExpandedKeys` or `expandedKeys`.

Only the visible rows (plus 5 extra above and below, `virtualScrollBuffer`) are in the page; the rest are created when scrolled to, so a long tree is not fully in the DOM. The tree scrolls inside its own container (vertical scrollbar) and needs a bounded height.
Row height follows `size`: `xs` 24px, `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (or `virtualScrollItemHeight`); the indent per level is 8px (`xs`), 12px (`sm`), 16px (`md`) plus 4px padding.
Clicking a branch's chevron expands or collapses it; the children appear right under it and the chevron turns 90 degrees when open; expanding does not select.
Expansion is uncontrolled from `defaultExpandedKeys`, or controlled by `expandedKeys` (then the tree changes only when the app updates it); `onExpandedChange(keys)` fires on every toggle.
Expanding a node also records all of its ancestors as expanded.

`selectionMode="single"`: clicking a selectable row selects it and clears the previous one; clicking the selected row again clears the selection (`onSelectionChange([])`); the selected row is highlighted.
`selectionMode="multiple"`: clicking a selectable row toggles it; any number of rows can be selected; adjacent selected rows are highlighted as one block (rounded corners only at the block ends).
`selectionMode="checkbox"`: every row shows a checkbox; clicking the row or its checkbox toggles it; `onSelectionChange(keys)` receives the array of selected node keys.

Checkbox mode with `propagateSelection` (default): checking a branch also selects all its selectable descendants (also those collapsed or hidden by a filter), unchecking clears them, checking all selectable children selects the parent, and a branch with some but not all children selected shows a mixed checkbox (`aria-checked="mixed"`).
Checkbox mode with `propagateSelection={false}`: each node is selected on its own; a parent shows no mixed state.

A node is not selectable when its `selectable` is false, its 0-based level is not in `selectableLevels`, `isNodeDisabled(node)` is true or the tree is `readOnly`: clicking it does not select it (a non-selectable branch expands or collapses on a row click) and its label is dimmed.
Propagation skips non-selectable descendants: they are not selected by a parent, and a parent whose selectable children are all on counts as on even if a non-selectable sibling is off.
`selectedKeys` controls the selection (the tree changes only when the app updates it); without it the tree keeps its own selection.

`filterKeyword` filters while typing: a node stays when its label contains the text (case-insensitive), or a `filterFields` path in `node.data` contains it (dotted paths such as `address.postalCode`, objects compared as JSON text), or `filterNode(node, keyword)` returns true when given (it replaces the default match).

A filter shows the matching nodes with all their ancestors; ancestors of a match are opened automatically; a node that matches only itself shows without its non-matching children; clearing the keyword (or an all-whitespace keyword) restores the full tree with the earlier expansion.
The check state of a branch while filtering is read from the whole tree, not from only the visible rows.
`loading`: the rows are replaced by a centred spinner; no row is shown or selectable and chevrons do nothing while it is on; the root has `aria-busy="true"`.

Keyboard focus is roving: exactly one visible row is the Tab stop (`tabindex="0"`, the others `-1`; the root is `-1` while rows exist); Tab from outside lands on that row and moves out of the tree on the next Tab.
`renderNode(node, state)` replaces the row label with the returned node; `state` is `{ enabled, expanded, selected, partiallySelected, focused }`.

The ref handle `expandAll()`, `collapseAll()`, `expandNode(key)` (with ancestors), `collapseNode(key)` and `toggleExpanded(key)` change the expansion; in controlled mode they only call `onExpandedChange`.
`readOnly`: selection is frozen, row clicks and Enter or Space on a row do nothing, checkboxes are disabled, rows are `aria-disabled`; the chevrons and the arrow keys still expand and collapse.

doesNot.text: Does not select anything with `selectionMode="none"` (default): rows are not highlighted, have no checkbox and no `aria-selected`; clicking a branch row only expands it.
Does not select a branch on a row click in `single` and `multiple` mode instead of expanding: a selectable branch selects on a row click and expands only from its chevron or the arrow keys.
Does not show an empty state, "no results" text or error: with no data, or when a filter matches nothing, the tree is an empty box.
Does not sort `data`; rows follow the array order.
Does not support drag and drop (dragging a row onto another changes nothing).
Does not lazy-load children by itself (`children` must be present in `data`); a node without `children` is a leaf.
Does not block interaction with `disabled`: it only sets `aria-disabled="true"` on the tree root (use `isNodeDisabled` per node or `readOnly`); there is no visual change from it.
Does not emit `onSelectionChange` from `expandAll` or any expansion action.
A filter does not change `selectedKeys`: selected nodes hidden by a filter stay selected.
Does not mark a non-selectable node as disabled: `selectable: false` and `selectableLevels` leave the row without `aria-disabled` (only `isNodeDisabled` and `readOnly` set it).

defaults.text: `selectionMode` `none`, `propagateSelection` true, `size` `xs`, `loading` false, `disabled` false, `readOnly` false, `filterKeyword` empty, `virtualScrollBuffer` 5, `selectedKeys` and `expandedKeys` uncontrolled and empty.
The root has `role="tree"`, `aria-multiselectable="true"` for `multiple` and `checkbox` (`false` otherwise), no default accessible name.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, responsive): row height, indent, text size and corner radius.

`ariaLabel` / `aria-label`, `ariaLabelledby` / `aria-labelledby`, `ariaDescribedby` / `aria-describedby`, `id`, `tabIndex` (replaces the root's tab index): set on the tree root; the accessible name is what finds the tree.
`selectableLevels`, `isNodeDisabled`, node `selectable`: `Tree#12`; `propagateSelection`: `Tree#10`, `Tree#11`; `filterFields`, `filterNode`: `Tree#15`.
`readOnly`: `Tree#22` and sets `data-readonly="true"` on the root.
`virtualScrollItemHeight`, `virtualScrollBuffer`: row height estimate and extra rows rendered; `className`, `style`, `pt`: styling of the root.

builtInText.text: Chevron `aria-label`: `Expand <label>` / `Collapse <label>` (English, not translated), see `TreeNode#5`.
No other built-in text (no empty text, no loading text; the spinner has no text).

keyboard.text: ArrowDown / ArrowUp move focus to the next / previous visible row; Home / End to the first / last visible row; the keys do not wrap.
ArrowRight on a collapsed branch opens it; on an open branch moves focus to its first child; on a leaf does nothing.
ArrowLeft on an open branch closes it; otherwise moves focus to the parent row; on a root row with nothing to close does nothing.
Enter or Space on a focused row activates it (selects or toggles the checkbox; a non-selectable branch expands), see `TreeNode#2`.
Keys pressed with Alt, Ctrl or Meta, or typed inside a custom node's own input or menu, are ignored by the tree.
Moving focus to a row far down a long list scrolls it into view first.

states.text: Per node: collapsed / expanded, selected / not selected (checkbox: also mixed), enabled / disabled, see the TreeNode contract.
Tree: normal, loading (`aria-busy`), read-only (`data-readonly`), `aria-disabled`; empty is a normal state with no rows.
Focus: the focused row shows the standard focus (no outline of its own) and a cut label opens its tooltip (`TreeNode#9`).

testApi: `Spectra.findTree(name)` / `Spectra.queryTree(name)`: the element with `role="tree"` and `data-ui-section="tree.root"` found by its accessible name; `Spectra.shouldNotFindTree(name)`.

`getNode(label | key)`: the row whose label equals or contains the text; scrolls the virtualized list to find it; throws with a hint (tree gone / error state, no rows, ancestor collapsed). `getNodes()`: rows currently mounted. `getNodeLabels()`: labels of mounted rows top to bottom. `getChildLabels(label)`: direct children labels of an expanded node in order. `hasNode(label)`: `true`/`false`.
`expandNode(label)` / `collapseNode(label)`: set the state of one branch (open ancestors first when needed); `expandAll()` / `collapseAll()`: all branches.

`selectNode(label)` / `deselectNode(label)`: act only when the state differs (clicks the checkbox in checkbox mode, the row otherwise); open ancestors first when needed; `getSelectedNodes()`: labels of rows currently mounted that are selected or checked; `shouldHaveSelectedNodes`-style readers per wrapper.
`isLabelTruncated(label)` / `shouldBeLabelTruncated(label)` / `shouldNotBeLabelTruncated(label)`.
`focusItem(label)`, `getFocusedItemLabel()` / `shouldHaveFocusedItemLabel(label)`; drive keys with `Spectra.pressKey('ArrowDown')`.
`isDisabled()` (`aria-disabled` on the root), `isLoading()` (`aria-busy` or the spinner; `false` when the tree has left the page), `isReadOnly()` (`data-readonly`).
Row wrappers: see the TreeNode contract.

components.name: TreeNode

does.text: A row shows, from left to right, the chevron button (invisible but space-keeping on a leaf), the checkbox (checkbox mode only) and the label; the row is indented by its level and carries `aria-level` (level + 1, so a root row is 1).

Clicking the row, or pressing Enter or Space on the focused row, activates it: a selectable node is selected or unselected (checkbox mode: checked or unchecked); a branch that is not selectable (`selectable: false`, level outside `selectableLevels`, `isNodeDisabled`, or `selectionMode="none"`) expands or collapses instead; a non-selectable leaf does nothing.
In `single` and `multiple` mode a selectable branch selects on a row click and expands only from its chevron.

A selected row (single or multiple) is highlighted (primary container colour) with `aria-selected="true"`; unselected rows in those modes have `aria-selected="false"` and a hover highlight while enabled.

The chevron button toggles the branch without selecting it (the click does not reach the row); its `aria-label` is `Expand <label>` when collapsed and `Collapse <label>` when open; it is not a Tab stop (`tabindex="-1"`).
On a leaf the chevron button is `aria-hidden` and invisible, and carries no `aria-expanded` on the row; a branch row has `aria-expanded="true"` or `"false"`.

In checkbox mode the checkbox shows checked when the node is selected (or, with propagation, all its selectable descendants are), mixed (`aria-checked="mixed"`) when only some are, empty otherwise; the checkbox `aria-label` is the node label; the row has `aria-checked` `true`, `false` or `mixed`.

A node not selectable by `selectable: false`, `selectableLevels`, `isNodeDisabled` or `readOnly` has `data-selectable="false"` (selectable ones `"true"`), a dimmed label and no pointer hover highlight; its checkbox is disabled.

A label that does not fit (cut by an ellipsis or clamp) shows its full text in a tooltip on hover and when the row gets keyboard focus (focus-visible) after the Tooltip delay (300 ms); a label that fits shows no tooltip; moving focus to a fitting label closes it. A pointer click focus does not open it.
With `renderNode` the label area is the returned node (no automatic tooltip); `state.focused` becomes true after the same 300 ms of keyboard focus so a custom label can open its own tooltip.
Clicking inside the checkbox toggles it without also firing the row click.
A node with `isNodeDisabled` true is `aria-disabled="true"` on the row but its chevron still expands and collapses it; the same holds in a `readOnly` tree.
A rendered row can be recognised by `data-key` (the node key) and `data-index` (position in the visible list).

doesNot.text: A non-selectable node (`selectable: false`, `selectableLevels`) is not `aria-disabled` and not blocked from expanding.
The chevron does not select the node, and a row click on a selectable branch does not expand it (`TreeNode#3`).
With `selectionMode="none"` no row has a checkbox, `aria-selected` or `aria-checked`, and no row is ever highlighted.
The checkbox and the chevron are never Tab stops; only the row is.
A leaf has no children to open: clicking its hidden chevron area does nothing.
A read-only row does not react to a click or to Enter or Space (including a branch that would otherwise expand on a row click).
A loading tree shows no rows at all, so no row is ever selected while loading.
The tooltip does not show for a label that fits.

defaults.text: Collapsed, not selected, enabled, tabindex `-1` (only the tree's one tab stop is `0`).
Row `role="treeitem"`; label text is `node.label` as given; the chevron icon points right.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: Node `selectable: false`: not selectable (see `TreeNode#2`, `TreeNode#8`).
Node `children`: makes it a branch with a visible chevron; `children: []` counts as a leaf.
Node `data`: only used for `filterFields` and the app's `renderNode`.
Tree props that shape the row: `size`, `selectionMode`, `propagateSelection`, `selectableLevels`, `isNodeDisabled`, `readOnly`, `renderNode` (all in the Tree contract).

builtInText.text: Chevron `aria-label`: `Expand <label>`, `Collapse <label>` (English, not through `t()`).
No other built-in text.

keyboard.text: Tab lands on the row that is the tab stop; Enter or Space activates the row (`TreeNode#2`); arrows and Home/End move between rows (`Tree#42` to `Tree#44`).
Keys pressed inside a custom node's own control do not activate the row (only keys whose target is the row itself do).

states.text: Collapsed / expanded (`aria-expanded`), selected / unselected (`aria-selected` or `aria-checked`), partially selected (`aria-checked="mixed"`), leaf (no `aria-expanded`), selectable / not selectable (`data-selectable`), disabled (`aria-disabled`), focused.
Loading: the tree shows a spinner instead of rows (`Tree#18`).

testApi: `Spectra.findTreeNode(label)` / `Spectra.queryTreeNode(label)`: a row by its label text; also reachable as `tree.getNode(label or key)`; `Spectra.shouldNotFindTreeNode(label)`.
`getLabel()`: trimmed label text. `getLevel()`: 1-based (`aria-level`; a root row is 1, its child 2).

`isExpanded()` (`aria-expanded` true), `isLeaf()` (no `aria-expanded`), `isSelected()` (`aria-selected` or `aria-checked` true), `isPartiallySelected()` (`aria-checked="mixed"`), `isSelectable()` (`data-selectable`, falling back to checkbox enabled), `isDisabled()` (`aria-disabled` true; not set by `selectable: false`); each has `should*` / `shouldNot*`.
`getToggleButton()`: the chevron button (found by its `Expand` / `Collapse` label; throws on a leaf). `getCheckbox()`: the checkbox element; throws when the tree is not in checkbox mode.
`toggle()`: clicks the chevron with `force` (works on an `aria-disabled` branch). `select()`: clicks the checkbox, else the row.
`dragTo(target)`: drags the row onto another; Tree has no drag and drop of its own, so nothing changes.
`getContainer()`: the row element (`data-ui-section="tree.node"`).

components.name: TreeSelect

does.text: Clicking the trigger button (or Enter or Space on it) opens a dialog with the node tree. The dialog works on a draft: every node click changes the draft only, the field and `onChange` stay as they were.
The selection commits only on the dialog's [Select] button: `onChange` fires with the draft and the dialog closes. Nothing commits on a node click, on Enter in the search, or on closing the dialog.

[Cancel] closes the dialog and throws the draft away: no `onChange`, the field shows the last committed selection, and reopening shows the committed selection (not the draft). The dialog's close button (`Close dialog`), Escape and a click on the overlay do the same (the overlay click is the Dialog default `closeOnOverlayClick`).
[Select] with an empty draft and `allowEmptySelection` true (default) commits an empty selection (`onChange(undefined)`) and closes: the field goes back to its empty look.

Multiple (`selectionMode` `checkbox`, default, or `multiple`): the trigger shows the count of committed nodes found in `data` (a key not in `data` is not counted), not their labels: `1 item selected`, `{n} items selected`; with none it shows the placeholder (`Select`). The value is an array of node keys, `onChange(string[] | undefined)`, `undefined` when empty.

Single (`selectionMode="single"`) with a committed node: the field shows a badge with the node LABEL (not the key) and an edit button `Edit selection` that reopens the dialog; there is no trigger button then. The value is the node key, `onChange(string | undefined)`.
Single with no committed node: a trigger button with `selectLabel`, else `placeholder`, else `Select`.
Single: clicking the selected node again deselects it in the draft (empty draft); a click on another node replaces the draft.

Search in the dialog: a text field above the tree filters nodes by label (case-insensitive substring, plus `filterFields` in the node data, or `filterNode` when given); matching nodes show with their ancestors, expanded; a clear button `Clear` appears while there is text; Enter does nothing; the text is reset when the dialog closes; searching does not change the draft.

Selectable nodes: a node is not selectable when its `selectable` is false, its level is not in `selectableLevels` (0-based), or `isNodeDisabled` returns true, or the field is `readOnly`; its checkbox is disabled and a row click does not select it. A non-selectable branch expands or collapses on a row click.

Checkbox mode propagates by default (`propagateSelection` true): checking a branch adds its selectable descendants (and the branch key itself if selectable); a branch with some descendants selected shows a mixed checkbox; unchecking removes them; checking all children checks the parent.
On open, the ancestors of the committed nodes are expanded.

Validation: with `allowEmptySelection` false and an empty draft, [Select] shows `You must make a selection` (role `alert`) and the dialog stays open, no `onChange`; `validateSelection(keys, node)` returning a string shows that text and keeps the dialog open; the message clears on the next selection change and on reopen.
Single with `singleClearable`: a clear button `Clear selection` commits an empty value at once (no dialog) and calls `onReset`; the field goes back to the trigger button.

`loading`: the trigger button shows `Loading...` and is inert (a single committed value still shows its badge, not the loading text); in an open dialog the tree shows a spinner, the search field is hidden, and [Select] is disabled.

`readOnly`: the trigger button (multiple, or single with no value) still opens the dialog, but the single edit and clear buttons are disabled; the dialog has no footer (no [Cancel], no [Select]), no node can be selected and a row click does nothing, the branch toggle buttons still expand and collapse; the dialog closes by its close button or Escape.

doesNot.text: The field never shows node labels for a multiple selection (only the count); labels are read through the dialog or `getSelectedNodes()`.
A node click never commits: no `onChange` before [Select].
Cancel, close button, Escape, overlay click never commit.
No error message for an empty selection unless `allowEmptySelection` is false (or `validateSelection` returns text).
No text and no row for an empty tree, and none when the search matches nothing (no "No data" row); the tree area is just empty.
Single mode: no clear button unless `singleClearable`; no edit button when `singleEditable` is false (then a committed value has no way to reopen the dialog).
Single mode never emits an array; multiple mode never emits a string.
`selectionMode="multiple"` has no checkboxes and no propagation: a row click toggles one node.
The multiple placeholder is `Select`, same as single; the text `Select items` exists nowhere in the component.

defaults.text: `selectionMode` `checkbox`; `data` `[]`; `allowEmptySelection` true; `loading`, `readOnly`, `disabled` false; `defaultOpen` false; `singleEditable` true; `singleClearable` false.
Dialog title `Select`; [Cancel] and [Select] footer; no sub-header, no top content.
Root is `role="group"`; its name is `ariaLabel` / `aria-label`, else the surrounding Field label; no default `aria-label`.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `dialogHeader` (passed through `t()`), `subHeader`, `topContent`, `headerContent` (replaces the title), `footerContent` (replaces [Cancel] and [Select] and the error message).

`placeholder`, `selectLabel` (single only; ignored in multiple), `selectedCountLabel`, `loadingPlaceholder`: replace the matching text on the trigger; `selectedCountLabel` is shown as given, `{count}` is not interpolated.
`singleEditable`, `singleClearable`, `onReset`: `TreeSelect#14`, `TreeSelect#22`.
`isNodeDisabled`, `selectableLevels`, node `selectable: false`, `propagateSelection`: `TreeSelect#10`, `TreeSelect#11`.
`filterFields`, `filterNode`: `TreeSelect#9`. `renderNode`, `virtualScrollItemHeight`, `virtualScrollBuffer`, `expandedKeys`, `defaultExpandedKeys`, `onExpandedChange`: tree rendering and expansion.
`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`: control the dialog from outside; `disabled`: the trigger and edit and clear buttons are disabled and the dialog cannot open.

builtInText.text: Trigger: `Select` (single, and multiple with none; locale en, through `t()`); loading: `Loading...`; count: `1 item selected`, `{count} items selected` (`No items selected` is the zero text of the string and is not shown, the placeholder shows instead).

Dialog: title `Select`; buttons [Cancel] and [Select] (label and `aria-label` `Cancel`, `Select`); search `Search` (placeholder and `aria-label`); search clear `Clear`; close `Close dialog`; error `You must make a selection`.
Single mode buttons: `Edit selection` and `Clear selection` (`aria-label` and `title`).
Tree: each branch toggle has `aria-label` `Expand {label}` or `Collapse {label}`, and each checkbox `aria-label` is the node label; the toggle text is an English literal in the code, not translated.

keyboard.text: The trigger is a native button: Tab focuses it, Enter or Space opens the dialog. A disabled trigger is skipped.

In the tree (on a node): ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home, End move focus; ArrowRight expands a branch or moves to its first child; ArrowLeft collapses or moves to the parent; Enter or Space toggles the node's selection (or expands a non-selectable branch).
Escape closes the dialog and discards the draft.
The search field takes Enter as a no-op (no commit).

states.text: Closed empty: trigger button. Closed with selection: count (multiple) or badge + edit (single).
Open: dialog with search, tree, footer; draft separate from committed value.
Disabled, loading, read-only: `TreeSelect#34`, `TreeSelect#15`, `TreeSelect#16`.
Error: `TreeSelect#13`.

testApi: `Spectra.findTreeSelect(name)`: by the accessible name (`aria-label` or the Field label); `Spectra.queryTreeSelect(name)`: `null` when missing.
`getTriggerButton()` (the edit button when a single value is held), `getTriggerLabel()`, `openDialog()`, `edit()`, `clear()`, `focus()`, `isFocused()`.
`getBadge()`, `getBadgeText()` (single, the label), `getEditButton()`, `getClearButton()`, `hasBadge()`, `hasEditButton()`, `hasClearButton()`, `hasSelection()`.
`selectNode(labelOrKey)`, `deselectNode(labelOrKey)`: open the dialog, change the node (opens collapsed ancestors) and confirm with [Select]; `getSelectedNodes()` (labels).

`getDialog()`: dialog wrapper with `getHeaderText()`, `getSubHeaderText()`, `setSearchValue(text)`, `getSearchValue()`, `clearSearch()`, `getErrorMessageText()`, `hasErrorMessage()`, `cancel()`, `confirm()` (the [Select] button), `selectNode()`, `deselectNode()`, `expandNode()`, `collapseNode()`, `expandAll()`, `collapseAll()`, `getSelectedNodes()` (the draft), `getTree()`, `isOpen()` (`shouldBeOpen()`, `shouldNotBeOpen()`).
`isOpen()`, `isDisabled()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isLoading()`.

components.name: TreeSelectDialog

does.text: When `visible` is true it opens a dialog with the header `Select` (or `header`), an optional `subHeader`, a search field, the node tree, and a footer with `Cancel` and `Select`; frame behavior is `Dialog` (`Dialog#1`).
Node clicks change a temporary selection only: `onSelectionChange` and `onSingleNodeSelectionChange` fire only when `Select` is pressed (as in `TreeSelect#2`).
`Select` with a valid selection calls `onSelectionChange(keys)` and `onSingleNodeSelectionChange(node)`, then requests close through `onVisibleChange(false)` (commit as in `TreeSelect#2`).

`Select` with nothing selected and `allowEmptySelection` true commits an empty selection and closes (as in `TreeSelect#4`): `onSelectionChange([])` and `onSingleNodeSelectionChange(undefined)`; an emptied multiple selection commits as `[]`, not `undefined`.
`Cancel` calls `onHide`, then `onVisibleChange(false)`, and discards the temporary selection (as in `TreeSelect#3`).

Escape, a click on the backdrop and the header close button (`Close dialog`) do the same as `Cancel` (`Dialog#3`, `Dialog#4`, `Dialog#5`): `onHide`, then `onVisibleChange(false)`, selection discarded.
Every close only requests it (`Dialog#7`); with a controlled `visible` the dialog stays open until the app sets `visible` false.
Each time the dialog opens, the temporary selection is reset to `keys`, and the validation message and the search text are cleared.
On open the ancestors of the `keys` nodes are expanded (as in `TreeSelect#12`), together with `defaultExpandedKeys`.
The search field filters the tree as in `TreeSelect#9`; a clear button appears while there is text and empties it; searching does not change the selection.

A failed validation behaves as in `TreeSelect#13`: the dialog stays open, the message shows in the footer (`role="alert"`, `aria-live="polite"`), no callback fires, and the message clears on the next selection change.

`validateSelection(keys, node)` runs on a non-empty selection (a returned string is the message, `null` is valid); with `allowEmptySelection` false and nothing selected the message is `You must make a selection` (as in `TreeSelect#13`).
`ref.treeComponent` exposes the embedded Tree's handle.
Focus trap, page blocking and scroll lock are the `Dialog` ones (`Dialog#1`, `Dialog#8`).

doesNot.text: No trigger button and no field: the dialog renders only while the app sets `visible` (the trigger and committed value display belong to `TreeSelect`).
A node click or closing the dialog does not commit anything (as in `TreeSelect#18`, `TreeSelect#19`).
Enter in the search field does nothing (it does not submit or select).
The validation message is not shown when neither `allowEmptySelection` false nor `validateSelection` is set (nothing can fail).
In `single` mode only the first key of `keys` is used; extra keys are ignored.
`onSingleNodeSelectionChange` is given `undefined` outside `single` mode (the node is tracked only there).
With `readOnly` there is no footer at all: no `Cancel`, no `Select`, not even a supplied `footerContent` (as in `TreeSelect#16`).
While `loading` there is no search field and `Select` cannot be pressed (as in `TreeSelect#15`).

defaults.text: Closed (`visible` false); `selectionMode` `checkbox`; `allowEmptySelection` true; `data` empty; `loading` false.
Dialog size `sm` (400 px), with its close button, Escape and backdrop closing (`Dialog#21`, `Dialog#23`).
Title is an `h2` reading `Select`; `Select` button is green (`success`), `Cancel` is a text button.
Search field has placeholder and `aria-label` `Search`, a search icon at its start, and the `xs` size.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `header`: replaces `Select` (a string is translated through `t()`); `subHeader`: an `h4` under the header.
`headerContent`: replaces the title entirely; `topContent`: content above the search field; `footerContent`: replaces `Cancel`, `Select` and the validation message.
`selectionMode`: `single` selects one node, `checkbox` selects with checkboxes, `multiple` selects several, `none` selects nothing.
`readOnly`: the tree cannot change and the footer disappears, so only the close button, Escape or the backdrop closes it.
`loading`: as in `TreeSelect#15`; `Cancel` still works.
`isNodeDisabled`: matching nodes cannot be selected.
`expandedKeys` / `onExpandedChange` control expansion; `defaultExpandedKeys` start it; remaining Tree props (for example `selectableLevels`, `propagateSelection`) pass to the Tree.
`keys`: the initial selection on every open; `pt`: styling.

builtInText.text: Same texts as `TreeSelect#36`: title `Select`; buttons `Cancel` and `Select`; search `Search`; clear button `Clear`; error `You must make a selection`; close button `Close dialog`.

keyboard.text: Escape closes it like `Cancel`; Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside the dialog.
Enter in the search field is swallowed.
Tree keyboard navigation is the embedded Tree one, as in `TreeSelect#40`.

states.text: Open and closing: root `data-state` and inert as in `Dialog#41` and `Dialog#42`.
Validation error: the message shown in the footer until the selection changes or the dialog is reopened.
Loading: spinner in the tree, no search, `Select` disabled.
Read-only: no footer, tree inert.

testApi: `Spectra.findTreeSelectDialog(header)` by the header title or `aria-label`; `Spectra.queryTreeSelectDialog(header)`: `null` when missing.
`getHeader()` / `getHeaderText()`, `getSubHeader()` / `getSubHeaderText()` / `hasSubHeader()`.
`getSearchInput()`, `getSearchValue()`, `setSearchValue(text)`, `clearSearch()`, `hasSearchInput()`.
`getErrorMessage()` / `getErrorMessageText()` / `hasErrorMessage()`.
`getCancelButton()`, `getSelectButton()`, `cancel()`, `confirm()` (presses `Select`).
`getTree()` (a Tree wrapper), `selectNode(labelOrKey)`, `deselectNode`, `expandNode`, `collapseNode`, `expandAll()`, `collapseAll()`, `getSelectedNodes()`.
`isOpen()`, `isReadOnly()`, `isLoading()`, with the generated `should*` pairs.

components.name: TriStateCheckbox

does.text: Shows one of three states: unchecked (`false`, empty box), checked (`true`, filled primary box with a check mark) and indeterminate (`null`, filled primary box with a dash).
Each click advances the state in a fixed cycle: unchecked, then checked, then indeterminate, then unchecked again.
Each click calls `onChange` with the new value (`true`, `null` or `false`), not an event.
Clicking the visible `label` text advances the state the same way.
Uncontrolled (`defaultValue`): it keeps its own state and follows the cycle.
Controlled (`value`): it shows what `value` says; a click only calls `onChange`, and the display changes only when the parent passes the new `value`.
The check mark and the dash draw in with a short animation when the state changes.
The native input is flagged indeterminate while `null`, so assistive technology reads it as mixed.
With `label` the text sits to the right of the box and names the control; with `description` the secondary text shows under the label and is the input's `aria-describedby` target.
`invalid` shows a danger border (danger fill when checked or indeterminate) and sets `aria-invalid="true"`.
`onFocus`, `onBlur` and `onClick` fire from the input.

doesNot.text: A click cannot jump straight to indeterminate from unchecked or to unchecked from checked; the order is fixed.
Does not change and does not call `onChange` while `disabled`.
Does not render a label or description when none is given.
Does not propagate state to other checkboxes (no parent or child logic).
Does not draw a mark for the unchecked state; the box is empty.
Has no `required` prop and no required asterisk of its own; `aria-required` is only passed through to the input.
Does not offer a reverse layout (label before the box).

defaults.text: Starts unchecked when neither `value` nor `defaultValue` is given; the first click then gives `true`.
`size` is `xs` (16 px box); enabled; not invalid.
The input carries `aria-invalid="false"` while valid.
No label, no description, no name.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `defaultValue: null` starts indeterminate; `true` starts checked.
`value`: makes it controlled (`null` is a valid controlled value).
`label` / `description`: text beside the box; `aria-label` is used when there is no visible text.
`size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` (also responsive): larger box, icon and text (20, 24, 28 px).
`disabled`: greyed box and text, no change on click, input disabled.
`invalid`: see Does.
`name`: the input's `name` for native form submission; the input `value` is the text `true` or `false` (none while indeterminate).
`id`, `tabIndex`: the input's id and tab order (default id is generated).
`className`, `style`, `pt`: styling of the wrapper (or the box when there is no text).

keyboard.text: Tab moves focus to the input and a focus halo shows around the box.
Space on the focused input advances the cycle like a click.
A disabled one is skipped by Tab.

states.text: Unchecked: empty box with a neutral border.
Checked: primary box with a check mark.
Indeterminate: primary box with a dash.
Invalid: danger border and danger text; filled danger when checked or indeterminate.
Disabled: dimmed box and text; hover, focus and press halos are off.
Focused: halo around the box.
Loading: none (no such prop).

testApi: `Spectra.findTriStateCheckbox(label)` by `aria-label` or label text; `Spectra.queryTriStateCheckbox(label)` is `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindTriStateCheckbox(label)`.
`getValue()` (`shouldHaveValue(true | false | null)`).
`isChecked()` (`shouldBeChecked()`), `isUnchecked()` (`shouldBeUnchecked()`), `isIndeterminate()` (`shouldBeIndeterminate()`), with `shouldNotBe*`.
`toggle()` clicks once (advances the cycle); `check()`, `uncheck()`, `setIndeterminate()`, `setValue(value)` click until the target state is reached.
`getContainer()`, `getBox()`, `getIcon()` (the svg inside the box; it is always present, also unchecked, where its mark is just not drawn), `hasIcon()`.
`getLabel()`, `getLabelText()` (`shouldHaveLabelText(text)`), `hasLabel()`, `getDescription()`, `getDescriptionText()` (`shouldContainDescriptionText(part)`), `hasDescription()`.
`isDisabled()`, `isInvalid()`, `isRequired()` (from `required` or `aria-required`), `isFocused()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.

components.name: TriStateSwitch

does.text: Shows one of three states: neutral (`null`, thumb on the left, empty track), positive (`true`, thumb on the right, green track) and negative (`false`, thumb on the left, red track).
The first click on a neutral switch makes it positive and calls `onChange(true)`.
Each later click flips between positive and negative and calls `onChange` with the new boolean (not an event).
Clicking the visible `label` text flips it the same way.
Uncontrolled (`defaultValue`): it keeps its own state and follows the click order above.
Controlled (`value`): it shows what `value` says; a click only calls `onChange`, and the display changes only when the parent passes the new `value`; the parent can set `null` to return to neutral.
The input carries `aria-checked="mixed"` while neutral and `aria-checked="true"` or `"false"` otherwise.
With `label` the text sits next to the track and names the control; with `description` the secondary text shows under the label and is the input's `aria-describedby` target.
`invalid` sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the input and shows a danger border and danger label and description.
`onFocus` and `onBlur` fire when the input gains or loses focus.

doesNot.text: A click never returns the switch to neutral; only `value` or a new mount with `defaultValue` does.
Does not call `onChange` and does not change while `disabled` or `loading`.
Does not render a label or description when none is given.
Does not use the `id`, `aria-describedby` or `aria-required` props from a surrounding `Field` (it uses `inputId` and `description`), and carries no field layer of its own.
`aria-label` is dropped when a visible `label` is given.
Neutral does not look like negative in colour: neutral has no fill, negative is red; both put the thumb on the left.
Does not show custom track or thumb content (no such props).

defaults.text: Neutral (`defaultValue` null), enabled, not loading, not invalid.
`size` is `xs` (32 by 16 px track); `labelPosition` is `after`.
`role` is `checkbox` on the input (not `switch`).
The input always carries `aria-invalid`, `"false"` while valid.
No label, no description.

onlyWhenConfigured.text: `defaultValue` / `value`: the starting state; `value` (including `null`) makes it controlled.
`label`: visible text, hides `aria-label`; `labelPosition: 'before'` puts label and description left of the track.
`description`: secondary text under the label.
`size: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` (also responsive): larger track, thumb and text.
`disabled`: greyed track and text, no pointer events, input disabled.
`loading`: a spinner shows on the thumb, the input is disabled.
`invalid`: see Does.
`inputId`, `role`, `tabIndex`: the input's id, role and tab order.
`className`, `style`, `pt`: root styling only.

keyboard.text: Tab moves focus to the input and a focus halo shows around the thumb.
Space on the focused input advances the state like a click; Enter does not.
A disabled or loading switch is skipped by Tab.

states.text: Neutral: thumb left, no fill, neutral border.
Positive: thumb right, success (green) fill.
Negative: thumb left, danger (red) fill.
Invalid: danger border; label and description in danger colour.
Disabled: dimmed track and text; loading: spinner in the thumb and input disabled.
Focused: halo around the thumb.

testApi: `Spectra.findTriStateSwitch(label)` by `aria-label` or label text; `Spectra.queryTriStateSwitch(label)` is `null` when missing; `Spectra.shouldNotFindTriStateSwitch(label)`.
`getContainer()`, `getInput()`, `getTrack()`, `getThumb()`.
`getValue()` (`shouldHaveValue(true | false | null)`): reads `aria-checked` (`mixed` is `null`).
`getState()` (`shouldHaveState('neutral' | 'positive' | 'negative')`), `isNeutral()` / `isIndeterminate()`, `isPositive()`, `isNegative()` with their `shouldBe*` / `shouldNotBe*`.
`toggle()` clicks once (advances the state machine); `setPositive()` and `setNegative()` click until the state is reached.
`isDisabled()` (true while loading too), `isLoading()`, `isInvalid()`, `isFocused()`, `focus()`, `blur()`.
`getLabel()`, `getLabelText()`, `hasLabel()`, `getDescription()`, `getDescriptionText()`, `hasDescription()`, `getLoadingIcon()`, `hasLoadingIcon()`.
